title: Five Bold Buffalo Bills' Predictions for 2026 Second Half
full_text:
At 7-1, the Buffalo Bills are tied for the best record in the NFL and have the No. 1 seed in the AFC right now. They're coming off a statement victory over the Minnesota Vikings , winning 23-6 against one of the top defenses in the league.
With eight games behind them, the Bills are at just about the halfway point. They've seen enough of their team to feel confident that they can match up against anyone, although they were also smart enough to admit there were some concerns.
That's why Brandon Beane made a move at the NFL trade deadline , bringing in veteran safety Amani Hooker in exchange for a second-round pick. With all that behind us, let's look ahead to the final nine games and make some bold predictions for the Bills' second half of the season.
Buffalo gave up at least 30 points in four of their first six games of the season. Since the bye week, however, they've surrendered 16 points over two games. Bills On SI's Ralph Ventre recently wrote that this defense, which struggled mightily against the pass to begin the year, gave up no passing touchdowns over the past two games as they shut down the Ravens and Vikings. The two teams combined for just 250 passing yards and completed fewer than 50 percent of their attempts.
Buffalo did face backups in each game, but it's clear their defense has been improving. Now, with the addition of Hooker, look for that to continue. They won't be as dominant against starting quarterbacks, but this bold prediction has Jim Leonhard's defense playing at a top-10 level for the remainder of the year.
Amani Hooker has been a solid player throughout his career, but comes to Buffalo on a hot streak. He has a league-leading five interceptions , thanks in large part to his three interception performance during the Tennessee Titans' Week 8 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals.
That will go down as his final game with the Titans, but there are still plenty of highlights left for Hooker. In this bold prediction, he continues to play at an incredibly high level and picks off four more passes this season. That should be enough for him to finish atop the leaderboard for the season.
Following an explosive debut with the Bills , DJ Moore has slowed down tremendously. A shoulder injury has been part of the problem as he's missed two full games, while being limited in others. What we have seen, however, is that Moore can be a difference-maker when healthy.
Moore currently has 285 yards and two touchdowns, but in this bold prediction, he's able to stay healthy and pad his stats. Look for Moore to finish with 900 yards receiving and eight touchdowns.
As good as Josh Allen has been for the Bills, he hasn't had huge numbers when it comes to passing yardage. While he did have a four-year stretch with more than 4,000 yards, he hasn't hit that mark since the 2023 season. After eight games in 2026, he's on pace to achieve that once again as he has thrown for 2,027 yards. In this bold prediction, he picks that pace up a bit as the season goes along, allowing him to finish with more than 4,000 yards through the air for the first time in three years.
Greg Rousseau was off to a tremendous start with six sacks in the Bills' first three games. He then went three games without a sack, but has picked things up again as he has one in each of the past two games.
Rousseau has been a stud under Jim Leonhard and that should continue in the second half of the season. That's why this final bold prediction has Rousseau racking up seven sacks in the final nine games, giving him a total of 15 on the year.

title: Bills' Defensive Captain Doubles as Most Disappointing Player at Season's Midpoint
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills' defense is showing signs of life following a slow start to the season.
Some defenders—like sixth-year veteran pass-rusher Gregory Rousseau, second-year defensive lineman Deone Walker , and rookie cornerback Davison Igbinosun —have already started to shine on a consistent basis.
Others, however, have been stuck in the mud, so to speak, waiting to break loose.
Defensive captain Bradley Chubb, who is in his first year with the Bills after joining the team via free agency this past March on a three-year, $43.5 million deal following stints with Denver and Miami during his first eight years in the NFL.
Sandwiched around an ACL tear that caused him to miss the entire 2024 campaign, Chubb had previously tallied a total of 19.5 sacks between his last two fully healthy seasons in 2023 and 2025—which included 8.5 quarterback takedowns just one year ago—so, it was expected that the former No. 5 overall draft pick would provide some stability opposite of fellow pass-rusher Gregory Rousseau this year.
So far, though, that hasn’t been the case . . . hardly, in fact.
The 30-year-old did manage to earn captain status within Buffalo’s locker room in just his first season with the club, but the 6-foot-4, 268-pound outside linebacker’s play between the white lines through the first eight games has been sorely lacking.
Even though Rousseau currently finds himself second in the entire NFL with eight sacks entering the middle of November, which ties his career-high , there has been seemingly no help at all from his fellow pass-rushers on Buffalo’s roster.
So, keeping that in mind, something must change.
The Bills can’t keep relying on Rousseau to be the only legitimate threat off the edge as the calendar inches closer to December.
And, considering Chubb was Buffalo’s biggest offseason addition on the defensive side of the ball other than safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson, who is rightfully no longer on the team , there needs to be a sense of urgency from the ninth-year veteran.
While it’s true that the Georgia native’s leadership can’t be understated, the same can also be said for his lack of production so far.
On pace for just three sacks for the entire 17-game stretch of the 2026 regular season at this point, which would mark a career-low for any season he’s played more than seven games, there’s no denying that Chubb isn’t holding up his end of the bargain. In total through eight games, he has just 18 tackles, a mere eight quarterback hits, two tackles for loss, one-and-a-half sacks, and only one pass deflection, which came last week against the Minnesota Vikings on a screen pass that should've been intercepted. But, unfortunately the veteran wasn't able to make the play.
Once thought to be a solid counterpart for Rousseau, Chubb is looking more like another failed experiment —a la Joey Bosa last season—rather than being a solution to any of Buffalo’s pass-rushing problems.
Moving forward, it’ll be imperative that the Bills get some sort of increased production from Chubb in terms of getting after the opposing gunslingers, especially with players like Kansas City’s Patrick Mahomes, Green Bay’s Jordan Love, and Chicago’s Caleb Williams still to come on the schedule.
There’s also New England Patriots’ quarterback Drake Maye, who seems to have Buffalo’s number thus far in his young career , on the schedule once more, too.
Needless to say, if the Bills want any chance at capturing the No. 1 seed in the AFC in January— and possibly more —then it’ll be imperative that Chubb start providing the type of statistical impact that he was brought in to make.
Sunday’s road outing against the Jets, who have surrendered the fourth-most sacks in the league with a count of 28, would be a good place to start.

title: Did Buffalo Bills Do Enough at NFL Trade Deadline?
full_text:
This year's NFL trade deadline was rather busy, but Buffalo Bills fans are only concerned with what their team did. And this year, they made an impressive move as they added the league's leader in interceptions , Amani Hooker.
Hooker fills a major need since the Bills were thin at safety, especially after releasing C.J. Gardner-Johnson , but they did pay a pretty penny. Buffalo surrendered a second-round pick, but we have to admit, Hooker is far superior to any player they could have added near the end of the second round in 2027.
Of course, the question of value isn't the only one that needs to be answered. In addition to that, fans want to know if the Bills general manager Brandon Beane did enough to shore up the roster for the postseason push. According to Albert Breer, they did.
Breer said the Bills did enough , but he's not looking at the move for Hooker in a vacuum. He's still taking into consideration the fact that Beane made a big move this offseason to get wide receiver D.J. Moore , who also was added for a second-round pick. As Breer points out, that means Beane gave up the team's second pick in consecutive seasons to address their two biggest needs.
"My answer to that question is yes. And I think sometimes the way we look at these moves is, well, why didn't they take a bigger swing? And you're not looking at the totality of the calendar year, you're just looking at what they did over the last couple of weeks," Breer said.
"The Bills already made a big move in trading for DJ Moore. And so when you've already offloaded some draft capital, it does limit, to some degree, what you can do in the current year because you're looking at the big picture of things."
Breer talked about how they didn't think they could get Hooker, but the fact that the Jacksonville Jaguars picked up Jessie Bates from the Atlanta Falcons set the staget. Beane pulled off the move as the deadline approached, and the Bills feel like they added someone who can be a fixture in their defense for years.
"But the Bills view Hooker as a player that's not far off from Bates, a guy who's a true post safety who will complement Cole Bishop, who they move around a bunch. They can play down in the box. He has ball production, which is obviously a big piece of the picture, and they have him signed for the next couple of years, too," Breer said.
"So, all the way around, they feel like they were able to add a pretty important piece to make that safety position, now with Bishop and Hooker, a very real strength. And so the defense has gotten better over the course of the last few weeks. They've gotten a little more comfortable playing in Jim Leonhard's system."
Breer is correct that the Bills will have to figure things out when it comes to adding developmental players, but as we've seen in recent years, Beane isn't afraid to make moves during the draft. Sure, fans hate seeing their team trade out of the first round, but Beane does this to add enough young, and affordable talent, so that he can roll the dice on players such as Hooker.
As for the question of whether they did enough, I would have to agree with Breer. The Bills had just one glaring weakness, which was at safety. They filled that, and have been playing better over the past two weeks on defense. That sets the stage for an exciting postseason in Western New York.

title: Bills' Once-Deficient Defense Literally Operating at 1985 Bears' Pace After Bye Week
full_text:
Well, that escalated rather quickly.
The Buffalo Bills ' defense faced its share of ridicule over the season's first six weeks.
Owning one of the bottom-ranked pass defenses and allowing more than 28.0 points per game, first-year defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard's unit was at a crossroads of sorts heading into its bye.
"It's time to be good at something," said Leonhard, challenging Buffalo's defense in early October.
The Bills' defense took Leonhard's words to heart if the latest two performances provide any indication. Coming out of the Week 7 bye, Buffalo put together back-to-back efforts rarely seen in NFL circles.
In particular, edge rusher Greg Rousseau has somewhat suprisingly stepped up as has second-round rookie cornerback Davison Igbinosun amongst others .
Although it happened against substandard quarterback play, Buffalo has accounted for a two-game clip unlike any other in more than 40 years. In fact, the last team to do what the Bills just did is the legendary 1985 Chicago Bears, who went on to dominate the New England Patriots in Super Bowl XX.
Defeating the Baltimore Ravens at home in Week 8 followed by the Minnesota Vikings on the road in Week 9, Buffalo flatout stifled the opposing passing attacks. Granted Lamar Jackson lasted only one play for the Ravens, who turned to Tyler Huntley and Joe Fagnano to get through the game. The Vikings started Carson Wentz with Kyler Murray unavailable.
The Bills did not allow a passing touchdown while limiting the Ravens to 91 yards through the air and the Vikings to 139 pass yards. Buffalo also held both teams under the 50 percent completion mark, adding multiple sacks and takeaways in each win.
Reaching a level that no team has since the '85 Bears, the Bills recorded multiple sacks and 3+ takeaways in back-to-back games while holding the opponents under 200 total yards, under 50 percent completions and without a touchdown pass ( per Buffalo Bills PR ).
“I feel like the last two weeks, take the quarterbacks into account who they are. The game plans put our guys in position to make plays," said Leonhard. "It allowed us to help dictate how to play the game, what they had to do, how aggressive they could be, or not be, in certain situations. That's the job of a defense, is finding the best way to attack an offense, given who they have on the field, and go win games."
With the New York Jets (2-7) and Geno Smith up next, one has to think it's not entirely out of the question that the Bills make it three in a row. It may not be likely, but it's certainly possible.

title: Joe Brady Confirms Amani Hooker's Status for Bills vs. Jets Week 10 Game
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills made one of the biggest trades at the deadline on Tuesday when they acquired safety Amani Hooker from the Tennessee Titans.
It was a trade that was sorely needed, as the Bills had a major need at the safety position, even before the release of C.J. Gardner-Johnson .
The only concern was that Hooker would only have mere days to grasp as much of the playbook as he can before the Bills meet the New York Jets on Sunday afternoon and he might not be ready to make his Bills debut right away.
Well, the Bills have since confirmed what Hooker's status is for Sunday.
Hooker did say in his first media availability with the team that he would play , so that was the first sign he would go.
“Oh I’m gonna play on Sunday. Yeah. I’ll be ready to go," Hooker said .
However, the decision isn't just up to the player. The coaching staff has to be comfortable that he knows enough of the playbook to be sent out there after just a handful of days with the team.
Apparently, the Bills do feel comfortable with Hooker, as head coach Joe Brady confirmed Hooker is "definitely going to play."
So, now that we know Hooker is going to suit up, the next question is: will Hooker play a full workload?
With the Titans, Hooker played nearly every snap, but it's fair to wonder if he'll be ready to do so for the Bills in Week 10.
Brady did not have a definitive answer for that and said the team would evaluate the practice tape.
However, he also noted that he and defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard have been impressed with how quickly Hooker has picked everything up.
"Everything that we were told about or that we've known about him has kind of held true," he stated. "Jim's been extremely impressed with how quickly he's able to pick stuff up, be able to communicate in our language and kind of go from there. "
"We'll evaluate the tape today and kind of get a feel of what does it look like in terms of play time going into the game. From a comfort level we don't want to put him out there and do anything that is not fair to him and the team. But he's been extremely impressive and excited he's definitely going to play and excited to see whatever that role looks like," Brady added.
None of what Brady said is surprising at all. We know Hooker is a high IQ football player from his days with the Titans and we fully expected him to get acclimated rather quickly.
From the sounds of it, Hooker is grasping things fast enough that he will at least be able to play the majority of snaps for the Bills in his debut.
The majority of the snaps Hooker doesn't play will likely be soaked up by Damar Hamlin, who started at safety in each of the last two games.
When Hooker is on the football field, we expected him to play free safety.
Hooker is a well-rounded safety, so he can play anywhere, but he does his best work on the back end, where he's solid in coverage and has a nose for the football.
We also know the Bills could use an upgrade in that area of the field, as Buffalo enters this game against the Jets sporting the fourth-worst pass defense in the league that has given up a whopping 28 completions of 20-plus yards.
If all goes well, Hooker should help improve both of those issues.

title: Buffalo Bills' Most Surprising Player at Midway Point of 2026 NFL Season
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills have reached the halfway point of the season after notching yet another win in Week 9, so it's a good time to look back on the year that has been thus far.
We certainly can't say we're surprised to see how well the Bills have done following a 7-1 first half. After all, Buffalo was widely viewed as a Super Bowl contender yet again entering the 2026 campaign.
What has been a surprise is the performance of one defensive player in particular who we've pegged as the team's biggest surprise from the first half of the season.
There's a few players to choose from but we're going with edge rusher Greg Rousseau, who is in the midst of a career year.
There was even more pressure on Rousseau than usual going into this season after he inked a four-year, $80 million contract extension back in March.
With eight sacks in eight games, which is tied for the second-most in the NFL, Rousseau has answered the challenge.
Those eight sacks already tie his career-high that he set in 2024. Rousseau racked up six sacks over his first three games before going quiet over the next three, but he has since bounced back with two sacks in his last two games.
Here’s #Bills Greg Rousseau single-handedly ruining a #Vikings in the mid second quarter. I’ll just let the tape speak for itself. #BillsMafia @BuffTrenchTalk https://t.co/N6DgO3JaZu pic.twitter.com/PFOuNuqkYb
According to Pro Football Focus , Rousseau's 51 total pressures and 87.1 pass-rush grade rank first and fourth at the position, and he has even proven to be an asset against the run with a grade of 62.4.
If Rousseau keeps up at his current pace, he'll finish with a total of 108 pressures and 17 sacks. The latter mark would rank as the third-most in a single season in franchise history behind Bruce Smith (19.5 in 1990) and Bryce Paup (17.5 in 1995).
After racking up his first six sacks of the season in the month of September, Rousseau talked about what he believed was the reason behind his incredible surge .
Rousseau gave a few reasons, the first of which is the scheme change under new defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard.
"I feel like sometimes it's easy to get caught up in the numbers, but I feel like I was rushing good before in the previous few years. But I'd definitely say, man, the scheme's been great. Just being able to stand up and kind of get on my angle and kind of have more space, be able to get to my length more," Rousseau said.
In addition to that, having guys like Deone Walker and Ed Oliver up the middle causing fits for opposing offensive linemen has helped free Rousseau up with more favorable matchups on the outside.
"You got Deone (Walker), Ed (Oliver), in the interior doing what they're doing. Even like Dewayne Carter in the last game. It's like taking candy from a baby. You know what I'm saying?" Rousseau said. "Like when they're getting vertical or they're doing their thing, they're penetrating or whatever, working off them. It makes it real easy."
It's no doubt a symbiotic relationship upfront. In the same breath, with Rousseau wreaking havoc on the outside, that is freeing up Oliver and Walker, also, so Rousseau's impact is more than just about his sack production.
After five seasons, we've come to expect solid production from Rousseau, but in 2026, he's providing elite production instead, which amounts to a very pleasant surprise for the Bills.

title: GM Dan Morgan’s Biggest 2026 Mistake Could Haunt Panthers’ Playoff Hopes
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers are still in the hunt in the NFC South, but the lack of depth has been exposed by several injuries. This is a question for general manager Dan Morgan to answer.
Although the Carolina Panthers have a losing record, they are still in contention for the NFC South Division title. But the second half of the season will test the depth that general manager Dan Morgan brought in for this team.
The last three games for the Carolina Panthers have shown that there are many problems with this team, even though they are still in the race for the NFC South with a 3-5 record.
Morgan's biggest mistake this year was not bringing in more depth at cornerback.
Will Lee III and Akayleb Evans have also dealt with injuries, further depleting the Panthers' secondary. With Lee unavailable against Denver and Evans on injured reserve, Carolina had little dependable depth behind its starting cornerbacks. Against the Broncos, the Panthers were forced to start Wilson and Thornton, who struggled in the game.
We looked into the Panthers' issues with cornerback depth in a previous article , but now the problems are fully visible.
The Panthers were called for four defensive pass interference penalties against Denver. One of Wilson's penalties was declined in favor of a taunting penalty against him on the same play. Two of the accepted DPI penalties came on drives that ended in Denver touchdowns.
When a defense is getting beat consistently on the outside, that is a very difficult situation to overcome.
While injuries are part of football, Morgan did not do enough to make sure there were players available on the roster who could step in when a starter went down.
The secondary simply does not have enough dependable depth to handle the loss of both Horn and Jackson.
There were several cornerbacks who could have been of interest to the Panthers as the November 10 trade deadline approached.
The Panthers have limited salary-cap space and would have had to consider the cost of bringing in a player for the short term, as well as the draft capital that would be required to acquire that player.
As previously discussed in why the Panthers stayed quiet at the trade deadline, Morgan ultimately decided not to make a move.
The Panthers will have to find a long-term solution at the cornerback position, but for now, they are relying on the players already on the roster until some of the injured players return to the field.
In other news, Carolina's injured players are making progress toward returning to the field. On Wednesday, the practice windows for cornerback Mike Jackson, running back Jonathon Brooks and wide receiver Xavier Legette were opened, while Jaelan Phillips returned to practice after missing the last three games. Jackson was listed as doubtful for Sunday's game against New Orleans.
The Panthers are trying to build a team for years to come, and Morgan does not want to trade for a player who could hurt the team in the long run.
Carolina is currently in a position where every game counts, and the secondary cannot continue to be a liability.
Morgan's biggest mistake this season was not making a trade for a player who could help the team in the long run. He built a team with a lot of depth at many positions but not enough in the secondary.
The secondary must improve for the Panthers to have any chance of reaching the playoffs. If the team fails to do so, many will point to Morgan's decisions in building the roster.

title: Biggest Problem Could Cost Them a Chance to Win the NFC South
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers are still in the hunt to win the NFC South, but the first half of the season under third-year head coach Dave Canales has been anything but consistent.
The first half of the season for the Carolina Panthers has been a mix of good and bad. They have played some of the best teams in the league and shown they can match up with them. But there have also been some bad losses to teams lower in the standings. Right now, the Panthers are 3-5 on the season and on a three-game losing streak.
The biggest problem that the Carolina Panthers have had this season is their lack of discipline. The Panthers have committed too many penalties, and that is something head coach Dave Canales needs to work on with the team.
Carolina has been penalized 70 times for 635 yards this season, an average of 8.8 penalties for 79.4 yards per game. Last year, the Panthers averaged 5.6 penalties for 44.8 yards per game. That is a significant increase and a problem that has continued throughout the season.
The errors have hurt Carolina in several games this season, including the season opener against Chicago, when the Panthers were penalized 11 times for 84 yards; the game against the Eagles, when Carolina was penalized 13 times for 149 yards; and the game against the Broncos, when the Panthers were penalized 13 times for 119 yards.
In several games this season, the Panthers have extended opposing drives because of the penalties they have committed. This was especially noticeable against the Broncos, when defensive pass interference penalties repeatedly helped Denver keep drives alive.
After the Denver game, Canales said, “When you play a good opponent, you have to minimize the mistakes, and 100 yards of penalties in the first half was a big one. We're asking our corners to challenge outside, but we got to be clean with our hands.”
These errors must stop. The penalties are giving opponents better field position and allowing them to gain more yards than they would have otherwise.
Carolina Panthers head coach Dave Canales has some serious changes to make on the field, similar to the changes he has made with the coaching staff this season. He let go of defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero and promoted defensive line coach Todd Wash to the interim defensive coordinator role.
The Carolina Panthers can still win the NFC South in the second half of the season, but they are going to have to play much better than they have in the first half. The Panthers have very little room for error if they want to make the playoffs at 3-5.
Canales has already made a major change to the coaching staff. Now, he needs to find a way to get his players to clean up the mistakes that keep putting the Panthers in difficult situations. If the penalties continue, Carolina could find its playoff hopes slipping away.

title: Panthers Have Bigger Aspirations, but Are They Good Enough to Get There?
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers find themselves in an interesting position for the second half of the 2026 NFL season. The Panthers have lost three straight games but still remain in the thick of the NFC South race with the opportunity to make the playoffs.
While Carolina is not a playoff-caliber team yet, it is showing signs of life as a 3-5 team. There are also many reasons for concern as to whether or not this team can play with any consistency.
The Carolina Panthers fell to the Denver Broncos, 26-21, in Week 9 action. Quarterback Bryce Young completed 28 of 39 passes for 276 yards and three touchdowns in the loss. However, he also had an interception in the end zone and lost a fumble late in the game that was recovered by the Broncos. The Panthers also had 13 penalties for 119 yards in the loss.
The Panthers have lost three straight to the Buccaneers, Packers and Broncos. In each of those games, mistakes were made that were capitalized on by the other team.
The reason Carolina is still in the hunt for the playoffs is because of the division it plays in. The Panthers and New Orleans Saints are both 3-5 and tied for first place in the division. Tampa Bay and Atlanta are both 3-6.
Carolina can remain in the division race without having to make up too many games on the first-place teams. Last year, the Panthers won the NFC South with an 8-9 record.
Winning the division and making a playoff run are two different things, though. The Panthers need to find a way to become more consistent.
This will be a huge game for the Panthers as they look to get back on track and win in New Orleans. If they can get a win against the Saints, then they will be in a good position in the division as well as stopping their current slide. Carolina has Baltimore and Tampa Bay after New Orleans.
There is still plenty of time for the Panthers to turn things around, but the NFC South gives them plenty of opportunities.
The main thing that the Panthers are looking for in the rest of the season is to be able to play some consistent football. The defense needs to be able to stop teams from scoring, and the offense needs to stop making mistakes like they have been in the last few games.
This team wants to do more than just compete in the NFC South this year. Whether or not they have the goods to make another run at the playoffs is yet to be determined, but the next few weeks will provide answers to that question.

title: Week 10 Fantasy Football Projections for Bryce Young, Tetairoa McMillan & More
full_text:
This week, the Carolina Panthers will travel to New Orleans to take on the Saints in a game that should be of interest to many fantasy football players.
The Panthers are coming off a 26-21 loss to the Broncos in Week 9, in which Bryce Young had one of his better games of the season. He completed 28 of 39 passes for 276 yards with three touchdowns and one interception. The Saints have given up a lot of yards to opposing quarterbacks this season, so Young could have a big game this week.
Carolina’s offense features a number of players who can be of value to fantasy owners in Week 10, including Tetairoa McMillan, Chuba Hubbard and Darren Waller.
After throwing three touchdowns against the Broncos last week, Young could have another big game against the Saints.
Carolina’s offense is going to need to protect Young better than it has in the past, but the Saints have struggled to pressure opposing quarterbacks. Young could have time to get the ball to his receivers in order to put up some numbers.
McMillan is also expected to have a big game for the Panthers’ passing attack. McMillan has been one of Young’s main targets this season, and the Panthers are going to need him to make plays in order to win this game.
The Almanac’s Week 10 fantasy projections have Young throwing for 257 yards and 1.8 touchdowns. McMillan is projected to catch approximately five passes for 68 yards.
The Saints are struggling to stop teams from throwing on them this season, which could mean big games for both Young and McMillan. They could be good fantasy options at quarterback and wide receiver for owners in need of help at those positions.
Bryce Young projection: 257 passing yards, 1.8 passing touchdowns, 18.6 projected DraftKings fantasy points.
Tetairoa McMillan projection: 5.1 receptions, 68 receiving yards, 14.9 projected DraftKings fantasy points.
Chuba Hubbard has been an important part of Carolina's offense this season, and the Saints have struggled to stop the run this year, so he could have another solid game.
The Saints have given up a lot of yards to opposing running backs this season, and Hubbard has been getting plenty of carries as well as some catches out of the backfield. He could have another big game on Sunday.
Jalen Coker is another Panthers receiver who could provide some value in fantasy lineups. He is projected to catch approximately four passes for 51 yards against New Orleans.
While McMillan is projected to have a better game than Coker, the wide receiver could be a solid fantasy option for those in need of a receiver. He has been getting plenty of looks in Carolina’s passing game, but the team has several other receivers on the roster as well.
Darren Waller had a big game against the Denver Broncos last week, catching eight passes for 90 yards and one touchdown.
The Saints have given up some yards to opposing tight ends this season, and Waller’s projected stats are approximately three receptions for 35 yards. He could still have some opportunities to score in the passing game.
The Panthers will be looking to build on last week's offensive performance against Denver, and Young, McMillan and Hubbard could be among Carolina's better fantasy options this weekend.

title: Panthers’ Most Disappointing Player in 2026 Has Been a Huge Surprise
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers have severely underperformed so far this season. At 3-5, Carolina has lost three straight and has clear flaws on the roster. The defense hasn't lived up to preseason expectations, but injuries are a huge part of why.
The secondary has been thin since Week 3, and that should change this weekend with Will Lee listed as questionable and Mike Jackson returning to practice despite being listed as doubtful on Friday.
The biggest question entering this season was how much of a leap, if any, would Bryce Young take. It's clear that Young has improved; his poise, conviction, ball placement, and subtle pocket movement have all been outstanding.
Two years ago, when the Panthers were objectively awful, Bryce Young was the problem for the first half of the season; that's not the case anymore. The Panthers' biggest problem right now is the offensive line . One player in particular has been at the forefront of that unit's issues.
Rasheed Walker was supposed to be one of the steals of free agency for Carolina. In 2025, Walker started at left tackle for the Green Bay Packers and excelled as a pass blocker. Walker posted a 94% pass-block win rate, which ranked 11th in the NFL.
Walker allowed five sacks for the entire 2025 season with Green Bay. Now, through eight games in Carolina, he's allowed five sacks. It's not just giving up sacks; Walker has allowed 45 QB pressures in 2026. For context, the league leader in pressures allowed is Spencer Fano, with 52.
Walker remained the starting left tackle for Carolina against Denver, and as he's done throughout the season, he allowed pressure, as Nik Bonitto won the one-on-one matchup, and forced a fumble from Bryce Young, which ended the game.
Walker got beat badly on that play, but, to give him a little bit of grace, he shouldn't have been on an island against one of football's best pass rushers.
It's still a failed assignment, though, and the problem is that Carolina's offensive line is too injured to make a change. If Taylor Moton were healthy at right tackle, then Monroe Freeling would have to get a chance at left tackle.
From an offensive line perspective, the schedule is daunting. After Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints, Carolina plays the Ravens, Buccaneers, and Vikings. All three teams rank in the top 13 in pass-rush win rate; the Buccaneers are eighth, and the Vikings are No. 1 in the league.
Not a very encouraging schedule to look at with how bad the offensive line, and especially Rasheed Walker, has been in 2026.
Preston is an experienced sports writer focusing on NFL, College Football, NBA, and MMA topics. He is a passionate Charlotte and Oklahoma sports fan and graduated from the University of Science and Arts Oklahoma in 2025 with a Bachelor of Arts in Communications degree with a focus in journalism.

title: Ideal Offensive Line Solution is Sitting on FA Market Waiting for Panthers
full_text:
It’s far from an intimidating quartet. Every team in the NFC South has won exactly three games this season. And each of the four clubs has at least five losses. The 3-5 Carolina Panthers face the 3-5 New Orleans Saints on Sunday at the Superdome, with the 3-6 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (off this week) and 3-6 Atlanta Falcons in third and fourth place, respectively. All of these teams could certainly use some help in terms of reinforcements.
Moe Moton of Bleacher Report had a few suggestions for Dave Canales’s club, one on each side of the football. On defense, he explained that edge rusher Haason Reddick, who played for the Panthers in 2021 and spent this past season with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, could help a team that has managed to come up with only a dozen sacks in eight games.
As for the offense, the tackle situation has been a nightmare. Left sider Ikem Ekwonu has not played a down after suffering a ruptured patellar tendon in last season’s playoff loss to the Rams. Veteran right tackle Taylor Moton missed the start of the season recovering from blood colts. In his second start of 2026, he went down with a broken fibula and is currently on injured reserve.
Former Packers’ blocker Rasheed Walker has started all eight game at left tackle for Canales’s squad, while 2026 first-round pick Monroe Freeling began the season at right tackle, gave way to Moton for two games, and is now back in the starting role. There have also been three different starters at left guard. Entering Week 10, Carolina had the 27th-ranked offensive line in the league via Pro Football Focus . I t’s certainly a group that could use some help, and Moton may have the solution.
“Taylor Decker may be waiting for the right situation to sign with a contender. He’s a 33-year-old career left tackle who earned a Pro Bowl nod in 2024. After 10 seasons, his tenure with the Detroit Lions ended after he refused to take a pay cut. The 10-year veteran requested his release…”
Bryce Young gets strip sacked and the Bucs defense takes it back for 6! The Panthers are getting punched in the mouth in the first half. pic.twitter.com/JU7aYDDJvF
During his stay in the Motor City, the 16th overall pick in the 2016 NFL draft played and started 140 regular-season games, as well as five postseason contests. The former Buckeye graded out 41st out of 89 qualified tackles via PFF in his last NFL season in 2025.
“ The Carolina Panthers are trying to get back to the postseason, ” explained Moton, “but Bryce Young has taken a lot of hits. He's already taken 26 sacks, just one fewer than all of last season. Left tackle Rasheed Walker is struggling in pass protection, allowing five sacks on 367 pass-blocking snaps, per Pro Football Focus .”
It certainly wouldn’t hurt to have a proven performer with playoff experience such as Taylor on the roster. And it’s worth noting that more than half (14) of those aforementioned 26 sacks absorbed by Young have come during Carolina’s current three-game losing streak.

title: Panthers Need Ickey Ekwonu, But Other NFL Teams Might Have Final Say
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers continue to wait for the return of Ikem Ekwonu, the team’s starting left tackle, who suffered a torn patellar tendon in his right knee during the team’s playoff loss to the Los Angeles Rams in January.
The Panthers have the 26-year-old left tackle under contract for the remainder of the season, but then he could become a free agent. Bleacher Report lists Ekwonu as the No. 46 potential free agent for 2027 , which means other teams could be willing to pay more for a starting left tackle than the Panthers can afford.
Ekwonu was the No. 6 pick in the 2022 NFL Draft by the Carolina Panthers. He has been the Panthers' starting left tackle for the past four seasons.
In Carolina’s loss to the Los Angeles Rams in the playoffs last January, Ekwonu suffered a torn patellar tendon in his right knee. He has yet to play in any games this season as he continues to recover from the injury.
Kristopher Knox of Bleacher Report believes that several teams could be interested in signing the 26-year-old left tackle if he is healthy. He is young enough to be a long-term solution at the position for another team.
Of course, any team considering signing Ekwonu would have to be concerned about the serious knee injury that the tackle sustained in January. He hasn’t played in any games this season, and there’s no guarantee he’ll return to the same level of play that he displayed before the injury.
But the Panthers have another problem to deal with, as Ekwonu's contract will expire at the end of the season. If the Panthers can’t come to terms on a new deal with him, then other teams in the NFL could look to sign him.
Carolina picked up the fifth-year option on Ekwonu’s contract in April 2025. This kept the tackle under contract with the Panthers through the 2026 season.
Carolina is going to have to make a decision on whether to sign Ekwonu to a long-term contract or go with the current group of offensive tackles.
The Panthers have had so many problems this season with their offensive line that having to worry about the left tackle position after this season is the last thing Carolina needs.
Carolina signed Rasheed Walker in free agency to play left tackle while Ekwonu recovers from his knee injury. However, Walker’s struggles in pass protection against Denver were on full display in the loss to the Broncos.
In the Panthers’ loss to the Broncos, Walker was beaten by Nik Bonitto, who forced a sack-fumble on Bryce Young and recovered the ball. The turnover effectively ended any hopes of a comeback by the Panthers.
The other young offensive tackle on the roster is Monroe Freeling. The Panthers drafted Freeling in the first round of the 2026 NFL Draft , and he is currently listed at right tackle.
While Carolina does have another young tackle in Freeling, it doesn’t mean that the team has to move on from Ekwonu. It all depends on how he looks when he returns to the field.
There is also the question of when Ekwonu will return to the field. Head coach Dave Canales said recently that the left tackle is making progress, but he has not given a time frame for when Ekwonu will be back on the field.
Carolina would like to see Ekwonu back on the field before the season ends. That way, the team can see what he is capable of, and Ekwonu can show that he is still a very good player.
Ikem Ekwonu wants to stay with the Carolina Panthers, and general manager Dan Morgan wants to keep the 26-year-old left tackle with the team.
Morgan has previously expressed his desire to keep Ekwonu in Carolina, although the two sides have yet to announce a long-term agreement.
There is a possibility that Carolina wants to keep Ekwonu, but another team is willing to pay more for his services. This is something that the Panthers would have to deal with if Ekwonu were to hit free agency.
Right now, the team needs Ekwonu to return to the field, and then it can deal with the rest of the season and other teams potentially searching for a left tackle.
Carolina has had Ekwonu protecting Bryce Young’s blind side since Young entered the NFL in 2023. Whether or not the Panthers can keep him there for several more years remains to be seen.

title: The Panthers Desperately Need Defensive Help and Not at Cornerback
full_text:
Dave Canales’s team has lost its last three games. Shaky offensive play, some untimely turnovers, and numerous defensive issues have all contributed to the Carolina Panthers being outscored a combined 96-53 in setbacks to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (43-13), Green Bay Packers (27-19), and Denver Broncos (26-21) —two of those defeats at home.
The Panthers are hurting on defense, literally, in two specific areas. Starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson were placed on injured reserve on September 30. Veteran pass rusher Jaelan Phillips has missed the last three games. And that aspect of the defense suffered a big blow even before the 2026 season was edge performer Nic Scourton was lost for the season when he tore his ACL on the first day of training camp.
When the #Panthers allow Princely Umanmielen (3) to hunt the QB, you see things like this. Speed and quickness against Penei Sewell using a dip-rip through contact to get pressure and a hit on Jared Goff. pic.twitter.com/mNNFrD1PVs
The numbers had become very repetitive the past three seasons, and the pass rush has still not progressed for the aforementioned reasons and more. Canales’s club and the Miami Dolphins are tied with an NFL-low 12 sacks, both in eight games. And to update a significant statistic, no team in the league has fewer quarterback traps (101) than the Panthers dating back to 2023.
Currently, Carolina’s top three sacks artists are second-year pro Princely Umanmielen (3.0), Phillips (2.5) and 2026 free-agent pickup Devin Lloyd (2.0). The NFC South leaders went two straight games without a sack until last Sunday when Patrick Jones II dropped Broncos’ quarterback Bo Nix. All told, 11 of the team’s dozen QB traps came during the team’s 3-2 start.
Earlier this week, NFL writer Moe Moton of Bleacher Report focused on 10 performers that are still on the open market that teams could add at a bargain price. Moton had a few suggestions for the Panthers in terms of fit, and when it came to the defensive side of the ball, he pointed to a player that has spent some time in Charlotte.
“Coming out of Temple in 2017, Haason Reddick entered the league as a hybrid defender who can play inside and outside linebacker and settled into a pass-rushing role off the edge in his fourth season. Reddick logged at least 11 sacks in four consecutive campaigns between 2020 and 2023, but his production declined sharply after the Philadelphia Eagles traded him to the New York Jets in 2024, partly because of a lengthy holdout.” That included 11.0 sacks in 16 games with the Panthers in 2021.
In his final two seasons with the Birds (2022-23), Reddick started all 34 regular-season games. He totaled a combined 27.0 sacks, five forced fumbles, and three fumble recoveries in those contests. He also played and started in four postseason contests over that span.
During Philadelphia’s 2022 playoff run which led to an appearance in Super Bowl LVII, he amassed 3.5 sacks, one forced fumble, and a fumble recovery. Reddick earned a pair of Pro Bowl invites those two years before things went a little south. He spent 2024 with the New York Jets and logged one sack in 10 games.
“ Reddick signed with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2025 ,” added Moton, “logging 31 tackles (6 for loss), 2.5 sacks and eight pressures in 13 games (12 starts). In a designated pass-rushing role, Reddick should be able to make an impact. He could be a solid fit for the Carolina Panthers, who have generated the second-lowest pressure rate at 16.5 percent…”
Panthers’ general manager Dan Morgan struck gold with the August additions of tight end Darren Waller and linebacker Bobby Okereke. Could he add another proven veteran who could aid the team during this rough stretch? There are certainly concerns at cornerback and won’t truly be resolved until Horn and Jackson return ( the latter returned to practice on Wednesday ). However, it’s the pass rush that’s been a problem for far too long.

That includes television, as he spent more than two decades at ESPN, and was part of shows that garnered five Emmy Awards. He also spent the 2015 NFL season with Thursday Night Football on CBS/NFLN.

title: Carolina Panthers Mailbag: No Trades, First-Place Matchup, and More
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers did not have a busy week, but there's plenty going on with them. It's an important week moving forward, and there are some key storylines coming up. Here's what you need to know.
This, to me, feels very much like the Panthers using a cop-out. The NFC South is abysmal, and the day before the deadline, both the New Orleans Saints and Atlanta Falcons offloaded good players. That leaves the Panthers and Tampa Bay Buccaneers at even strength.
The Panthers have lost three in a row and obviously feel no sense of urgency. They are going to get healthier, but until then, how much longer can they keep losing? The Panthers don't have a ton of flexibility to make moves, so it's not all that surprising. It is a little disappointing, though.
A team in a tight divisional race, with the ridiculous number of injuries the Panthers have sustained, should be adding players to offset the losses and keep them in the race. Instead, the Panthers seem to be banking on everyone else being just as bad. It may well work out, but they could've taken matters into their own hands and probably should have.
When the Panthers were 3-2 and in first place, life felt so good. It felt like they were about to really seize control and take a huge step forward as a franchise. Three losses later, life does not feel good, but they incomprehensibly remain in first place.
That is, until Sunday. A fourth straight loss, this time to the New Orleans Saints, would hand the division lead to the Saints. It's only the middle of the season, but this is a monumental matchup. It is borderline must-win.
The Panthers have overlooked the Saints far too much over the last couple of seasons. Dave Canales-led teams often come out flat when there's a moment like this. Hopefully, that won't be the case this week, but it's hard to have much confidence there.
On paper, though, the Panthers should be slightly better than the Saints here, but that really hasn't mattered before.
Reports suggest that the Panthers and Bryce Young are on their way to an extension worth over $50 million. This is both fair and unfair, appropriate and inappropriate. The report came out during that brutal two-week stretch in which he took 11 sacks, but he's back on the upswing again.
The version of Young we've seen this year, including those two awful games, is absolutely worth $50 million. He's made the most porous offensive line work to the tune of the fourth-most yards per game. He's had to endure receivers coming in and out of the lineup with injuries and a rookie play-caller.
The "problem" is that it's a small sample size. I fully believe this version of Young is here to stay, and that he will never again be questioned as a starting-level QB. The thing I wish would happen is the Panthers using his bad first two years and mediocre third year as a way to get a discount.
Sadly, it doesn't work like that, but it would help the team out a lot. But ultimately, Young has earned a lucrative extension with his play, and that's really all anyone can ask for.
The defense under Todd Wash for his first game as coordinator was not night and day from Ejiro Evero's, but it was better. It's going to take some time for the players to adjust to a slightly new system, so we still saw some lingering Evero things last week and may this week.
What we didn't see, though, were third-and-long conversions (excluding pass interference conversions, but when you're working with practice squad cornerbacks, that's what happens) due to inexplicable coverages. They stopped the run pretty well, too.
They flocked to the ball and played downhill a lot more. The system still needs to be ironed out, but Wash has the players playing hard, and there's not much more we can ask for in the wake of firing a coordinator.
Zachary Roberts is a journalist with a wide variety of experience covering basketball, golf, entertainment, video games, music, football, baseball, and hockey. He currently covers Charlotte sports teams and has been featured on Sportskeeda, Yardbarker, MSN, and On SI.

title: Winners and Losers From Panthers’ Silent Trade Deadline
full_text:
Carolina Panthers GM Dan Morgan has decided to stand pat at the NFL trade deadline for the second consecutive year. The decision by Morgan not to add any pieces to the current roster to help the team in the second half of the season will likely be scrutinized by fans, as the Panthers have lost three straight games and are dealing with injuries to several key players.
But with Carolina sitting at 3-5 on the season, the Panthers are still very much in the NFC South division race. So, while some players on the roster could benefit from Morgan’s decision to stay put, others are sure to have a tougher go of it in the second half of the season.
The biggest winner of the deadline for Carolina is defensive tackle Derrick Brown. According to reports, several teams were calling Morgan regarding the defensive tackle, but the GM was not interested in moving one of the top defensive players on the roster.
But there’s also the fact that Brown is a player the Panthers have invested a lot of money in. So unless someone was offering up a king’s ransom for the defensive tackle, it makes sense that the Panthers would hold on to him.
Players who could benefit from Carolina’s decision to stay put include those on the injured list who are slowly but surely making their way back to practice. Cornerback Mike Jackson, wide receiver Xavier Legette, and running back Jonathon Brooks have all had their 21-day practice windows opened.
The Panthers are hoping that with the return of Jackson and Horn, the Carolina secondary will be able to play at a high level for the rest of the season.
Another winner is Carolina’s future draft capital. The Panthers didn’t give up any draft picks to acquire a player for the remainder of this season.
There are currently eight picks that the Panthers have in the 2027 NFL Draft. Carolina still has plenty of needs to fill, and Morgan will have plenty of opportunities to do that in the offseason.
Of course, that doesn’t mean the Panthers will find great players with those picks. But the GM will have the opportunity to address the team’s needs in the offseason.
The biggest loser of the Carolina Panthers trade deadline is likely going to be quarterback Bryce Young. Carolina’s offensive line has been very inconsistent this season, and the offense has struggled to string together consistent drives.
Young was sacked 11 times in losses to the Buccaneers and Packers. While the Panthers’ offensive line showed some improvement against the Broncos, Young was stripped of the football on a sack during the team's final offensive possession.
Another offensive lineman or even another weapon in the passing game would have been nice for Young. Instead, he will have to continue to rely on the players currently on the roster to get the job done and hope for more consistency from the offense.
One area of the team that could have used some help is the cornerback position. The Panthers have been hit hard by injuries in the secondary as of late, and that was on full display against Denver.
When the Panthers’ cornerback depth is tested, it’s not always pretty. Against the Broncos, the Panthers relied on a bunch of guys who weren’t expected to see much action this season. Marco Wilson and Corey Thornton combined for four accepted pass interference penalties, with another flag against Wilson declined in favor of a taunting penalty.
This could be an issue for the Panthers as they are trying to win the division. Hopefully, the Panthers will get Jackson and Horn back soon, but until then, they will have to rely on their current depth.
The Panthers could have addressed the cornerback position with a trade, but instead, Morgan chose to stand pat with the players currently on the roster. This means that if another injury were to occur in the secondary, the team would have to rely on that same depth.
The silent trade deadline also did not bring any players to Carolina who could help the team’s chances of winning the NFC South.
Despite having a 3-5 record, the NFC South is still there for the taking for the Carolina Panthers. Right now, the Panthers are tied with the New Orleans Saints at 3-5, while the Falcons and Buccaneers are both 3-6.
The decision not to make a trade is an interesting one. Morgan had the opportunity to explore acquiring a player who could help the Panthers now, but decided to keep the draft picks instead and wait for the injured players to return to the field.
There are good arguments for both sides of the decision. Carolina is not a team that is one player away from winning a Super Bowl. Trading away valuable draft picks for a short-term solution is not the way to build a team for the long term.
But there is also something to be said for taking advantage of an opportunity when it presents itself. Carolina doesn’t know how often it will be in a position to win the division with a losing record.
Morgan made his decision, and now the Panthers have to make it work. If the Panthers can find a way to win the NFC South, then standing pat at the deadline will have been the right move.
But if the injuries continue to pile up and Carolina misses the playoffs, then there will be questions about why Morgan didn’t make a trade when he had the chance.
Mark Livingston is a South Carolina native and recent Penn State graduate with a degree in Digital Media and Journalism. He previously wrote for Greenville Sports Media, where he covered various sports and teams across the Carolinas. His experience includes game coverage, feature stories and interviews.

title: Four Chicago Bears Are Earning Contract Extensions For 2027 and Beyond
full_text:
With Caleb Williams still on a cheap rookie deal for the next few years before his inevitable monster contract extension kicks in down the road, the Chicago Bears will have some financial flexibility.
And, with that flexibility, the Bears can dump resources into some players at other positions who have proven their worth during their time in Chicago.
At the halfway point of the season, there are four Bears players who are either in a contract year or will be in 2027 that have earned an extension from the team with their play.
After falling short in the starting left tackle competition at camp, Benedet was thrust into the role after Braxton Jones went down with an injury that proved to be a season-ending issue .
The Bears probably could've turned to Ozzy Trapilo at some point in the last few weeks, but with Benedet playing well, they haven't done that.
Through nine games, Benedet sports a respectable 68.4 pass-blocking grade, according to Pro Football Focus , and he has allowed just one sack and 18 pressures.
In the run game, Benedet is sporting a grade of 73.3, which ranks 19th among tackles in the NFL.
Benedet is an exclusive rights free agent after this season, so the Bears have some control. However, they might want to lock him up for more than just next year as a potential long-term left tackle or, at the very least, a long-term swing tackle.
When the Bears acquired Jackson in a trade with the Rams in 2025, his career was in trouble. Jackson missed most of the season with an injury and wasn't effective when on the field.
But Jackson has flipped the script with the Bears and once again looks like one of the best guards in the NFL. This season has been particularly impressive, with Jones ranking fourth in run-blocking grade (85.1) and fifth in overall grade (83.1) among guards while not permitting a sack and giving up just 16 pressures.
Jackson is under contract for another year, but he doesn't have any guaranteed money left on his deal, which makes him an obvious candidate for a long-term extension even more.
Chicago would benefit from locking him up long term, also, as the team can lower his $12.2 million cap hit for 2027 in the process.
Jackson started his ascension last season, when he was a pleasant surprise for the Bears in his first year in Chicago.
And the veteran linebacker has picked up where he left off and is seeing an increased role as a result, with his snap share going from 26% last season to 43% this season.
Jackson remains one of the best coverage linebackers in the NFL, as evidenced by his PFF grade of 76.2 in that area, which ranks sixth at the position. He also has one interception.
His run defense hasn't been great, but Jackson's coverage ability makes him a great complement to Devin Bush.
Jackson still has one more year left on his deal, but with T.J. Edwards getting long in the tooth, the Bears might want to lock Jackson up for the long haul before his value rises even more.
Lewis has no doubt proven his worth this season thanks to his versatility and amounts to a home-run signing for the Bears.
With injuries at slot cornerback and safety, Lewis has split his time between the two positions and has played well, with his 70.2 coverage grade ranking 17th among safeties.
Lewis isn't going to be a free agent in 2027, but the Bears might be wise to lock him up for another year or two before 2028, and he certainly deserves a raise, also.

title: Jeffery Simmons Was Frustrated With Titans After Trade to Bears
full_text:
Defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons has expressed on a few occasions how happy he is to be with the Chicago Bears.
But upon initially being traded to Chicago from the Tennessee Titans, he wasn't exactly thrilled about it.
Simmons made the honest admission during an appearance on "The Rich Eisen Show," saying he was initially frustrated because he didn't think Tennessee would trade him since he was such an important member of the franchise.
"I just didn't think that would happen to me, especially going into Year 8," Simmons said.
"I was really pissed off that it really happened right then and there because... I was still going out there playing my tail off and giving Tennessee and their organization everything I had when I stepped on that field, in the locker room, practice field, in this community."
It's understandable why Simmons felt that way. He had become a stalwart in Tennessee and the face of the franchise and many, including Simmons himself, believed he was untradeable.
Simmons was one of two players left from the 2019 Titans team that went to the AFC Championship Game, along with safety Amani Hooker, who has now also been traded , also.
In fairness to the Titans, they didn't want to trade him, but the historic package Bears general manager Ryan Poles threw at Tennessee was just too good to pass up on, especially for a rebuilding team like the Titans.
Despite his frustration with the Titans, Simmons said he is happy in Chicago and it's already feeling like home. Simmons even went as far as to say he hopes to finish his career with the Bears.
"These last two weeks have been unbelievable," Simmons admitted. "The fans of Chicago, they breathe football. To pack out the stadium, even on Monday night in Seattle, I got chills to hear how many fans and see how many fans we had in Seattle."
"Then you come back home to another primetime game Sunday night in Chicago, that was unreal running out of that tunnel for the first time. It's definitely feeling like home and I'm looking forward to hopefully end my career there, whenever that may be," he added.
Going from the Titans' fan base to the Bears' is quite the jump for Simmons.
Tennessee's fans have often been criticized for allowing fans of the opposing team to invade their stadium, so seeing Bears fans show up in big numbers at a road game is definitely something Simmons hasn't seen during his career.
Simmons is also going from a team that has been terrible for years now and is currently in the process of a rebuild to one that is a legit Super Bowl contender in 2026 .
And, being on a true contender and playing in a bigger market and in more primetime games means Simmons has more eyes on him than ever. Simmons has often flown under the radar in Tennessee, but that will no longer be the case now that he's with the Bears.

title: Five Chicago Bears Who Improved the Most in Season's First Half
full_text:
Improvement is easier to measure subjectively than objectively.
The Bears completed nine weeks of an 18-week season with several players standing out above their previous performances with the team. Although some of said improvements can't be entirely gauged with regular team statistics, most can be detected this way or merely by looking at analytics.
Coach Ben Johnson threw out a rew names of role players who have improved over the course of the season, like James Lynch and Daniel Hardy. However, they're participating in less critical roles than the starters as backups and special teams players.
There are five players in particular who stepped up their games when called on to start or play most of the downs.
Here are the most improved Bears for the season's first half.
The Bears are 7-2 and are getting 4 key players back: • Kyle Monangai: Expected back Week 11 • Malik Muhammad: Expected back Week 11 • Dayo Odeyingbo: Eligible to return Week 11 • Coby Bryant: Potential December return Getting healthy couldn’t come at a better time. pic.twitter.com/C56IXIRhn9
Enough with all of the motivated Dayo jokes. Odeyingbo only got to play in five games prior to his quad injury, and now will likely return either at home in the next game with New Orleans or at Detroit on Thanksgiving. Odeyingbo's numbers did reflect better play than last year, when he played eight games and then suffered a season-ending Achilles injury. It's remarkable, in fact, that he showed up better statistically considering the injury he had.
Maybe it's the experience factor. He's already been through an Achilles injury in his past and knew what to expect. Although he played only 147 snaps on defense, he had three sacks. That was two more than he had all last season. He also had nine pressures, or three more than last year. His three tackles for loss were one more for five games than he had last year in eight. The Bears definitely haven't had their money's worth out of him considering his contract, but the little they got to see before his injury indicates they could get another nice boost on their defensive line when he returns.
3 players are expected to be back for Bears as we head into second half of the season & @BearsCork looks at their importance! As we head into the bye, I genuinely think this team still has another gear to find. And the best part? Help is on the way all fresh heading into the… pic.twitter.com/oQtNeiKjm0
Maybe you can't teach an old dog new tricks but he can perform old ones pretty well when he's healthy enough.
Jarrett hasn't had the knee sprain to worry about that he had last year. A bit different defensive line approach emphasizing a quicker attack by all defensive linemen and less time tied up with blockers definitely played to his strength. Jarrett has the NFL's highest run-stop win rate for defensive tackles in the first nine weeks, according to ESPN's run-stop win rate metric. He's at 44%.
Expect his pass rushing to improve now, as well, with Jeffery Simmons lining up alongside. Jarrett will rarely get a double team now. The eight pressures he has for the first half is only three short of what he had for all of last year. He has missed only three tackles as a Bear.
Bears Grady Jarrett ate his Wheaties before these two HUGE pass rush plays! pic.twitter.com/pelZYWyBHG
The more people start to pine for Ozzy Trapilo, the more Benedet produces. He did it last week while playing through a shoulder injury. Benedet's weakness last season in his first extensive playing time was pass blocking. This year he is fourth in the NFL in ESPN's pass block win rate among tackles, at 92%. Benedet began taking starter's reps in Week 4 against the Jets and has been rock solid. Pro Football Focus has Benedet graded 22nd among 71 tackles in the NFL, 19th blocking the run and 41st as a pass blocker. He's at one sack allowed and four penalties committed. They can afford to wait on Trapilo as long as Benedet is performing this way, that is, if Trapilo can even get his job back. Fighting through the shoulder injury alone in the last game earned him high marks in the eyes of Ben Johnson. "I think it's tremendous growth," Johnson said. "Certainly him as being a young player, just understanding that this team still needs him. We talk about how there are going to be games over the course of the season where you're not 100%, and yet we need you going out there and giving every little ounce you got in your 90% or you're 85%.
Theo Benedet is one tough football player who has done a good job protecting Caleb Williams' blind side, even when banged up, as @kfishbain discussed on the @RahimiGrote Show. pic.twitter.com/jqmhNw8l4j
"I think that was a case of him (Sunday) night pushing through and being out there for his buddies. I think that's all over this roster right now."
Already emerging as a force by the end of last season and the playoffs, Booker has only improved despite not being used as a starter. He still gets starter's reps but they kept him off the field for the first play of the defense's opening series seven out of nine games. Booker already is only eight tackles short of last year and has half a sack more than he made all of last season with a team-high five. He has reached a career high for tackles for loss with six, and needs six pressures in his final eight games to pass last year's total of 18. "His intensity, his effort, they keep getting better week-in and week-out," Johnson said.
If an Austin Booker extension had to look something like: 3 years, $45M (30M in guarantees) Would you do it? Booker’s stats so far this season: 🏈: 27 tackles 🏈: 5.0 sacks 🏈: 2 forced fumbles 🏈: 1 pass defended (turned into INT) pic.twitter.com/JYGvcG81Zj
It would be easy to join the dog pile on him after the nightmare four interceptions against the Buccaneers but a first half of brilliance despite that game and three missed due to injuries says he'll have fairly impressive numbers by season's end.
PFF just got done shocking everyone with its examination of passers to date and determining: "Nobody has a higher adjusted completion pct (81.5%) than Caleb Williams."
This hardly seemed possible last year when everyone blasted him for wildness or for taking the tough pass over the easy win. He is 16.6% higher in completion percentage (68.7%) than he was for last season. PFF has Williams second among regular starters for overall accuracy, trailing only Joe Burrow. They have Lamar Jackson and J.J. McCarthy ahead of him but obviously Jackson isn't going to play again this year and McCarthy is playing only as a sub for Jaxson Dart. They also list him behind only C.J. Stroud, Bryce Young, Joe Burrow and Drake Maye among starters for ball placement.
He also has the highest EPA per attempt on non-first reads in the league.
That's the leap Bears fans were waiting for. Accuracy was the knock coming out, and now he's at the top of the league in it.
Footwork improvement and accuracy throwing have combined with his knowledge of the offense in Year 2 to lead to this boost, one not apparent on Sunday night but definitely there when the Bears beat the two Super Bowl teams from last year, among others. When the season was about to begin, Johnson noted the changed approach from Williams. This especially pertained to professionalism and his accuracy as a passer.
“He’s taking a lot of pride in his approach right now and it trickles down to everyone around him," Johnson said.
Williams' total reversal when it comes to accuracy is the type of thing that can carry a team a long way, maybe even into mid-February.

title: Which Chicago Bears Are on Pace For an All-Pro Season?
full_text:
We're officially halfway through the season, and the Bears sit atop the NFC North with an impressive 7-2 record. They're also riding high with four straight wins going into their Bye Week.
With it being midseason, season-long predictions are being revisited in droves. They're also handing out awards for how players have performed over the first half of the year. ESPN's Bill Barnwell named four Chicago Bears (Joe Thuney, Darnell Wright, Jeffery Simmons, and Devin Bush) to his midseason All-Pro team.
We made our All-Pro predictions back in July , and three of the five players we mentioned are enjoying great seasons. Another has started heating up after a rough start to the campaign, and the fifth... Well, we don't need to talk about how the fifth player has performed.
How might the Bears favor when it comes to All-Pro voting at midseason?
Joe Thuney might not be playing as well as he did last season, when he was named the NFL's inaugural Protector of the Year . Still, he's played well enough to be in strong consideration for an All-Pro nod by the end of the season.
Thuney will also be aided by name recognition. That's not supposed to matter when it comes to All-Pro voting, but it almost always does. Thuney is still recognized as one of the league's best o-linemen, and the voters are well aware of that fact.
Darnell Wright was actually previously a victim of name recognition. While he didn't reach the All-Pro level until last season (when he received his first All-Pro nod), he was also a notable Pro Bowl snub in 2024. It took him playing through a torn UCL before the league gave him the recognition he deserved.
Wright has taken his game to another level this season. With a few other right tackles falling off (or moving to the left side), his path to another All-Pro nod got a bit easier. The fact that he's all but cemented his status as the league's premier right tackle doesn't hurt matters, either.
Was there ever any doubt? Jeffery Simmons was named a first-team All-Pro on a 3-14 Titans team last season. He's now on a 7-2 Bears squad with at least three more standalone games the rest of the way.
Simmons has completely reshaped Chicago's defense , and he already has six sacks over the first half of the season. The NFL landscape features quite a few elite DTs, but Simmons is arguably the best. He's a near-lock to be recognized with his fourth All-Pro nod.
Admittedly, I was a bit surprised to see Bush on Barnwell's All-Pro list. He's obviously stacked a few great performances in recent weeks, but a few quiet ones earlier in the season place him well behind a few other 'backers in the stat sheets. For what it's worth, it's also a stat-stuffing position, so the quiet start makes it difficult to overcome a lack of early-season production.
Still, Bush has put together a few great performances in recent weeks . If he can carry that momentum over the rest of the season, and Chicago's defense reaches another level with Simmons commanding opposing offenses' attention, he'll have a chance. His progression has been one of their most promising developments on defense.
Caleb Williams' four-interception performance on Sunday night might've put the nail in his MVP candidacy. His All-Pro hopes are still alive, though. He has played lights out in four of six games this year. One of the other games was in monsoon-like conditions, so it's easy to give him a pass there.
The most significant factor that could prevent Williams from All-Pro recognition is how many QBs are playing at a high level. The league is oversaturated with quality QB play, and, unlike Williams, many haven't missed any action. Still, it's certainly possible if he can consistently play as he did over his four great games.
