title: Why It's Only Going to Get Tougher for the Bears in Season's Second Half
full_text:
The first half of the season tested the Bears in numerous ways and the second half figures to be trying for different reasons.
With all due respect to Tampa Bay's defense, the Bears' offense seemed to hit a wall of its own making in the last game.
It didn't represent their efforts through much of the season's first half, although turnovers have been a consistent problem. More precisely, fumbles have been an issue, not the interceptions. Caleb Williams' one bad day truly was this compared to what he'd done both throughout the rest of his season and his career.
Their defense saw only a teaser of what defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons can mean to them, as he had shortened work weeks for both games played. He played after two practices, and then the entire team had a short work week due to the Monday night game and extra day off after travel back from Seattle. They're overworking him and perhaps in the season's second half they'll find a way to better distribute his reps.
“I’m still super high on Caleb, but we need to be honest about the year he’s having so far. At times spectacular… but he’s played 6 game - 4 he was excellent and 2 he was awful.” @getnickwright pumps the breaks on the Caleb Williams hype pic.twitter.com/jeppKq47wd
The second half of the season challenges the Bears most because half of their eight opponents will be very familiar divisional teams, all over .500. They'll also get division leaders Buffalo and Jacksonville, with only New Orleans and Miami ranking among the league's have-nots over the first half.
Then again, the actual matchup challenges their second-half opponents represent are a bit less taxing for their offense. They'll need Simmons at his best and eventually even get Coby Bryant healthy and in the lineup if they're going to stop some of the offenses they'll face down the stretch.
Williams and the offense will face the league's worst pass defense twice. That's Detroit. Coming out of the break they face a Saints pass defense ranked 28th. The Bears play a Jacksonville team very balanced, but one problem the Jaguars have had is against the pass. The Jaguars rank 22nd stopping the pass, although they have made changes with three defensive additions.
"The answer is Caleb Williams. ... Caleb Williams has got that 'IT' factor." @EvCoRadio weighs in on the NFC North QB he trusts the most in the playoffs 🔥 pic.twitter.com/3i4QPxulOr
The Bears play a Buffalo defense ranked 29th in stopping the pass. The only top-10 pass defense they play is Minnesota in the season finale. The Vikings are No. 2 at stopping the pass. Green Bay is 11th, and the two Packers safeties and an improved pass rush do make them a challenge for Williams and his receivers.
With Kyle Monangai possibly returning for the next game after missing five straight, the offense badly needs the balance he brings to the running attack. They were a cold 98.6 yards a game rushing in those five without him, a torrid 196.2 in four games with him. The 196.2 yards included a Week 2 game against Minnesota's dominant defense.
Scenes when Kyle Monangai comes back and puts together the greatest RB season in NFL history pic.twitter.com/I6JQD9Jpth https://t.co/XXVmnKdGG2
“Kyle's a big part of that running game, and I think he's proven his worth over the last year and a half," coach Ben Johnson said. "So, like I said last week, whenever we're able to get him back on the field, it's going to make us a better team and certainly a better running game.”
They'll need the running game at full force because the second half of their schedule includes only one run defense in the league's bottom tier and that's the Saints in the first game back.
They're going to run up against four top-10 rushing defenses and, after New Orleans, none ranked worse than 18th. It's been tough sledding for D'Andre Swift and the ground game in the last five weeks, and the opposition doesn't figure to get easier.
Bears are a problem. On their worse day thry beat the #3 defense in the league. Simmons turned our D into animals.
The Bears' offensive line came charging out of the early bye week last year and took over. They could use the same thing coming out of this bye, even after half the NFL schedule.
Adding Simmons gives them the help stopping the run and rushing the pass that they could need to get through a second-half of opponents loaded with the ability to put up points.
They're going against the top-ranked yardage and scoring offense in Buffalo, twice face Detroit's fifth-ranked scoring and yardage offense, host Jacksonville's fourth-ranked scoring offense, must stop Green Bay's second-ranked passing attack, and no one could really know what they'll see from Minnesota's offense by the finale with Kirk Cousins back but it can't be as bad as it was in the season's first half or even in the game the Bears squandered against the Vikings and Carson Wentz.
There are only a few anemic offenses on the slate. Miami is 31st in scoring and 28th on offense but they can run it (12th) with a QB who might be better at that than passing it. New Orleans' offense is nowhere near as bad as its defense has been and beyond the Saints and Dolphins, all of the remaining opponents could have one real strength offensively to lean on against the Bears.
“[The Buccaneers] actually put out the formula of how to … potentially beat the Chicago Bears.” @TheSamAcho breaks down his takeaways from SNF’s game after the Bears beat the Bucs with a last-minute field goal ✍️ pic.twitter.com/CnNf8rYI5m
Only a few NFL teams in the first half displayed as much balanced statistically as the Bears, ranking third in offense and rushing and 12th in passing, but ninth on defense -- sixth against the run and 14th against the pass. It shows an ability to handle whatever the second half of the season throws at them.
The offense seems poised to regain the explosiveness shown in the season opener, while it doesn't hurt having a defensive weapon now in the middle of the line to snuff things out before they get started.
"I think there's a great opportunity at hand just to look at these first nine games and come away with what we're doing well and what we can lean on going into the last stretch of the season and certainly some areas of improvement that we need to get better at moving forward," Johnson said.
They'll have to because it doesn't get easier in the season's second half, particularly with four games within the NFL's toughest division.
Jeffery Simmons traveled 422.04 yards in the first half. The most of any Bucs or Bears defensive lineman or edge defender from scrimmage. It was even more than Bucky Irving's 371.58 yards, per @NextGenStats .
💥 The Simmons Smash 💥 pic.twitter.com/2ZPw0Net2m

title: Chicago Bears Rookie Power Rankings at Halfway Point of 2026 Season
full_text:
The Chicago Bears' bye week comes at the halfway point of the 2026 campaign, so now is as perfect a time as ever to reflect on what has transpired over the first half of the season.
When it comes to the Bears' 2026 NFL Draft class , which has seven players in it, there have been a few players who have managed to make a massive impact.
However, we cannot say the same for the rest of the class because the other five players have made minimal to no contributions over the first nine games.
With that in mind, here's our power rankings of all seven of the Bears' 2026 draft picks.
We were surprised to see the Bears spring for a center as early as they did with Jones in the second round of the 2026 NFL Draft because they had just traded for Garrett Bradbury .
As expected, Bradbury ended up being the starter at center and has not relinquished that job, even though he has seen his fair share of struggles.
Jones has only seen snaps on special teams, with 47 in total, so it's hard to gauge where he stands until he sees some snaps on offense, something that may not happen in 2026.
We figured Elliott faced an uphill climb to see snaps on defense in his first season with a trio of Devin Bush, D'Marco Jackson and T.J. Edwards in front of him, and that has proven to be true, with the rookie not seeing any through Week 9.
Elliott has gotten plenty of run on special teams, but he has not so much as recorded a single tackle. The latest blemish on his season was being a healthy scratch in Week 9 .
As a fifth-round rookie linebacker, we expected Elliott to make an impact on special teams, but he hasn't even checked that box.
There was plenty of hype surrounding van den Berg when he was drafted because of his elite athleticism. But we also knew he was just a sixth-round draft pick and expectations should never be high for those kinds of players.
However, after van den Berg put together a strong preseason , his showing was part of the reason why the Bears felt comfortable trading away Gervon Dexter and, as a result, expectations drastically changed for him.
Unfortunately, van den Berg hasn't met those expectations. After seeing 21 snaps in Week 1, van den Berg hasn't appeared for more than 11 in any game since, and over his last four games he has played 16 snaps in total and was a healthy scratch in Week 8 .
Through nine games, van Berg has just one tackle and one pressure. That's certainly not what the Bears were hoping for following the Dexter trade.
Another surprising pick at the time, Roush has spent most of his year as the TE3 behind Colston Loveland and Cole Kmet, but his role has increased since Kmet was lost for the season with a significant knee injury.
Despite playing more snaps on offense than any other rookie, Roush has made minimal impact in the passing game with five catches for 56 yards, and he has a pair of drops.
But those drops aren't the only gaffes he has had. The rookie has committed a few bad penalties, and his mistake as a blocker on a field goal in Week 2 against the Minnesota Vikings led to the attempt getting blocked, which proved to be crucial in the divisional loss for Chicago.
When it comes to blocking, Roush has been serviceable, with PFF grades of 66.5 in run-blocking and 68.4 in pass-blocking.
Roush has a golden opportunity to make a big impact the rest of the way now that Kmet is out, but we'd be lying if we said we're impressed with what he has put on tape through nine games.
The third of three surprising picks in a row for the Bears, Thomas hasn't gotten much run on offense this season, which was pretty much expected with Luther Burden, Rome Odunze and Kalif Raymond ahead of him on the depth chart.
Thomas has recorded just seven catches for 54 yards and one carry for 11 yards. Again, we never expected him to have a big role, but we also thought head coach Ben Johnson would find more ways to get him involved than he has.
Thomas' biggest contribution has come on kick returns, where he's averaging a healthy 25.5 yards per return, which ranks 16th. His 23 returns of 20-plus yards is also tied for the fifth-highest mark and only four players have more kick return yards in total.
Thomas' season hasn't been without mistakes, though, as he has recorded three penalties, including a bad one in Week 9 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers that put him in Johnson's dog house .
Not only has Muhammad been better than expected this season, he has been the Bears' best cornerback overall .
In seven games, the Texas product has given up a completion rate of 54.8% and a passer rating of 79.9, both numbers that are vastly better than those of Jaylon Johnson and Tyrique Stevenson.
What's even more impressive is Muhammad has been effective both in the slot and on the boundary despite having very little experience in the former area of the field in college.
There's certainly an argument to be made that Muhammad has been the Bears' best rookie this season, but he's at least the second-best behind Thieneman.
When he was taken with the No. 25 overall pick in April, Thieneman was expected to make an immediate impact in his first season. Well, he has done just that.
Thieneman currently leads the team in tackles with 57, and he has 2.5 tackles for loss, 1.5 sacks, five passes defensed and one interception.
Thieneman's coverage numbers are solid, with the rookie giving up  a completion rate of 51.9% and a passer rating of 70.4, and his Pro Football Focus run defense grade of 70.8 is impressive, also.
Safe to say, Thieneman has been everything the Bears could have hoped for in his first season in the NFL.

title: Who Should Bears Fans Root for During Week 10 Bye?
full_text:
We've hit the midpoint of the 2026 NFL season, and the Chicago Bears are finally getting a much-needed break. They're on their bye week following an ugly, undeserved Week 9 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , giving them a chance to rest, make a few tweaks to their game plans, and hopefully get a few injured players back.
Though the Bears won't be playing football on Sunday or Monday, there are still some games that Bears fans will want to pay close attention to. These games could have major implications on playoff seeding, which is now just eight weeks away. The Bears currently hold the top spot in the NFC North and are very much in the running for the No. 1 seed in the NFC.
History may say that playoff positioning is just about set by this point in the season, but it'd be better for the Bears to punch their postseason ticket well in advance of Week 18. With that in mind, here are five games for Bears fans to keep tabs on this Sunday, and who they should be rooting for in each one.
The Lions may no longer be the NFC North juggernaut that they were in 2023 and 2024, but they're still a dangerous squad. The Bears still have to play them twice, which means they could leapfrog the Bears in a hurry when it comes to playoff seeding or the division title. The Bears need to handle their own business, and I'd be shocked if they could not get one win over Detroit this year, but it would sure help if the Patriots could give the Bears some breathing space by picking up a win in Germany.
Additionally, Bears fans should be rooting for the Patriots the rest of the season. The Bears vanquished New England in a sensational Week 7 primetime game , and a higher winning percentage for New England could potentially help Chicago in terms of determining tiebreakers.
At 7-1, the Niners currently hold the No. 1 seed in the NFC, but the Bears are hot on their heels. If the Bears want to take the top spot and earn the Wild Card bye in the playoffs, they're going to need the Niners to stumble a bit, and that starts with a trip to Dallas to take on the Cowboys.
Unfortunately for the Bears, the Niners improved their roster quite a bit recently. They made a deal for former Indianapolis Colts defensive tackle DeForest Buckner two weeks ago, then traded for Keenan Allen at the deadline. The NFL is an 'any given Sunday' league, but the Cowboys will be hard-pressed to beat a rejuvinated Niners squad, especially since they'll be fresh off their bye week.
Sunday, 4:05pm ET on CBS (both)
I'm making this one a two-fer, and here's why. Both the Rams and Seahawks are a little behind where they probably expected to be at this point, but it's far too early to count them out. They could still get hot and string enough wins together to push the fourth- and third-place finishers of the NFC North out of the playoff picture, and that could very well include the Bears.
The best-case scenario for Chicago, and, truthfully, the entire NFC North, is for every NFC Wild Card spot to go to an NFC North team. This would shutout both the Seahawks and the Rams, teams who have proven to be dangerous in January. The Bears do hold one tiebreaker with their statement Week 8 victory over the Seahawks , but it'd be better if it doesn't come to that.
I really struggled determining who Bears fans should root for in this one. On the one hand, the Vikings have lost only two games and their trade for Kirk Cousins completely changes their offense moving forward . Instead of a moribund offense being dragged along by an elite defense, this offense will now likely carry its own weight and even be able to pick up slack from the defense should they ever struggle.
On the other hand, the Packers have been playing lights-out football lately, and they're still awaiting the return of star pass rusher Micah Parsons. There are some major red flags to the way they're winning, chief among them being an unsustainable rate of takeaways, and it remains extremely unlikely that they'll be able to win in December and January with a historically bad run game, but it's worked for them thus far.
This one comes down to your personality as a Bears fan. If you're on the pessimistic side, you might think the Bears aren't likely to win the division, so it'd be better for the Vikings to win, reclaim the top spot in the NFC North, and push the Packers further behind the Bears in the race for a Wild Card spot. If you're optimistic, you'll have to hold your nose and root for Green Bay so that Chicago will be better positioned to seize their second-straight NFC North crown.

title: Chicago Bears GM Ryan Poles' Biggest Mistake of 2026 NFL Season
full_text:
General manager Ryan Poles might be the most popular he has ever been during his tenure with the Chicago Bears.
Poles recently pulled off a blockbuster trade with the Tennessee Titans for superstar defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons that we believe will end up being one of the best trades in franchise history, let alone of his tenure.
Simmons is already making a massive impact over two games and even though it took a historic package to get the deal done , the trade is starting to look like a steal for Chicago.
Interestingly enough, that trade might not have happened had he not made a big mistake upfront before the season started.
The addition of Simmons no doubt changes the outlook of the Bears' defensive line, but Poles trading Gervon Dexter to the Atlanta Falcons was the biggest mistake he has made in 2026.
Of course, the Bears unloaded Dexter in a trade with the Falcons before the season started.
While we understand he was never a good fit in Dennis Allen's defense, there were still several problems with that decision.
The first issue was the return Poles got, which was a fifth-round pick and defensive back Clark Phillips.
Chances are that fifth-round selection won't amount to anything, and Phillips has played 58 snaps on defense and has two tackles and one QB hit.
For a starting-caliber player like Dexter who is a plus pass-rusher, we feel like the Bears should have gotten more, and at the very least, a starting-caliber player in return or a better pick.
The next problem is the Bears overestimated the kinds of impacts they would get out of the guys they had pegged to replace a player who was the team's best interior pass-rusher.
Chicago expected Kentavius Street and Jordan van den Berg to step up, but neither really answered the bell.
Street had one sack, which came in Week 1, and he posted a bad run defense grade of 46.2. He is now likely to miss the rest of the season because of a knee injury .
The rookie has been even worse. After playing 22 snaps in Week 1, van den Berg hasn't played more than 11 since. Over his last four games, van den Berg has played eight and five snaps, was a healthy scratch, and then played a season-low three snaps.
In all, van den Berg has one tackle, one pressure and one QB hit in eight games played, and the Bears saw their interior defenders post one sack combined before Simmons arrived.
Hindsight is always 20/20, but it was always a risky proposition to depend on Street and even Neville Gallimore, both of whom have been backups during their careers, and a sixth-round rookie to replace a starter like Dexter.
Meanwhile, Dexter is having a pretty good season with the Falcons.
He does only have 1.5 sacks, so he's on pace to finish with less than he had in 2025, but Dexter also is tied for 10th in pressures among interior defensive linemen, and he is posting the best run defense grade of his career with a 66.4, per Pro Football Focus .
Dexter has more sacks and pressures than the guys who were tasked to replace him combined.
Because of the Dexter trade and the failure of the guys who were pegged to replace him to step up, the Bears found themselves with a big need along the interior before the deadline.
Thankfully, Poles was able to seal that up in a big way with the trade for Simmons that took a historic package to get done.
We love that trade, but let's not pretend Poles wasn't fortunate to be able to make it. It absolves him of the mistake he committed with the Dexter trade, but it doesn't erase the fact that Poles is guilty of having made that mistake in the first place.
Perhaps that trade never happens if Dexter stays, but we can't say that for sure. We could have seen a scenario where Poles acquires Simmons and then flips Dexter after, and it's also possible that Poles could have gotten more for Dexter at the trade deadline.
Whatever the case may be, Poles has managed to come out smelling like a rose.

title: 8 Biggest Trades Bears Made Under Ryan Poles, Ranked By Significance
full_text:
The Chicago Bears are now two weeks removed from the earth-shattering Jeffery Simmons trade that unlocked their defense. They sent two first-round selections and a fourth-round pick to the Titans for Simmons and a fifth-round pick. If his first two games donning the blue and orange are any indication, they definitely underpaid .
Acquiring Simmons was one of Bears general manager Ryan Poles' best moves since taking the helm in 2022. It was far from his only consequential trade, though. He's always kept the phone lines open when it comes to trade conversations.
Here are the eight biggest trades Poles has made, ranked from eight to one in terms of significance.
A draft-day trade that saw them move down one spot might not seem as significant as other moves Poles has made, and it didn't include as much draft capital as others, but it was still monumental. Many believed DT Jalen Carter was the best player in the 2023 NFL Draft, and the Bears could've landed him with the ninth overall pick due to character concerns.
Poles trusted his judgment because he knew he had an ace in the hole . They instead drafted Darnell Wright, who has arguably become the league's best right tackle. They also knew the Eagles wouldn't take him, so they moved down one spot and picked up a fourth-round pick. They turned that extra pick into punter Tory Taylor, who has developed into a weapon in his third season.
Carter is a great player, but it's safe to assume they don't have any regrets at Halas Hall.
Khalil Herbert showed legit flashes over his first three years in Chicago after the team selected him in the sixth round of the 2021 NFL Draft. However, largely got phased out in year four, carrying the ball only eight times over the first six weeks. They shipped him to the Bengals for a seventh-round pick ahead of the trade deadline.
Why does this one rank so highly in terms of significance? The butterfly effect, of course. The Bears drafted Kyle Monangai with the pick they received for Herbert. Monangai was one of the biggest steals of the 2025 NFL Draft , and he picked up right where he left off this year before suffering a turf toe injury in Week 4.
The other DJ Moore trade (more on the first one later, obviously). They shipped Moore and a sixth-round pick to Buffalo for a second-round selection this offseason. With the depth that the Bears accumulated at receiver, many saw it as a necessary evil to create some cap space ahead of free agency.
Very few expected them to receive a second-round pick for Moore, though. Not after putting up a career-low 682 yards last season. Even fewer expected the Bills to inherit his four-year, $110 million contract. The Bears wound up trading the pick down, and eventually turning it into Sam Roush and Malik Muhammad II (after trading up to select him). All things considered, this was a great deal for Chicago .
Not all significant trades work out in Chicago's favor. Roquan Smith was one of the league's best young linebackers in 2023, but he seemingly wasn't happy with the Bears' new regime after Ryan Poles took over. He briefly requested a trade ahead of training camp before eventually being a good soldier.
Poles decided the damage had been done, though. They traded the then three-time All-Pro to the Ravens for a second-rounder, a fifth-rounder, and AJ Klein, who only lasted two weeks in Chicago. The Bears turned those picks into two contributors, Gervon Dexter Sr. and Noah Sewell. It was still a bad move, though.
Sure, they didn't want to pay Smith $20 million per year. However, they didn't mind paying Tremaine Edmunds $18 million per year the next offseason. Only one of them has come close to living up to that contract, and it wasn't the one who was cut before he could finish it.
Mismanagement by former GM Ryan Pace left Chicago's salary cap situation in ruins when Poles took over. They were a team going nowhere fast, and they needed to tear it down to build it back up. Poles knew liquidating Mack's massive contract was the quickest way to provide a jolt to the rebuild. They traded him to the Chargers for a second- and sixth-round pick in his first significant move on the job.
Did the trade age well? Not really. Mack was his usual dominant self over the next two seasons, accumulating 25 sacks. It's worth noting that Mack would've been rotting with a massive contract on a rebuilding Bears team (like he is now on a stingy and underwhelming Chargers team) over the next few years if they hadn't pulled the trigger, though.
Meanwhile, the Bears turned the picks into Jaquan Brisker, Elijah Hicks, and Trenton Gill (they turned the 2023 sixth-round pick into two 2022 seventh-rounders). Again, significant isn't always good.
To Poles' credit, he seemingly figured the whole trading thing out by year three. His ties to Kansas City might've helped him land a future Hall of Fame guard for a fourth-round pick in the 2025 offseason.
Thuney didn't allow a single sack last season, and he went on to be named the NFL's inaugural Protector of the Year for his efforts. He's also picked up right where he left off over the first half of 2026.
Their decision to trade a sixth-round pick to the Rams for Jonah Jackson (literally one day before acquiring Thuney) is a noteworthy honorable mention . Both players have fortified the interior of Chicago's o-line.
Speaking of Poles' ties to Kansas City, that connection also helped acquire Jeffery Simmons. He previously worked with Titans GM Mike Borgonzi in Kansas City, and the trust between the two is not only what got the deal over the finish line, but it's what got it over the starting line. Well, that, and Poles offering up two first-round picks right off the jump.
The trade could be a rare win/win for both sides. Simmons has completely unlocked Chicago's defense. It's obvious how this trade helps them . From the Titans' perspective, they now have ample draft capital at their disposal (and more cap space) to accelerate their rebuild.
Was there ever any doubt as to which trade would take the top spot on this list? Their decision to move off the first overall pick in 2023 largely shaped the Bears' current roster. Sure, Carolina being a dumpster fire that season (and subsequently helping Chicago get the first pick in 2024) helped, but that was still a calculated move by Poles. Acquiring Moore was a huge factor in their struggles, as Bryce Young had no reliable pass-catchers to throw to.
The Bears turned that one pick into Darnell Wright, Tory Taylor, Caleb Williams, Tyrique Stevenson, Luther Burden III, Sam Roush, Malik Muhammad II, and three years with DJ Moore. Hang it in the Louvre.
Jerry Markarian has been an avid Chicago Bears fan since 2010 and has been writing about the team since  2022.  He has survived the 2010 NFC Championship Game, a career-ending injury to his favorite player (Johnny Knox), the Bears' 2013 season finale, a Double Doink, Mitchell Trubisky, Justin Fields, and Weeks 8-17 of the 2024 NFL season. Nevertheless, he still Bears Down!

title: Another Last-Ditch Stadium Idea to Sell Bears on Hospital Site Arises
full_text:
When the Illinois legislature convenes next week for its lame duck session and considers Bears stadium legislation , it's possible they could be looking at a different suggestion.
It's an old idea somewhat altered, and there's no guarantee the Bears are even going to rate this as an option based on what they've said in the past.
The Capri Investment Group and GRIT Chicago is proposing a 75,000-seat indoors stadium at the old Michael Reese Hospital site in the Bronzeville neighborhood, 2.3 miles south of Soldier Field and at the lakefront. It would be connected to McCormack Place.
The Bears currently have said they're considering Hammond for their stadium but are willing to weigh an Illinois option.
Developers on Thursday unveiled a $10 billion proposal for a large-scale development district in Bronzeville that would include a domed stadium for the Bears. https://t.co/hBwAx1Ip1A
The Illinois funding mechanism being considered later this month or in early December in Springfield was developed after Gov. J.B. Pritzker and some Chicago area politicians put it together, and is based on the Bears constructing the stadium but selling it back to the local government. The team would  then lease it for a nominal fee to avoid paying taxes. However, they would have to pay taxes on any property where they build hotels, restaurants or other businesses near the stadium.
The plan is meant for an Arlington Heights project, but could also apply to a Chicago-based plan.
An early look at the Titans’ new $2.2B Nissan Stadium, aimed for completion in February 2027. pic.twitter.com/bjvo7ZFXSu
This newly proposed project is for an estimated $10 billion stadium a bit west of the previous Michael Reese Hospital plan that was discussed. It keeps the Bears playing within the city limits, but there are problems with it.
For one, the property was deemed too small in the past by both Bears ownership and NFL commissioner Roger Goodell. The new plan addresses this somewhat, but in the process also demolishes six buildings where people currently reside.
This is to be built on 100 acres of property and that's larger than the original plan for a stadium at this site, however it's nothing compared to the 326-acre Arlington International Racetrack site the Bears currently own.
The new plan includes hotel and businesse. The company's proposal includes 2,000 hotel rooms, 300,000 square feet of retail/restaurants, 400,000 square feet of office space, a 500,000-square-foot youth sports complex, and a 400,000-square-foot wellness center.
🚨EVERY #NFL STADIUM RANKED🚨 1: Allegiant 2: Arrowhead 3: US Bank 4: Mercedes Benz 5: Lincoln Financial 6: SoFi 7: Lumen 8: Empower 9: Lambeau 10: Superdome 11: NRG 12: Gillette 13: Ford 14: State Farm 15: AT&T 16: Hard Rock 17: M&T 18: Paycor 19: Lucas Oil Thoughts on this…? pic.twitter.com/sE6ALI6Fi4
It includes some changes to Chicago public transportation to let fans get to the facility and 3,500 structured parking spaces, which seems entirely inadequate. They would need to build a 29th Street Metra station and a CTA Green Line station that would be half a mile from the stadium.
Another potential draw for the Bears is that the company is offering to buy the Arlington Heights property if the Bears pursue this Chicago option.  The Arlington Heights property is 326 acres, though, which doesn't quite sound like an even trade off.
This entire plan sounds like another one of Chicago's half-baked ideas thought up quite often during the Brandon Johnson and Lori Lightfoot mayoral administrations for hanging onto the Bears.
There's another new proposal in the Bears' stadium saga, this one relating to Bronzeville, as @leilarahimi and @LouCanellis discussed. pic.twitter.com/60gisAYCTV
The site has already been studied and rejected for good reasons. It's much like the Johnny-come-lately idea of putting a stadium near the point where the Calumet River and Lake Michigan meet at the site of the old U.S. Steel South Works, or even the idea from the village of McCook to put one there. While there would be advantages to the Michael Reese property over some other sites suggested in the past, the Bears have already drawn up and have plans for the stadium in Arlington Heights on their own property and the Indiana offer is probably the best overall because of cost and taxes.
Getting their act together has been a problem in Chicago for years no matter the project or change. This one looks no different. The state needs to consider that legislation so the Bears can get their Arlington Heights stadium construction started as soon as possible.
The only real obstacle will once again be Chicago politicians, who can't accept the fact the team is owned by someone else and they've already decided to move it outside the city. This stadium plan released by Capri is going to provide fuel for those Chicago politicians to argue against Arlington Heights once again.
Any emerging, attention-grabbing Bears stadium proposals should face this question first … Is the Bears organization actually invested or engaged at all in said proposal? If not … 🤔 Question 2: Can the Bears, with patience thinning and other league owners seeking clarity,…

title: Joe Burrow Gets Honest About His Recovery From Multiple Serious Injuries
full_text:
Joe Burrow is no stranger to severe injuries in his NFL career. He suffered a torn ACL in his rookie campaign, tore a ligament in his wrist in 2023, and suffered a turf toe injury that required surgery last year. The largest hurdle he has had to overcome with each injury however, are the mental gymnastics that occurred with each one.
Burrow confirmed this week that each injury presented larger mental hurdles than the injury itself. He stated that while his knee injury in his rookie campaign posed less concern mentally, and that the injuries to his wrist and toe are what caused the most anxiety mentally.
"It's always more mental for sure, I tore my ACL in 2020 in my rookie season and that one was tough for sure, but I didn't know any better, I was young and had never experienced anything like that before, so you're just putting one foot in front of the other," Burrow said of his knee injury. "In 2023 I hurt my wrist, and then last year I hurt my toe, and then its like 'oh come on man what's going on' because I put so much work into this."
Burrow added to his thoughts in a press conference later and said that the mental process is always different with every injury. He said he allows himself to feel emotions through anger and sadness and has quickly bounced back from those feelings, adding that once he has done so, the rehab process is easy.
"The mental process is always different with every injury that you have, the first thing is I'm always just really mad and sad, I let myself feel those emotions and then pretty quickly you just get back to work," Burrow said on his mental process . "I love what I do, if you love what you do and you wanna be better every single day, the rehab process is easy once you can flip your mind to just try and get better and try and to get back there with your guys."
He explained that he is fortunate to have improved with each injury, pointing to the rehab process and that it intensely works different muscles that do not see normal activity.
"Fortunately I've been able to improve after every injury I've had, and I think with the rehab process, a lot of times those exercises that you're doing hit muscles that you haven't quite worked that intensely as you are at the time, and that can help you come back better and stronger," Burrow said.

title: Joe Burrow Ranked Shockingly Low in Latest QB Stock Report
full_text:
It has been an interesting week for the Cincinnati Bengals. After an impressive victory over the Atlanta Falcons in Spain on Sunday, the focus shifted to what the team might do before the trade deadline.
Well, fans got their answer to that on Tuesday when the Bengals made one trade, but then rescinded the move not very long after. It was a day filled with hot takes as the fan base now wonders if the rest of the AFC has passed the team by. However, they still have to line them up and go to work.
This weekend is a major matchup for the Bengals. The team will be looking to get revenge on the Pittsburgh Steelers, who bested the Bengals earlier this season. The Bengals will need to be on their A game, which hasn't been an issue for quarterback Joe Burrow.
Burrow has been at MVP level of play this season, and Fox Sports' recent quarterback rankings have the Bengals' quarterback's stock rising before a massive AFC North showdown.
Henry McKenna has Burrow as the sixth best quarterback in the league heading into Week 10. That's one spot higher than McKenna had him last week.
"Every week, Burrow has put on a clinic," wrote McKenna . "The only downside has been his six interceptions."
The quarterbacks ahead of Burrow on the list are Trevor Lawrence, Brock Purdy, Patrick Mahomes, Jordan Love, and Josh Allen.
It seems the interceptions seem to be an issue with Burrow's stock; however, Love and Allen have the same number of interceptions but with fewer touchdown passes than Burrow.
Six interceptions isn't ideal, but the 23 touchdown passes are enough to look past the turnovers at the moment.
Three of Burrow's six interceptions on the year came in the team's 43-36 win over the Tennessee Titans. It wasn't the ideal performance, but the Bengals quarterback still managed to throw five touchdown passes and add a rushing touchdown in the win.
Burrow is once again playing at an elite level. If he continues at this pace, it would be foolish to not have him as one of the top names in the MVP conversations.
There's really no excuse to have Burrow sixth. He's been one of the best players in the NFL all season long and is in the MVP race. A win over the Steelers on Sunday would help his stock—and his case for MVP.

title: Bengals Have Clear Opportunity to Bolster O-Line After Veteran OT's Release
full_text:
A lot of the Cincinnati Bengals' fan base was not thrilled over the team's lack of movement at the trade deadline. While the team did have one deal in place, it appeared that a backpedal move may have scared the front office away from making any other moves.
The rest of the AFC contenders made moves before the deadline, however, the Bengals may feel they already have the roster to lead the conference. Whatever the case may be, that doesn't mean the team still can't add to their roster.
On Friday, the Philadelphia Eagles made a roster move that could be of great interest to the Bengals. But will the team take a closer look at making a roster addition?
The Eagles have announced that the team has waived offensive tackle Fred Johnson. Johnson has not made a start for the Eagles this season, but did start in the 2025 season in eight games.
That may sound like a familiar name to many fans. Johnson spent the first three years of his career with the Bengals. During his time in Cincinnati, Johnson made eight starts for the Bengals from 2019 to 2021.
Not that the Bengals are having issues on the offensive line this season. Recently, Pro Football Focus ranked the Bengals' offensive line as the eighth-best offensive line in the NFL heading into Week 10.
It may not be a move that makes the headline splash fans were hoping for a few days ago, but this could be a massive move if the Bengals were to see the injury bug hit their offensive line.
While the Bengals could put a claim on Johnson since he is on waivers, the team could also wait to see if the former Eagles lineman clears waivers and sign him potentially for the practice squad.
It's definitely a strategic move if the Bengals decide to add Johnson to the roster. The Bengals are entering the most vital part of the season.
Sunday's matchup with the Pittsburgh Steelers is going to tell a lot about this team. A win will keep them in the driver's seat of their own postseason destiny. On the other hand, a loss will give the Steelers the edge as the postseason race heats up.
If the Bengals plan on a deep playoff run, it can't hurt to add a little depth to the unit that is tasked with protecting the most important asset on the roster.

title: Bengals Rule 1 Player Out for Sunday, Don't Appear Ready to Return Anybody from IR
full_text:
Cincinnati Bengals head coach Zac Taylor declared starting left guard Dylan Fairchild good to go for Sunday night’s game against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
Fairchild suffered a pectoral injury late in Sunday’s 34-17 win against the Atlanta Falcons in Madrid, and he was a limited participant in Wednesday evening’s walk-through practice. But Fairchild was a full participant Thursday and Friday.
The only player ruled out on the injury report is safety Kyle Dugger, who has missed four of the last five games with a quadricep injury.
Asked if Dugger, a former Steeler, is a candidate to land on Injured Reserve, Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said he was not, indicating the safety could be close to returning to action.
Three Bengals, who are currently on IR, had their 21-day practice window opened Thursday, but the team is listing all three as doubtful for Sunday night’s battle for first place in the AFC North Division.
Cornerback Jalen Davis, wide receiver Andrei Iosivas and rookie guard Brian Parker II were all listed as full participants Thursday and Friday.
Parker, the team’s fifth-round pick out of Duke, has been on IR since Aug. 30 with a knee injury.

title: Bengals-Steelers Rest Disparity Could Be Even More Problematic Than First Thought
full_text:
A lot has been made about the rest disparity that will be in play Sunday night when the Cincinnati Bengals, who are coming off their international game in Madrid, play host to the Pittsburgh Steelers, fresh of their bye.
This will be the sixth game in which one team is returning from an international game and the other a bye, and the teams returning for their off week are 5-0.
But that’s only part of the history working against the Bengals this week.
That’s because the Steelers are on one of the best post-bye runs in NFL history with a nine-game winning streak.
The last time Pittsburgh lost a game after its bye week was 2016, when it fell 21-14 at Baltimore as 3.5-point favorites.
The nine-game, post-bye run is the second longest active winning streak in the league and the third longest since the NFL began using bye weeks in 1990.
The Buffalo Bills own the longest active streak at 12 in a row after knocking off the Ravens 36-10 following their Week 7 bye this year.
The NFL record is 13 in a row, set by the Philadelphia Eagles from 1999-2011 (there were two bye weeks in 1993).
During the Steelers’ current nine-game streak, four of the wins have come on the road, including two of the last three.
And four of the last five have come with Pittsburgh as the underdog.
Here is the list (with point spread):
2025: Week 6 vs Cleveland, W 23-9 (-6)
2024: Week 10 at Washington, W 28-27 (+2.5)
2023: Week 7 at LA Rams, W 24-17 (+3)
2022: Week 10 vs. New Orleans, W 20-10 (+1)
2021: Week 8 at Cleveland, W 15-10 (+4.5)
2020: Week 5 vs. Philadelphia, W 38-29 (-7.5)
2019: Week 8 vs. Miami, W 27-14 (-14)
2018: Week 8 vs. Cleveland, W 33-18 (-8.5)
2017: Week 10 at Indianapolis, W 20-17 (-10.5)
The Steelers are 25-12 all-time in the week after a bye. That .676 winning percentage is tied for fifth best in the league behind the Ravens (22-8, .733), Eagles (27-10, .730), Broncos (27-10, .730) and Bills (27-11, .711).
The Bengals have been the Steelers' opponent after a bye six times, but the most recent was way back in 2008, with the Steelers winning that game 38-10 in Cincinnati.
From 1990-98, the Steelers came out of their bye to face the Bengals five times, with Cincinnati winning three of those contests.
The Bengals are 12-26 after a bye for a .346 winning percentage that ranks last in the league. But they have won four of their most recent six, including the Week 7 game at Baltimore this year.
The other teams in the bottom five of post-bye winning percentages are the Raiders (13-24, .351), Browns (12-20, .375), Seahawks (14-23, .378) and Jets (15-22, .405).
Under Zac Taylor, the Bengals are 4-4 in the week after the bye.
Surprisingly, the Taylor-led Bengals have only played three games in which the opponent was coming off a bye, and they are 1-2 in those contests.
They lost 27-18 at Green Bay last year, won 17-13 vs. Seattle in 2023 and lost 19-17 to the Giants in 2020.

title: Cris Collinsworth Makes Powerful Statement About Joe Burrow Ahead of Bengals-Steelers Showdown
full_text:
Joe Burrow is in the middle of an MVP-caliber season for the Bengals. However, this week's matchup is arguably the most critical game of the season so far, as the Bengals welcome the Steelers to Paycor Stadium on Sunday Night Football. Cincinnati legend Cris Collinsworth is set to call the game nationally and recently shared his thoughts on Burrow's elite performance this season so far.
Collinsworth acknowledged the effort Burrow has put into his performance and the weight he has placed on himself as the leader of the football team. He also acknowledged how the Bengals offense functioned during his time with the team in the 80's.
"He works very hard at his craft, but he's basically taken this entire team on his shoulders, and I think everybody down there would tell you that," Collinsworth said . "From just analyzing football, it's always been you got to have a little bit of everything, when Cincinnati's been good in the past and my teams went on to the Super Bowl, it was Pete Johnson, Ickey Woods, James Brooks and we had that sort of balance."
Collinsworth admitted after that both the Packers and Bengals have shifted that balance into the most drastic pass-heavy approach he has witnessed.
"We're seeing two teams that are taking all of that and shifting that paradigm in a way that I've never seen," Collinsworth said . "The Green Bay Packers being one, their offensive line can't block anybody running the football, the Bengals are much better than that, but it's like maybe they do just have to throw it, as you're watching the Atlanta game and I was like 'why would you not give it Joe Burrow and throw it every time?"
He later explained that Burrow separates himself from other elite quarterbacks in the league by throwing at the exact correct moment. Collinsworth then detailed that this facet of Burrow's ability allows Zac Taylor to call deep passes more often. He also said that Burrow and Mike Gesicki work the middle of the field better than other combinations he watches.
"He seems to throw it every time it's the absolutely correct thing to do, and so as a coach what that does for you is it allows you to call a lot of deep passes, he just doesn't miss the opportunities," Collinsworth said . "They also have this great combination with Gesicki being enough of a threat going down the middle of the field that they work the middle of the field better than a lot of the combinations that I see."

title: Cincinnati Bengals WR Ja'Marr Chase Gives 2, Um, Thumbs Up to Disrespecting Steelers
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals 2022 season opener against the Pittsburgh Steelers is most known for Joe Burrow’s four turnovers and the loss of long snapper Clark Harris, resulting in missed game-winning kicks at the end of regulation and in overtime of a 23-20 loss.
Wide receiver Ja’Marr Chase remembers the game for something else.
Actually, two of something else – both of his middle fingers.
Chase infamously threw double birds in the face of Pittsburgh safety Minkah Fitzpatrick, and the gesture was immortalized by a photographer. And that picture has been printed and made into shirts, blankets and other mementos that often find their way back to Chase.
The receiver said he’s often asked to sign items with the photo on them.
“Because I want to do it again,” Chase said. “But I don’t want to get fined. But I love it. It’s a cool picture, honestly.”
The display in 2022 resulted in the first fine of Chase’s career, as the NFL docked him $23,870 for “multiple unsportsmanlike conducts.”
The double birds didn’t draw a flag on the field, but he was penalized 15 yards for taunting after an incomplete pass on fourth and 2 with 1:51 remaining and the Bengals trailing 20-14.
Chase has been fined five other times in his career, although the one for obscene gestures in Week 2 against Houston was rescinded.
He also drew a $15,914 taunting penalty and fine later in 2022 against Kansas City; a $31,599 fine for verbally abusing an official in 2024 at Kansas City; a $19,697 fine for an obscene gesture against Baltimore in 2024; and a one-game suspension that amounted to a loss of $507,156 for spitting on Pittsburgh’s Jalen Ramsey last year.
Sunday’s game against the Steelers will be two days shy of the one-year anniversary of that incident.
While Chase said he doesn’t want to get fined again, he said he would accept the punishment and flash the double birds to another team in the right situation.
“If it was the Super Bowl, yes,” he said. “I would definitely do it again.”
What about an AFC Championship Game against the Steelers.
“I might have to call Chad (Johnson) for that one,” he said.
While Chase won his appeal of the fine in Houston this year, he knew there was no way he would win an appeal after the double birds in 2022.
“There's no appealing that fine because I'm red handed in photos. It's hard to get out of that one.”

title: Ja’Marr Chase Delivers Brutally Honest Take on Bengals-Steelers Rivalry
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals and Pittsburgh Steelers enter Sunday night's game tied for the top spot in the AFC North at 6-2.
It's one of the biggest regular season meetings between the teams in years, but Ja'Marr Chase still puts the Bengals' rivalry with the Kansas City Chiefs a tier above it.
Asked where Pittsburgh ranked among the rivalries he's been part of in his career, Chase said on Thursday that it was "pretty up there." The Bengals superstar stopped short of picking a No. 1, saying, "I don't have nobody number one."
The follow-up yielded a more definitive answer from Chase. When asked whether the Pittsburgh rivalry was on par with Cincinnati's rivalry with Kansas City when both teams were rolling, Chase replied, "No, no, no." He put the Chiefs rivalry "way higher."
Some of the biggest games of Chase's career came against Kansas City, and the first one produced one of his best individual performances. As a rookie, he caught 11 passes for 266 yards and three touchdowns in a 34-31 win over the Chiefs. The Bengals overcame three separate 14-point deficits that afternoon and clinched the AFC North on Evan McPherson's field goal as time expired.
Four weeks later, the teams met again at Arrowhead Stadium, with a Super Bowl berth on the line. Cincinnati fell behind 21-3 but rallied to win 27-24 in overtime. The following season, Kansas City earned a rematch in the AFC Championship Game and won 23-20 with a field goal as time expired.
In just over a year, the teams had played a game that clinched a division title and two others that determined who would represent the AFC in the Super Bowl.
Sunday's meeting with Pittsburgh has its own stakes, though they aren't as high as the stakes in the matchups with the Chiefs.
These AFC North rivals are both 6-2, which is the best combined winning percentage for a Bengals-Steelers matchup this late in the season since 2009 according to NBC. The winner will also take sole possession of first place in the AFC North.
The Bengals are trying to win their fifth-straight game and avoid being swept by Pittsburgh for the first time since 2023.

title: Browns Rookie Earns High Praise From Head Coach Amid Growing Pains
full_text:
There have been plenty of storylines following the Cleveland Browns all season long.
However, one that has lost some of its spotlight since the opening few weeks is the development of the team's rookie offensive linemen.
Following several struggles along the offensive line in recent weeks, most notably from veteran Tytus Howard, rookies Austin Barber and Spencer Fano have been overshadowed.
And honestly, it isn't hard to understand why.
Even with both Barber and Fano playing well, quarterbacks Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders have been sacked a total of 38 times across nine games , averaging out to over four sacks a game. If Cleveland wants to legitimately contend by the time the playoffs roll around, the line is going to have to be better.
Head coach Todd Monken spoke about Fano in particular, saying that the issues the line has gone through have allowed the ninth overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft an opportunity to learn and grow.
"It’s so cool for him because of the way he’s wired, how he works at it — highly intelligent, very prideful, but it’s not easy being indoctrinated into playing left tackle as a rookie," he said. "And every week it feels like there is no off week, right? There isn’t an off week of these guys that are paid to get to the quarterback.
"And it really stresses your mental stamina, play after play, right? There is no ‘oh, I get a little bit of a smoke break here’. Oh, no, right. You don’t get that."
Fano currently ranks 17th out of 71 in the league in overall Pro Football Focus grade , placing him among some of football's best offensive tackles. In pass rush, there is still work to be done, with him ranking 39th out of 71, but his rushing ranking of 22nd pushes him back up towards the top of the ladder.
As Monken mentioned, even with him being moved from right tackle, which he was accustomed to in college, to left tackle, the 22-year-old has made incredible strides quickly.
He went on to say that the difference in competition is something that Fano has had to learn to be ready for, especially with edge rushers being so dynamic at the NFL level. One play he could be going up against a veteran before a shifty, young rusher comes flying his way the next.
Browns HC Todd Monken talked about the growing pains Spencer Fano is going through as a young tackle in the NFL and said there's "no smoke break" to catch your breath "It’s so cool for him because the way he’s wired, how he works at it, highly intelligent, very prideful, but… pic.twitter.com/qE0e7PTtyt
"You know, and then they roll (Jadeveon) Clowney in there, and they roll other guys that are young and trying to get the quarterback," Monken continued. "Like, that’s what’s the coolest thing about being a part of professional sports and being in professional football. Everybody’s got really good players, and it really challenges you.
"And I like his mental makeup. I like the way he’s wired. He’s only going to continue to get better."
Fano's next chance to return to the field and try to lead the Browns' offensive line comes on Sunday, Nov. 15.
The Browns play host to the Houston Texans from Huntington Bank Field at 1:00 p.m. EST.

title: Texans Rule Out Two Key Players Ahead of Browns Matchup on Sunday
full_text:
On Friday, the Cleveland Browns, just two days ahead of their matchup against the Houston Texans at home, announced that they would be without safety Ronnie Hickman and fullback Mike Burton.
Rookie Browns wideout Denzel Boston was also ruled questionable , putting the team in an even more difficult spot on Sunday against the Texans.
But the Browns aren't the only team banged up.
Following the Browns' injury report, a few hours passed, and the Texans issued their injury report ahead of Sunday's game, ruling out newly acquired wideout Marvin Harrison Jr. and defensive end Danielle Hunter.
Most importantly, the Texans may be without defensive end Will Anderson Jr., too, as the 6-foot-4, 243-pound defensive end is reportedly dealing with an ankle injury.
The #Browns won't face DE Danielle Hunter or WR Marvin Harrison Jr. on Sunday—and DE Will Anderson Jr. is in question with an ankle injury. https://t.co/wM1hRzoezb
For the Texans, not having Anderson Jr. on Sunday is something that could be a big impact, as the two-time pro bowler has put together a great season with 9.5 sacks in only eight games . Anderson Jr. has surpassed his 2023 rookie sack total (7.0 sacks) and will look to surpass the career high he set last season with 12.0 sacks.
Offensively, the Texans are looking to get Harrison Jr. involved more following their trade with the Arizona Cardinals, as Harrison Jr. became a part of the franchise on October 12 and has only been targeted 11 times in the three games played.
On the season, with both the Cardinals and the Texans, he has only been targeted 24 times with 11 receptions, averaging around 13.2 yards per reception. That is good enough for just 145 receiving yards and two touchdowns.
He hasn't had a big impact on the game this season, but missing Sunday keeps him behind the curve as he tries to adjust to the new system in Houston.
With Harrison Jr. out, the Texans will have to work in other guys on the offensive side of the ball.
While Anderson Jr. ruled questionable, the Texans know they will be without at least one defensive end in Hunter, as he is dealing with a hamstring injury.
Hunter has played in all eight games ahead of the matchup against the Browns and has played in all games since 2022, dating back to his days with the Minnesota Vikings. Hunter has been with Houston since 2024 and will miss his first game as a Texan on Sunday.
With the Texans' injury report being out and a good chunk of important pieces being on the list, Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson could have bought himself another week to succeed as the starter.
Defensively, the Browns will have a much easier time at locking down the passing game with Harrison Jr. inactive.
The two sides will clash at 1:00 p.m. EST from Huntington Bank Field on Sunday, Nov. 15.

title: Browns vs. Texans: 3 Matchups That Could Decide Sunday’s Game
full_text:
Houston has won three of its last four after a 0-4 start.
A Texans win would pull them within half a game of Cleveland and give Houston the head-to-head edge in the AFC playoff race.
Luckily for the Browns, the Texans are beatable, and here is why:
Denzel Boston leads the Browns with 507 receiving yards and averages 15.8 yards per catch. The Houston Texans have allowed 31 completions of 20 yards or more this season, tied for the third most in the NFL. Boston will have a chance to build on his six catches for 98 yards against New Orleans, including a 60-yard reception.
DENZEL BOSTON MOSSED HIM pic.twitter.com/ZZdzSZtnpj
The caveat comes down to blocking, as the Browns' offensive line has struggled in recent weeks and has allowed 38 total sacks this season , the most in the NFL. If Deshaun Watson has time to get the ball deep to Boston, the Browns have a fighting chance.
Rookie left tackle Spencer Fano will be central to Cleveland’s chances of keeping Watson upright. Fano ranks 17th out of 71 qualifying NFL tackles with a 74.5 overall grade, according to PFF. Fano allowed a season-high eight pressures against Pittsburgh in Week 8.
Now he faces a Houston pass rush led by Will Anderson Jr., the Defensive Player of the Year betting favorite with an NFL-high 9.5 sacks.
Love to see this. KC - orbit motion decoy (holds BS LB) Fano - down block on Simmons (All-Pro) Boston - crack block on PS safety Barber - counter kickout Fannin - counter pull for PS ILB Judkins - tight course, make CB miss Every key player mentioned here is 22yo or younger. pic.twitter.com/XW4Xue6x7h
Fano’s best game of his young career came against the Tennessee Titans, when he earned a 92.2 overall PFF grade and allowed just two pressures on 41 pass-blocking snaps.
If Fano can come close to that performance, Cleveland will have a better chance to give Watson time to attack Houston downfield.
Jared Verse’s production has been debated in Cleveland this season. Verse has just 15 pressures, according to PFF, and no sacks through nine games, despite being a key part of the Myles Garrett trade and viewed as a cornerstone of the Browns' defense.
Verse acknowledged that he hasn’t played well and said he spoke with the team psychologist about what he described as a “mental block.”
#Browns DE Jared Verse said he's reflected a lot on his struggles this season and believes he's identified areas to help him be more productive, but a lot of that work has been on the mental side. It's why he took time to meet with the team psychiatrist to help him "self-build."… pic.twitter.com/8pxPv0OxgX
His next test comes against Houston right tackle Trent Brown. Brown ranks 42nd among 71 qualifying tackles with a 64.2 overall PFF grade. Brown has allowed 19 pressures and two sacks on 342 pass-blocking snaps, according to Core Football Labs.
Even if Verse doesn’t get his first sack, forcing C.J. Stroud out of the pocket could help limit Houston’s deep passing game.
Make no mistake, the Texans are not an easy matchup. Stroud has four 300-yard passing games this season, including a 384-yard, five-touchdown performance last week against the Chargers.
If Cleveland gives Watson time to find his receivers downfield and keeps Stroud from doing the same, the Browns can head into the bye at 6-4.

title: Browns Hit With Major Injury News Ahead of Week 10 Showdown With Texans
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns might have seen the return of quarterback Deshaun Watson from concussion protocol after he missed last week's game.
But the team will now potentially be without a different key member of the offense this weekend.
On Friday, Nov. 13, the Browns announced another batch of injuries ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Houston Texans at Huntington Bank Field on Sunday.
First announced by ESPN NFL Insider Daniel Oyefusi, rookie wideout Denzel Boston was listed as questionable heading into the weekend due to a toe injury.
Browns WR Denzel Boston (toe) is questionable. FB Mike Burton and S Ronnie Hickman have been ruled out.
The 6-foot-4, 215-pound rookie has been one of the Browns' most exciting offseason additions to the offense , coming out of the draft quickly and making his impact. Across his first nine games, he has 32 receptions for 507 yards and three touchdowns, averaging 15.8 yards per reception.
His connection with Deshaun Watson has been o ne of the more welcomed things this season , even though the two had no prior experience with one another before this past offseason.
Without him on Sunday, Cleveland would have to turn to a combination of Tylan Wallace and Isaiah Bond to slide into the final wide receiver spot.
Alongside Boston potentially being inactive, the Browns received unfortunate news that safety Ronnie Hickman and fullback Mike Burton would be out on Sunday. Not listed as questionable, Burton is dealing with a calf injury, while Hickman is still recovering from a concussion.
Burton missing Sunday's game is going to be a hit to the rushing attack for the Browns, an area of the offense that has struggled all season long. With him out, the workload is going to be pushed even more onto the passing attack, especially with Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson still searching for a rhythm as the back half of the season gets underway.
While having any bodies on the injured list is going to be an issue, the Browns have found a nice replacement for Hickman for the time being.
Taken in the second round of the draft this past year, Emmanuel McNeil-Warren's initial status in the Browns' defense was somewhat unknown.
However, through limited opportunities, he has shown that he has an awful lot in the tank to give the team. Through nine games, he has 42 combined tackles, three tackles for a loss and three pass deflections , all while routinely being in the right position at the right time.
His role has changed each week, but in Week 10, it seems his opportunity to become a long-term, key piece of the Browns' defense is his for the taking.
The Browns and Texans will face at 1:00 p.m. EST from Huntington Bank Field, with Boston's final status expected to be released prior to the game.
Cade Cracas is a sports media professional with experience in play-by-play, broadcasting and digital storytelling. He is a recent graduate of Ashland University with degrees in digital media production and journalism.

title: Deshaun Watson’s Return Against Houston Comes With a Major Opportunity for Cleveland
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns host the Houston Texans at a pivotal point in their season. They are the AFC's eighth seed, just one spot out of a wildcard position.
If they lose, they will head into their bye week on a three-game losing streak at 5-5. However, if they win, they start their four-game home stand with a win and improve to 6-4.
#Browns Todd Monken said "the intention was for Deshaun to start." Just wanted to run it by the staff.
Todd Monken turns back to Deshaun Watson as starting quarterback after he missed last week to rest from a concussion injury. Watson returns to face the team that drafted him before things went sour and they were forced to trade him.
He is 1-0 against the Texans, winning his first game in a Browns uniform.
No game has been bigger than this one for the Browns. The Texans come into Cleveland after drubbing the Los Angeles Chargers, improving their record to 3-5. CJ Stroud has had a great season, and he is looking to translate his stat line into more wins. The Texans will come in with all the momentum and motivation, as they need this win to keep their playoff hopes alive.
The Browns return to Cleveland after a three-game road trip. Cleveland is ready to welcome them back after starting the season 3-0 in their home stadium. The Texans are 3-1 on the road, so it will be a great test of which team has the advantage.
Watson and the offense will have to start faster than normal. Their tendency is to start games slowly before turning it on in the fourth quarter and winning late in games. Houston’s offense has been high-flying, and all their wide receivers are finally healthy. The Browns’ defense has been gashed on the ground, but Houston has thrived through the air.
The Texans are probably the second-best team that the Browns will face the rest of the way, outside of the Cincinnati Bengals. If they can win this game, then the playoffs become more likely entering the bye week.
They are tied with the New England Patriots in the standings, but the Patriots earned the last wild card spot due to their record against AFC opponents. The Browns can help their cause by beating the Texans as the Patriots play an NFC team this week.
Watson also needs to beat the Texans personally. If the Browns fall and there is breathing room between them and the playoffs, then they will likely pivot to Shedeur Sanders at quarterback. After three quarters of undesirable play last week, Sanders put together an incredible fourth quarter and overtime.
Monken remained steadfast that Watson would start following his return from concussion protocol.
A similar situation arose early in the season when it was believed that the team would switch to Sanders if Watson performed poorly against Baker Mayfield and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Watson led a fourth-quarter comeback, and he kept his job.
He now faces the next piece of what is considered one of the worst trades in NFL history, with a familiar consequence on the line . The Browns will complete the revenge tour after their bye week against Kevin Stefanski and the Atlanta Falcons.
Monken took a lot of heat for naming Watson the starter at the beginning of the season, but he proved right after they started 5-2. He now goes back to Watson with full faith that he gives the team the best chance to win. Monken can earn a lot of credibility with a good performance from the offense and a win on Sunday.
Both teams in Sunday’s matchup need the win just as much as the other. The Texans tanked the Browns for four seasons after the trade for Watson. The only winning season the Browns had since was in 2023, in which Watson was injured.
It ended after a blowout loss in the playoffs to the Texans.
The Browns have their chance to bury the Texans’ season and force them to make a decision on extending their quarterback, which could alter their franchise.
Watson has returned just in time for the Browns’ biggest opportunity of the season to beat his former team.
Graduated from Bowling Green State University with a Journalism degree. Written and contributed to numerous media outlets. Cleveland sports victim.

title: Browns Have 3 Major Offseason Needs That Their Trade Deadline Silence Made Clear
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline passed at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday, and the Browns made zero moves. Cleveland finds itself in a strange position with a 5-4 record; however, the Browns aren't in "win-now" mode like many teams that were active at the deadline.
There were a few position groups the Browns could have considered trading for, but since they didn't make a move, here are three offseason needs that Cleveland must address in 2027.
The Browns have one of the best pass-catching tight ends in the NFL in Harold Fannin Jr., but the lack of depth behind him is concerning. Cleveland has only two tight ends on the active 53-man roster: Fannin and Blake Whiteheart. Many teams carry four to five tight ends, so the Browns need to figure out how to add more depth at the position next offseason.
The good news is that the Browns don’t need to add a high-level tight end since they have Fannin. But they should look for additional blocking tight ends so Fannin can focus more on the passing game instead of having to stay in to chip-block. It’s also important to have tight ends who can contribute in the running game.
Expect the Browns to sign a veteran tight end in free agency and to draft one in the first four rounds of the 2027 NFL Draft.
The Browns faced challenges coming into the season, particularly on defense, after trading away the NFL's best pass rusher, Myles Garrett, to the Rams and getting Jared Verse in the deal. Verse performed solidly during his two seasons with Los Angeles, recording 12 sacks in 34 games. But this season, he has yet to register a single sack in nine games.
Additionally, the Browns' second-best pass rusher entering the season was expected to be Alex Wright, who unfortunately tore his Achilles during training camp.
Cleveland will need to address the pass rusher position in the offseason. The Browns may consider making a move in the first or second round of the draft and could also sign a veteran free agent at a lower cost.
The Browns have two strong starting linebackers in Carson Schwesinger and Quincy Williams, but like their tight end position, there isn’t much depth behind them. If the Browns lose Schwesinger or Williams for any length of time during the season, the defense could take a significant hit.
They have struggled to stop the run in recent weeks, allowing an average of 130.6 rushing yards per game, which ranks among the worst in the NFL.
Cleveland needs to add more depth at linebacker. This would let it use three or even four linebacker sets at times to improve its chances of stopping the run game.
Daniel is a sports writer from Northeast Ohio. He has followed the Browns, Cavs, Guardians, and Buckeyes for years and loves sharing his thoughts on the team.

title: Todd Monken Gives One Concerning Update on the Browns' Offensive Line
full_text:
As the Cleveland Browns get ready to try and cut a two-game losing streak that would throw them back in the thick of the race for the playoffs, the offensive line’s play will be heavily scrutinized over the second half of the season.
No position group received more attention on the open market during the offseason than the O-Line, and after the first nine games, it’s safe to say the experiment isn’t working.
The Browns' offensive line ranks among the bottom-dwellers in the league when it comes to yards before first contact in the run game, and things look even worse in the passing game. Cleveland’s two starting tackles, Tytus Howard and rookie Spencer Fano, have the two highest pressure rates allowed in the entire NFL, and as a whole, Cleveland is the team that has allowed the most sacks (38) for the year, too.
Here's a look at the worst 10 starting tackles in the NFL right now when it comes to pressures allowed. And man, do I have bad news for the Browns... pic.twitter.com/Mby8wczjTd
To top things off, Howard leads the league with seven false start penalties , while guards Zion Johnson and rookie Austin Barber are among the six players tied for second place in holding penalties, with four apiece.
But if you were expecting to see some personnel changes for the second half of the season, don’t hold your breath.
Monken told reporters on Wednesday that his offensive line is set, and he isn’t planning on making any changes along the unit.
“I don’t see it that way. I mean, our starters are the starters. We addressed it again today: who the biggest culprits are. And they’re our guys. And they’re like, like we said before, I mean, they’re like our kids. We’re not going to just change out our kids. I mean, we’re not going to change out our players. They’re our best players. We got to get our best players. And we have a very diligent team. We have a lot of guys that love playing football, but the stats are what they are. I mean, we’ve got to look in the mirror and say, ‘at some point, this is it.’ I mean, that we just can’t continue down this road.”
When pressed about not reaching the point where changes are needed, Monken doubled down on his stance.
“I haven’t reached that point. We can’t change out our starters. I mean, I’m not changing out our starters. I mean, they’re either going to, they’re either going to buy into those types of things and the mental stamina that it takes to hold their water on defense or for us to have discipline offensively. But we’re not going to be the team we can be, because there are starters for a reason, right? If the other guys we thought gave us a better chance to win, they’d be in there.
"So, it’s all of us. How do we coach it better? How do we get our guys to dial in in the most critical moments, when it matters most?”
The Browns understandably didn’t want to pour more resources into this unit before the trade deadline after an offseason deal for Howard, adding Johnson and Elgton Jenkins in free agency, and then spending two draft picks, including a one inside the Top-10 on the group, but staying this course will lead nowhere... fast.
But zero roster changes doesn’t necessarily mean no changes at all . At some point in the preseason, Teven Jenkins was projected as the team’s starting right tackle before a back injury opened the door for Barber, who hasn’t looked back since. And there were some doubts about Fano too, with Monken acknowledging at one time that Dawand Jones could open the season at left tackle.
If that’s the case, then it’s not like the five current starters have always been head and shoulders above the rest.
And who’s to say Fano wouldn’t actually play better at right tackle than Howard? And Barber better than Fano on the left side? Both are coming off playing those positions in college for Utah and Florida, respectively. Those moves could open the right guard spot for Jenkins, as it seemed was intended.
Finally, Monken admitted during the offseason that he’d prefer to see Elgton Jenkins at guard instead of center, so there’s another possible piece that could be moved in search of a better fit overall.
Because at the end of the day, you do want your five best players on the field, but you also want them playing in their best possible spots, and sometimes leaving out one of the top five players for a better fit in one specific position maximizes the talent of the unit.
Alas, with Monken steadfast in keeping his “kids” where they are, and reinserting Deshaun Watson and his elongated dropbacks at quarterback --not that Shedeur Sanders fared much better in avoiding sacks against the Saints-- the inevitable result for Cleveland is written on the wall.
Rafael brings more than two decades worth of experience writing all things football.

title: 3 Winners, 2 Losers from Browns 2026 Trade Deadline Stand
full_text:
Despite the Cleveland Browns having some obvious holes in the roster, the team decided to not make any moves before the NFL trade deadline.
Let's take a look at some winners and losers after no deals were made.
The Browns' offensive line this year has simply been atrocious.
According to the numbers from PFF, Tytus Howard is the lowest-ranked member of this browns offensive line.
While there weren't many rumors, most likely due to the overhaul of the unit this past offseason, the Browns could have considered trading for some veteran linemen off of teams that were looking to sell.
Now, Howard gets to continue to start at Right Tackle for Cleveland, and try to turn his first year in the brown and orange around.
After the 2026 NFL Draft, it was pretty clear the Browns were ready to move on from Jerry Jeudy.
Since then, KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston have both broken out in their first year and are the top two rookie receivers in the entire NFL.
Meanwhile, for Jeudy, sure, he has made some big plays for Cleveland, but he still clearly remains underutilized and targeted.
Before the deadline, many thought the Browns would deal Jeudy to a receiver-needy team where he could get back to his true WR1 days.
Instead, Jeudy remains on a Cleveland team that has already appeared to move on to younger options.
One of the needs on the Browns roster is cornerback depth.
Behind Denzel Ward and Tyson Campbell sits Myles Harden, who has had some highs and lows this season.
After no moves were made, Harden now solidifies his playing spot on the roster, at least for the rest of the season, making him a winner.
Deshaun Watson is a loser for two reasons.
Despite many thinking the Browns would try to deal either Dillon Gabriel or Shedeur Sanders, they both remain with the team. Along with Taylen Green, the Browns will most likely finish the season with four QBs rostered.
This also puts pressure on Watson, who has Sanders as his backup. Let's not forget the game Shedeur just had against New Orleans, despite the loss.
On top of the pressure to perform, Watson has to continue doing it with the current offensive line.
As mentioned before, the unit has severely underperformed and allowed the most sacks in the entire NFL.
The final winner for the Browns is Isaiah McGuire, who gets to keep his starting reps after Cleveland did not trade for an edge rusher.
Throughout the weeks leading up, the Browns were rumored to target a defensive lineman
Now, Cleveland holds with its entire roster, giving guys like McGuire the chance to keep getting starting reps
