title: Why Browns Didn’t Move Shedeur Sanders or Dillon Gabriel at Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns chose not to make any moves at the NFL trade deadline on Tuesday, surprising many who expected them to trade a quarterback, especially with four currently on their active roster. With injuries surging across the league, demand for quarterbacks is higher than ever.
While it was clear that Deshaun Watson and Taylen Green weren’t going anywhere, players like Shedeur Sanders and Dillon Gabriel could have been potential trade candidates.
The Browns likely didn’t receive the price they wanted to trade either Gabriel or Sanders, so they decided it was wiser to maintain their quarterback depth instead.
Cleveland selected Gabriel in the third round of the 2025 NFL Draft. Although he may not seem like the franchise’s future quarterback, he could still play a backup role in 2027 and 2028. Sanders, another 2025 draft pick, just started a game against the New Orleans Saints on Sunday.
While he might not be the ideal candidate for the starting quarterback position, the Browns likely want to give him a fair evaluation before the next season.
The Minnesota Vikings were in urgent need of quarterback assistance at the trade deadline but ultimately opted for veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders. They probably had no intention of trading for either Sanders or Gabriel, which is another reason the Browns didn’t make any moves; teams in need of quarterbacks were unlikely to reach out to them.
With a 6-2 record, the Vikings weren't going to consider Sanders or Gabriel, since neither has made a significant impact in the NFL. They were searching for someone who could lead them to the Super Bowl immediately.
However, the Browns may still part ways with Sanders or Gabriel during the offseason. Cleveland is likely to draft a quarterback in the first round of the 2027 NFL Draft and intends to keep Green in the quarterback room. They will probably need to sign a veteran quarterback to start, at least until the rookie is ready.
This could lead to five quarterbacks in the room, making it unlikely that the Browns will carry all five into training camp next season. Therefore, either Sanders or Gabriel is likely to be the odd one out.
Sanders still has an opportunity to start a few more games this season. The Browns could enter their bye week 5-5 if they lose to the Houston Texans on Sunday. This situation might prompt head coach Todd Monken to change quarterbacks and move away from Watson.
Daniel is a sports writer from Northeast Ohio. He has followed the Browns, Cavs, Guardians, and Buckeyes for years and loves sharing his thoughts on the team.

title: Browns' Jared Verse Opens Up On Health Questions Amid Strugglesome 2026 Season
full_text:
The 2026 NFL season h as not been kind to Cleveland Browns edge rusher Jared Verse.
After joining the team this past offseason in a blockbuster trade with the Los Angeles Rams, the expectations were set high for Verse, especially with the Browns giving up future Hall of Famer Myles Garrett in the process.
But through the first nine weeks of the season, Verse has struggled greatly.
On Thursday, Nov. 12, he gave an update on where his health was at and if it was affecting his play at all, while also giving Browns fans some grace on their frustrations with him.
"I am upset with the way I have been playing," he said. "I don't think it is anything physical. There's nothing wrong with my body. I don't think it is anything like that. I think it is the mental aspect of the game, and I think I attacked it."
If the 26-year-old had been dealing with some sort of injury, it would have made sense to see him with just 20 combined tackles and four for a loss.
But instead, it looks like it is just something upstairs he is trying to work through.
"I think it was definitely a mental block," he said. "I train my body every day to push myself to the limits of what I am physically capable of doing...I think I have taken the steps to figure out what it was after meeting with a couple of people and everything like that."
Verse went on to defend Browns fans who have been frustrated with his lack of productivity, as the criticism that has come his way as of late has been heavy.
"...We can be here all day, and I can talk to you about each key play we have played all season... It is just simple to say the Browns fans are upset about it; I am upset about it; we all have a reason to be upset about it," he said about Browns fans being upset with his play. "I just haven't done enough, and I think that I have taken the time to figure out what the issue was and attacked it. I think I am ready for this week."
Whether or not he wants to admit it, that likely is also playing a part in his mental state. Having to fill such big shoes that Garrett once had in Cleveland is a tough task, and with his slow start to the year, his lack of production has to be weighing on him.
Either way, Cleveland needs the 2024 Defensive Rookie of the Year to return to that dominant form he once displayed, not just to show that the trade wasn't a complete flop on the Browns' end, but also to help guide this team to a playoff spot in the back half of the season.
The Browns return to the field on Sunday, Nov. 14, from Huntington Bank Field against the Houston Texans. The two sides play at 1:00 p.m. EST.
Against a dynamic and mobile quarterback like CJ Stroud, all eyes will be on how Verse can disrupt their passing attack.

title: Cowboys Legend Leighton Vander Esch Drills $1M Kick in Pat McAfee College GameDay Contest
full_text:
Dallas Cowboys fans tuning into ESPN College GameDay got a treat when a familiar face made an appearance. Leighton Vander Esch, a first-round pick in 2018 out of Boise State, was there to represent his Broncos.
LVE was also there to try and make a kick for $1 million.
Every week, Pat McAfee allows a fan to kick a 33-yard field goal for $1 million. This week, they also had Vander Esch come out to try a kick, although he was playing for charity.
After missing badly on his first attempt, Vander Esch was allowed to try again. This time, he drilled it right down the middle , which meant McAfee would donate $1 million to the Make-A-Wish foundation.
Leighton stepped up for Luca and @MakeAWish with a $1 Million kick 💰❤️ pic.twitter.com/MPl7ytklyB
Boise State fan Easton Hanson also got a chance to kick for $1 million and he drilled the attempt.
GameDay is live from Boise State on Saturday as the No. 24 Broncos host the Oregon State Beavers. Kickoff is at 6:00 p.m. EST and will take place at Albertsons Stadium.
The Broncos are 8-1, whereas the Beavers come into this one with a record of 5-4.
Vander Esch wasn't a popular selection when first announced as Cowboys' fans felt he was selected too high. Dallas had the 19th overall pick and linebacker wasn't seen as an impactful enough position for such a selection. There were also concerns about his medical history as Vander Esch entered the league with a lingering neck issue.
That feeling changed in a hurry as LVE made a huge impact. He recorded 140 tackles and two interceptions as a rookie, leading to a Pro Bowl selection. That was impressive enough on its own, but he also started just 11 of the 16 games he played.
Unfortunately, the neck injuries ended up playing a major role in his career. He suffered another neck injury in 2019, leading to surgery. He missed nine games that year and another six in 2020 due to a broken collarbone.
Vander Esch suffered yet another neck injury in 2023, forcing him to miss all but five games. He then retired from the game at just 28 years old . It was tough to see him go, especially at such a young age, but he proved to be a stud during his six-year career, even if he never earned the respect he deserved.

title: Jerry Jones' Comments on Brian Schottenheimer Suggest Cowboys Coach Won't Get Fired
full_text:
When it comes to Dallas Cowboys fans right now, head coach Brian Schottenheimer is public enemy No. 1.
Since taking over the Cowboys in 2025, the team is a dreadful 11-14-1 under Schottenheimer, including a disappointing 4-5 this season.
But it isn't just about the record.
Despite having the fifth-best scoring offense in the NFL, it still feels like the Cowboys aren't operating at their best, something many believe is on the play-calling of Schottenheimer. There is also an incredible lack of discipline, which is another stain on Schottenheimer's tenure as head coach.
All of this has led fans and analysts alike to believe that Schotty should get fired . However, based on what Jerry Jones said recently, that might not happen anytime soon.
During his latest appearance on 105.3 The Fan on Friday, Jones made it sound like Schottenheimer isn't going anywhere anytime soon, with Jones once again expressing his confidence in the embattled head coach.
Jones also noted that he believes Schottenheimer will get better as a head coach in the year or years ahead.
That's right, year or years.
"Given the ability to live to tell about it, Brian will be a year from now, two years from now, three years from now, he'll be much more (prepared) for the kinds of challenges a head coach has," Jones said. "There's no question, you pay a price when you're doing it for the first time. ... I still like (our) bet (on him)."
Cowboys fans don't want Schottenheimer to finish out the season, let alone get one or more years. So, that's what makes Jones' comments especially jarring.
What makes Jones' faith in Schotty even more perplexing is the fact that the Cowboys believe they have the talent necessary to succeed, which is part of the reason why they didn't make any trades on deadline day.
“It shows you that we’re confident in our roster and our best football is still ahead," Schottenheimer said after the trade deadline passed without a Cowboys deal.
So, if the roster is good enough but the team is still playing at an unacceptable level, there's only the coaching left to blame.
To be fair to Schottenheimer, he isn't the only culprit on the staff, as defensive coordinator Christian Parker has left a lot to be desired with his play-calling, also.
But Schottenheimer is the head coach and the buck ultimately stops with him. There is a lot of blame going his way, whether it's because of the play-calling, his in-game decision-making or the lackluster culture that, according to a few former Cowboys , has players not giving full effort and doing boneheaded things like DeMarvion Overshown did in Week 9 with his penalty .
If this season ends the way we think it will, which is with Dallas not making the postseason yet again, and the Cowboys give Schotty another chance in 2027, the fan base will be beside itself and hope for this franchise getting on track will be at an all-time low.

title: Cowboys Named Landing Spot For Former Pro Bowl RB in Free Agency Amid Tyler Goodson injury
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys' No. 2 running back spot has had a run of bad luck this year because of injuries.
Before the 2026 season started, the Cowboys lost Malik Davis to a season-ending hip injury . Now, Dallas' latest RB2, Tyler Goodson, is expected to miss multiple weeks with his knee injury.
That leaves the Cowboys depending on Israel Abanikanda behind Javonte Williams this week. Dallas also added Kendre Miller to the practice squad.
Safe to say, neither one of those backs are reliable and Dallas may want to explore the free-agent market if Goodson misses an extended period of time.
In an article listing off the best bargain free agents still available after the trade deadline, Bleacher Report's Moe Moton linked Dallas to former Pro Bowl running back Najee Harris.
"Dallas Cowboys executive vice president Stephen Jones expects backup running back Tyler Goodson to miss time with a knee injury," Moton said.
"The Cowboys signed Kendre Miller to their practice squad, but he has a history of injuries. Harris could be a solid complement to Javonte Williams in the Cowboys' ground game.
"Best fits: Dallas Cowboys, New England Patriots."
In 2026, Harris latched on with the New York Giants and played in five games before he was cut for complaining about how the Giants handled their backfield touches.
“It’s hard to get into a rhythm with one or two plays,” Harris said to reporters in October. “If you’re getting a play here and then get taken out for a series, there’s nothing you could do. I’ve never been through none of this before.”
Harris didn't see much success with the Giants, with the veteran running back tallying just 3.2 yards per carry. He did have one solid game, though, when he posted 52 rushing yards on nine carries, good enough for 5.8 yards per tote.
That showed Harris still has something left in the tank after suffering a torn Achilles in 2025.
Harris totaled four 1,000-yard seasons and one Pro Bowl nod over the first four years of his career when he served as a workhorse back for the Pittsburgh Steelers.
But things have gone downhill for him since then, as he suffered a torn Achilles in 2025 and didn't do much during his stint in New York.
While Harris isn't an explosive back and won't offer much of a change of pace from Williams, he is good between the tackles, and is an asset as a pass-catcher and in pass protection.
Most importantly, he's just a reliable back who is going to offer more stability than anyone the Cowboys have on their roster currently.
We suspect the Cowboys will stand pat for now if Goodson is only going to miss a game or two, but if he's going to be out any longer than that, we could see a Harris-Cowboys union in the near future.

title: Cowboys Add 6-Foot-4 CB With Rare Physical Tools in New 2027 Mock Draft
full_text:
Defense has been a focus for the Dallas Cowboys for the past several seasons. They have been cycling through defensive coordinators ever since Dan Quinn left and every year, they seem to get worse.
While a lot of the blame falls on the coaching staff and the lack of consistency, there are still some spots in need of an upgrade. One such position is at cornerback, where the Cowboys have had some serious underperformers.
The lack of trusted options in the secondary has Cody Williams of FanSided focused on a cornerback in his latest 2027 NFL mock draft. With the 21st overall pick, Williams has Dallas selecting Kelley Jones from Mississippi State .
The first thing that stands out about Jones is his immense size. Listed at 6-foot-4 and 205 pounds, Jones is built like a wide receiver and isn't afraid to use his size. He's scheme versatile, but is best utilized in press coverage.
He is still raw and that's why not every draft pundit has him as a first-round pick. It could also be a problem for Dallas if their coaching staff doesn't show some serious growth. Still, he could be a day one starter, and while it would be ideal to pair him with Joey Porter Jr. , Williams says there's a chance he could be his replacement if Porter leaves in free agency.
"My gut tells me that the Cowboys would love if there was a linebacker or an offensive tackle falling to them in this spot, but I don't think they can go wrong on defense in many spots overall regardless. The pick for me is Kelley Jones, because Dallas simply can't move forward without making substantial upgrades in the secondary," Williams wrote.
"Jones could either replace Joey Porter Jr. if he leaves in free agency or pair with him on the outside, which would move DaRon Bland back into the slot where he's always performed better."
Given the fact that Dallas sent a second-round pick to Pittsburgh for Porter, they will surely do all they can to keep him around. With Jones and Porter as starters, it could spell the end for DaRon Bland, especially since they truly love using Caleb Downs in the slot.
That's not a bad thing since Bland has been a problem this season and is showing no signs of turning things around. Even with his need to develop, Jones would be a significant upgrade at a fraction of the price.

title: Cowboys-49ers Start Time Could Be Impacted By FAA Nationwide Ground Stop
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys are set to host the San Francisco 49ers at AT&T Stadium on Sunday afternoon in a clash between two historic NFC rivals.
However, the FAA's nationwide ground stoppage on Friday could have an impact on the 49ers' travel plans to Arlington until further announcements are made. The FAA's ground stoppage is due to communication issues impacting air traffic control. All flights already in the air can land, but no new flights can take off.
The game is set to kick off at 3:25 p.m. CT on Sunday. San Francisco was set to take off on Saturday around 1 p.m. PT, per 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan, but those plans could be altered given recent developments .
The ground stoppage obviously has a massive impact on the NFL ahead of Week 10's slate of games. If the 49ers are unable to make it to Texas in time, the league would have no choice but to reschedule the game, which would affect the rest of the NFL season.
49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan met with reporters on Friday, but wasn't aware of the FAA's announcement until told by the media. "I didn't know. I just first heard," Shanahan said. He added that the 49ers will go through a normal walk-through on Saturday morning, but the plans after that remain up in the air until the FAA provides further updates about when flights can resume.
"It'll be a normal walk-through time for us. We're just going to get there a little bit later," Shanahan said.
That's certainly wishful thinking from Shanahan. As of Friday evening, no one really knows when scheduled flights will be able to take off.
Any delay in the 49ers' travel plans could be viewed as somewhat of an advantage for the Cowboys ahead of Week 10's kickoff. However, in a worst-case scenario where the game has to get rescheduled, it could impact the rest of Dallas' schedule during the regular season.
Would other games have to be pushed back? Would the Cowboys-49ers have to play at a later date? No one really knows until the FAA shares what's next.
If the game goes on as scheduled, the Cowboys will be looking to end a four-game losing streak against the 49ers that started during Dallas' heatbreaking playoff loss to San Francisco in 2022.

title: Colin Cowherd Hits Cowboys With Brutal Reality Check Ahead of 49ers Showdown
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys escaped with a narrow win over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 9, but they were far from impressive . Dallas made an unreal amount of mistakes with two turnovers while committing 14 penalties.
That's why, despite the Colts being a team that was selling at the deadline, this contest went down to the final seconds. While the win means Dallas is still technically alive in the NFC East , they should have no confidence going into Week 10 against the 7-1 San Francisco 49ers .
San Francisco is currently the No. 1 seed in the NFC and they're among the best coached teams in the sport. That's why Colin Cowherd believes Kyle Shanahan will make it look easy when going against Brian Schottenheimer, even coming up with a brutal comparison between the two coaches.
"Niners take on the Cowboys in Dallas. That sounds big. It is also a big coaching mismatch. Kyle Shanahan may very well be the best coach in this league. He gives Sean McVay fits and Schotty and the Cowboys staff, let's just say this is like a U.S. Warship against your dad's fishing boat. Live on Fox. I can't find a way Dallas wins," Cowherd said on The Herd.
"Let's just say this is like a U.S. warship against your dad's fishing boat. I can't find a way Dallas wins." @colincowherd on the coaching mismatch between Kyle Shanahan's 49ers & Brian Schottenheimer's Cowboys pic.twitter.com/WKAgQQxRwU
Cowherd went on to say how important coaching is in the NFL, and broke down what poorly coached teams do.
"Coaching matters in this sport, more than any other sport. There's three things that poorly coached teams, not all on Schotty, it's on his staff too, that poorly coached teams do. Number one, a lot of mistakes and penalties. Dallas leads the NFL in penalty yards. Number two, is uneven. They can't put anything together week after week. Schotty's got one, once since he's been in Dallas, back-to-back wins."
As for his last point, Cowherd discussed how Dak Prescott and Brandon Aubrey are just two of the players who are regressing under Schottenheimer and his staff.
"The other thing is, even really good players, on poorly coached teams have regression. Dak Prescott, everything's down. Completion percentage down. Passer rating down. Yards are down. And by the way, it's getting worse. Last five weeks, Dak Prescott with CeeDee Lamb and Pickens is completing 61% of his throws. So it's a classically poorly coached team where a lot of mistakes, really uneven half-to-half, week-to-week, even good players, even their kicker now, their great kickers having a bad year."
None of this is fun to hear, but it's also impossible to argue against Cowherd. Sure, Jerry Jones made the absolutely ridiculous claim that highly-paid coaches don't always lead to success, but Cowherd's points are valid.
He even discussed how Shanhan runs one of the most complex offenses in the NFL, yet gets no penalties. As for Schottenheimer, Cowherd said he has a stripped-down, "Jurrassic" offense, yet the team can't do anything right and continues to get flags.
This week, Schottenheimer and the Cowboys can make a huge statement against the best team in the conference. Unfortunately, the work they've done since Schotty took over ahead of the 2025 season suggests this could go about as well as Cowherd expects it to.

title: George Pickens Emphatically Confirms Week 10 Status For Cowboys-49ers
full_text:
For the first time since he was acquired in a trade in 2025, veteran wide receiver George Pickens missed a game with the Dallas Cowboys last week.
Pickens, who was dealing with a hamstring issue that he has been battling for multiple weeks, was limited all three days last week before drawing a questionable tag and being inactive .
This week, Pickens started off with a pair of limited practices over the first two days, which was a bad sign because that's how he started off last week before ultimately sitting out.
But, on Friday, when the Cowboys are going to release their final injury report, Pickens left no doubt about whether or not he will play.
According to Calvin Watkins of The Dallas Morning News , the Cowboys wideout made an emphatic statement about his chances of playing on Sunday.
"You gonna see me out there. You got to turn the TV screen on," Pickens said.
When asked if this is the best he has felt in a while, Pickens had another interesting response.
"When you turn that TV on, get some food make sure if you have a wife or girlfriend, make sure you hug her, love her and when you turn the TV on, you should see me," Pickens added .
The Cowboys have not yet released their final injury report as of this writing, but I think it's safe to assume he'll be out there on Sunday.
Pickens has posted 533 yards and two touchdowns in the eight games he played this season. Assuming he doesn't miss another game, he's currently on pace to tally 1,065 receiving yards and four touchdowns.
That would be a far cry from what he posted last season when he ripped off career-highs in receiving yards (1,429) and touchdown (nine).
A big reason for Pickens' drop in production has been the presence of fellow wideout CeeDee Lamb.
Lamb missed three games due to injury last season and exited a few others early, which left more work for Pickens. In fact, some of Pickens' best performances came while Lamb was sidelined.
But Lamb has not missed any games this season and has, as expected, returned to his role as quarterback Dak Prescott's favorite target, which has no doubt cut into Pickens' opportunities.
Through nine games, Lamb is having a monster season with 70 receptions, 904 receiving yards and seven touchdowns. He also leads the NFL with 108 targets, so Prescott has looked his way a ton in 2026.
But Pickens is still having a solid campaign for a No. 2 receiver and that doesn't change the fact that he would be a No. 1 target on a lot of teams around the league.

title: Jerry Jones Isn't Buying DeMarvion Overshown's Explanation for Dumb Penalty in Cowboys' Win
full_text:
DeMarvion Overshown was responsible for one of the dumbest things you will ever seen on a football field during the Dallas Cowboys' Week 9 win over the Indianapolis Colts.
After a massively important turnover in the fourth quarter of the game, the Cowboys linebacker, who was inactive because of an injury, ran onto the field and was flagged for unsportsmanlike conduct, which cost the Cowboys 15 yards.
Overshown has since apologized to his team and said he was not aware he would get penalized for doing what he did.
“I really didn’t know the rule until I heard Dee Winters, he yelled, ‘D-Mo, you can’t be out here!’ That’s when I looked back and I already saw the ref pointing," Overshown said , per Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram.”
“I was just caught up in the moment. … I apologized to the team (after the game). It can’t happen again. It won’t happen again," Overshown added.
When asked about Overshown's explanation for his egregiously dumb act, owner Jerry Jones said he doesn't believe the veteran linebacker didn't know the rules.
"I don't think that (Overshown didn't know). I think that he's been involved in football at Texas and he's been involved here, and he knows that at every level a non-participant can't run out on the field," Jones told 105.3 The Fan .
Whether Overshown knew it or not, it was egregiously stupid for him to do what he did and only feeds into the narrative that the Cowboys are not a disciplined team.
“It is (unacceptable). … It’s not a good look. It’s not a disciplined look," Stephen Jones said on Monday. "We certainly didn’t play a disciplined game yesterday with (14) penalties. We have to be better than that.”
Will head coach Brian Schottenheimer actually hold Overshown accountable and bench him to teach him a lesson?
Well, we'll find out soon enough on Sunday because Overshown is slated to return to action after his latest absence.
That said, we won't hold our breath for Schottenheimer to punish him in any significant way since we've seen players do dumb stuff and not get punished before ( see: Rashan Gary ).
Right after it happened, quarterback Dak Prescott was very clearly angry at his teammate on the sideline , and Prescott wasn't afraid to admit that was the case when speaking to reporters this week.
“I was pissed," Prescott stated, per NFL insider Ed Werder. "I spoke my mind, and I don't think I've ever been short or shy in a moment when it's you know truly, truly bothered me. And yeah, that was just a big play … the turnover happened and a flag comes out and it's just like we did some great stuff here, let's not minimize it.”
The penalty cost the Cowboys' offense 15 yards, setting Dallas up at its own 15-yard line.
The first play of the drive saw Javonte Williams gain 15 yards on a carry, and then the Cowboys picked up nine more yards after that before facing a fourth-and-1 at their own 39.
Without the penalty, the Cowboys would have been in Indianapolis territory and maybe Dallas goes for it on that fourth down instead of punting like they did, in which case they could have grabbed a bigger lead or at least run off more clock.
Thankfully for Overshown, the Cowboys managed to win the game in the end or else the penalty have gone down as an even bigger blunder that would have been talked about for years to come.

title: Dallas Cowboys Rookie Power Rankings at Midway Point of 2026 Season
full_text:
We are halfway through what has been a miserable season for the Dallas Cowboys, and the showing from the team's 2026 NFL Draft class has been a microcosm of how things have gone.
Only one of the team's draft picks has made a consistent and positive impact through nine games, and that has made the seven-man draft class a major disappointment overall.
Luckily, there is still time for those rookies who haven't done much to right the ship, but it has no doubt been an ominous start for six Cowboys selections.
With all that in mind, let's take a look at a rookie power rankings featuring the team's latest draft class as we hit the midway point.
The Cowboys' seventh-round pick, Smith failed to make the 53-man roster out of trainging camp before being brought back on the practice squad.
Smith has not gotten into a game this season, and when Dallas needed a wide receiver off the practice squad last week amid injury issues, fellow rookie Jordan Hudson , not Smith, got the elevation.
That tells us everything we need to know about Smith's standing with the team currently.
A fourth-round pick in April, Moore has not played a single snap this season because of the hip injury he suffered before the regular season began.
Moore has a chance to return soon, though, as he was designated to return from injured reserve this week, which gives him 21 days to be activated or else he has to miss the rest of the season.
The Florida product entered the NFL with injury concerns and he has done nothing to shake those concerns.
Shelton lands in this spot by default since he has actually played snaps this season with five on offense and 23 on special teams.
There has been nothing to write home about for the fourth-round pick, though, and it's very clear he needs a lot more development, which we knew dating back to the preseason when he was completely overmatched .
The Cowboys clearly told us that when they decided to trade for Broderick Jones instead of relying on Shelton as a swing tackle.
Overton has seen a fairly healthy 29% of snaps this season and has played in every game with no fewer than 21.1% of snaps on defense in each, so at least he's involved.
Overton hasn't done a ton with those snaps, though, as he's tallied just eight tackles, one pass defensed and one fumble recovery.
According to Pro Football Focus , Overton has six pressures and is posting less than ideal pass-rush and run defense grades of 53.4 and 51.8.
After shining in training camp and the preseason and making some plays early in the regular season, hype for Barham was palpable.
It looked like Barham was going to be playing a major role for the Cowboys for the rest of the season after he got chances to start and wear the green dot, but he has since gone in the opposite direction.
Barham saw a season-high 60 snaps in Week 7 but went down to 21 the game after that, and then 16 in Week 8 and a season-low three snaps in Week 9.
The Michigan product is expected to get more run at outside linebacker this week, but that's only because of the injury to Donovan Ezeiruaku, so his increased run may not last long.
As Barham has gone backwards, Lawrence has gone in the other direction, at least in terms of his role.
After not seeing more than 43.5% snaps over the first five games, Lawrence has seen his playing time increase over his last three, with snap shares of 52% and 49.4% in two games in that span.
He also got the starting nod over a struggling Ezeiruaku in those games.
That said, his production hasn't been all that impressive with just one sack and nine pressures. He is also on injured reserve for at least three more games after coming down with a high-ankle sprain.
Downs has been the Cowboys' best rookie and it isn't even close.
Downs has played a significant role in every game, bouncing between the slot and safety because of injuries.
He has played 84.8% of snaps or more in every game but one, which was the Week 8 loss to the Arizona Cardinals when Downs left early because of a concussion . Downs has played 100% of snaps in six contests.
In nine games, Downs has registered 55 tackles, which is the most on the team by a whopping 17, and he has two sacks, two tackles for loss, three passes defensed, one pick and three forced fumbles, so he's doing literally everything for Dallas.
It hasn't all been perfect, though, as Downs' coverage numbers leave a lot to be desired with his 75% completion rate allowed and 107.3 passer rating surrendered when targeted.
Even still, Downs has been the bright spot in what has been a disappointing draft class thus far.

title: Dallas Cowboys Elevate Familiar RB Reinforcement Amid Tyler Goodson Injury
full_text:
As the Dallas Cowboys gear up for a Week 10 showdown with the San Francisco 49ers , the team is being forced to play some roster gymnastics to deal with a sudden lack of depth at running back.
The Cowboys watched backup running back Tyler Goodson firmly establish himself as RB2 behind Javonte Williams during his breakout game in Week 9 against the Indianapolis Colts , but unfortunately, it came at a cost.
Goodson suffered sprains to his MCL and ACL in his left knee , which will sideline him for a few weeks. As a result, a familiar name will be elevated from the practice squad for Sunday evening's game at AT&T Stadium.
According to Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer , running back Israel Abanikanda will be elevated from the practice squad to serve as Williams' primary backup.
Abanikanda has been with the Cowboys since midway through the 2025 season, signing to the practice squad on November 30, 2025. After the season, he signed a reserve/future contract with the team.
Abanikanda was released by the Cowboys as part of the final roster cuts after the preseason, before re-signing to the team's practice squad just 24 hours later. Earlier this season, Abanikanda was signed to the active roster following an injury to Malik Davis, which landed him on injured reserve, before he was waived and re-signed to the practice squad.
Now, Abanikanda is back on the active roster for a second stint, and we'll have to see whether he sees some extended action as the Cowboys look to continue establishing the running game to open up the passing attack.
While Abanikanda has bounced between practice squads throughout his NFL career, he has appeared in just six games, carrying the ball 22 times for 70 yards during the 2023 season with the New York Jets.
Throughout his career, Abanikanda has had stints with the Jets, 49ers, and Green Bay Packers before joining the Cowboys.
We'll find out in a matter of days whether he sees an increased workload during his second stint on the team's active roster. Kickoff between the Cowboys and 49ers at AT&T Stadium on Sunday afternoon is set for 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX. It's a crucial game for the Cowboys, so get your popcorn ready.

title: Broncos Rookie Report Card at the Bye: The Hits, Misses, and Surprises
full_text:
The 7-2 Denver Broncos are on bye this week. And given how the NFL placed Denver's bye about as close to the season's halfway point as it gets, it's a perfect opportunity for evaluation.
We've already covered the Broncos' player grades at the bye , with nine weeks of data to factor in, and we've also scrutinized GM George Paton's top extension candidates . Today, it's time for a Broncos rookie report card at the bye, including a grade.
Until last week, Coleman was the only Broncos rookie with meaningful playing time. The Broncos made seven draft picks last spring, and four of them — including Coleman — made the 53-man roster.
Coleman has been active for five games this season, but he didn't touch the ball in his first-ever game, which was Week 1 against the Kansas City Chiefs. In Week 2, the rookie suffered an ankle injury on his first career touch, and though he exited the game for a spell, he returned to play a key role in scoring the go-ahead touchdown and grind out the clock against the Jacksonville Jaguars.
That ankle injury turned out to be more severe than it seemed, and the Broncos placed Coleman on injured reserve. After four weeks, though, the rookie was ready to go, so the Broncos activated him for their road game against the Arizona Cardinals.
Coleman carried the ball nine times for 54 yards in Arizona and caught two passes for 15 yards. That game set a new precedent in the Broncos' backfield, with the rookie outearning J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey in snaps and touches.
It's been that way ever since. Coleman is the Broncos' new RB1. He has totaled 191 yards and three touchdowns on 41 carries (4.1 avg), with 13 receptions for 128 yards. He's made a big impact in every game in which he's touched the ball.
Despite swirling rumors linking the Broncos to the running back trade market , the team stood pat at the deadline because of Coleman's emergence. With veterans J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey (when he returns from IR in Week 13) behind him, Coleman is poised to play a major role in the Broncos' offense down the stretch.
Coleman's four-week stint on IR is the only reason he doesn't get an A+ at the bye.
Despite being the Broncos' highest draft pick this year (Round 3), Onyedim was a healthy scratch for two months, until finally getting to dress last week against the Carolina Panthers. He played 10 snaps , finishing with a tackle and a forced fumble, and was the Broncos' highest-graded run defender of the day, per Pro Football Focus .
Given how badly the Broncos have struggled against the run this season, it makes you wonder why they waited so long to dress Onyedim. He was one of the 2026 draft class' top run-defending defensive tackles, and he proved exactly why in his first career game.
It May have taken an injury to Eyioma Uwazurike to spark some change at Broncos HQ, but here's to hoping the team has realized that Onyedim is perfectly capable of contributing. If this team stands a chance at making another deep playoff run, this defense has to get better against the run in a hurry, and Onyedim can help it do just that.
Onyedim would have a higher grade if he'd seen the field more. He gets a passing grade, for now, but I expect far more to come.
Casey made the 53-man roster, but is yet to dress for a game. He's viewed as the future at left guard, but with Ben Powers on the final year of his contract, the Broncos seem content to let him finish out the season.
However, head coach Sean Payton hinted that personnel changes up front could be coming over the bye, but it's unlikely to be Powers. Casey was impressive during the preseason, playing both guard spots, and if the Broncos decided to look his way, I'd be encouraged about his outlook.
Alas, I doubt it happens. Even if the Broncos made a change at left guard, Matt Peart would likely be the next guy into the fray. Unless they have to, Payton's Broncos don't love playing rookies, especially in the trenches, but Casey has a bright future beyond 2026.
Like Casey, Bentley has been a healthy scratch all year long. He was the fourth and final tight end to make the roster, and so far, he's remained in developmental mode as the Broncos play veterans Evan Engram, Adam Trautman, and Nate Adkins.
Bentley is much closer to seeing the field than Casey, though. All it would take is one injury ahead of him on the depth chart, and the Broncos would have to dress Bentley.
Time will tell, but the Broncos like their seventh-round tight end out of Utah a lot. He didn't do much during the preseason besides block, but he earned a spot on the roster, beating out fifth-round tight end Justin Joly, who was waived and claimed by the Miami Dolphins.
Katsis didn't make the 53-man roster out of camp, but he was retained on the practice squad. In Week 3, with Marvin Mims Jr. injured, the Broncos elevated Katsis for a key home tilt vs. the Los Angeles Rams.
The undrafted rookie had quite the NFL debut, returning three punts for 39 yards and four kickoffs for 107 yards. Katsis's 146 total return yards were the most by a returner making his debut in franchise history.
If that's not a positive harbinger for what the future could hold for Katsis, I don't know what is. That being said, the Broncos haven't elevated him since then, as Mims has managed to stay healthy, though the veteran returner is having a career-low year.
There's a reason why the Broncos loved Katsis after the draft, making him a priority free-agent signing. His presence could explain, in part, why the Broncos have yet to extend Mims.
Like Onyedim, Katsis only has one game under his belt, but he set franchise records, so he's at a C+. Still too small of a sample size to justify a higher grade.
Undrafted out of Cal, Austin competed in camp and the preseason and earned a spot on the practice squad. He was elevated for Week 5's road game against the Los Angeles Chargers, and while he didn't see the field on defense or special teams, the Broncos like him a lot.
Austin is very physical for his size and has a nose for the ball. The Broncos have prioritize the first-year Sean Fresch Jr. of late, when it comes to practice-squad elevations, mainly due to his returner versatility.
At this point, Austin is angling for a futures contract after this season, which would buy him another opportunity to compete in training camp next year in hopes of making the 53-man roster.
Austin was elevated for a game, but he did not see the field, so he remains ungradable.

title: Why Re-Signing Sean Fresch Jr. Is an Important Move for Broncos
full_text:
Sean Fresch Jr. is back with the Denver Broncos.
When the Broncos thought they were acquiring Los Angeles Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley via trade, they waived Fresch to make room on the 53-man roster. Then Henley failed his physical, and the trade fell through , which leaves a roster spot currently open.
Meanwhile, Fresch passed through waivers unclaimed, so the Broncos quickly re-signed him to the practice squad, where he's spent all but one game this season competing. He's appeared in four games this season — making his NFL debut in Week 5 against the Chargers — and was actually promoted to the Broncos' 53-man roster ahead of Week 9's game against the Carolina Panthers.
Out of the gate, the 5-foot-9, 181-pound defensive back returned the opening kickoff in Carolina 41 yards to set Bo Nix and the Broncos' offense up with great field position. Fresch would finish the day with 62 return yards on two attempts, averaging 31 yards each.
Counting the three previous games Fresch appeared in as a practice-squad elevation, he's totaled six kick returns for 153 yards (25.5 avg). He has also made three solo tackles on special teams, covering punts and kicks.
Fresh originally went undrafted out of Rice last year. No team offered him a contract as a priority free agent after the draft, but the Kansas City Chiefs invited him to try out at their rookie minicamp. Alas, he didn't receive an offer.
So, Fresch bided his time and eventually took his talents to the UFL, signing with the San Antonio Brahmas. When the Brahmas went under, he entered the UFL draft, where the St. Louis Battlehawks selected him in January 2026.
Fresch went on to lead the league in punt return yardage, earning All-UFL honors. The Battlehawks made it to the playoffs, but lost in the semi-finals to the Louisville Kings.
That game was on June 7. The Broncos signed Fresch on June 15 , along with his Battlehawks teammate Hakeem Butler. Both former UFL stars shined early in OTAs and minicamp, but when training camp arrived, Fresch continued to ascend while Butler fell off and was eventually waived.
The Broncos knew they were getting a playmaking returner in Fresch, but they may have slept a little bit on what he brought to the table as a defensive back. He looked good in the preseason, and when the final roster cuts came, he may not have made the 53, but the Broncos quickly re-signed him to the practice squad.
Fresch's 25th birthday was on Wednesday — the same day the Broncos waived him to make room for Henley — but I'm sure the discussion centered around the team's intention to keep him in the fold if he cleared waivers. And that's exactly what happened.
With Marvin Mims Jr. and Ja'Quan McMillian being in a contract year , the Broncos have some post-2026 options in case they're unable to re-sign either. Fresch could check both boxes, in terms of his upside, especially as a returner.
As a defensive back, Fresch still has much to prove, but now that he's back on the practice squad, the Broncos are going to give him the opportunity to do just that. It wouldn't be a surprise if they promoted him again to the 53-man roster before Week 11's home game against the Las Vegas Raiders.
Even if they don't promote him, Fresch's three practice-squad elevations have reset, so the Broncos can use him on game day for the foreseeable future.

title: Film Room: Why Broncos Coveted Daiyan Henley—and Could Pursue Him Again
full_text:
In a surprising twist, the Denver Broncos are not acquiring linebacker Daiyan Henley from the Los Angeles Chargers, after all. The trade was nullified due to Henley failing the Broncos' physical on Wednesday night.
Denver had originally sent a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick to their division rivals in exchange for their outstanding coverage linebacker, but a knee issue got in the way of the deal being finalized. Denver tried to renegotiate with the Chargers after Henley's visit and physical, but they couldn't agree on terms in the long run.
Henley would have been the best coverage linebacker the Broncos have had in at least the last five seasons, and he would have fit a major need for this defense. His ability to match and mirror against tight ends and running backs in the passing game is fantastic, and he has the range and length to be a high-quality tackler at the second level.
I dove through the first five games of the season to see exactly what the Broncos were targeting. While Henley may not be Fred Warner over the middle of the field, Denver could have gotten a high-quality player that they could extend as a building-block piece for the future.
Let’s get into the tape, because Henley is in a contract year, so if the Chargers don't find a way to re-sign him, the Broncos could very well circle back in 2027 free agency.
Henley has 77th% arm length at 33". This is great use of that length in the run game. His size as a tackler could be an issue, though pic.twitter.com/PtTdt0CO8x
Henley (jersey No. 0) isn’t just a great coverage linebacker. He is an exceptional tackler because he has incredibly long arms and uses sound technique. Those long arms also do a great job to keep blockers at bay and allow him to make plays in the running game.
He uses his length really well to shed blockers at the point of attack, and has enough speed to shoot gaps and chase down ball carriers with relative ease. His technique to wrap up and drag players to the ground is very good, and he doesn’t miss a lot of tackles when he gets home.
When Henley uses his length to shed blocks, its really fun to watch. Good upper body strength on this rep, too. pic.twitter.com/RBVIreP6U8
There are several examples of Henley using his length to his advantage, but he also shows great lateral agility and athleticism to keep himself clean at the second level. His speed and sideline-to-sideline range flash all over his tape, and he can bring some power when he gets a head of steam.
Check out this rep against Denver. He identifies Jaylen Waddle on a reverse, then sprints to the sideline and obliterates Nate Adkins before making the tackle. That’s an incredible play to catch up to Waddle, who is one of the most explosive players in the league.
Henley's range and athleticism is awesome on this rep. That's Jaylen Waddle who he chases down. Not to mention blowing up Nate Adkins before he makes the tackle. pic.twitter.com/FhV3dRZfGW
Speaking of speed and athleticism, Henley is fast enough to cover any running back out of the backfield or tight end over the middle of the field. He is a fluid mover in space, understands route combinations and leverage, and has great feel for zone coverage.
Watch this man coverage rep against the Broncos. Denver likes to use running back RJ Harvey on wheel routes because he is incredibly explosive in space.
Henley presses down, then mirrors Harvey along the sideline, going stride-for-stride in phase. This is a high-quality rep against an upstart receiving back.
This is a fantastic coverage rep for Henley. Harvey runs the wheel, and Henley is step for step going up the sideline. pic.twitter.com/k0BxkZK3ek
Even though Henley has gotten beat more often than he has in the past, his ability to diagnose and react is still very good, and he knows when to pass receivers off to the next zone and stay within his assignment. He had a couple of bad reps against the Buffalo Bills, but those were mostly miscommunication issues between him and his teammates.
When communication is clear, Henley’s zone coverage is among the best in the league. He does a great job of getting depth and flattening to the route, staying underneath the receiver, and keeping his eyes on the quarterback to try to make plays on the ball.
Like this rep against the Arizona Cardinals, who tested him against Trey McBride working vertically up the sideline. Henley’s positioning is textbook on this rep, as he passes McBride off to the next zone but keeps climbing the sideline.
Solid zone coverage rep against Trey McBride. Stays under the route and in phase before passing off and getting depth on the boundary. pic.twitter.com/2N8WRVZQp8
Despite having great length, Henley is undersized for the position (6-foot-0, 225 pounds), and it really shows as a run defender when he has to take on blockers at the point of attack. He doesn’t have the mass or the power to stack and shed blockers, and he tends to get washed out of the play when blockers get attached.
Listed at 225, Henley's size can be an issue if blockers get attached. This isn't as bad as it looks, but you can see him getting pushed around. pic.twitter.com/WWcfRhtpLP
Even though he mitigates this issue with his athleticism, there are too many examples of Henley getting bullied in the running game. It was an issue with him at Washington State, and it hasn’t gotten better as his career has gone on.
Going back to the Denver game, watch left guard Ben Powers blast Henley off the ball and drive him downfield. Henley’s length can’t and won’t save him every play.
This is a Ben Powers tweet. Henley gets bullied. pic.twitter.com/IYT8AmvWr7
Those size concerns also translate to his lackluster blitzing ability. The Chargers didn’t ask him to blitz a lot, but when he did, the results weren’t pretty. For some reason, the Chargers would also ask him to come off the edge as a pass rusher on occasion, and those results were even worse.
This is the best blitz rep I've seen from Henley so far, and im through 3 and a half games. it's not a strong suit of his game. pic.twitter.com/oW4LFotvvf
There’s a lot to like about Henley’s game, and he would have been a fantastic addition to an already loaded Broncos defense. I have 25 additional Henley clips on my X feed to check out, with multiple examples of what we discussed here.
Henley is certainly a starting-caliber player in this league, but with Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad playing quality football in their own right, the Broncos wouldn't have needed Henley to play every down . The Broncos might have been able to hide Henley's deficiencies in the run game and focus on his coverage versatility as a dime linebacker.
Again, though, Henley is in the last year of his rookie contract, so it wouldn’t surprise me to see the Broncos make a run at him as a free agent next offseason. And that's why we moved forward with publishing this film breakdown.

title: George Paton Running Out of Time to Extend 4 Broncos During the Bye
full_text:
The Denver Broncos hit their Week 10 bye at 7-2 , leading the AFC West.
The chaos of the NFL trade deadline and the botched Daiyan Henley deal with the Los Angeles Chargers have distracted from the scrutiny of a very important Broncos storyline.
Will Denver extend any players during this year's bye?
Remember, Broncos GM George Paton was a busy boy over last year's bye, extending center Luke Wattenberg , defensive lineman Malcolm Roach , and kicker Wil Lutz . The season prior, Paton locked up left tackle Garett Bolles with a four-year deal during Denver's Week 14 bye.
The precedent is set, and the 2026 Broncos have more than one player in a contract year who's worthy of a new extension. There are still a few days left for Paton to get something done before the team's attention turns fully to the Las Vegas Raiders, so let's examine where things might stand.
The Broncos' nickel cornerback is playing on his one-year restricted free-agent tender , earning $5.8 million. He's set to be an unrestricted free agent after this season.
McMillian has appeared in all nine games thus far, with three starts, totaling 31 tackles (21 solo), four tackles for a loss, three sacks, seven pass breakups, and an interception. That interception helped Denver defeat the Seattle Seahawks in overtime back in Week 6.
At 26, McMillian is still young, and the Broncos can rely on his prime playing window remaining open for at least another three or four years. I'm not sure what more he has to do to earn an extension, but if the Broncos believe that Jahdae Barron would be able to fill the nickel role next year seamlessly, they've got another thing coming.
McMillian remains the Broncos' top extension candidate at the bye.
Moss, a 2023 third-round pick, has had some bad injury luck in his contract year. He dealt with a rib injury that set him back early this season, and suffered a concussion in the Broncos' Week 9 win over the Carolina Panthers.
But when Moss has been on the field, he's been excellent. He's only missed one start, totaling 27 tackles (17 solo), eight pass breakups, and one interception.
Moss has also done a much better job of avoiding penalties this season, though he hasn't been perfect. Through half the season, he's only further reinforced that he's one of the best No. 2 cornerbacks in the NFL, and worthy of a second contract.
If the Broncos don't extend Moss, some other team will pay him north of $20 million per year next spring, and that's the rub. The Broncos are already paying Patrick Surtain II big money, with significant cap dollars also tied up in safety Talanoa Hufanga, and they have to start planning for Bo Nix's extension, which could come as early as next offseason.
Jones was signed in 2024 to replace Justin Simmons, and he turned in a great year. Jones wasn't as good in 2025, but he has rebounded back to his 2024 form this season.
Jones is dealing with a hamstring injury that cost him a start last week, but otherwise, he's been a very reliable player for the Broncos. He has 55 tackles (34 solo), five pass break-ups, a fumble recovery, and two interceptions.
Jones has been a great complement to Hufanga; they make one heck of a safety duo. It's unfortunate that Hufanga has missed the last four games with an ankle injury, but Jones did some heavy lifting while his starting partner has been out.
At 28, Jones is still in his prime window, so if the Broncos were to re-sign him to a two-year extension, it would keep him around through 2028, and give the team an opportunity to reevaluate right after he turns 30. The Broncos don't have a viable replacement option to anticipate in 2027, so it would make a lot of sense to approach Jones now in hopes of getting him re-signed to a deal that is somewhat team-friendly.
Mims has been disappointing in his contract year. There's no getting around it. He's had some bad injury luck, but when he's been on the field, the production hasn't been there.
As a receiver, Mims's effort is lacking, and he's simply not making plays when given the opportunity. Thus far, he has just 10 catches on 16 targets for 92 yards, with five carries for 30 yards.
Mims hasn't been as dynamic as a returner, either. As a punt returner, he's had a few good returns, but   he's averaging a career-low 10.8 yards per return thus far.
If the Broncos are looking for red flags, there are plenty to be found. Mims hasn't been the same since he changed agents in the offseason, and it's definitely come out in the wash.
The Broncos could still look at re-signing Mims in the offseason, but I'd be stunned if an in-season extension came his way. He simply hasn't earned it this year.
Given their age and relative impact this season, I don't think either Powers or Engram is on Paton's mind at the bye. Powers has been solid at left guard, but not spectacular, and the Broncos have already made plans for his departure after this season, drafting Kage Casey in the fourth round.
Engram has struggled to pick up the new blocking responsibilities the Broncos gave him this year, and has just 17 catches on 30 targets for 169 yards and a touchdown. The Broncos don't really have a post-2026 replacement for Evans in the fold, but it's a question the team will likely look to answer in the offseason.

title: Broncos Bye-Week Report Card: Grading Every Player Through 9 Games
full_text:
With the Denver Broncos on a bye week , we can examine how each player has performed through nine weeks of the season.
After each game, I analyze each player on a snap-by-snap basis to hand out individual grades, but the minimum snap requirement to qualify for a grade is 20 per game.
The Broncos' bye week this year came as close as it gets to the midway point of the season (with 17 games), offering an ideal opportunity to reflect on each player's grade so far. Among the players with at least 250 snaps who have appeared in the last three games, let's examine how each individual has graded out — from highest to lowest — starting with the offense.
Bolles is coming off his worst game of the season against the Carolina Panthers, where he had 13 bad blocks, his first game with more than eight bad blocks this season. He's been a stalwart at left tackle despite the Broncos' collective offensive line issues and has had multiple games without allowing any pressure on the quarterback.
Over the past few games, the Broncos have made a slight tweak to what they're doing up front, and it has negatively impacted Meinerz’s play, but not in a disastrous way. He has had a slight drop-off over the last few weeks, but he has still been one of the best guards in the NFL.
Meinerz had nine bad blocks and four whiffed blocks against the Panthers. Up to that point, he hadn't had more than five bad blocks and two whiffs in a game this season.
While Waddle hasn’t had the biggest impact on the stat sheet, with only 337 yards on 30 receptions so far this season, his impact goes beyond the numbers. He has forced teams to cover differently, opening the door to big opportunities, even when the offense has passed on some.
Sutton has also not had the impact on the stat sheet that many were expecting, and has had some hiccups as a blocker as well. The last three games have seen him improve each week — with three of his five highest-graded individual games this season.
Powers gets a lot more hate and vitriol t han he deserves , but he's been one of the Broncos' two highest-graded offensive linemen in the last two games. His last three games have been his best this season.
McGlinchey's grade is strange because he has been among the lowest-graded players in an individual game four times this season and has as many games graded below the 50 average mark as he does above 60. However, his two best games keep his grade out of the low 40s.
It's been a roller coaster ride for Engram this season. He has stepped up in some big moments, but has struggled to make a consistent impact. His grade is okay, but the Broncos brought him in, hoping for far more than he's given them.
Some early-season showings drag down Nix’s grade, but his last three games have improved steadily. This has been a trend for Nix since arriving in the NFL, and there's every reason to expect he will continue to ascend after the bye.
Wattenberg is another who had some disastrous games earlier in the season, but he seems to have found solid footing. There are still major issues in the run game, but he has put together four straight games where his lowest individual game grade was 63.2.
If we could separate Franklin the blocker from Franklin the receiver, he would probably have the highest and lowest grades on the offense. His play as a blocker has been exceptional this season, and probably the best on the team, but his route running and effort as a receiver have been questionable.
Trautman has struggled to be the ‘great blocker’ that he was hyped up to be when the Broncos re-signed him, though we all knew better. He has some bright moments as a blocker, but they are too few and far between, and his role as a receiver is a glorified 'security blanket,' and that's putting it as positively as possible.
Remember, each player needs to have played in the last three games, plus have at least 250 snaps to qualify for a mid-season grade. That means Jonah Elliss and Talanoa Hufanga don’t qualify even though both have over 250 snaps; neither has played in the last three games.
With that said, let's get into the player grades on defense.
Not only has Allen been the Broncos' best defender, but he's also been one of the best in the NFL. Out of 51 qualifying defensive linemen, he leads the NFL in total pressures and win percentage, ranks third in pass-rush productivity, and ranks sixth in batted passes.
Allen has been exceptional this season, and with his conditioning, there is no reason to expect a drop-off.
Bonitto ranks second on the team in pressures with 30 and has done well as a run defender for most of the season. He's had a few bad moments as a run defender and has been caught badly in coverage, but his impact as a pass rusher is elite, even with a slower start to the season than was ideal.
Teams know how to attack Surtain, and they've done so with some success. But outside of three such routes, he's nearly impossible to attack through the air. His play as a run defender has also been the best I have seen in his NFL career.
Roach has had some big games this season and has found his footing to be a consistent threat and impact player on the defensive line. Not only is he tied for the third-most pressures on the team (behind Allen and Bonitto), but he also leads the team in batted passes.
Moss has some issues, and he gets targeted a lot due to playing opposite Surtain, but he has consistently played well. In eight games played this season, Moss has graded 60-plus in six and 70-plus in three.
Strnad has been the Broncos' coverage linebacker, and he has done quite well. His tackling, however, has been an issue, with 11 missed tackles and the second-highest missed-tackle rate among linebackers in the NFL. There's a reason the Broncos wanted Daiyan Henley , though the trade fell through.
Jones was a questionable presence in 2025, but he's closer to the 2024 version of himself this season. He's playing for a second contract, and the Broncos may reach out about an extension. Jones has four games where he graded in the 70s, and a fifth where he was at 69.3 (out of the eight games), though he was inactive in Week 9.
Jonathon Cooper doesn’t qualify for a grade, but with his legal issues and contract situation, the Broncos could part ways with him in the offseason. Robinson has excelled as a pass rusher with his explosiveness off the line and has mostly done well as a run defender, though the Panthers got some big wins against him.
McMillian is a nickel defender with size limitations, and teams have found ways to attack him, but he also plays bigger than he is and is very aggressive. The nickel corner has been vital to the Broncos' ability to generate takeaways this season and has shown his ability as a blitzer when called upon.
Singleton is a tackling machine, but also a missed tackle waiting to happen. He has the most tackles in the NFL and the sixth-highest missed-tackle rate, while leading NFL linebackers in raw missed tackles, with 40 more snaps this season than the next-highest linebacker. Teams have also found ways to target and isolate Singleton in coverage, which has always been his weak spot.
Jones is a solid player, and he has posted a slightly above-average grade through nine games. He does some things well and consistently, and there are areas he struggles with, like double teams.
The Barron experiment is likely to end soon. In his first start, he played relatively well, but outside of that, he's been a disaster on the field.
Barron plays stiff as a board, and his football awareness is lacking. The only good thing about his play has been his reliability as a tackler in space, as shown when he gets beaten in coverage and allows a catch.
The Broncos showed a lot of faith in Uwazurike, but he has largely been a letdown this year. There have been some excellent moments, but we're talking about two or three plays per game while he is playing an average of 38 snaps per game.

title: Broncos Fire Back at Chargers' Accusations Over Failed Daiyan Henley Trade
full_text:
The Daiyan Henley trade is off.
Late Wednesday night, the Denver Broncos made the announcement , shocking fans and media alike. The Los Angeles Chargers posted a welcome-back meme for Henley around the same time, confirming there was no trade.
We learned on Thursday that it was officially due to a failed physical. Adam Schefter reported that the Broncos had concerns about Henley's knee after his physical, but they still wanted him — just not at the price of the previously agreed-upon 2027 fourth-round pick and 2028 fifth-round pick, given what they discovered during the physical.
Pro Football Talk 's Mike Florio reported that Henley's physical in Denver revealed some arthritis in one knee. That didn't match up with the picture of health that L.A. reportedly presented of Henley to the Broncos.
But Denver was still interested in keeping Henley. According to 9NEWS ' Mike Klis , the Broncos went back to the Chargers to negotiate a different price. L.A. didn't budge, so the trade was canceled.
Chargers GM Joe Hortiz claims that he was transparent about Henley's health status and that the Broncos were aware of the veteran linebacker's situation before agreeing to terms on the trade. Every team evaluates injuries differently, which is why these transactions come with the caveat of "pending a physical."
According to ESPN 's Lindsey Thiry , Hortiz wouldn't confirm Schefter's report that it was Henley's knee that failed to pass Denver's physical, let alone Florio's report of finding arthritis, but the Chargers GM claims he shared any health concerns with the Broncos before they agreed to the trade.
"We came to terms on it, made the agreement, they called us up and were asking us to amend the trade based on the physical," Hortiz told Thiry. "And in our minds, the physical's a binary thing. It's pass or fail. And they wanted the player still. They wanted to change the terms. They used it, and we weren't going to do it."
Henley has dealt with a knee and shoulder injury this season, though he's played through both. Hortiz was adamant that the Broncos were aware of Henley's health status.
"Yep, absolutely," Hortiz told Thiry when asked whether he was transparent with Denver about Henley's health. "'Hey, he's dealing with this, but he's expected to practice and play for us this week.' And I think that was their plan. They certainly wanted him still."
As for Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh, he expressed his frustration with how the botched trade unraveled and why he believes the NFL should close the "loophole" that allows a buying team the prerogative to ask for different compensation after the deadline passes.
"The Broncos based a pass-fail on a medical grade on whether we would take less compensation, and we wouldn't, and we didn't," Harbaugh said. "In my opinion, it's one of those loopholes the league should really look into because it sets a bad precedent, [and it] continues to set a bad precedent."
According to Klis, when Henley's knee turned out to be a bit more concerning than the Broncos had been led to believe, the Chargers "brushed off concerns." The Broncos reached out to the NFL, and the league confirmed that, given the failed physical, Denver could approach the Chargers about changing the compensation if they still wanted Henley.
"Per league source, it was only after Henley flunked his physical — in which several medical opinions were sought — [the] Broncos got [the] NFL involved and received confirmation it was OK to revisit the compensation, as there is precedent for these situations," Klis reported on X.
Harbaugh and the Chargers are trying to present this as Denver basing the pass-fail of Henley's physical on whether L.A. would renegotiate the compensation, but the Broncos are pushing back on that through Klis, even going so far as to reveal that they reached out to the NFL about it, after the linebacker's physical produced results that didn't match what they'd been told when they agreed to send a fourth- and fifth-round pick for him.
The Broncos claim they had a "long-term view of the player," per Klis, which is why they were still willing to make a trade with the Chargers even after Henley failed the physical. The Chargers wouldn't accept any new terms, so that was that.
"Regardless of compensation, it was well within Broncos rights to simply flunk him on physical and move on. Instead GM George Paton tried to find a solution for a difficult situation. Again, within the Broncos rights and the NFL aware every step," Klis reported on X.
Now, some people around the NFL are using the botched Henley trade as a referendum on the "loophole" within league rules that allows for teams to change the terms of a deal, pending the physical, even after the trade deadline has passed. For the seller, the argument is that it puts them at a disadvantage because, with the deadline passed, it's not like they can go back to other interested suitors.
For the buyer, as the Broncos were in this scenario, the loophole offers protections and flexibility in the event that a physical uncovers conditions that may not have been disclosed when the trade was agreed upon in principle. That allows the buyer to seek value commensurate with what their physical evaluation found, in the event that it doesn't line up with how the seller presented the player's bill of health.
Some people believe that the rules should be based 100% on the physical: if the player passes, the trade goes through at the agreed-upon price. Period. End of story. If the player fails his physical, then the buyer has only one recourse: cancel the trade.
There are two sides to every story. We've reported both sides, leaving it up to you to decide what really happend.
Did the Chargers try to pull a fast one on the Broncos and sneak an injury past a division rival? Or did the Broncos try to leverage a failed physical in bad faith to strong-arm a better deal for Henley after the deadline had passed?
A third possibility is that the Chargers were transparent with the state of Henley's health, but that the Broncos' medical standards were different, or they could have even discovered more in the physical than the Chargers were aware of.
Teams can view the severity of a player's injury differently. That's why some teams will spend money on a given player in free agency who may have a checkered injury jacket while other teams won't even consider signing them.
Add into the botched Henley trade the rariety of it being between two division rivals, and perhaps we shouldn't be all that surprised that it fell through in spectacular fashion, with both sides pointing the finger.

title: Broncos at the Bye: 5 Warning Signs That Could Derail the Playoff Push
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are halfway through their bye.
Sitting at 7-2, the Broncos have to feel great about navigating their initial gauntlet of a schedule as well as anyone could have predicted. That doesn't mean there aren't things to improve, though.
Coming out of the bye, the Broncos have only one plus-.500 opponent on the schedule until Week 16's Christmas Day bout with the Buffalo Bills. Already winners of five in a row, the Broncos have a great chance to extend their winning streak, and really go on a run.
All of Denver's 2026 goals are still on the table, including a second straight AFC West crown, the No. 1 playoff seed in the AFC, and a potential Super Bowl berth. But if the Broncos don't address these five warning signs at the bye, the season could potentially swerve off the rails.
Let's break down what Sean Payton must fix before hosting the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 11.
The Broncos' offense has been one of the worst this season, but it has steadily improved since Payton took back the play-calling duties in Week 5. The one lingering problem, though, remains the run game.
Jonah Coleman's return from injured reserve three weeks ago was a godsend, but the rookie alone hasn't been enough to elevate the Broncos' ground game out of the doldrums. Fans hoped that a running back trade ahead of Tuesday's deadline could change things, but the Broncos made no such move.
The reason Denver stood pat and didn't trade for a running back? The coaches know that it's not a running back issue; it's a blocking issue , as Payton himself pointed to on Wednesday in an appearance on The Herd with Colin Cowherd.
Payton also hinted that personnel changes could be coming up front, so that's something we'll be watching for over the next few days. But Payton and run game coordinator Zach Strief have to look at everything, including personnel and blocking concepts, to figure out how to spark this ground attack.
Coleman can do a lot of heavy lifting, as he's already proven over the past three weeks. But he can't do it alone. The Broncos have to get to the bottom of why their offensive line and tight ends are performing so poorly as run blockers.
The Broncos currently field the 27th-ranked rushing offense, averaging 91.4 yards per game. Coleman has elevated that average by about 10 yards per game, but it's not enough.
At some point, veteran running back J.K. Dobbins has to start carrying his fair share of the water, too. The only thing the Broncos have going for them on the ground is Coleman and the continued excellence of All-Pro left tackle Garett Bolles and All-Pro right guard Quinn Meinerz.
Offensively, the Broncos ranked 31st in third-down efficiency, converting just 32.4% of their attempts. Defensively, it's far from ideal: Denver ranks 21st, allowing conversions on 41.2% of opponent attempts.
If you can't stay on the field as an offense, the points aren't going to come. If you can't get off the field on third down as a defense, you'll allow too much yardage and put yourself in unfavorable red-zone situations.
Offensively, the Broncos took a big step in the right direction in Week 9's road win over the Carolina Panthers, convering 60% of their third-down attempts. That was great to see, and it was due to the Broncos executing better on first and second down, which set up more favorable third-down situations.
The Broncos' defense also did much better on third down against the Panthers, allowing just 3-of-10 to be converted, so both units showed progress in this area before hitting the bye. Let's hope the coaches can get to the bottom of this issue and keep the Broncos' third-down efficiency improving down the stretch.
The Broncos' scoring has improved dramatically over the past three weeks, averaging 28 points per game. It has helped them climb out of the bottom three scoring teams, putting them at No. 20 this season, averaging 22 points per game.
As quarterback Bo Nix's confidence has flooded back and the Broncos have moved past the brutal defenses they had to face through the first eight weeks, which included Steve Spagnuolo and the Kansas City Chiefs twice, the Jacksonville Jaguars, the Los Angeles Rams, and the San Francisco 49ers, the offense has begun to climb out of its shell.
The Broncos definitely have offense moving in the right direction at the bye, but there's still plenty of work to be done to bolster this unit as a bona fide playoff-caliber force to be reckoned with. One week might not be enough time to solve all the problems, but just fixing the run game/blocking issues will have a major trickle-down effect on the Broncos' third-down efficiency and scoring.
The Broncos started off the season with one of the most historically bad tackling showings ever. It has improved, but it's still far from where it needs to be.
The 2026 Broncos' defense hasn't been on the same level as it's 2025 counterpart, and its tackling woes are one of the reasons why. It comes out in the wash against the run and pass, allowing teams to pick up free yardage by simply making the first guy miss.
The Broncos have missed a whopping 102 tackles this season, the most in the NFL. Their 13.7 missed-tackle percentage leads the league, too, according to SFData9ers on X .
It's not the mark of a playoff-worthy defense. The Broncos' one saving grace has been their situational defense. When the chips are down in end-of-game sequences, this defense has continued to answer the bell, and it's still rushing the passer among the best in the NFL.
But if the Broncos can't shore up their tackling issues, playoff opponents like the Bills, Chiefs, Bengals, and others will have a heyday.
The Broncos' defense has been inexplicably leaky this season. Granted, they've faced a who's-who list of some of the NFL's best quarterbacks, but even against Bryce Young last week , the Broncos allowed five explosive plays — three through the air and two on the ground.
We can chalk some of that up to the injuries Denver has dealt with in the secondary, with starting safety duo Talanoa Hufanga and Brandon Jones ruled out in Carolina, and cornerback Riley Moss suffering a concussion early on, but it's not the whole story.
Yardage-wise, the Broncos' defense has allowed 2,076 yards through nine games. Only three teams have been worse than Denver in this area; it's not a winning stat.
So how do the Broncos keep coming out on top in these games? Again, it comes down to Nix's fourth-quarter magic and the defense's clutch-time composure.
If defensive coordinator Vance Joseph can get to the bottom of the explosives, and that includes on the ground, where Denver is allowing 124.3 yards per game, the Broncos could become a juggernaut. As the schedule continues to open up for them, I have a feeling the Broncos' defense will show some major signs of improvement, but Joseph has to batten down the hatches on some of these fundamental flaws.
