title: Insider Provides Context to Botched Broncos Trade for Daiyan Henley
full_text:
The Denver Broncos stunned the NFL world late Wednesday night by announcing that their trade for inside linebacker Daiyan Henley has been called off . The team did not specify why it was backing out of the pact it made Tuesday with the Los Angeles Chargers.
Hours after the dust settled, ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter provided a bit of clarity, reporting that Denver had medical concerns over Henley — specifically, his knee — that Los Angeles didn't share.
The Broncos, after flagging the issue, attempted to negotiate a revised trade deal, presumably without the 2028 fifth-rounder included in the original agreement. The Chargers rebuffed, and the deal was dead.
"It is not uncommon for one team to have some medical concerns about a player while another does not. In this case, Denver had concerns about Henley following his physical," Schefter wrote on X. "Even then, the Broncos still wanted Henley with Denver and LA discussing revised trade alternatives throughout the day, taking into account those concerns. In the end, no agreement was reached. The deal was off."
Pro Football Talk's Mike Florio later noted that Denver discovered arthritis in Henley's knee, which explains why the club got cold feet at the eleventh hour.
“The Broncos discovered an issue with Henley’s knee,” Florio wrote Thursday . “It has, we’re told, arthritis.” He added that a source with neither the Chargers nor the Broncos told PFT that most, if not all, starting linebackers in the NFL have some degree of arthritis in their knees.
Henley has appeared in all eight games for the Chargers thus far this season, notching 51 total tackles (21 solo), two passes defensed, one interception, a forced fumble, and a half-sack. He was limited prior to Week 6 with a listed knee injury; he was designated as questionable but ended up playing.
Obviously, the Broncos prefer to have Henley on the roster today rather than the prospect of facing him again later this season. They made a purposeful acquisition in the hopes of improving the pass coverage within their linebacker corps — something Henley excels at .
It's a bummer in that sense, but the Broncos obviously felt that Henley's condition could have long-term ramifications and wasn't worth the capital they agreed to surrender for him. How that ends up shaking out will be determined.
Moving forward, however, is the status quo: Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad as the starting ILBs, with Karene Reid and Jordan Turner as the primary backups. The Broncos also have seventh-round rookie Red Murdock on the practice squad; Murdock may eventually see playing time now that Henley is no longer in the picture.
Denver also has an open spot on the 53-man roster after waiving defensive back Sean Fresch Jr. to initially make room for Henley.

title: Ben Powers Isn't Broncos' Biggest OL Problem, But He Could Pay the Price
full_text:
With the Denver Broncos on bye, head coach Sean Payton appeared on The Herd on Wednesday.
Among other things, Payton expressed his dissatisfaction with the Broncos' blocking up front and hinted at potential personnel changes during the bye.
Looking at the Broncos' offensive line this season, it obviously hasn't been good enough. The unit could do with a shakeup, given that the Broncos still rank in the bottom 10 in rushing.
Not everyone on the unit is playing poorly, as left tackle Garett Bolles and right guard Quinn Meinerz have been among the NFL's best at their respective positions. You'd hope that would be the case, though, given that they're both first-team All-Pros.
That leaves left guard Ben Powers, center Luke Wattenberg, and right tackle Mike McGlinchey as the options to consider benching over the bye. Of those three, none has drawn as much vitriol from fans and some Broncos media members as Powers has, but it's not deserved — not fully, at least.
This isn’t to say Powers has played particularly well, but he hasn’t been the biggest culprit behind the O-line's failure to launch. That would be McGlinchey, followed by Wattenberg, then Powers.
Before getting into the data, there's an argument that Powers makes the most sense to bench because of extenuating circumstances. Of the three, he's the only one in the final year of his contract .
Denver also has better options to replace Powers, making him easier to bench than McGlinchey or Wattenberg, especially factoring in their respective contracts.
Behind Powers is Kage Casey, whom the Broncos drafted this past April to be their starting left guard in 2027, and they seemed pleased with his development in practice this past summer. The Broncos could decide to make the switch, see if Casey can handle it, and get answers for next year, though that could be tough to balance with their Super Bowl aspirations if it doesn't go swimmingly.
The Broncos also have Alex Palczewski, their sixth offensive lineman, who stepped in for an injured Powers at left guard for much of last season. While fans seemed to love Palczewski, he was vastly overrated and finished the season among the bottom 10 worst guards in nearly every offensive-line metric.
Also, Palczewski has performed better on the right side than on the left. Keep in mind that he currently fills the sixth O-line spot, which means that moving him into the starting lineup at left guard would mean replacing two players in the team's top six.
If it wasn’t for McGlinchey’s contract, or if Denver wasn’t afraid to bench him and could break free of the sunk-cost fallacy, Palczewski at right tackle would make sense. It would be better than Matt Peart or Frank Crum at right tackle (if Crum comes off injured reserve). Denver could consider benching McGlinchey and putting Casey at right tackle, too, though it would be extremely unlikely.
However, regardless of who replaced him, the first obstacle to benching McGlinchey would be overcoming the sunk-cost fallacy, believing that because he has one of the highest cap hits on the team, he should be on the field. His play has not been anywhere close to commensurate with his contract.
As for Wattenberg, the Broncos just gave him a four-year, $48 million extension a year ago, and are likely stuck with him through the 2027 season. The team could view Alex Forsyth — who's in the last year of his deal — as an upgrade in run blocking, but his pass protection has been a massive downgrade whenever he's been called upon.
After going over the tape again, Powers gets a lot more hate than he deserves. Is he great? No. He's an average player playing at an average level, while Wattenberg and McGlinchey are playing among the worst at their positions in the NFL.
This season, Powers has allowed a 2.7% blown-block rate with 14 blown blocks, while McGlinchey is at 18 blown blocks and a 3.5% blown-block rate, and Wattenberg is at eight blown blocks and a 1.6% blown-block rate, though Wattenberg has faced nearly 1/8th of the one-on-one blocks that Powers and McGlinchey have.
Digging deeper into run-game-specific metrics, since the Broncos' lack of a ground attack has become such an issue, Powers has just four blown blocks, as does McGlinchey, while Wattenberg has five. That means 10 of Powers's blown blocks have been in the passing game, compared to 14 from McGlinchey and three from Wattenberg. Remember, again, though, Wattenberg is rarely asked to block one-on-one, which is important context.
In other run-game metrics, like yards before contact, with each player as the lead blocker, and forced bounces allowed (where the lineman doesn't clear the lane and the back is forced to bounce to another hole), Powers ranks among the top 20 guards in the NFL in each category.
At the same time, Wattenberg ranks in the bottom six, with McGlinchey in the bottom eight in both categories. Again, Powers hasn’t been great, but he's not the worst player on the O-line. Sorry, Broncos fans.
There is even an adjustment for the quality of defensive linemen faced, and the Broncos have gone against some serious talent this season. With those adjustments, Powers ranks higher than he does without them, while McGlinchey is the same, and Wattenberg is actually worse.
While I haven't gotten into it much, Powers is also dealing with a Lisfranc injury he suffered against the Jacksonville Jaguars last season, which required offseason surgery. For offensive linemen, returning to normal play after an injury takes about 11 months, and Powers had surgery in February or March, but he doesn't get the same benefit of the doubt that other Broncos do.
So, one last time, I ask: does Powers deserve to be benched?
The answer is no, but Powers is the most likely option to bench because of the Broncos' lack of reliable depth at the other positions and because sitting him down wouldn't force the team to confront the sunk-cost fallacy, as it would with Wattenberg or McGlinchey.
There are risks to benching Powers, as chemistry and communication are vital on the offensive line, but the Broncos' starting five hasn't been good enough, so we could see changes, whether they're fair and just to the individual or not.
After this season, the Broncos should strongly consider finding three new starters and significantly upgrading their O-line depth.

title: Broncos' Daiyan Henley Trade With Chargers Falls Through in Stunning Reversal
full_text:
The Daiyan Henley trade has been called off.
The Denver Broncos made the announcement late Wednesday night, saying the Henley deal with the Los Angeles Chargers had fallen through. It was due to a failed physical.
"The proposed trade involving Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley will not be finalized. We have great respect for Daiyan as a player and person, and we wish him all the best moving forward," the statement read.
pic.twitter.com/vFJ7MYS2UN
The Chargers responded by posting a "Welcome back, Daiyan" meme on their X account.
https://t.co/Ewbs7j6Yga pic.twitter.com/QzaZ40ZFF7
The deal for Henley, agreed to in principle ahead of Tuesday's NFL trade deadline , would have sent the Broncos' 2027 fourth-round pick and 2028 fifth-round pick to the Chargers in exchange. The Broncos will obviously be holding onto those picks.
Henley is about to turn 27 and is in the fourth and final year of his rookie contract. He's a two-time team captain in L.A. and is poised to lead the Chargers in tackles for the third straight season.
Broncos fans were excited about the prospect of Henley working into the linebacker rotation with Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad, especially given his coverage chops. Alas, unless the Broncos seek to sign him as a free agent in the spring, we'll never know how Henley would have fit in.
The Broncos are on bye, with their next game not until November 21, when they'll host the Las Vegas Raiders at Mile High. The Raiders have a new starting quarterback — Fernando Mendoza — and a pair of tight ends who've combined for over 1,000 receiving yards and seven touchdowns already this season.
Let's hope the Broncos have a better answer for Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer than they have the tight ends they faced in their last three games, to whom they allowed 330 yards and three touchdowns.
Apparently, the Broncos weren't as copacetic with Henley's knee issue as the Chargers were, and sought different compensation. In the end, the Broncos and Chargers couldn't come to an agreement and the trade was off.
That's what we know. It's a shocker, but the Broncos weren't comfortable giving up a fourth- and a fifth-rounder for a linebacker they like, but whose knee may have been suspect.

title: Lions Elevate Linebacker For Patriots Game
full_text:
The Detroit Lions have elevated one player from the practice squad for their matchup with the New England Patriots on Sunday.
Detroit has elected to elevate veteran linebacker Owen Pappoe for the matchup, which will mark Pappoe's debut with the Lions. The Auburn product was signed to the practice squad last week in the wake of injuries to linebackers Jack Campbell and Jimmy Rolder.
Along with Pappoe, the Lions also added veteran K.J. Britt off the New England Patriots' practice squad. Because the Lions poached Britt, he is on the team's active roster. It's the first time Detroit has utilized Pappoe as an elevation.
Pappoe has appeared in one game this season as a member of the Tennessee Titans, that being their Week 2 game against the Philadelphia Eagles. He was on the Titans' practice squad to start the season, but was waived in October and remained a free agent until the Lions added him on Nov. 4.
The veteran is in his fourth NFL season, having played the first three with the Arizona Cardinals. In his career, he has appeared in 50 games with two starts and notched 66 combined tackles, a forced fumble and two passes defensed.
The Lions' linebacking corps was dealt a devastating blow by the injuries to Campbell and Rolder, both of whom landed on injured reserve. In the case of Campbell, it was a scary scene as he was carted off the field on a backboard and transported to a local hospital where he has remained while being evaluated for his injuries.
Lions linebackers coach Shaun Dion Hamilton explained the importance of Campbell to Deroit's defense and the impact he had as the on-field defensive play-caller working with defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard.
"He's the coach on the field. He's a branch of Shep," Hamilton said, via Audacy . The biggest thing wearing the green dot is poise and confidence. Poise in the midst of chaotic situations, and no matter what, if it’s the wrong call, right call, confidence with everyone to make it."
Detroit arrived in Germany on Friday and have been enjoying some of the festivities. On Saturday, team owner Sheila Hamp entertained Lions fans at a pub in Munich to celebrate the team's presence in the international community.

title: Detroit Lions Owner Sheila Hamp Taps Keg in Germany
full_text:
Detroit Lions owner Sheila Hamp is also joining in on the festivities in Germany, one day ahead of the teams Week 10 matchup with the New England Patriots.
A video has surfaced of Hamp tapping a keg, with the assistance of staff at Hofbräuhaus, the official team pub this week.
Activations in Munich has been filled with Lions supporters this week. Wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown has been filling in the coaching staff and his teammates on things to say and what to eat.
With the Lions have marketing rights in Germany and St. Brown's popularity, there is an expectation the game on Sunday will be more like a home game at Ford Field.
Head coach Dan Campbell, speaking with a large group of reporters, took the opportunity, when asked, to share what the game of football has meant to him.
"It gave me an opportunity to make a life and do something I absolutely loved with a group of guys, in any given time, 53 who have the same goal and you're all going the same direction," said Campbell. "And the blood and the sweat and the tears that it requires to have the same goal. It builds character in your team. It builds character as an individual, and it allows you to overcome anything in life that may come your way. Unfortunately, there are some things that, I tell the team all the time, one day you're going to get hit. You're going to get rocked with something really tough in your life. And I hate to say it, I don't want it to happen, none of us do, but you will, and you're going to have to be the rock .
"But, you're going to know how to overcome it and you know who you can lean on too, your brothers who have gone through everything you've had to go through here," Campbell added further. "I just think it's special that way and it gives guys an opportunity that may not have all the bells and whistles all wet just because they do all the little things right and they maximize everything that they have and their ability. That's the best way I could do it or say it.”

title: Detroit Lions Week 10 Rooting Guide for Best Possible Playoff Outcome
full_text:
The Detroit Lions are firmly in the mix of the NFC North divisional race.
Entering Week 10, the Lions sit in second-place in the division behind the Chicago Bears with a 6-2 record, which is good enough for the fifth seed in the NFC playoffs at this point in the season. The Bears, who are 7-2, are on a bye week this week so a win for Detroit would put them in a first place tie.
The Lions are unbeaten in the division , while the Bears have two losses to divisional opponents in Green Bay and Minnesota. Because they have not played head-to-head, Detroit would hold the tiebreaker if both teams are 7-2 at the end of Week 10 based on divisional record.
Even though the Lions enter Sunday's game against New England in second-place in the NFC North, with the Bears on a bye there is a scenario where Detroit could enter Week 11 as the NFC's No. 1 seed.
Here's a look at who Lions fans should be rooting for in Week 10, as these outcomes together with a win by Detroit would be the best possible outcome for the team.
Panthers at Saints: Saints 1 p.m., FOX.
The Lions hold the head-to-head tiebreaker over the Saints thanks to their overtime Week 1 win, so if New Orleans was to make a push for the Wild Card Detroit would hold the advantage. However, the Lions lost to Carolina in Week 4.
These two teams are playing for first-place in the NFC South, though both enter the game with losing records. Of these two teams, Carolina did more damage against the Lions and would be a tough matchup again if they met in the Wild Card Round, say in the 4-5 matchup in Carolina, so root for the Saints to take over the division lead.
Vikings at Packers: Packers 1 p.m., FOX.
This game is a big one for the divisional race. All four NFC North teams are at least .500, and there is a future where all four could get into the postseason with three Wild Card spots available. Detroit has beat both of these teams in their first head-to-head matchup, so they currently hold the tiebreaker over both.
A loss for either team doesn't take them out of the playoff race, but a third loss for Minnesota would be big for Detroit's divisional chances as they both currently sit at 6-2. According to the New York Times' Playoff Simulator , Detroit's chances of winning the division with a win and a Green Bay win would go up to 34 percent, while a win and a Vikings win would put their chances at 31 percent.
Conversely, the Lions' overall odds of making the postseason would be higher if the Vikings win, as a fourth loss for Green Bay would be detrimental in a competitive NFC playoff picture.
However, the Lions have always viewed winning the division and starting the playoffs at home as key, so Lions fans should side with the outcome that leads to a better chance of that happening.
Chiefs at Falcons: Chiefs 1 p.m., CBS.
One key is to root for AFC over NFC in inter-conference matchups, so go with Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs. The Falcons' offense is certainly capable of making a late-season push at the division or a Wild Card spot, but if they were to fall to 3-7 that would be a difficult challenge even in the lowly NFC South.
Rams at Cardinals: Cardinals 4:05 p.m., CBS.
The Rams remain one of the NFL's most talented teams, with veterans like Matthew Stafford, Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald leading the way. Though injuries and some early season struggles have put them in a tough spot, they could certainly be dangerous in the event that Detroit were to square off with them in the postseason.
As a result, root for the Cardinals to repeat their performance from earlier in the season when they beat the Rams at SoFi Stadium. A loss would drop the Rams to 5-5, thus putting their playoff chances at 24 percent, per the NYT playoff simulator.
Seahawks at Raiders: Raiders 4:05 p.m., CBS.
This is favorable because it's AFC over NFC, but also because the Seahawks are another team right on the fringe of the Wild Card competing with the Lions. They're another talented roster, but the reigning Super Bowl champions have had some struggles with consistency.
This outcome gives Lions fans the opportunity to root for the No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza, who will be making his first career start after the Raiders traded Kirk Cousins to Minnesota. The Seahawks' playoff percentage would drop to 45 percent with a loss.
49ers at Cowboys: Cowboys 4:25 p.m., FOX.
San Francisco remains a game up on the rest of the field in the race for the NFC's No. 1 seed at 7-1. However, a loss would drop them to 7-2, and a Lions win would bump them ahead of both the 49ers and Bears thanks to their record within the NFC.
If San Francisco were to lose to Dallas, it would be their second loss to an NFC opponent this season after falling to Atlanta earlier in the year. Detroit's first loss came to an AFC opponent, so they would have the upper hand in that tiebreaker. Both of Chicago's losses came to NFC opponents as well.
There's plenty to be decided beyond Week 10, but if the Lions win and the 49ers lose, Detroit would control its own destiny for the No. 1 seed heading into Week 11.
Lions playoff percentage if all these outcomes come true: 79 percent chance to make playoffs, 35 percent chance to win the NFC North.

title: Two Detroit Lions Ruled Questionable Against Patriots
full_text:
The Detroit Lion s have released their official injury designation report, ahead of their Week 10 contest against the New England Patriots.
Wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown and running back Sione Vaki were designated as questionable for the contest against the AFC East squad.
Previously, Detroit ruled out safety Kerby Joseph, center Cade Mays and cornerback D.J. Reed .
Offensive coordinator Drew Petzing was asked by reporters earlier this week about the consistency St. Brown has showcased in the last several weeks.
“I mean, probably in his career. I mean, it's almost historic, I think. I mean, I don't know all the numbers, but between number of catches, yards, touchdowns, how many ever years, six years, he's one of the best," said Petzing. "And I think you kind of hit the nail on the head. It's every single game, it's every single day, it's every single play. The guy plays the game with such amazing effort, intensity, and kind of that sense of urgency. You feel it the first play of practice , you feel it in the walkthrough, you feel it in the way he goes through meetings.
"And I think it shows up on the field because he plays that way and it's impressive to be around. It's impressive to watch. And I think it's one of the reasons he's one of the best there is.”

title: Dan Campbell Shares in Germany How City of Detroit Shaped Lions
full_text:
Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell was greeted in Germany by many foreign reporters seeking to learn more about him and his 6-2 football team.
The former NFL tight end shared what Amon-Ra St. Brown has been trying to teach him about Germany, and how the City of Detroit helped to shape his vision of the roster he and general manager Brad Holmes have built since 2021.
”We don’t have the beach. We don’t have all this, now the summers are unbelievable," said Campbell. "But things come a little bit harder out in that area. I always equate it to, it’s people that’ll do anything for you. They’d give you the shirt off their back if you needed it. And they’re all about doing the hard stuff. And when I came to Detroit to take over as head coach, man, I wanted to build a team that they could relate to."
Campbell, now in his sixth season leading the Lions, marveled at how many supporters traveled from Michigan and beyond to enjoy the weekend festivities in Munich.
Additional Detroit Lions NFL Insider Analysis: Three Players Under Most Pressure Against New England Patriots in Germany
"We want to be a team that they can look at and say, ‘I respect that. I respect the way they go about their business. That there is something gritty about it.' It is hard work. It is inspiring football. It’s not the easy way out. And so those are really the type of fans we have, man. Just good, wholesome people that really care about each other. They put in good days’ work. And man, they back us up and support the heck out of us. And we love them to death.”
When asked what he was hoping to experience out of football, Campbell expressed he certainly was going to drink a German beer before returning to the Motor City.
“You don’t come to Germany without getting a German beer," said Campbell. "I know that. So, I will definitely have a beer before I leave, that’s for sure. I don’t know which one or what, but I’m getting one.”

title: 3 Detroit Lions Players Under Most Pressure Against Patriots
full_text:
The Detroit Lions will have several players looking to make their presence known when they square off with the New England Patriots Sunday morning in Munich, Germany. With the regular season entering a critical stretch, the Lions need consistent productivity across both sides of the ball to sustain the momentum.
With that said, here are the three Lions players under pressure the most to deliver strong performances against New England.
With D.J. Reed out again (hip), the Lions need Rakestraw to look like the capable cover corner they thought he was upon drafting him in the second round in 2024. Unfortunately, the Missouri product hasn't looked like that guy throughout the majority of his career.
He started for the first time in Week 7 against the Packers, allowed three receptions on four targets his way and a passer rating of 106.3. Plus, he earned a Pro Football Focus coverage grade of 64.9 and an overall mark of 65.2 for his efforts.
He's produced a mixed bag of results since, and certainly needs to deliver a strong effort against Drake Maye and the Patriots’ passing game Sunday.
Scruggs will get another start in place of Cade Mays in Week 10 against New England. The fourth-year interior lineman has performed admirably in place of the banged-up Mays thus far this season, earning a 75.3 overall mark from PFF. It ranks as the second-best grade among all qualified centers (36 players).
He'll face a big test on Sunday, going up against New England defensive tackles Christian Barmore and Milton Williams. Based on his play so far in 2026, though, I believe that Scruggs will be up for the challenge.
Like Rakestraw, TeSlaa has mostly been a disappointment since being drafted by Brad Holmes & Co.
A variety of fans and pundits thought the second-year wideout would take the next step in 2026, and he simply hasn't through the season's first nine weeks . The Arkansas product hasn't had more than one catch each of the past four games, and he's also been the recipient of no more than two targets each of the aforementioned contests. It's a clear sign of the fact that Jared Goff and the Lions don't have a lot of confidence in the 24-year-old .
Speaking of Goff, he hasn't thrown for more than 176 yards each of the past two weeks. So, if TeSlaa proved to be a bit more reliable, it would go a long way toward Goff finding more success through the air against the Patriots and future opponents.

title: How the NFL Trade Deadline Changed Detroit Lions 2026 Depth Chart
full_text:
The Detroit Lions are getting set for an international matchup with the New England Patriots.
On Sunday, the Lions will battle with the reigning AFC Champions looking to win a fifth game in a row. They'll be doing it with another addition, as they traded for safety Andre Cisco prior to Tuesday's trade deadline.
Here's a look at the Lions' depth chart following the trade deadline as they prepare for Sunday's game against the Patriots.
Starter: Jared Goff. Backup: Joshua Dobbs. Practice squad: Luke Altmyer
Goff missed practice Wednesday with a chest injury, but was a full participant in Thursday's session and isn't expected to be out for Sunday's game. He's been a key cog in the offense this year with how consistent he's been, but he's looking to snap a two-game skid with an interception after not throwing one in the first five games.
Starter: Jahmyr Gibbs. Backup: Sione Vaki. Reserves: Jacob Saylors. Practice squad: Jabari Small. Inactive: Isiah Pacheco (Injured reserve).
Vaki has not practiced this week with an ankle injury, but did play on Sunday. If he can't go, Saylors is also dealing with an injury though he's been a full participant each of the first two days of practice. This could potentially create an opportunity for Small to be elevated from the practice squad for the second straight game.
Starters: Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, Isaac TeSlaa. Backups: Tay Martin, DeAndre Carter. Practice squad: Dominic Lovett, Lucky Jackson. Inactive: Kendrick Law (Injured reserve), Tom Kennedy (Injured reserve).
Sunday will be a special game for St. Brown , whose mother hails from Germany. He has roots in the area, and as a result will be motivated to have a big performance. Williams will be looking for a bounce-back game after a quiet showing against the Dolphins, while Martin and Carter both had their first catch of the season last week.
It's worth noting that St. Brown has been limited in the first two days of practice this week, and he could potentially carry a designation into Sunday's game.
Starter: Sam LaPorta. Backup: Brock Wright. Reserves: Tyler Conklin. Practice squad: Jackson Meeks, Miles Kitselman, Thomas Gordon.
The Lions waived Meeks as the corresponding move for the acquisition of Cisco, but were quick to bring him back on the practice squad. Conklin had surpassed him as the third tight end in recent weeks, and will presumably stay in that role.
Because Meeks is new to the practice squad this year, the Lions could still utilize him as an elevation three times before they'd have to consider re-adding him to the active roster.
Starters: Penei Sewell (left), Blake Miller (right). Backup: Larry Borom. Practice squad: Devin Cochran. Inactive: Gio Manu (Non-Football Injury).
The Lions continue to roll with Miller, who had some difficulties last week against Chop Robinson but rebounded with a good second half showing. Borom remains the first option in jumbo packages, with the Lions also utilizing defensive lineman Skyler Gill-Howard as an extra blocker at times.
Starters: Christian Mahogany (left), Tate Ratledge (right). Backup: Miles Frazier. Practice squad: Elijah Klein, Mason Miller (Practice squad injured list). Inactive: Ben Bartch (Injured reserve).
Mahogany appears to be back in the good graces of the coaching staff after being benched for disciplinary reasons last week. He will presumably return to his starting spot at left guard, with Miles Frazier being the backup after a tough first start.
Starter: Juice Scruggs. Backup: Ratledge Reserve: Seth McLaughlin. Inactive: Cade Mays (Out, Ankle).
Mays has already been ruled out, so it will be Scruggs again manning the pivot for Detroit's offensive line. Ratledge is the emergency sub, with McLaughlin also being available in case of an emergency.
Starters: Alim McNeill, Tyleik Williams. Backups: Skyler Gill-Howard, Levi Onwuzurike. Reserve: Mekhi Wingo. Practice squad: Aiden Keanaaina, Jeffrey M'ba, Ben Stille, Taki Taimani.
The Lions have the rotation down pat between Williams and Gill-Howard next to McNeill, with Williams being the run-stuffer and Gill-Howard playing in pass-rush situation. McNeill has also had a fabulous start to the year, with 5.5 sacks up to this point in the season.
Starters: Aidan Hutchinson, DJ Wonnum. Backups: Derrick Moore, Tyler Lacy. Reserves: Eric O'Neill, Ahmed Hassanein. Practice squad: Anthony Lucas. Inactive: Payton Turner (Injured reserve).
Wonnum is expected to return to action after missing last week's game while in concussion protocol. Still, Moore could get some extended opportunities after recording two sacks last game, which was a pleasant surprise after a slow start to his rookie season.
Starters: Derrick Barnes, Malcolm Rodriguez. Backups: Trevor Nowaske Amen Ogbongbemiga, Joe Bachie. Reserve: K.J. Britt. Practice squad: Owen Pappoe. Inactive: Jack Campbell (Injured reserve), Jimmy Rolder (Injured reserve), Damone Clark (Injured reserve), Devin White (Injured reserve).
The Lions will need their linebacker depth to shine as Jack Campbell is on injured reserve. It was a season-high in snaps for Malcolm Rodriguez last week, and he delivered a solid performance.
Detroit has several veterans it could lean on in a rotation, and Britt could also potentially get an uptick in action after playing only on special teams last week. As a former member of the Patriots' practice squad, Britt could also provide some unique insight on the Patriots' offense after repping against them in practice.
Starters: Roger McCreary, Rock Ya-Sin. Backups: Khalil Dorsey, Ennis Rakestraw. Reserve: Nick Whiteside. Practice squad: Aamaris Brown. Inactive: D.J. Reed (Out, Hip).
Reed has already been ruled out for Sunday's game, meaning the rotation of cornerbacks will be down a member. McCreary and Ya-Sin played the highest amount of snaps last week, but all five of the team's active options will likely get opportunities on Sunday.
Starters: Brian Branch, Chuck Clark. Backups: Keith Abney (Nickel), Andre Cisco Reserve: Christian Izien. Practice squad: Myles Bryant. Inactive: Kerby Joseph (Physically Unable to Perform), Avonte Maddox (Injured reserve), Thomas Harper (Injured reserve).
The addition of Cisco sets up an interesting dynamic . Branch and Clark have played well together since the former returned from his Achilles injury, and Kerby Joseph could still return as soon as next week. As a result, it will be interesting to see where Cisco fits in a fully healthy safety room.
Regardless, Campbell stated that he expects Cisco to suit up on Sunday. The former Jet has had some moments this season despite being a reserve, as he had a sack against the Lions in Week 3. He's an intriguing addition, and he should get an opportunity to contribute on Sunday.
Kicker: Jake Bates. Punter: Jack Fox. Long-snapper: Hogan Hatten. Kick returners: DeAndre Carter, Jacob Saylors Punt returner: Carter.
Saylors has been a full participant in practice this week and as a result should be in line to return to action after missing last week. He'll be paired with Carter on kick returns, while Carter will handle the punts.

title: Detroit Lions Had 'Hard Conversations' With OL Christian Mahogany
full_text:
Detroit Lions left guard Christian Mahogany has accepted responsibility for breaking team rules and vowed to make it up to his teammates and the coaching staff.
Offensive coordinator Drew Petzing, speaking to local reporters before the team departed for Germany, addressed his level of faith in the former sixth-round draft pick moving forward.
“I'm not going to speak to the specific conversation, but again, I think there are some hard conversations," said Petzing. "You’ve got to challenge some people, but I think he responded and was really pleased with the way he handled it and looking forward to see what he does going forward.”
Mahogany was benched against the Miami Dolphins after repeatedly violating team rules. Head coach Dan Campbell the decision had to be made, given he has clear expectations for the roster.
Despite missing a game, the expectation is Mahogany will return to the starting lineup against the New England Patriots.
Additional Detroit Lions NFL Insider Analysis: Was 2026 Season Ruined Due to Brad Holmes Inactivity at Trade Deadline?
Petzing does not see the game off taking away from the 26-year-old's ability to produce at a high level this week and moving forward.
“I think one of the things he has done when he's been in there which has been great is he's played hard," said Petzing. "Hasn't always been perfect, but he's playing at a hundred miles an hour and I think that's so important up front.”
Mahogany was disappointed in himself, but understood what needed to occur moving forward to avoid further disciplinary actions. He has already spoken to Petzing, head coach Dan Campbell and offensive line coach Hank Fraley.
"I’m not going to either. I’m not going to disobey him," Mahogany said, via the team's social media channel. "It sucks what happened, but I have to grow up and I have to stop breaking team rules. It is what it is. I let my teammates down, I let my organization down and it won’t ever happen again."
He later added, "You just gotta eat it on the chin. That’s who I am. I’m not a person that’s gonna sulk. It sucked not being out there, because I let my teammates down. I don’t want to do that, I did, and that’s on me."

title: Spot the Ball: 10 Thoughts Ahead of Detroit Lions Matchup With Patriots
full_text:
The Detroit Lions are getting ready for an overseas journey and a marquee matchup.
On Sunday, while Lions fans in Detroit are waking up, the team will be getting set to take on the New England Patriots. Kickoff is set for 9:30 E.T., with the Lions as the dedicated home team for the game at Allianz Arena in Munich, Germany.
Here are 10 thoughts surrounding the Lions' Week 10 matchup with the Patriots.
Coming into Sunday's game, quarterback Drake Maye is tied for the NFL lead in interceptions with 11. As a result, the Lions' defense could be in a position to be opportunistic and take the ball away, setting their offense up in good field position in the process.
My eyes are on Brian Branch, who already has an interception to his name in the three games he's played this season. Because of his versatility, he could be in a position to take the ball away at some point throughout Sunday's game.
Since coming back from the Achilles injury that ended his season last year, Branch has looked increasingly comfortable over his three games. He played every snap last week, and looked capable of being a leader for the defense that is missing one of its captains.
The Lions will be playing their first game on foreign soil since 2015, as they have only played two overseas games prior to Sunday. Both were in London, and they took place in back-to-back years starting in 2014.
In their first appearance overseas, that 2014 game against the Atlanta Falcons, they were able to rally and stage a thrilling comeback victory. They won that game 22-21 thanks to a last-second field goal from Matt Prater.
The following year, the Lions returned to Wembley Stadium and took on the Kansas City Chiefs. The results were not as favorable that time, as they were defeated 45-10 by the Chiefs.
The Patriots have dominated the history between these two teams, with the Lions winning just two of those matchups since 2000. Much of that time was in the Tom Brady era, a likely first-ballot Hall of Fame quarterback who led the Patriots from 2001-19.
Detroit defeated New England in November of 2000, and again on Sunday Night Football in 2018 for Matt Patricia's first win as the team's head coach. However, the Patriots won the other five meetings in that time frame leading up to this season.
If the Lions were to win on international soil, it would be a big win and their fifth in a row. A five-game win streak would be the longest for Detroit since the 2024 season, when they ripped off 11 wins in a row.
The Lions did make one trade at the deadline, and while there will be ire for the lack of aggressiveness, general manager Brad Holmes did add some depth in the secondary by acquiring Andre Cisco.
The former New York Jet will provide depth at the safety position, and has experience both playing as a free safety as well as in the box. He could pair nicely with Brian Branch, or supplement Branch by working some in the box in certain packages.
It appears likely that Cisco will make his Lions debut on Sunday and make the trip to Germany with the team.
The performance of Drake Maye has been a huge storyline for the Patriots throughout the season. For a player who finished second in MVP voting last year, the showing through the first eight games has been less than stellar.
Through three games, Maye had just one touchdown pass against six interceptions. While he has rebounded somewhat, his turnover numbers remain jarring after he threw eight interceptions all of last season.
Maye is coming off a disastrous first half performance against Green Bay, where he threw three interceptions before the break before bouncing back in the second half.
If the Lions want to continue their recent stretch of strong defensive play, keeping Maye uncomfortable is a good place to start. In addition to his 11 interceptions, he has also been sacked 20 times and has struggled with consistency.
The NFC North has been the best division in football up to this point in the season. All four teams are at least three games over .500, with the Chicago Bears leading the way at 7-2. Detroit is right behind them along with Minnesota as both teams are 6-2, while the Packers sit in fourth at 6-3.
Part of the reason the division has been so good is how well they've handled opponents outside the division. Through Week 9, the NFC North is 20-4 against teams outside of their own division. Ironically, two of those losses belong to the Lions, who are the only undefeated team in divisional play.
Meanwhile, the Bears are 7-0 against teams outside the division, but have yet to win a game within the NFC North. If the Lions are going to keep pace in the divisional race, they need to keep up with their peers and continue handling business against teams outside the North.
Detroit got a spike in production from rookie Derrick Moore , who recorded the first two sacks of his NFL career against Miami. Moore saw an increased workload with DJ Wonnum ruled out, and even with Wonnum potentially finding his way back into the mix on Sunday Moore has made a claim for more snaps.
Elsewhere on the injury front, Dan Campbell said Wednesday that D.J. Reed and Cade Mays both have small chances of playing, while Kerby Joseph will wait at least one more week for his debut.
If Mays and Reed are both unable to play, it will mean another start for Juice Scruggs at center and more opportunities for the likes of Rock Ya-Sin and Ennis Rakestraw alone with Roger McCreary at cornerback.
The Lions are one of the NFL's most popular teams in Germany, and the local fans will be hoping to see them put on a show. In their best-case scenario, the offense finishes the first drive with a touchdown as opposed to a field goal, setting the tone with an explosive play early.
Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams are both actively involved in the offense, while Jared Goff keeps the ball moving with crisp passes to both as well as Sam LaPorta. As with any Lions game that goes according to plan, Jahmyr Gibbs feasts in the second half and grinds away the clock in a comfortable win.
While Maye has struggled in his third NFL season up to this point, he still has the arm talent to make a defense pay. With Reed potentially out, the Patriots could make the Lions secondary pay through the air.
If the Lions are inconssistent on offense, it puts more pressure on the defense. While Kelvin Sheppard's defense has been solid as of late, they could revert back to their early season ways in this worst-case scenario.
Ultimately, if the Lions start slow and allow New England to build a two-score lead, they would struggle to get enough stops to give their offense a chance to come back late.
Sunday's game will be a homecoming of sorts for Amon-Ra St. Brown, whose mother was born in Germany. He has developed a strong reputation in the country, which has fans excited to watch him live in action on Sunday.
Because of the strong ties he has to the area, I think the Lions will do everything they can to have him have a big game. They've shown some interesting looks for St. Brown in recent weeks with coordinator Drew Petzing, and he could have another big day in store.
It won't be easy, but I believe the Lions will ultimately scheme up a way for St. Brown to approach double-digit catches, and as a result he could go over 150 yards against the Patriot defense.

title: It Took Nine Games for Christian Watson to Do What Hadn’t Been Done in Four Seasons
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – It’s true that the Green Bay Packers haven’t had a 1,000-yard receiver since Davante Adams in 2021. It’s more than that, though.
The Packers haven’t had a receiver reach even 860 yards since 2021.
Well, Christian Watson has put that sentence in the past tense.
Through just nine games and headed into Sunday’s rivalry showdown against the Minnesota Vikings, Watson has 879 receiving yards. That ranks third in the NFL. He’s on a pace to not just break the team’s 1,000-yard drought but to blow past it like a rocket blows past the speed of sound.
Watson is on pace to finish with 1,660 yards and 13 touchdowns. Only nine receivers in NFL history have hit 1,600 yards and 13 touchdowns in a season, though Seattle’s Jaxon Smith-Njigba is on pace to crush those numbers, as well.
It took Watson about half a season to obliterate his career-high 620 receiving yards from 2024 and match his career-high seven touchdowns catches from his rookie season in 2022.
The 1,000-yard marker has always been a notable milestone for running backs and receivers alike. Watson, however, is not impressed.
“Honestly, you’d have to ask me at the end of the season when I achieved that or surpassed that,” he said on Thursday a few days before Sunday’s showdown against the Vikings. “Right now, it’s not something I’m looking into too much.
“We’re only halfway through the season so just hitting 1,000 – for me, the way I’d look at it is getting 120 more yards for the rest of the season doesn’t really sound too exciting for me. It’d be something that I’ll look at it at the end of the season, but I’m excited about how much I’ve been able to be an impact for this team so far. Obviously, God willing, hopefully I’m able to continue to do that and celebrate the stats after the season.”
Watson is having a season worth celebrating.
Adams in 2021 set the franchise record with 1,553 receiving yards in 16 games, a 97.1-yard average. Watson is on pace to beat that number by more than 100 yards. In terms of receiving yards per game, Watson’s 97.7-yard average would rank fifth in Packers history; Don Hutson averaged 110.1 yards per game in 1942 and Billy Howton averaged 102.6 yards per game in 1952. During the Super Bowl era, only Adams’ 98.1 yards per game in 2020 would beat Watson’s production.
Watson, of course, has made a killing in the vertical passing game. On passes thrown 20-plus yards downfield, Watson has caught 10-of-19 targets for 382 yards and three touchdowns. He’s third in catches, first in yards, tied for first in touchdowns and 10th in catch percentage (out of 45 receivers targeted at least eight times).
After the New England game, coach Matt LaFleur said the Packers were turning low-percentage throws into high-percentage plays.
With his size, speed and skill, Watson has changed the math.
“I think theoretically it’s a low-percentage throw when you look at it across everybody doing it,” Watson said. “I think if you really dive into individually, it’s going to be a higher percentage for certain individuals and a lower percentage for other individuals.
“I think it’s just something that we got a lot of reps at. Obviously, something that we’ve built a lot of trust in that area so, at the end of the day, that’s what it comes down to: Obviously, 10 [Jordan Love] just trusting us to go make a play. I think we’ve got a lot of banked reps in that area. That’s obviously been a big part of our explosiveness in our offense, a big part of our offense in general. We’ve done it a lot so, obviously, we rely on each other in those moments when we need those plays.”
Incredibly, Watson is 5-of-5 in contested-catch situations on the deep passes, so it’s not as if it’s been a bunch of wide-open connections.
Watson rather sheepishly admitted to being impressed by some of his catches, whether it was the bomb for his second touchdown against Chicago or last week’s one-hander on a crossing route.
“It’s definitely times where, obviously, made a big play,” Watson said. “Obviously, I like to say that I expect myself to make those plays all the time but it’s definitely times where I look back and a little proud of myself for making that kind of play or that level of play. Probably the answer that you don’t want is I expect myself to make those plays. That’s usually my first thought is really just excitement overall.”
The Packers will face a big challenge against the Vikings on Sunday. Minnesota in first in the league in touchdown passes allowed and opponent passer rating and second in passing yards allowed per attempt.
The Vikings have allowed only one 100-yard receiving game all season. That was Watson’s 147 yards in Week 1.
Their blitz, blitz, blitz-some-more scheme has made life hell on quarterbacks. However, the Vikings’ all-blitz defense also leaves voids in the secondary if everyone can take care of business. That’s easier said than done, obviously, considering the Vikings are No. 1 in points allowed, but the Packers made a bunch of big plays in the Week 1 loss.
“Honestly, it gives us a lot more opportunities, to be honest – obviously, as long as we take care of things up front,” Watson said. “We definitely have to be more on top of things, too, just being able to recognize that stuff with adjustments to our routes and stuff like that, too. If we handle it the right way, it’ll be opps for us, for sure.”
If the Packers handle it the right way, Watson might be walking off the field on Sunday with his first 1,000-yard season and the team might be celebrating its seventh win.

title: Packers-Vikings Final Injury Report: Seven Starters Out or Questionable
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers listed 12 players as out, doubtful or questionable, including seven starters, for Sunday’s game against the Minnesota Vikings.
Four players are out: running back Josh Jacobs (finger), edge Micah Parsons (knee/illness), center Sean Rhyan (ankle) and tight end Josh Whyle (concussion). Jacobs, Rhyan and Whyle didn’t practice this week; Parsons practiced all week but the team wants to give him one more week to get ready.
“He looks great but he just doesn’t have a ton of reps under his belt,” coach Matt LaFleur said before Friday’s practice. “So, we want to try to continue to build him up.”
Linebacker LB Zaire Franklin (shin), who didn’t practice all week, is doubtful and almost certainly will miss a fourth consecutive game.
Jacobs, Parsons, Rhyan and Franklin are starters. Four more starters are questionable: safety Javon Bullard (ankle/knee), safety Xavier McKinney (foot) and edge Lukas Van Ness (back).
McKinney (foot) was added to the injury report on Friday. Right guard Kevin Zeitler (ankle and triceps) practiced on Wednesday and Thursday but did not practice on Friday. Zeitler’s status could impact the team’s plan at guard; left guard Aaron Banks (knee/hip) is off the injury report.
McKinney is tied for the NFL lead with five interceptions.
"This is a must win for us... Being last in the division, losing to them the first time, understanding how competitive this division is?" - Xavier McKinney #packers #vikings pic.twitter.com/uX4TCDNS1k
Van Ness and Bullard returned to practice after missing the first two days of the week. Bullard said he’d play after Thursday’s practice and Van Ness essentially said the same thing on Friday.
“I’m doing good, thank you,” Van Ness said. “It felt good to get back on the grass today.”
Van Ness leads the team with 4.5 sacks. Of the 70 edge defenders with at least 140 pass-rushing snaps, Van Ness ranks 13th in pass-rush win rate, according to Pro Football Focus.
“It’s a weekly challenge, always finding something to improve on,” Van Ness said. “Coach LaFleur always says it’s 1 percent. You’re either getting worse or you’re getting better. No matter who you’re talking about, anyone can find something to improve on.
“We’ve come back week after week, evaluated the tape and continue to keep our nose down and our head down and keep working. If we see that, you talk about December and January football, that’s when you see these teams really come together and then compete for a Super Bowl.”
Running back Chris Brooks (ankle) and receiver/returner Skyy Moore (ankle), who have been designated to return, were limited participation all week and are questionable. To play on Sunday, they will have to be added to the roster on Saturday.
After Friday’s practice, Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell told reporters that Kirk Cousins will start at quarterback.
“The way he threw the football this week, it’s a really cool thing to see,” O’Connell said.
However, tight end T.J. Hockenson (wrist/chest) and linebacker Blake Cashman (concussion) are out. Another starter, defensive end Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins (ankle), is out, as well.
Cashman is a stud. With 76 tackles, he is one of 18 players with 70-plus tackles this season. He leads that group with 4.5 sacks, eight tackles for losses and 10 quarterback hits and is tied with Packers safety Evan Williams for first with seven passes defensed.
Hockenson leads the team with 35 catches; the next Vikings tight end, Gavin Bartholomew, has only seven.
Receiver Jordan Addison (thumb) was added to the injury report and is questionable. He was limited participation at Friday’s practice.
For the second consecutive year, Lukas Van Ness is Green Bay’s nominee for the NFL’s Salute to Service Award. In its 16th year, the award honors a league member who demonstrates “an exceptional commitment” to honoring and supporting the military.
Van Ness’ grandfather served 27 years and earned the rank of lieutenant colonel in the U.S. Army.
“It’s really an honor to be able to recognize all the amazing men and women that support our country and allow us to do what we do out here on the football field,” he said. “Being able to do this for my second year is really special, especially with my grandfather, who served.”
He added: “We have a platform of being able to bring recognition to those service members and those who have served and then, ultimately, those who have paid the ultimate sacrifice for not only us but our country, it’s really, really special. It’s a really cool initiative that the NFL does.”
The Packers have won five of their last six games, due in large part to the play of the defense, which has done more than survive without Micah Parsons.
“We just have a really competitive group of guys,” he said of the edge group of Van Ness, Barryn Sorrell, Brenton Cox and Dani Dennis-Sutton. “Whether it’s myself or Barryn or B-Cox or Dani, there’s no fall-off in talent.
“We’re all super-capable. We can all go out there and play at a high level. It’s been really fun to be able to rotate out there with different guys, work on some different packages and have the flexibility to throw us wherever on the field on any given circumstance. I’m really proud of how we’re all playing. It’s been cool to see us all step up.”

Doubtful: LB Zaire Franklin (shin).
Questionable: RB Chris Brooks (ankle), S Javon Bullard (ankle/knee), G/T Travis Glover (knee), S Xavier McKinney (foot), WR Skyy Moore (ankle), edge Lukas Van Ness (back), G Kevin Zeitler (ankle/triceps).

title: Packers Friday Update From Practice: Two Starters Return; New Questions Emerge
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – On Thursday, Green Bay Packers standout slot Javon Bullard proclaimed he “definitely” would play on Sunday against the Minnesota Vikings.
“I ain’t missing no game. I ain’t missing no game, man,” Bullard said after missing a second consecutive day of practice. “I care about this team. I care about my brothers, man.”
Sure enough, Bullard was suited up and went out for the start of Friday’s practice, the last one of the week before Sunday’s rivalry rematch. Also returning to practice after missing the first two days was starting edge Lukas Van Ness.
However, new questions emerged.
On Fridays, reporters only get to watch the players go through their lengthy pre-practice routine. Two players who had practiced on Wednesday and Thursday did not participate.
One was star safety Xavier McKinney. The NFL co-leader with five interceptions stretched in the back a bit and talked with a trainer but did not go through warmups. He was not on the injury report to start the week.
If any player can play while missing one day of practice, it’s the two-time All-Pro.
“Honestly, I think it’s just the way I prepare,” he said after picking off two passes against the Patriots. “Every day, I try to give these guys in this locker room my best self, the best version of me, whether that’s in the meeting room, the practice field and then, obviously, when we get out here on gameday, I go out there and you see the product I put out there.
“But that’s throughout the week something that I’ve worked on. I think it’s me getting into a feel of things and just me playing free, being an instinctual player that I am and going out there and making plays.”
The other was right guard Kevin Zeitler, who was in the conversation to start this week after making his Packers debut last week against New England. He had been limited participation this week with an ankle injury. Zeitler did have a practice jersey on, so it’s possible he went out later.
If Zeitler is too banged up to go, the Packers could revert back to Aaron Banks at left guard and Laken Tomlinson at right guard – the duo the past two weeks. Mekhi Becton would be an option, too, and Travis Glover returned to practice this week after missing the last two games with a knee injury.
Four more players didn’t practice on Friday, missed the full practice week and almost certainly won’t play on Sunday.
Linebacker Zaire Franklin will miss a fourth consecutive game with a shin injury. Fortunately for the Packers, Isaiah McDuffie and Ty’Ron Hopper practiced all week after dropping out of the New England game.
Center Sean Rhyan will miss a third consecutive game with an injured ankle, with John Williams getting thrown into the fire against the blitzing Vikings.
Running back Josh Jacobs was scheduled to have surgery on Friday to repair his broken right ring finger.
Tight end Josh Whyle will miss a second consecutive game with the concussion he sustained during the Thursday night game against Carolina.
Star edge Micah Parsons was back on the practice field after going through team drills during Thursday’s padded practice. He looks great, LaFleur said, but said the team wants to “continue to build him up” before returning him to game action.
So, no, he will not play against the Vikings.
The status of Lukas Van Ness and Javon Bullard, obviously, will be critical given the stakes of the game.
Bullard, a second-round pick in 2024, is having his best season. He had a total of four passes defensed during his first two seasons but has seven this season.
“I know he’s going to do everything in his power to be there,” LaFleur said of Bullard before Friday’s practice. “We’ll see how he’s feeling today. It’s always concerning when a guy doesn’t practice twice but if I know Bull the way I think I do, he’s going to do everything in his power to be out there.”
Van Ness leads the team with 4.5 sacks. He ranks 13th among edge defenders in pass-rush win rate, according to Pro Football Focus, just behind the Vikings’ Dallas Turner and the Raiders’ Maxx Crosby
Also, running back Chris Brooks and receiver/returner Skyy Moore, who have been designated for return from injured reserve, completed 3-for-3 practice weeks and “definitely” have a chance to play on Sunday.
“We’ll get through today and then see where they’re at and make a decision,” LaFleur said.
The final injury reports of the week will be released after Friday’s practices. For now, here are the reports from Thursday.
Packers Thursday Injury Report
Did not participate: S Javon Bullard (ankle/knee), LB Zaire Franklin (shin), RB Josh Jacobs (finger), C Sean Rhyan (ankle), edge Lukas Van Ness (back), TE Josh Whyle (concussion).
Limited participation: LG Aaron Banks (knee/hip), RB Chris Brooks (ankle), G/T Travis Glover (knee), LB Ty’Ron Hopper (illness), WR Skyy Moore (ankle), edge Micah Parsons (knee/illness), WR Savion Williams (groin), G Kevin Zeitler (ankle).
Full participation: WR Bo Melton (gameday concussion evaluation), K Trey Smack (right calf).
Note: Brooks, Moore and Parsons have been designated to return and are within their 21-day practice window.
Vikings Thursday Injury Report
Did not participate: LB Blake Cashman (concussion), TE T.J. Hockenson (wrist/chest), DL Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins (ankle), WR Jauan Jennings (calf), QB Kyler Murray (hamstring), OLB Kyle Van Noy (calf).
Limited participation: S Jay Ward (knee), QB Carson Wentz (ankle).
Full participation: S Theo Jackson (quad).

title: Packers-Vikings: A Big Rivalry Rematch With Big Ticket Price
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – It doesn’t get much bigger than Sunday’s Packers-Vikings game at Lambeau Field.
It’s a rivalry game and a border war between a pair of six-win teams with an eye on reaching the playoffs – and much more.
According to TickPick, the average ticket price is $559. It’s the most expensive Packers-Vikings game on record and also the second-most expensive Packers home game on record, behind only the Oct. 11 game against the Bears, which had an average ticket price of $755. The previous high was $494 against the Cowboys in 2022.
According to TickPick, the average ticket price for this Packers-Vikings matchup is 90 percent more than it was for the Week 1 game in Minneapolis.
The get-in price for this game is sitting at $313, up a little over Thursday.
Based on TickPick data, 24 percent of ticket buyers have a Wisconsin billing code and 19 percent have a Minnesota billing code, with the rest of the purchasers coming from outside the neighboring states. TickPick usually sees Wisconsin accounting for about 36 percent of sales for Packers home games.
That could be noteworthy, because the Packers are counting on Lambeau Field being a big advantage in the rematch.
“It’s a division game. It’s like the playoffs already,” cornerback Keisean Nixon said. “I think everybody’s got six wins in our division, right? It’s going to come down to our division, so every time we play somebody in our division, it’s a playoff game. When they come to Lambeau, that’s just like homefield advantage. You’ve got to take advantage of it.”
The Packers lost to the Vikings 39-22 in Week 1. Green Bay led 22-17 after three quarters but got destroyed 22-zip in the fourth.
The Vikings started 6-0 but have lost two in a row. To save their season, they acquired quarterback Kirk Cousins at the trade deadline.
“It’s a different system, but at the same time, Kirk, he’s a savvy vet,” Javon Bullard said. “A quarterback that’s played a lot of ball in this league, that’s  seen a lot in this league, and we got our hands tied with him. But, at the same time, he’s coming into Lambeau and playing us. This is a nasty defense also.
“Of course there’s going to be certain tendencies that he has. Certain things just don’t go away from last week because he was just with a (different) team; they just not going to go away. But, at the same time, he is a quarterback that’s capable of making those tough throws. He’s a quarterback that has a great mind, sees things before the play. So, you better be dialed into that.”
The bad news for the Packers is they lost the first matchup so are in last place in the NFC North, even with their 6-3 record. The good news is the teams have split the series five of the last six years. Green Bay has won three of the last five at Lambeau, including 23-6 last year.
The Packers are 3-0 in noon games this year.
According to the Opta Supercomputer , the Packers have a 60.8 percent win probability. They are 3-point favorites at FanDuel Sportsbook . The over/under is 42.5, with both teams’ defenses posting top-10 EPAs .
The key to the game will be handling the attacking Vikings defense, which will blitz Jordan Love off the bus.
“Absolutely, and he does a great job of that, just playing each play as its own play,” coach Matt LaFleur said on Friday of Love playing with patience. “That’s the mindset. We’ve gotten in trouble, and I think most teams do, when you try to force it.
“You’ve got to allow it to come to you and try to take what they’ve giving you. If that’s a checkdown, take the checkdown. If it’s a deep shot, then certainly we want to capitalize on those opportunities. This defense doesn’t give you a ton down the field.”

title: Vikings Thrive in ‘World of Chaos.’ Here’s How Packers Can Survive Blitzing.
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Brian Flores has tipped decades of defensive philosophies upside down.
Flores’ blitz-happy defense will take center stage when Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers host the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday.
Asked if there was any rhyme or reason to how Flores will attack, Packers coach Matt LaFleur offered a simple response.
“Yeah, it’s called pressure,” he said.
That’s for sure. It’s pressure at an unprecedented and unthinkable level.
The Vikings hired Flores to run their defense in 2023. In 2022, they blitzed 24 percent of the time, according to Stats Perform’s Opta Data . That means they did not blitz 76 percent of the time. This season, their blitz rate is 75.3 percent.
Incredibly, since 2000, the second-highest blitz rate during that span was the 2009 Jets at 56.4 percent. So, the Vikings’ blitz percentage is almost 20 points higher.
“We see those conversations about the blitz rates, and everybody thinks it’s wild – and rightfully so. It is wild,” safety Harrison Smith said on former All-Pro cornerback Richard Sherman’s podcast. “We talk about it sometimes inside. Who decides that four was the baseline amount you’re supposed to send?”
Not long ago, defensive coordinators saved their blitz packages for third downs or other need-to-pass situations. Flores will blitz anytime, anywhere, any situation.
According to Sumer Sports, Flores blitzes a staggering 80 percent of the time on first-and-10 passing plays. On third-and-long (third-and-7-plus) it’s “only” 70.6 percent.
“They’re going to pressure the crap out of us, and we’re going to have to either take advantage of it or prepare to play against it,” tight end Tucker Kraft said.
How can the Packers take advantage?
Minnesota’s defense is one of the best in the era. Maybe one of the best of all-time. It ranks first in points allowed, first in total defense, first in sack percentage and first in the red zone.
With the Vikings’ defense taking the offensive, opponents are averaging 4.5 yards per play on first down. That’s the second-best mark in the league.
Teams have a fighting chance on the ground, with the Vikings ranked 14th with 4.04 yards allowed per first-down carry. The Packers, of course, have struggled to run the ball for most of the season.
There’s a lot more risk-reward through the air, where the old-school mantra of three things can happen when you throw the ball and only one is good. The Vikings are first with 5.1 yards allowed per first-down passing play. They have a league-high 11 sacks.
“Just look at what they’ve done consistently week in and week out,” LaFleur said. “It’s a struggle for every offense to go out there and score points on them. Not even score points but move the ball consistently.
“I think they do a great job of getting people behind the sticks. There’s more third-and-longs than I feel like I’ve ever seen at this point of the year, in many cases, throughout the entire course of a year, and we’re halfway through. I think they do a great job of just applying pressure and you make mistakes. That’s why it’s so important for us to play a clean game.”
Yes, because it’s going to be hard enough to get 4 yards on first down as it is, let alone with false starts leading to 5-yard penalties or missed assignments setting up sacks.
First-down success is a big reason why the Vikings rank third on third down. The average third down against Minnesota requires 8.3 yards, tied for the longest in the league. The Vikings are allowing a league-low 4.2 yards on those plays with a league-high four interceptions.
Flores has such a diverse bag of tricks that even experienced quarterbacks have looked completely unprepared.
“You’re guessing a lot of the time out there,” quarterback Jordan Love said. “I think that’s why you’ve got to be great as a quarterback trusting your reads. I think your eyes are really critical against this defense. They’re very vision-based, kind of just melting and flowing with the quarterback, where they’re looking, and I think guys got to be great in their routes and recognizing what coverages they’re getting, what we’ve got, pressure, things like that.”
While Love destroyed the Patriots with a series of bombs last week, that can’t be the plan this week. That doesn’t mean dinking and dunking the ball down the field, but it does mean trying to take advantage of the voids in the secondary created by the extra rushers before those extra rushers clobber the quarterback.
Last week, Buffalo won at Minnesota 23-6. Bills quarterback Josh Allen was 15-of-16 on passes thrown within 10 yards of the line of scrimmage. The quick passes got them going in a game that was 3-3 until late in the first half.
“We’ve to be able to take advantage, get the ball out quick,” Love said. “There was a couple opps in that first game where we missed just being able to get the ball out to guys in space, and we just couldn’t convert on some of those. You’re guessing a lot of times and, when you know they’re coming, you’ve got to find ways to get the ball out because they’re bringing extra guys every time and you know that.
“So, we’ve got to have a great plan, and I think we do have that. It comes down to just seeing it, not panicking when you get those pressures and just getting the ball out quick.”
The second key is running the football. That, of course, is a dicey proposition for the Packers.
However, the last three games, the Vikings allowed 154 rushing yards against the Colts, 230 rushing yards against the Lions and 134 rushing yards against the Bills.
Last week’s game against Buffalo is noteworthy. The Vikings allowed only 3.0 yards per carry, but the Bills kept giving it to James Cook, who thundered away for 2, 3 and 4 yards at a crack. It was ugly football at times but it kept the Bills in manageable situations. He averaged 2.2 yards per carry in the first half but 4.0 yards in the second half.
It was a similar plan of attack with Emanuel Wilson in the home win over the Vikings last year.
“Eventually, you end up making it a game that they weren’t willing to play,” Bills coach Joe Brady told reporters in Buffalo. “That’s a good football team and that’s a great defense. …
“The runs that go for 2 yards, you hope as the game continues on that that 2-yard run can go to 7. You have to stick with it, and it’s really hard with Josh Allen. I’ve got Josh Allen, and you’re running the football. But we felt like that was the way to win this football game, be able to wear the team down and not make it a dropback fest.”
The Packers don’t have James Cook, obviously, though they finally had a bit of a breakthrough last week against the Patriots. Still, they entered Week 10 ranked 32nd in rushing yards per game and 31st in yards per carry. But do they do have Love, which maybe will give Kaleb Johnson and Chris Brooks room to grind out 3 and 4 yards a pop.
Third, the Packers must continue to live in shotgun. While the league is migrating a bit more toward under-center offense, that’s not the way to attack the Vikings. In shotgun, the quarterback has vision on the defense throughout the play. Under center, he has to turn his back for a moment.
When the opposing quarterback is under center, the Vikings blitz 87.5 percent of the time, according to Stats. The Vikings allow almost 1.0 yard less per passing attempt when quarterbacks are under center.
Flores’ plan of attack when facing the Packers has been to blitz even more than usual. In Week 1, Love was blitzed on an astounding 87.0 percent of his dropbacks. (Blitzing used to be about the element of surprise. It was the opposite in this game; Love was not blitzed on six dropbacks and didn’t complete a single pass in those situations.) At Lambeau Field last season, Love was blitzed 83.3 percent of the time, so the communication factor might not matter.
Love knows the Packers must make the Vikings pay. More blitzers, obviously, means fewer players in coverage.

title: Packers-Vikings Thursday Injury Report: Three Promising Updates for Green Bay
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Javon Bullard, the Green Bay Packers’ standout nickel defender, missed a second consecutive day of practice on Thursday. Does that put his status for Sunday’s showdown against the Minnesota Vikings in doubt?
“I ain’t missing no game. I ain’t missing no game, man,” Bullard said after practice. “I care about this team. I care about my brothers, man. So, I’m definitely going to play Sunday. For sure.”
After the team conducted a job-through practice on Wednesday, Bullard was one of five starters who did not practice on Thursday – the big workday of the week with the players in pads.
The Packers lost to the Vikings in Week 1 but enter Sunday’s game having won five of their last six games to improve to 6-3. The Vikings started 6-0 but have lost two consecutive games, though they acquired quarterback Kirk Cousins on Tuesday to perhaps right the ship.
“I think, honestly, that’s a good football team over there,” Bullard said. “They well coached and got a lot of good players. I think they’re out of rhythm right now, just truthfully from what we’re seeing on film, and I think we got to capitalize on it. I think we got to capitalize on them not being in-sync right now.
“I think offensively it’s all about rhythm. If you clicking and moving on the offensive side of the ball, it’s really all about rhythm. Because at one point of time, our offense wasn’t clicking and now look at them. So, it’s all about rhythm. We know they got the players to do so. I think it’s all about one play at a time, dialing into our job and doing what we need to do. We don’t take them lightly at all. That’s a good football team over there, despite their offensive struggles and recent happenings, but that’s a great football team there so we can’t take them lightly.”
Along with Bullard’s optimism, kicker Trey Smack progressed from limited participation to full participation due to an injured right calf. He was the only change on the injury report.
Finally, with the team working in pads, Micah Parsons was on the field. The plan was for him to be integrated into team drills this week. That happened, as Tucker Kraft happened to mention when talking about the growth of the offense.
Micah Parsons races Dani Dennis-Sutton. pic.twitter.com/Ibaf1Ss4dG
“I'd say our offensive line, for sure. We've come together as a unit a lot more – a lot more gel now with these reps and some of the guys we brought in,” Kraft said. “Going to get Sean (Rhyan) back soon, but John (Williams has) been playing great. I'd say our defense right now is on a roll, and we're awaiting the comeback of Micah.”
And then came the money line.
“It's been good out there pressing against Micah. Took on a bull rush from him today. He's trying to back me into Jordan (Love's) lap. … No comment. Maybe it was a stalemate. I'm going to say it's a stalemate. Yeah, he'll be making his return soon. He's looking great, but our defense is rolling, and we just hope that they can remain consistent.”
Along with Bullard, linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin), running back Josh Jacobs (finger), center Sean Rhyan (ankle) and edge Lukas Van Ness (back) did not practice. Those five players aren’t just starters but important starters.
Franklin, who was inactive for the last three games, and Rhyan, who was inactive the last two games, would seem to be long shots to get ready for Sunday given their extended absences. Jacobs will have surgery on Friday, at which point the team will have a more definitive timeline.
The wild card is Van Ness; coach Matt LaFleur gave him a chance to practice on Thursday. That didn’t happen, obviously, but it signals that he is perhaps close.
Josh Jacobs won’t play, but the expectation is Chris Brooks will be activated from injured reserve.
That will be a key return. He’s carved out his niche in the NFL as a pass-protecting back, and that obviously will be vital against a Vikings defense that will blitz from the first game to the last.
However, Kaleb Johnson gave the Packers a breakthrough rushing performance against the Patriots, when MarShawn Lloyd was inactive with a knee injury. Lloyd isn’t on the injury report this week. Plus, Pierre Strong’s versatility has been an asset.
“I think the running game, especially the later you go in the season, the more important it is,” coach Matt LaFleur said. “As the weather turns, especially at home, you better be able to run the football.”
MarShawn Lloyd is not on the injury report. pic.twitter.com/dsfjl3UgvF
One of the Vikings’ best players, linebacker Blake Cashman, did not practice against due to a concussion.
Cashman was one of four Vikings who did not practice. Tight end T.J. Hockenson, defensive end Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins and safety Theo Jackson were the others. Versatile backup Kyle Van Noy did not practice, either.
Their injury report was unchanged from Wednesday.
