title: Packers Thursday Update From Practice: Parsons, Smack, OL, Injured Starters
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – With the biggest game of the season looming on Sunday, the Green Bay Packers kicked off Vikings Week with a season-high 16 players on the injury report. Five of those players are starters.
Plus, rookie kicker Trey Smack was among a long list of players who were listed as limited participation on Wednesday. Smack is dealing with an injured right calf, but coach Matt LaFleur was not concerned.
“Not on what I saw yesterday,” LaFleur said before practice on Thursday. “He went out there and did a good job, so I think he should be full go today.”
The Packers did not have a true practice on Wednesday. If they would have, five starters would not have participated. At Thursday’s practice:
Edge Lukas Van Ness (back), who leads the team in sacks, worked in the rehab group but was not on the field for the start of practice.
“Potentially,” LaFleur said when asked if Van Ness would practice. “We’ll try to loosen him up and see where he’s at.”
S Javon Bullard (ankle/knee) also stretched but did not go out for practice. He played in every game last season and the first nine games of this season. He is fourth on the team with 43 tackles, tied for fifth with four tackles for losses and tied for second with seven passes defensed.
LB Zaire Franklin (shin) missed the last three games following an injury sustained at practice before the Detroit game. He did not practice and seems destined to miss another game.
With Edgerrin Cooper on injured reserve, Franklin inactive and Ty’Ron Hopper missing almost all the game with what was called a chest injury, the Packers essentially played last week with their No. 3 (Isaiah McDuffie) and No. 5 (Nick Niemann) linebackers. Hopper was limited participation on Wednesday – due to illness, not injury – and practiced again on Thursday.
C Sean Rhyan (ankle) went down during the opening series at Detroit, then missed the last two games. LaFleur called him “day-to-day” on Wednesday but he did not practice on Thursday. John Williams, presumably, will start again.
RB Josh Jacobs (finger) will have surgery on Friday, LaFleur said. That’s when the team will have a better handle on his timeline; the early indication is it was a “clean” break and he might be back after missing only two games.
Here’s Zeitler and Belton working a combo drill today. pic.twitter.com/zHrLGjgQbr
Jordan Morgan will start at left tackle, Anthony Belton will start at right tackle and John Williams probably will start at center.
What about the guard positions? Based on the start of practice, it might be Laken Tomlinson at left guard and Kevin Zeitler at right guard, though that comes with the enormous asterisk that whatever the team shows at practice might not be (and oftentimes has not been) the same as how the team lines up in the game.
“Interested to see how it plays out this week with Zeitler, Laken, all of that and just how that’ll shake out,” offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich said on Tuesday. “That’s going to be big, but I like what I’ve seen from Zeitler in there. When he went in and played, he did a really nice job. So, it’ll be interesting to see how it plays out.”
Same as yesterday, Packers not practicing today: Bullard Jacobs Franklin Rhyan Whyle Van Ness Here is Micah Parsons. pic.twitter.com/xHScvBXWhK
Star edge rusher Micah Parsons went through drills with reporters present on Thursday. The goal was to have him take part in team drills this week; the Packers worked in full pads, so this would be a big day.
Parsons and running back Chris Brooks had their return-to-play window opened last week and receiver/returner Skyy Moore had his opened this week. They also were on the practice field.
“Well, he’s a big-time weapon, so if he’s able to go, that will definitely boost our returns, and then also we’ll see how we use him on offense,” LaFleur said of Moore.
The Vikings signed running back Damon Bankston to their practice squad. He served two stints on the Packers’ practice squad so might be willing to share a little intel.
On Wednesday, Vikings general manager Nolan Teasley explained why they reacquired quarterback Kirk Cousins at Tuesday’s trade deadline.
“He made sense for a lot of reasons,” he said. “There's familiarity with the offense, with the organization, with the coaching staff. His level of play; his production to this season; and everything just aligned. The quarterback position is one that can impact the entire team, and this roster, in all honesty, has earned the right to explore the potential to maximize where we can take this thing.”
The teams will release updated injury reports after they are done practicing on Thursday. Until then, here are the reports from Wednesday.

title: Here Are Packers’ 2027 Draft Picks After Potential Double-Whammy
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers reaped the rewards from the excellent additions in their 2022 draft class, then hoped to benefit even further from their departures in free agency.
This past offseason, the Packers let linebacker Quay Walker, receiver Romeo Doubs and left tackle Rasheed Walker go in free agency. Along with quarterback Malik Willis, who provided two superlative seasons as the backup quarterback after being acquired for a seventh-round pick, the Packers hoped they’d benefit from four top compensatory picks.
It hasn’t quite worked out the way the Packers were hoping.
Willis, as expected, signed a big contract with the Dolphins in free agency. Based on the $22.5 million average of his three-year contract, the Packers were in line to get a third-round compensatory pick.
Doubs was the odd man out at receiver, with the Packers choosing to give second contracts to Christian Watson and Jayden Reed rather than Doubs. He signed a four-year contract worth $17 million per season with the Patriots, which put the Packers in line to gain a fourth-round compensatory pick.
The Packers opted to go older and cheaper at linebacker with Zaire Franklin, so they let Quay Walker sign a three-year contract worth $13.5 million per season with the Raiders. That was projected to net the Packers a fifth-round compensatory pick.
Left tackle is a premium position – and is paid like one – so the Packers believed Rasheed Walker would land a big contract in free agency that would fetch them at least a fourth-round pick and possibly a third-round pick.
Compensatory picks are awarded by the league via a secret formula. Nick Korte of OverTheCap.com has mostly cracked that code – so much so that his expertise wound up killing a trade . Comp picks are based mostly on average annual salary but playing time is a factor.
Injuries have taken a bite out of the playing time for Willis and Doubs, and it might cost the Packers.
Malik Willis going on IR could be very problematic for the Packers' 2027 compensatory picks. Missing at least 4 games looks like it could be enough to knock down the round the Packers get for Willis going to Miami from the 3rd round to the 4th round. https://t.co/IxAqOG0doB
The Dolphins placed Willis on injured reserve this week due to a groin injury that had him looking like a shell of himself in the loss to the Lions. The hope is he’ll be back in four weeks, but there’s no guarantee.
“The injury had progressed enough where the medical team believed he needed the rest,” Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley told reporters. “It started as a groin injury that worked to his core. I'm not going to get into medical details because that's not my expertise. He'll get second opinions this week. You're going to ask questions, surgery, non-surgery. He's going to get more input this week and make a decision in our hopes that he'll be back after his four weeks. Which in time, if healthy, he'll return.”
In the latest projections at OverTheCap.com , the Packers are in line to get a fourth-round pick for Willis. A prolonged absence wouldn’t move the pick back another round but it would practically guarantee it wouldn’t rebound back into the third.
That’s huge. A third-round compensatory pick would have landed at around No. 101 overall. This year, the first of the fourth-round compensatory picks was made at No. 133.
Doubs spent last week’s Packers-Patriots game on injured reserve. Because he will miss at least four games, his compensatory pick fell from the fourth round to the fifth round. This year, the last of the fourth-round comp picks was at No. 140 and the first of the fifth-round comp picks was at No. 173.
Quay Walker has started all nine games for the Raiders, so the Packers remain in line to get a fifth-round pick.
In one of the more surprising developments in free agency, there was no market at all for Rasheed Walker. He wound up signing with the Panthers; his contract wasn’t even big enough to merit a compensatory pick.
So, the Packers hit the maximum of four compensatory picks with edge Kingsley Enagbare, whose one-year, $10 million deal with the Jets was projected to be worth a sixth-round pick. He’s started all eight games so that pick has stayed in the sixth round.
Once upon a time, the Packers were in line to have perhaps six of the top 140 picks in the loaded 2027 draft class.
They had no first-round pick from the Micah Parsons trade, but they had one pick in the second round, two picks in the third round (their pick and the Willis pick), three picks in the fourth round (their pick, the Rashan Gary trade and the Doubs pick) and two picks in the fifth round (their pick and the Quay Walker pick).
Now, based on OTC’s projected draft order through Week 9 , these could be their picks.
Second round: No. 53 (their pick).
Third round: No. 85 (their pick).
Fourth round: No. 112 (Rashan Gary trade), No. 120 (their pick) and No. 133 (Willis pick).
Fifth round: No. 158 (their pick), No. 171 (Doubs pick), No. 173 (Quay Walker pick).
Sixth round: No. 184 (Dontayvion Wicks trade), No. 214 (Enagbare pick).
Seventh round: No. 241 (their pick).
At the end of training camp in 2025, the Packers acquired offensive tackle Darian Kinnard from the Eagles for a sixth-round pick in 2027. Before this year’s draft, the Packers traded receiver Dontayvion Wicks to the Eagles for a fifth-round pick in 2026 and a sixth-round pick in 2027. The Eagles have one of the worst records in the NFL, so Green Bay could wind up picking near the top of the sixth round.
At the end of training camp this year, the Packers acquired running back Kaleb Johnson from the Steelers for a sixth-round pick in 2028 and tight end Mark Redman from the Rams for seventh-round pick in 2028. So, those trades will have no impact on the upcoming draft.

title: Packers-Vikings Wednesday Injury Report: Huge List Filled With Big Names
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers kicked off their biggest week of the season with their longest injury report of the year.
Officially, the Packers did not practice on Wednesday as they get ready for Sunday’s showdown against the Minnesota Vikings. If they would have, five starters would not have practiced and a total of 16 players were dealing with one issue or another.
Nickel Javon Bullard (ankle/knee), linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin), running back Josh Jacobs (finger), center Sean Rhyan (ankle), edge Lukas Van Ness (back) and tight end Josh Whyle (concussion) would not have practiced.
Rhyan was injured during the opening series at Detroit. So, he missed most of that game and then the next two games. Coach Matt LaFleur said Rhyan could “potentially” return this week, but that he would not have practiced on Wednesday might not be a good sign for Sunday.
That means John Williams could be in line for his third career start – and his first against the most aggressive defense in the league.
“Banked reps and experience, you can't beat that,” quarterback Jordan Love said. “If we were on a away game, it would be even more critical because sometimes John having his head between his legs, those are the guys that got to communicate a lot of looks. So, it'll be good for John to be at home, he'll be able to see everything and make all those calls.”
Franklin has missed the last three games due to an injury sustained at practice before the Detroit game.
Finally, Van Ness was a noteworthy addition. He played 32 of the 63 snaps against New England and contributed one tackle. He leads the team with 4.5 sacks.
The questions on the offensive line run deeper than center. Left guard Aaron Banks (knee/hip) would have been limited participation, a continuation of a season filled with injuries. He’s played only 137 snaps. Of his three starts, he was unable to go the distance against the Jets in Week 2 or the Patriots last week.
When Banks was knocked out of the New England game, Kevin Zeitler made his Packers debut. Well, he would have been limited participation, as well, with an ankle injury.
Linebacker Ty’Ron Hopper, who played only two defensive snaps vs. the Patriots due to a pregame chest injury, would have been limited due to illness; the chest is not mentioned on the injury report.
Kicker Trey Smack (right calf) and receiver Savion Williams (groin) were listed as limited participation, as well.
One starter not on the injury report is Love. He was knocked to the turf at one point last week and got up flexing his left hand.
“It was just one of those weird ones where it just get hits, so it’s fine,” he said.
Receiver Skyy Moore was designated for return after missing the last four games with an ankle injury. He is averaging 16.0 yards per punt return, highlighted by a 63-yarder against the Jets, and 27.5 yards per kickoff return. Both figures lead the team.
On offense, he caught seven passes for only 35 yards.
“He's been such a great returner for us,” Love said. “It'll definitely be huge to get him back and I'm grateful that we're able to get him back this week.”
Running back Chris Brooks (ankle) and edge Micah Parsons (knee/illness), who are entering their second week of practice after being designated for return, would have been limited. Brooks would be a big addition against the Vikings’ blitzing defense.
The big news in Minnesota – other than trading for Kirk Cousins – is that star linebacker Blake Cashman is in the concussion protocol. That’s never good news for any team or player, but that’s especially noteworthy considering the Vikings are coming off a Monday night game, so Cashman will have a day less to recover.
“He had the stinger evaluation going on and then did end up taking a hit, or more than likely giving a hit, later on in that game. He is currently in the concussion protocol,” Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell told reporters. “Obviously, short week. He's doing really, really well, but I'll keep you guys posted on him as we go through the week.”
Cashman leads the Vikings with 76 tackles, including seven tackles and two tackles for losses in Week 1. He’s in the top three on the team with 4.5 sacks, eight tackles for losses, 10 quarterback hits and seven passes defensed. Cashman is 10th in the league in tackles. From that group, nobody has more sacks, tackles for losses, quarterback hits or pass breakups.
In fact, no player with even 50 tackles has 10 quarterback hits. Cashman and Tampa Bay’s Josiah Trotter (70 tackles) are the only players with 60-plus tackles and seven PBUs. He is an elite player.
“Cash is an important part of our defense,” defensive coordinator Brian Flores said last season. “He’s a big part of what we do defensively from a communication standpoint, just an athleticism, football acumen. Getting other guys in the right positions, leadership. He does a great job.”

title: Packers Wednesday Practice Update: Walking Fine Line With Blitzing Vikings
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Green Bay Packers coach Matt LaFleur scrapped Wednesday’s practice in favor of a jog-through. That means less time on the practice field to get the offensive line in order for Sunday’s showdown against the Minnesota Vikings.
There’s no doubt that Jordan Morgan will start at left tackle and Anthony Belton will start at right tackle. After that, it’s anyone’s guess.
Well, not anyone’s guess. LaFleur has a handle on who will be the starting guards for the NFC North showdown at Lambeau Field. Will it be Aaron Banks at left guard and Laken Tomlinson at right guard with the No. 1 line for a third consecutive week? Or will Kevin Zeitler start at right guard, Tomlinson shift back to left guard and Banks move to the bench?
“We have an idea where we’re going to go. I’m going to hold that ‘til Sunday,” LaFleur said.
Plus, center Sean Rhyan, who suffered an ankle injury during the opening series at Detroit, could return to the practice field after essentially missing the last three games. John Williams has filled in admirably – and, obviously, could start against the Vikings given the team will have only two real practices this week.
“I think there’s a reason that we brought Sean back here and paid him, because I think he was playing really good football, and so he’s a starter for a reason,” LaFleur said. “Not to take anything away from John, I think the job John’s done is remarkable. To be able to come in there with little to no experience and to be able to play the way he’s done and set the table for the rest of the front and the guys on offense, I think it’s been remarkable.
So, to review, the Packers could have new starters at each of the interior positions. That lack of cohesion could be a factor against the Vikings. According to Stat Rankings, they blitz 75.3 percent of the time. The Buccaneers are a distant second at 45.4 percent.
Rhyan has a couple games of experience with Tomlinson at left guard. He has none with Zeitler at right guard. The Packers haven’t played a single snap this season with Rhyan joined by any combination of Banks/Tomlinson/Zeitler.
The Packers, of course, haven’t been able to build any continuity on the offensive line all season. Continuity is a big thing, especially in their biggest defensive test since the Week 1 loss to the Vikings. But talent is a big thing, too.
In that first game, the starting guards were Donovan Jennings and Jacob Monk. They entered that game with one career start – Monk at center at Minnesota in Week 18 of last season. Whoever the Packers will turn to on Sunday will have infinitely more experience.
“I think the biggest thing is just getting all 11 on the same page with all the different looks that you get,” LaFleur said. “You’re going to get pressure, and you’re probably going to get pressure in almost every situation.
“Just getting all those guys, up front especially, on the same page – we had some meltdowns at the end of the game that really cost us, where we didn’t have our guys on the same page, and one, we got knocked off a block, one of the sack/fumbles we miscommunicated protection.”
Micah Parsons returned to practice last week, where he was limited to individual drills for all three practices. The plan is for Parsons to progress to team drills this week. He won’t be on the field on Wednesday, though, due to illness.
Speaking of injured players, receiver/returner Skyy Moore spent the last four games on injured reserve with a high-ankle sprain and linebacker/captain Zaire Franklin missed the last three games due to an injured shin. LaFleur said he is “hopeful” they will return this week.
The Vikings beat the Packers in Week 1 with Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz as their quarterbacks. Their offense is among the worst in the league, though, ranking 27th with just 18.3 points per game. So, they sent a third-round pick to Las Vegas to bring back Kirk Cousins, who started for Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell in 2022 and the first half of 2023 before he sustained a torn Achilles in the Packers-Vikings game at Lambeau.
“Yeah, he’ll be out there,” said LaFleur, who coached Cousins while they were in Washington. “He’ll be starting, I’m fairly confident of that. Obviously, he’s got familiarity with their system. Even if he didn’t, he’s a really intelligent guy, and I think he’s been playing at a high level. I’m surprised they didn’t get more for him, quite honestly. I was shocked when I saw what they traded him for. It was mind blowing to me.”
Cousins is 5-4-1 with the Vikings against the Packers. He has seven games of a passer rating of at least 118.
In eight starts with the Raiders, Cousins ranks 11th in the league in passer rating, fifth in passing yards and second in touchdowns. For some perspective, Jordan Love is ninth in rating, first in yards and third in touchdowns.

title: Texans' 3 Biggest Keys to Victory vs. Browns in Week 10 Matchup
full_text:
The Houston Texans have a pivotal Week 10 game on the horizon against the Cleveland Browns , where a win would take them just one game away from getting back to a .500 record, and put them one step closer to clawing back into the AFC playoff picture.
However, taking home a win in this week's road trip against Cleveland is shaping up to be a task a bit easier said than done. Not only is this Browns team a surprising 5-4 through the first half of the season, but the Texans are heading into this game with multiple key injuries to account for.
That means for Houston, they'll have to hone in on a select few keys to victory in a select few areas of the game in order to secure that much-needed win, and continue building momentum before their short week of preparation for Week 11.
With that in mind, let's break down the Texans' three biggest keys to victory in this weekend's matchup against the Browns:
The Browns' passing defense could make things a bit tougher for the Texans through the air, especially with a talent like cornerback Denzel Ward likely locking down his side of the field . But where Houston could expose Cleveland's defense is within the run game.
Cleveland's run defense through the first half of the season has not been the most consistent. They rank 27th in opposing rushing yards allowed and 28th in rushing yards per attempt. On six occasions this season, the Browns have alllowed over 125 opposing rushing yards, and they're 2-4 in those same games.
If the Texans can lean on Woody Marks––and maybe even David Montgomery if he's deemed available for Sunday––for a strong showing, even without a fully healthy offensive line, that's an easy route for Houston to gain a leg up on an otherwise solid Browns defense.
The Texans were finally able to tweak some of their penalty issues in their latest matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers. Houston incurred just six penalties for 36 yards in Week 9, which was a much better result than the past few weeks in which this team had shot up towards the top of the league in total flags and yards given up from penalties.
However, that success in the penalty category has to continue moving in the right direction for the Texans in the second half of the season. Especially in a game like this where Houston will be without multiple key starters, the margin for error becomes a bit thinner than usual.
So for the Texans' offensive line in particular , limit the holds, the false starts, and the illegal shifts, and Houston can take advantage of a team in the Browns who have also struggled when it comes to penalties––as they currently lead the NFL in total penalties called against them with 82 (over nine per game).
The Texans will be without Danielle Hunter for the first time of his tenure in Houston this Sunday, as he's been ruled out with a hamstring injury that was seemingly suffered earlier this week in practice.
There's no doubt his loss is a big hit to the Texans' pass rush. However, being without Hunter only increases the responsibilities someone like All-Pro edge rusher and current NFL sack leader Will Anderson has on Sunday to make the job a bit more difficult for Deshaun Watson and the Browns offense.
The only problem? Anderson's status is also in question for Sunday. He's been listed as questionable due to an ankle injury suffered in Thursday's practice, and had left him as a DNP for the following day.
For one, the Texans need to hope that Anderson is good to give it a go against the Browns. If he's out, the task gets even tougher for this defense and their overall pass rush. But if Anderson is indeed healthy, he has to bring his A-game for a Defensive Player of the Year-level performance to keep this unit afloat.

title: Texans Need This Veteran to Step Up With Danielle Hunter Out vs. Browns
full_text:
The Houston Texans are officially without Danielle Hunter this weekend against the Cleveland Browns.
After Hunter had been deemed a limited participant in the Texans' team practice on Thursday with a hamstring injury, to then turn to a DNP one day later, the decision was quickly made for Houston to sit out their veteran pass rusher for Week 10.
Houston #Texans Friday Injury Report & Game Status Report for Week 10 at the Cleveland Browns: pic.twitter.com/qrw9og0Fa0
There's no doubt that losing Hunter is a significant loss for the Texans–– no matter how long the timeline for his absence is.
Hunter has been a massive part of the Texans' pass-rush success since he arrived back in 2024. This season, he's been active in each of Houston's eight games to this point, recording 19 tackles, three TFLs, four sacks, and a forced fumble.
In fact, Hunter has yet to miss a single game for the Texans throughout his two years in the building. He's had a perfect 17-game attendance in both 2024 and 2025, and was on pace to do the same again this year after being active for all eight games before.
But this week against the Browns, the Texans will have to improvise without Hunter as a piece of their defensive puzzle. And keeping that in mind, it means one key veteran on Houston's defensive line will need to step up for a big game in his place–– which is none other than Jadeveon Clowney.
Throughout the Texans' season so far, we've seen Clowney established in his role as the third defensive end on Houston's front; a valuable rotational piece operating behind Anderson and Hunter for depth and pass-rushing prowess in the stints that either of them are resting on the sidelines.
And it's a role that Clowney has performed rather solidly in. Through the six games he's been healthy for, Clowney has put together 12 tackles, four TFLs, and 3.5 sacks despite playing in just 37% of Houston's defensive snaps.
That 37% snap share is the lowest that Clowney has seen on any team throughout his entire career . He's being used less often than ever, but still remaining a potent contributor off the edge who can get to the quarterback and be a stout run-stopper.
However, when someone as pivotal as Hunter is taken completely out of the equation due to a hamstring injury, the role for Clowney quickly shifts into one that is way more important than before.
Clowney becomes the clear starter right next to Will Anderson (so long as he's also healthy), and his snap count likely jumps to around 70% of the Texans' reps on the defensive side; a similar count to what Hunter sees when he's on the field.
That means Clowney will be on the field for twice as much as he is on a week-to-week basis, and his abilities as a stout pass-rusher and run defender become even more vital than they were before as the Texans' third defensive end. More snaps mean more down-to-down responsibilities.
The Texans have a lot of talented players on their defense, yet their depth off the edge isn't nearly as strong when Hunter is out of the equation.
That puts the challenge on Clowney's shoulders to step up and be a worthwhile complement to Anderson Jr. throughout the day in Cleveland as someone who can limit the Browns' ground game, and getting a handful of pressures sent in on Deshaun Watson in the process.
While losing Hunter undoubtedly stings for the Texans over any stretch of time, having an experienced and productive depth piece behind him in Clowney might make the absence a bit easier to stomach.
Time will tell if Clowney will be able to excel in his expanded role this weekend against the Browns. But if he can, the road to a second straight victory for Houston becomes a whole lot easier to imagine.

title: Texans' Final Week 10 Injury Report vs. Browns Brings More Bad News
full_text:
The Houston Texans have released their third and final injury report heading into their Week 10 matchup against the Cleveland Browns .
And simply put, their injury report for this week is a lengthy one–– and it only grew larger over the course of the week in practice .
The Texans will be dealing with several absences heading into the weekend, and possibly more, depending on how the status of a few others shifts leading up to Sunday's kickoff.
Let's break down the latest from the Texans' injury report after the team released everyone's official statuses on Friday afternoon.
LB Azeez Al-Shaair (groin/personal) TE Brevin Jordan (finger/foot) DE Danielle Hunter (hamstring) WR Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) OL Keylan Rutledge (neck/shoulder)
CB Jaylin Smith (hamstring) RB David Montgomery (groin) LB Jake Hummel (groin) DE Will Anderson (ankle) OL Wyatt Teller (back/illness) OL Trent Brown (wrist)
So there's a lot to take away from the Texans' injury report. Yet, the biggest and perhaps most surprising absence that Houston will be faced with this weekend surrounds their veteran star edge rusher Danielle Hunter, who's been ruled out after logging a limited practice on Thursday and didn't participate on Friday.
As to how severe Hunter's injury is long-term, we don't really know yet. All we know is that Hunter likely suffered a hamstring injury during practice on Thursday, and it's serious enough to keep him out for one week–– and possibly more, knowing that the Texans are on a short week for Week 11.
Without him, Jadeveon Clowney becomes an immediately more important piece on the Texans' defensive line, and will likely start next to Will Anderson Jr. if he's indeed ready to go (more on him in a minute).
Azeez Al-Shaair is out for the Texans once again, seemingly with another groin injury that's kept him limited throughout the past several weeks .
And Al-Shaair's absence is notable for the Texans. He's a team captain, a Pro Bowl talent at the linebacker position, and the green dot signal-caller on Houston's defense who's often heralded for his communication and play recognition in the middle of the field in the front seven.
Without him, keep an eye on either Jake Hansen or Wade Woodaz to step up in the linebacker room as the starter who will play next to Henry To'oTo'o in the second level of the defense.
Onto the offensive side of the ball, the Texans will ultimately be without their rookie left guard Keylan Rutledge , who suffered a stinger, according to DeMeco Ryans, and didn't practice throughout the entire week in all three team sessions.
Without Rutledge, KPRC2 's Aaron Wilson reported that fourth-round rookie Febechi Nwaiwu––not Wyatt Teller––will be the next man up as the Texans' left guard. And that's a bit of an eye-catching decision from the Houston brass, if it holds leading up to gameday.
Nwaiwu has yet to be activated for a game this season. But should see that trend change in a big way for this weekend as a starter on the team's trip to Cleveland.
Another noteworthy name from the Texans' lineup who won't be playing on Sunday: their big trade acquisition of Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring), who was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, but would not suit up for Thursday or Friday.
And knowing that Harrison Jr. is dealing with a hamstring issue, there's a possibility that the Texans' wideout suffered that hamstring tweak in the middle of Houston's team session on Wednesday, and will now be forced out for a period of time.
Again, with the Texans having a short week to prepare for their Week 11 game against the Indianapolis Colts for next Thursday, that could wind up turning Harrison Jr.'s absences into one spanning multiple games, depending on how severe his hamstring issue really is.
As for those who still have a chance to play this Sunday in Cleveland, the two most important names to keep a watch on from now until inactives are revealed this weekend are David Montgomery and Will Anderson Jr.
Montgomery's case is simple: he's been dealing with a groin injury dating back to Week 5 against the Tennessee Titans, has been out for the past three games, but was a full practice participant on Friday, that gives him hope to finally get back on the field for Week 10.
However, for Anderson Jr., he deserves a bit more attention for his situation. He was a limited participant in practice on Thursday due to an ankle issue, and would inevitably not practice on Friday as a DNP.
If he and Danielle Hunter are forced to miss Week 10, that'd be a devastating loss for the potency of this Texans' pass rush. So stay tuned for more on his status in the coming days.

title: What Texans WR Nico Collins Said About Facing Browns CB Denzel Ward
full_text:
THe Houston Texans will see their No. 1 wide receiver Nico Collins face up against one of the better cornerbacks in the NFL this weekend as they take on the Cleveland Browns –– and that's none other than Denzel Ward.
Ward has been at the top of his game for multiple seasons in the league now, logging five Pro Bowl appearances throughout his nine years pro, and could be on the verge of another selection by the end of 2026.
Pro Football Focus has graded Ward as the No. 1 cornerback in the NFL through the first 10 weeks (90.5), as he's totaled some impressive stats with 26 tackles, two forced fumbles, three interceptions, three PBUs, and ranks top 10 in the NFL for passer rating allowed (42.5) and yards per reception allowed (7.2).
So there's no doubt this week against Ward will be a tall task for Collins to take on. However, he's certainly accepting that challenge to take on one of the best cornerback matchups in the NFL.
When Collins was asked on Thursday about the matchup he's set to see this weekend against Ward, there's no denying that he's excited to face the challenge of taking on one of the best cornerbacks in the NFL, but also facing a strong Browns secondary as a collective.
"Look forward to it, man. Denzel, man, been one hell of a player for a long time in this league. Great Pro Bowler, man. Great with his feet, hands, technique," Collins said to KPRC2's Aaron Wilson . "It's a great feeling to go against the best in this league, man."
"One of the best secondaries, great corners, great safeties. So, got to come ready... It's going to be a great weekend, man... All respect to Denzel, man. He’s one of the great corners in this league for a long time, and it's going to be a great game, man. Just excited to go against a high-level corner like that."
This season, Collins hasn't quite been the explosive downfield threat that he has been throughout the past two seasons. However, he also hasn't seen quite as many targets as he's been accustomed to in both 2024 and 2025 .
While Collins has averaged eight or more targets a game through the last two seasons, that number has shrunk to just 6.5 throughout the five games he's played in 2026. He's averaged 4.7 receptions and 64 yards per game, along with four touchdown receptions.
And this week, it might be tough for Collins to get those numbers back on track when facing one of the best cornerbacks in the NFL, but also one of the better secondaries in the NFL with what the Browns have to offer.
As a part of their impressive 5-4 record to date, the Browns also rank sixth in the NFL for passing yards allowed (1,809), eighth for passing touchdowns allowed (12), and fifth in net yards per passing attempt (5.6).
Cleveland's offense has had its own holes that have been exposed throughout the first half of the season––considering they're ranked 29th in total points––but their defense has remained a calling card for a lot of their early success.
So not only will this weekend be a tough outing for Collins with his matchup against Ward, but the same could be said for C.J. Stroud and his plans to attack the Browns through the air.
And if that limited day does happen to be the case for Stroud and their offensive attack, the road to victory for the Texans tends to become a whole lot tougher.

title: Texans at Risk of Losing Starting Offensive Lineman for Browns Game
full_text:
The Houston Texans could be without one key name on their offensive line for Week 10 against the Cleveland Browns.
And that's none other than their rookie left guard, Keylan Rutledge, who is at risk of missing his first-ever regular season game on Sunday.
According to KPRC2 's Aaron Wilson, Rutledge is still dealing with stinger symptoms from the injury that he suffered earlier this week in practice, thus making him unlikely to play on Sunday against the Browns.
#Texans starting left guard Keylan Rutledge, first-round pick, still dealing with stinger symptoms (neck, shoulder), per source. Considered unlikely to play vs. #Browns , barring unexpected change, and team is prepping rookie Febechi Nwaiwu for his 1st #NFL start, per sources
Without Rutledge in the lineup, fourth-round rookie Febechi Nwaiwu is expected to get the start at left guard, per Wilson.
There's no doubt that losing Rutledge is a notable loss for a Texans offensive line that's remained relatively healthy all season long. The only injury they've had to deal with through the first half of the season has been when Ed Ingram missed Weeks 2 and 3 due to a groin injury.
Throughout the first half of his rookie season, Rutledge has collected an overall grade of 45.6 via Pro Football Focus , which ranks 71st out of 75 eligible guards.
He's totaled over 500 offensive snaps played with two penalties, two sacks, three hits, and a whopping 25 pressures allowed through eight games.
Despite the numbers not exactly looking optimal for Rutledge, Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans has gone on record saying how impressed he's been with their first-round pick over the course of his rookie season due to his consistency.
“Keylan, he's stepped in and done some really good things for us," Ryans said heading into Week 9. "He’s played aggressive. He’s had some challenges as a rookie, but he’s weathered it really well. One bad play doesn't determine how his game goes. He's able to eliminate a bad play and move onto the next play."
"He's done a really good job of being steady in there; consistent force for us there on the inside. And I'm pleased to see how the rest of his season continues to progress. But, he's done a good job as a rookie. “Sometimes you lose sight that he’s a rookie, because he's been one of our most consistent guys up front."
Since the injury seems to be a minor stinger, we shouldn't expect Rutledge to be out of the lineup for long, even if he has missed back-to-back practices this week, and could be in to miss Week 10 against the Browns.
It is worth mentioning that the Texans do operate on a short week for Week 11, as they'll be facing the Indianapolis Colts on Thursday night. So that could make Rutledge's status a bit more interesting to watch unravel over the course of next week.
But until he's officially deemed ready to play once again, the Texans are expected to roll with another rookie at left guard in Nwaiwu; someone who showcased his positional versatility throughout his time in college at Oklahoma, and might be due for his first NFL start this Sunday .
Nwaiwu has been largely a non-factor on the Texans' offensive line so far this season, having frequently been a gameday inactive for most weeks.
However, it seems that Houston's coaching staff has built up some trust in Nwaiwu based on what he's showcased throughout his time in practice.
Knowing that the Texans also plan to start Nwaiwu over a more experienced name like Wyatt Teller speaks to how they feel about the young talent they have in the building and his ability to step in for Rutledge if he does ultimately miss out of Week 10.

title: Texans Cut Veteran RB to Sign WR Nikko Remigio to 53-Man Roster
full_text:
The Houston Texans have done some roster shuffling ahead of their Week 10 matchup against the Cleveland Browns .
One of those moves was to bring in former Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver and return specialist Nikko Remigio to the 53-man roster, who was recently waived from the Chiefs because of their recent trade deadline move to bring in wide receiver Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts.
But for the Texans to bring in Remigio, they had to make a move to cut another name within their roster to meet the NFL's 53-man roster limit.
And in this case, the Texans decided to let go a veteran in their running back room to make that space–– which was Dare Ogunbowale.
Ogunbowale was picked up from the Texans earlier in September from the Las Vegas Raiders' practice squad, which was where he had resided dating back to August after Houston had decided not to re-sign him this offseason.
And in the brief time that Ogunbowale was in the building for the Texans, he provided a bit of depth in the running back room , but also brought some of his special teams prowess to the table for a team that was struggling in that phase of the game.
Ogunbowale ultimately played 62 special teams snaps (43% snap share) and 16 offensive snaps (5% snap share) within the five games that he was with the Texans this season.
However, heading into Week 10, there's a chance that the Texans' running back depth could be looking a bit healthier than it has been throughout their past few meetings.
More specifically, David Montgomery's status is trending up from his groin injury suffered back in Week 5, as he was able to be a limited participant in Thursday's practice before facing the Browns.
So if Montgomery is healthy for this weekend, that leaves the Texans with four running backs on the roster, including Ogunbowale.
And in the case of Ogunbowale, he's been a nice piece to incorporate on the special teams side, but not as much on the offensive end that makes his spot on the roster a bit more expendable. In the five games he had played with Houston, he had zero rushing stats recorded, and just one reception for three yards.
Therefore, as the Texans decided to add another name to their receiver room–– likely in an effort to bolster their special teams–– it only made sense for Houston to cut ties with Ogunbowale in the running back room.
That means, for the Texans' running back room, they'll have three on their 53-man roster for Week 10 in Cleveland: that's Montgomery, Woody Marks, and Emari Demercado.
As to who will be available for that contest against the Browns remains to be seen, considering Montgomery was a limited participant on Thursday, and Marks didn't practice at all on Thursday with a knee injury.
At the very least, though, Ogunbowale won't be a part of that unit and will now move on from Houston to try and land on his feet somewhere else for the second half of the 2026 campaign.

title: 3 Texans Predictions That Could Define Week 10 vs. Browns
full_text:
The Houston Texans' Week 10 game against the Cleveland Browns is slowly approaching around the corner.
And it's a game for the Texans that'll be extremely important to take advantage of. They'll be taking the road trying to climb one game closer to .500, face up against another AFC Wild Card contender, and will be trying to build upon the 44-point outing they saw last weekend against the LA Chargers.
So what can we expect from the Texans in this game against the Browns? Will they rise to the occasion for a second straight win, or fall into similar pitfalls that they have in their five losses so far this season?
Well, let's sort through a batch of three bold predictions for the Texans to take our chances at guessing how things will unravel in Cleveland on Sunday:
This season has looked a whole lot different than 2025's output on the offensive side of the ball for Houston. The Texans are scoring a lot of points on a week-to-week basis, looking strong through their air attack thanks to some C.J. Stroud heroics , and they'll be looking to continue that trend in Week 10.
The Browns, while they haven't allowed 30 points to an opponent dating back to Week 1 against the Jacksonville Jaguars, have certainly gotten close a few times. And on top of that, they haven't really played a high-powered offense like the Texans many times this season.
If the Texans can keep their momentum through the air and the offense can continue to limit the penalties setting them back as they did last weekend, 30 points is wildly possible for this team.
So far this season, the Browns are 0-1 in games where they allow 30 points or more, and have yet to score 30 points a game themselves. This might be a simple recipe for Houston's success this weekend.
Last week, we saw Tank Dell get involved in a big way for what was his second game back from his 2024 knee injury . And with that extra involvement, he turned in about as good of a performance as you could expect from him: four receptions on nine targets for 105 yards and a touchdown.
And really, there's no reason why the Texans should stop trying to feed the ball to Dell in Week 10.
He's looking closer and closer to his pre-injury self, is comfortable with the extra workload , has given Houston another layer of playmaking to account for in the wide receiver room, and when he's firing on all cylinders, the better it is for C.J. Stroud.
C.J. Stroud to Tank Dell for the TD 🗣️ HOUvsLAC on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/r0q9mBmr5d
So we'll predict Dell to find the end zone once again in Week 10. It might not be as sweet as last week's, considering that reception marked his first touchdown in nearly two years, but points are points, nonetheless.
The Texans' secondary has not been the ball-hawking, interception-happy unit that they were all throughout last season in their first eight games of this year.
That becomes clear when looking at Houston's interception totals in the secondary. Not one player has recorded more than one interception on the season so far. In all, the Texans' defense has just four interceptions, which makes them one of nine teams in the NFL to log four or fewer interceptions on the season thus far.
It's a result that needs to turn around in the right direction for Houston in the second half of their schedule for this defense to be at it's true elite potential. And there might not be a better time to add onto their interception totals than this game against their former quarterback in Deshaun Watson.
I'll be keeping an eye on Calen Bullock to handle those takeaway duties: Houston's Pro Bowl talent heralded as one of the best ball-hawks at his position throughout the past two seasons, and needs some balls to come his way to hold up that status.

title: Texans' Injury Report Raises Concerns on Woody Marks, Marvin Harrison Jr.
full_text:
The Houston Texans have released their second of three injury reports of the week heading into their upcoming matchup against the Cleveland Browns.
And for one of the few times this season, the Texans' Thursday injury report happened to showcase a few more concerns from what was shown on the first day of practice –– particularly in the case of two key offensive pieces: running back Woody Marks and wide receiver Marvin Harrison.
Let's take a look at the latest on the Texans' injury report only a few days away from Week 10's matchup
LB Azeez Al-Shaair (groin/personal) RB Woody Marks (knee) TE Brevin Jordan (finger/foot) WR Marvin Harrison (hamstring) OL Keylan Rutledge (neck/shoulder)
RB David Montgomery (groin) DE Will Anderson (ankle) DE Danielle Hunter (hamstring)
WR Tank Dell (hand/shoulder) S Reed Blankenship (hand/concussion) CB Jaylin Smith (hamstring) LB Jake Hummel (groin) OL Blake Fisher (thumb)
Something that immediately sticks out from the Texans' Thursday injury report that wasn't present on their previous one: both Marks and Harrison Jr. were DNP in practice with their respective issues.
It'd be a noteworthy, but also rare absence for both players in the event they were set to miss this weekend's action in Cleveland.
Marks (knee) has been active in every game for the Texans so far this season. Throughout the past three weeks since David Montgomery has been sidelined with his groin issue, Marks has been the leader in Houston's backfield, claiming a lion's share of the offensive reps.
During last week's game against the LA Chargers , Marks put together 18 carries for 70 yards (3.9 yards per carry), making it his fourth-straight game logging over 70 all-purpose yards.
If he were to miss any time at all for Week 10, his absence could wind up being significant for a Texans backfield that's been stuck without Montgomery, and could continue to be against the Browns, depending on how his status shifts heading into the weekend.
In the event both were to miss out on Sunday, the Texans would be down to just two players in their running back room: veteran Dare Ogunbowale and recently-signed Emari Demercado.
In Harrison Jr.'s case, he also has yet to miss a game for the Texans this season since his arrival. His only missed game of the season came back in Week 5 when he was with the Arizona Cardinals and was left to sit out knowing that a trade to send him out to Houston was imminent .
His absence––if he were to miss this week with a hamstring ailment––would slim the Texans' receiver room down once more, considering they just had to deal with the loss of Jaylin Noel after Week 7 against the New York Giants .
That means more involvement for Nico Collins, Tank Dell, Xavier Hutchinson, and Kayshon Boutte, and especially so if the Texans' backfield is without its top two contributors in Marks and Montgomery.
Another injury to keep an eye on for someone who still practiced in limited capacity? Defensive end Danielle Hunter, who was not listed on the injury report on Wednesday, yet popped up as a late entry on Thursday with a hamstring issue.
Perhaps it's nothing to worry about for the veteran defender. But those hamstring injuries can be tricky depending on the severity, especially for a 32-year-old edge rusher. So he'll remain a name to monitor alongside Marks and Harrison Jr. as the Texans release their final injury report after Friday's practice.

title: Texans' C.J. Stroud Faces Long Odds in MVP Race at Midseason Mark
full_text:
The first half of the Houston Texans' 2026 season has been filled with some really solid play from quarterback C.J. Stroud .
Stroud is throwing for a career-high 281.4 yards per game on a 64.2% completion rate, along with a 16-2 TD-to-INT ratio. He has the sixth-best passer rating in the NFL at 104.8 and is one of five quarterbacks in the NFL to have thrown two or fewer picks on the season (min. 5 GP).
It's gotten to the point for Stroud where, if he keeps up this same level of production, there might be real questions around whether or not he could enter some MVP discussions as we get deeper and deeper into the season.
However, when looking at his odds heading into Week 10, there's certainly some more work to do before Stroud is considered anything close to true MVP consideration, let alone being a frontrunner for the award.
According to odds from FanDuel Sportsbook , Stroud is currently tied for the eighth-best odds at taking home this year's MVP award (+6000) right alongside Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes.
Seven other quarterbacks find themselves ahead of Stroud's own odds: including Caleb Williams (+5000), Kirk Cousins (+4000), Jordan Love (+750), Trevor Lawrence (+550), Brock Purdy (+550), Josh Allen (+370), and the current frontrunner for the award, Joe Burrow (+145).
It's some pretty nice company for Stroud to be surrounded by. And at the very least, being within those MVP discussions in any capacity is great for his stock this offseason when he's set to hit the negotiation table for his next contract .
However, if Stroud really wants to make a push for that MVP trophy this year–– rather than simply just be in the talks for it–– it's going to take a really dedicated effort over the second half of the schedule to make it happen.
And really, a lot of Stroud's chances simply come down to team record.
At 3-5 for a Texans team that's currently out of the postseason picture, it's really hard to consider the signal-caller of that offense a true MVP candidate, at least at this point in the year.
Now, could the Texans stack up a few wins and change the narrative just a bit ? Most definitely. With nine games left on the regular season schedule and several winnable games ahead for Houston, getting onto the right side of .500 can be within arm’s reach in no time.
But Stroud will need to continue playing at an elite level throughout that timeframe while the Texans are stacking up multiple wins; a task that's been much easier said than done through the first eight games of the year.
At the very least, Stroud deserves to remain on the MVP radar for as long as the Texans still have a fighting chance in the regular season. And if Houston climbs into the playoffs with a 12-5 or 11-6 record on the back of his production, it'll be hard to completely disregard him for the discussion.
So right now, Stroud might be falling a bit behind in the race. But give it a few more weeks, and things might shift for the better to potentially put him within reach of being the Texans' first-ever MVP in franchise history.

title: Texans Rookie Could Be in Line for Increased Usage in Week 10
full_text:
Through the first half of the 2026 season, the Houston Texans' rookie class has been a bit... underwhelming.
While yes, Keylan Rutledge has emerged as a pleasant surprise on the Texans' offensive line, others around the rookie class have either underperformed, or simply haven't gotten utilized as a part of the game plan on a week-to-week basis.
However, for Week 10 against the Cleveland Browns , there's a chance that the Texans could be handing over an increased workload to one member of their rookie class––and that's none other than second-round tight end Marlin Klein.
Throughout most of the season so far, Klein––the Texans' 58th-overall pick in the second round of this past draft––has been a bit of a non-factor within the Texans' offense, or even on the special teams side.
The 6-foot-6, 250-pound tight end out of Michigan played a combined 22 offensive snaps from Weeks 1 to 3, was inactive on game days from Weeks 4 to Week 7, and that was up until he was able to get a few more reps his way after the bye in Week 9 against the LA Chargers.
Klein saw 19 offensive snaps come his way, which was over double his season-high to that point. He also saw nine special teams snaps. The Texans, for the first time this season, made a more concentrated effort to get him involved.
It didn't result in any stats coming Klein's way, and that's certainly something the Texans want to see trend in a different direction. However, knowing he got involved in the offense much more than the prior eight games is certainly a success in itself.
Texans offensive coordinator Nick Caley also made it known that Klein has made "a lot of progress" ahead of the Texans' game against the Chargers, and will look for different situations to put him in moving forward.
“Yeah, no, he's made a lot of progress," Caley said ahead of Week 9. "I mean, all those guys, I feel, have done a good job. [Tight Ends Coach] James Ferentz does a really good job with those guys. He's getting better every single week."
"And again, like anything else, it's about focusing on the process, trying to get better, putting him in different situations, getting him exposure to different areas in the C-gap or off the ball in the run game, and then being able to move him around. It's like anything else. It's a continuous build for a guy like him, but it is for all of us.”
Having five tight ends on the 53-man roster does make the road a bit tougher for Klein to get involved on a consistent basis, which became clear during the first eight games on the schedule.
But now that he's continued to make noticeable progress in the eyes of the coaching staff, it becomes simpler to entrust a bigger workload in him on a week-to-week basis. And that seems likely to continue in Week 10 against the Browns.
That's especially so if one of the Texans' regular tight ends winds up missing any time. On Wednesday's injury report after practice , Brevin Jordan was a DNP due to a finger/foot issue. As it pertains to Klein's role against Cleveland, his status will certainly remain one to keep close watch on.
So looking ahead for Klein, expect to see much more of him within the Texans' offense as the season goes on, which might be able to provide their scoring attack a bit more versatility thanks to his upside as a blocker and a vertical threat in the passing game.
