title: Raiders vs. Seahawks: Breaking Down Who's Under More Pressure
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders hope a quarterback change and a return to Allegiant Stadium can help set them in the right direction. The Raiders and the Seattle Seahawks are at opposite ends of the spectrum. The two teams' endings to last season explain it well.
The Seahawks are the reigning Super Bowl Champions. Las Vegas finished last season with the No. 1 overall pick. Seattle's success led to Kubiak's arrival during the offseason. The Raiders' dismal 2025 campaign landed them their quarterback of the future: Fernando Mendoza.
The Raiders are beginning another chapter in the franchise's storied history. Las Vegas has desperately needed a young, mobile, and accurate quarterback. It appears they finally have one; he just had to ride the bench longer than most No. 1 overall picks.
Las Vegas has taken a cautious approach to Mendoza's development. Raiders' offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko shared his thoughts on what Las Vegas must do to support Mendoza, as there is only so much a rookie can do in his very first start.
“I think every player, especially as they grow, and again, I know I sound like a broken record, but Fernando [Mendoza], all of our players, we ask them to trust their training, trust their assignment, and then go out and make a play and do their job. And that’s when the best players they do play instinctually,” Janocko said earlier this week.
“So, they go out, they rely on that, and that’s part of being successful as a player in this league, is being instinctual. Because if you just run lines on a paper, that’ll take you so far. But it’s about playing the game and then fueling the game. It all comes with experience, and it all comes with just creating that general comfort and feel as you get into a game.”
Seattle started the season expecting to at least push for a playoff spot, if not make a deep postseason run. Las Vegas simply wanted to get their first season under head coach Klint Kubiak off the ground and running smoothly while building the team's connection internally.
The Seahawks will throw all they can at Mendoza to see how prepared he is and how well he works under pressure. The rookie quarterback praised Las Vegas' coaching staff and his teammates for helping him prepare for this moment.
“The coaching staff and I and personnel staff, we’ve watched, I would say, I’ve watched a good amount of film so far in my routine, especially a routine that I’ve modeled, whether it’s Coach [Andrew] Janocko, Coach [Mike] Sullivan, Coach [Klint] Kubiak, ones that they’ve recommended, and also taking from Kirk [Cousins]’s and Aidan [O’Connell]’s past processes,” Mendoza said earlier this week.
“And so, we’ve been doing the same process every week. So, continue on keeping the same thing and keeping the main thing the main thing, which is the process. They’re a very impressive team. They’re one of the best defenses in the league, so it’s going to be a great challenge. I’m excited to do my 1/11th out there.”
They are not under the most pressure to win the game, but the Raiders are the team under the most pressure on Sunday. This is specifically the case for Las Vegas' offense. The Raiders' defense did not make a major change to the starting lineup this week.
After giving Mendoza extra months of preparation and then starting him for the very first time against the team Kubiak won a Super Bowl with at the top of the year, starting Mendoza for the very first time this season unquestionably puts the pressure on Las Vegas.
Again, the pressure isn't necessarily on Las Vegas to win, but its offense has to benefit from Mendoza's arrival. The Raiders can lose, their defense can struggle, and Mendoza can struggle in his very first start. Both would be expected.
Yet Mendoza, at the very least, has to look ready for the moment mentally and physically. That is where the pressure falls for the Raiders on Sunday. Las Vegas' only competition is itself. If their offense looks better under Mendoza than in the past nine games, that is a win in itself.
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: Predicting Raiders' Top Offensive Catalysts Against Seahawks
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders are at a fork in the road right now, as the next three games are daunting.
During this stretch , the Raiders face the Seahawks, Broncos, and Browns, all of whom have above-average to elite defenses. To add another element to this matchup, Fernando Mendoza will make his first career start on Sunday. With that in mind, here are predictions for the Raiders' top offensive players against Seattle.
As mentioned, the No. 1 overall pick is making his NFL debut on Sunday. It's arguably the toughest matchup for a rookie quarterback to walk into in his first career start. Nevertheless, the Mendoza era has started in Las Vegas.
Other than Caleb Williams, Seattle's defense has made life a nightmare for quarterbacks. So if Mendoza struggles, Raider Nation shouldn't panic. Depending on how well Las Vegas' defense holds up, the rookie signal caller may have to throw more often than head coach Klint Kubiak would like.
Because of Las Vegas' porous offensive line, Kubiak will likely deploy quick passes to get the ball out of Mendoza's hands as quickly as possible. Mendoza needs the run game to open up passing lanes. Besides winning this game, making Mendoza as comfortable as possible should be Kubiak's main objective. That also increases the chances the Raiders pull off the upset.
To say the second-year running back has struggled this season would be an understatement. Jeanty hasn't surpassed 27 rushing yards in each of the last five games. If the 22-year-old running back struggles against the Bills and 49ers, Jeanty is facing an uphill battle to produce his first productive outing in weeks.
Now, Mendoza's mobility could open up rushing lanes for Jeanty. Nevertheless, the Boise State product has to be better. He hasn't lived up to the “generational talent” tag when he first entered the 2025 NFL Draft.
Bowers was the primary target in the first nine games, and that will be amplified with Mendoza under center. The rookie quarterback has shown the ability to go through progressions cleanly, but the star tight end will likely be his first read on most dropbacks.
The 23-year-old tight end is averaging nearly 10 targets, 6.8 receptions, and 94 yards per game. Bowers' production should mirror those season-long averages, despite facing one of the best defenses in the league.

title: 3 Things Fernando Mendoza Can't Control in First Raiders Start
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders are set to finally take the field with rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza leading the way. After a long wait, Las Vegas will roll out what they hope will be their last starting quarterback for many seasons to come. First, the Raiders must get through Sunday.
The Raiders' Week 10 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks will present its fair share of challenges. Las Vegas will need to execute at a high level and hope the ball bounces their way a time or two.
Below are three things the Raiders' rookie quarterback cannot control in his very first start, or in general, for that matter.
Las Vegas' offensive line has struggled to open up running lanes this season. Overall, the unit has done relatively well by many statistical measures. Still, the offensive line has spent the past few months working with Kirk Cousins under center; there will naturally be a few hiccups along the way.
If the Raiders' offensive line continues to pass block well and improves their run blocking, Las Vegas quietly has a chance to surprise the Seahawks on Sunday. If the line does not play well, Mendoza, like any quarterback in the league, will also struggle.
The offensive line has its deficiencies, but it probably deserves more credit overall than it has received this season. Some would likely be shocked by how well the unit has graded through nine games. The unit likely ranked even higher before last Sunday's loss.
No matter how the unit performs, it is not on Mendoza. If anything, it is the other way around. Las Vegas' offensive line must protect its rookie quarterback even better than it did for Cousins. Mendoza's mobility should bode well for the unit too, should he use it when possible.
Through the first half, Las Vegas is once again one of the league's worst rushing teams. They are nine games away from that being the case for the fourth straight season. The Raiders' inability to run the ball has hurt the offense and the team as a whole, especially Las Vegas' defense.
In their five losses, the Raiders' offense has been unable to sustain drives, let alone score points, while the game was still competitive. A large part of the reason the offense has struggled is that they can't run the ball. This will eventually negatively impact Mendoza, likely as soon as Sunday.
That problem has plagued the Raiders long before Mendoza or any of the coaches and running backs on the roster arrived.
It would be unreasonable to expect Las Vegas to magically run the ball well consistently simply because Mendoza is starting. If the Raiders cannot get their ground game going, at least marginally better than it has been in the season's first nine games, Mendoza will have a tall task.
The Raiders must get their ground game going on Sunday against the Seahawks, even if that means Mendoza adding two or three runs. Running the ball with Mendoza would give future opposing defenses a legitimate concern that has not been there this season.
In their losses, Las Vegas' defense has failed to play well, and it has been glaringly bad. However, in their wins, the Raiders' defense has shone. The unit has forced the fourth-most turnovers of any defense in the league this season. That is what Mendoza and the Raiders will need on Sunday.
At the very least, Las Vegas' defense has to keep the Seahawks from scoring touchdowns and hope Mendoza finds a rhythm. The unit cannot afford to fall behind early and hope the rookie can beat a Seahawks defense that is playing with a big lead, as has been the case for the Raiders this season.
Regardless of how well the Raiders' defense plays on Sunday, their performance is not on Mendoza, nor is it the rookie's responsibility to compensate should Las Vegas' defense underperform in Week 10.
That said, even though the Seahawks are the better team, I am interested to see how the Raiders' defense responds if Mendoza gets the offense going in the first half. Las Vegas' defense plays better when they know their teammates on offense have their back with points and long drives.
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: Raiders Receive More Fantastic Injury Report News Ahead of Seahawks
full_text:
Jimmy Garoppolo, Brian Hoyer, Aidan O'Connell, Desmond Ridder, Geno Smith, Kenny Pickett, Kirk Cousins.
The Las Vegas Raiders have had a revolving door at quarterback in recent seasons, starting eight different quarterbacks since 2023. The Raiders' roster finally bottomed out in 2025, registering its second straight season with a 10-game losing streak and securing the No. 1 overall pick.
After eclipsing last season's win total in the first half of the season, the Raiders were presented with a chance to smoothly transition into the Mendoza era. Trading Cousins gave Las Vegas' front office a third-round draft pick for a player who was unlikely to be on the team next season.
Despite the natural buzz that comes with the No. 1 overall pick finally getting to start, Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak was sure to emphasize the importance of Las Vegas doing what is necessary as a team to make the fact that they're starting a rookie quarterback an afterthought.
“I think the most important thing, like every week, is that you spend a lot of time worrying about you, worrying about your technique, worrying about studying, worrying about watching tape. Yes, we got to prepare them as coaches for what they’re going to see on the practice field, but as a player, you got to make sure you don’t overlook yourself first," Kubiak said earlier this week.
The Raiders returned to the practice field on Thursday ahead of Mendoza's first career start. With Sunday's matchup against the Seattle Seahawks just days away, Las Vegas appears to be about as healthy as it has been at any point this season.
The Raiders' injury report was light on Wednesday , as Thomas Booker, Trey Zuhn, and Foley Fatukasi participated in a limited fashion. Ian Thomas was listed but participated fully. Zuhn's participation, despite being listed with a concussion-related issue, was promising.
On Thursday, the injury report took another promising turn, as Zuhn practiced again. Booker and Zuhn were limited. Fatukasi and Thomas fully participated. The Raiders cannot get much healthier than that halfway through the season. This should work in their favor on Sunday against the Seahawks.
Although in a small sample size, Zuhn looks to be the best offensive guard on the roster this season. The Raiders have their hands full with him, but Sunday will be a long day for the unit without Zuhn. Still, Las Vegas must prepare for what happens if Zuhn can't play or leaves the game early.
Mendoza took another step toward his first professional start and now gets starter-level reps in practice. In addition to the half-season he has had to learn, this week's practices are invaluable ahead of Week 10 . The Raiders hope it gives them a spark under center on Sunday.
The rookie will have his growing pains , as all rookie quarterbacks do. However, with eight games remaining and the Raiders within striking distance of a possible playoff spot, now is the time to turn to the player they have already invested so much in.
The Heisman Trophy, National Championship-winning quarterback knows he has a lot to learn but refuses to be overwhelmed by the moment. Las Vegas' front office used the draft's top pick on Mendoza, in part, because of his poise in big moments. Sunday will be the first test of that poise professionally.
“I believe starting an NFL game is a new step, but a whirlwind? No. I would agree with Coach [Klint] Kubiak. Coach Kubiak, Coach [Andrew] Janocko, and Coach [Mike] Sullivan, and everyone in the quarterback room, including Kirk [Cousins], have done a fantastic job in aiding my development, and I can’t thank them enough. And now it’s my turn to do my 1/11th . And we have such a great offensive staff, and we have such a great offense,” Mendoza said on Wednesday.
Sunday is quietly an important day in the Raiders' storied history, regardless of whether they win the game. Las Vegas' Week 10 matchup against Klint Kubiak's old team signifies the Raiders fully turning the page and moving into the future, for better or worse. It is finally Mendoza season.
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: 2 Reasons Why Raiders Playoff Hopes Are Still Alive
full_text:
With a 4-5 record, the Las Vegas Raiders have been viewed as an afterthought when evaluating the AFC playoff picture.
While the Raiders have an uphill battle to reach the playoffs, crazier things have happened in this league. With that in mind, here are a couple of reasons why Las Vegas can challenge for a wildcard spot.
As things currently stand, I would say the top six spots in the AFC playoff picture are solidified, with the Bills, Broncos, Jaguars, Steelers, Chiefs, and Bengals occupying those spots. There will be some movement among those spots, but those six teams feel cemented. That leaves the No. 7 seed and the final wildcard spot.
At the moment, the New England Patriots take up that slot with a 5-4 record. For context, the Raiders are 4-5, so they're right there. The Cleveland Browns are also 5-4 at the No. 8 seed in the AFC. Yes, Las Vegas' upcoming three games are daunting, but the Patriots still have five games against teams above .500. Meanwhile, the Browns aren't trustworthy with Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders at quarterback. Not to mention, Las Vegas faces Cleveland in a few weeks.
The Houston Texans are a sleeper team to watch, despite being 3-5. Houston has a manageable schedule. Nevertheless, barring a substantial drop-off by one of the top six teams in the AFC, four teams are vying for one spot. That said, there's a chance the Raiders squeak in. All four of these teams battling for the No. 7 spot are vulnerable.
The next two weeks are very difficult matchups for the Raiders, with contests against the Seahawks and Broncos. So, by this time in a couple of weeks, Las Vegas' playoff aspirations could be bleak. However, considering that Seattle may have a quarterback issue on Sunday and Denver always allows opponents to hang around, the Raiders could split those two games, which would be monumental in maintaining ground in the playoff race.
After that, the Raiders face the Browns, Chargers, Broncos, Titans, Cardinals, and Chiefs. As mentioned, the Browns are always susceptible to a collapse with their quarterback situation. Meanwhile, Los Angeles, Tennessee, and Arizona are all teams the Raiders should beat. Now, Kansas City is the polarizing variable, as that game takes place in Week 18. It will be a road game, but depending on the playoff picture entering the season finale, the Chiefs could be resting their starters.
If that's the case, and the Raiders' playoff hopes are still alive, that could be a "free win" for the Silver and Black. Las Vegas' hopes are contingent on the next three weeks before the bye. Going 2-1 during that span, the Raiders are in legitimate contention for the wildcard, assuming none of the other three teams - Texans, Browns, and Patriots - create significant separation.

title: Dolphins-Colts Game Preview and Predictions: Can Miami Overcome Injuries?
full_text:
For a change, the Miami Dolphins are given a chance by more than just one or two national media members heading into their Week 10 game against the Indianapolis Colts — and that's despite the injury to starting quarterback Malik Willis.
The Dolphins will go into the game with a 1-7 record but after giving playoff contenders New England and Detroit a battle before losing at Hard Rock Stadium the past two weeks.
That, of course, with quarterback Malik Willis and standout defensive lineman Zach Sieler in the lineup, with both now on injured reserve. The Colts also have their issues, having traded four veterans — Quenton Nelson, DeForrest Buckner, Keenan Allen and Josh Downs — in the midst of a wildly disappointing season that's already seen GM Chris Ballard lose his job.
The Colts did retain star running back Jonathan Taylor and veteran defensive tackle Grove Stewart, who had been rumored to be on the move, and it's not like they're playing for draft position since their 2027 first-round pick belongs to the New York Jets as the result of the Sauce Gardner trade that keeps looking worse every day.
Indianapolis is favored by 3.5 points, according to the Fan Duel Sportsbook .
This is the second consecutive year the teams will face each other, the 2025 meeting coming in the season opener when the Colts humbled the Dolphins, 33-8, in a game that set the stage for Miami's disappointing 7-10 season that produced the regime change and rebuilding project that's going on right now.
That season-opening win was part of a fantastic start for the Colts, who once were 8-2 and very much looking like legit AFC contenders. The bottom then fell out and it hasn't stopped falling out, Indianapolis losing 14 of its past 16 games going back to last November 23.
This is why the Dolphins are being given a chance — even predicted by some — to win the game Sunday despite having a quarterback on his third team in two years ready to play his first real NFL snaps.
The Colts gave Dallas all it could handle last week before losing in overtime, and they may benefit from the uncertainty of their roster being done now that the NFL trade deadline has passed.
From this end, it's just difficult to give the Dolphins the nod here with an unproven quarterback who will have to work with the same subpar supporting cast that's hampered Willis so far this season, and without Aaron Brewer out on top of everyhing.
The Dolphins defense probably will be able to keep the score close, but we'd still call it something like 20-10 for the Colts.

title: The One (Tight End) That Got Away from the Dolphins
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins have looked to build up their tight end room in 2026 and currently feature three rookies at that position.
Against that backdrop, one would think there was more than a little bit of remorse in watching Elijah Higgins sign a contract extension with the Arizona Cardinals on Friday.
The Dolphins haven't often watched a late-round draft pick they cut as a rookie go on to have success with another team, but it's clearly what's happened with Higgins
You remember Elijah Higgins, right? The Dolphins drafted him as a wide receiver out of Stanford in the sixth round of the 2023 draft with the idea of making him a tight end, but ended up cutting him in the moves to the 53-player limit.
The Cardinals claimed him off waivers and he's gone on to make himself a nice career as the backup to starting tight end Trey McBride, sometimes starting in two-tight end sets as well.
The Dolphins kept three tight ends that year — Durham Smythe, rookie free agent Julian Hill and veteran Tyler Kroft. The latter played eight games that season, mostly on special teams, and didn't catch a pass all year.
His would be his final NFL season, and it's pretty obvious by now that the Dolphins messed up by not keeping Higgins instead of Kroft given what we know now.
Clearly, the Dolphins didn't do a great evaluation job on Higgins.
What made it more painful is that the Dolphins had only four draft picks that year, the result of the trades that brought Tyreek Hill, Bradley Chubb and Jalen Ramsey, as well as the tampering violation that cost Miami a first-round pick.
The other three picks that year were CB Cam Smith, RB De'Von Achane and T Ryan Hayes, and obviously only Achane has panned out.
Interestingly, Higgins was drafted after fellow tight end Hunter Long was included in that Ramsey trade that also cost the Dolphins a third-round pick.
The Dolphins went the veteran route at tight end the past two years with Jonnu Smith in 2024 and Darren Waller last year, but now their most grizzled player at the position is Greg Dulcich, who is only 26 and in his fifth NFL season.
Having a lot of youth at the position is fine, and maybe Will Kacmarek, Seydou Traore and Justin Joly all will go from intriguing rookies in 2026 to significant contributions sooner rather than later, but clearly the Dolphins could have used Higgins the past couple of years and into next season.
The case with Higgins is interesting because if you take a look at late-round picks (say, sixth or seventh round) that the Dolphins have cut, it's extraordinarily rare to see somebody go on to succeed with a second team.
That clearly happened with Higgins.

title: Tale of the Tape: How Kyle McCord Compares to Former Dolphins Backup QBs Heading Into Their First Start
full_text:
Ready or not, and the Miami Dolphins believe and hope he is, Kyle McCord is going to make his NFL debut Sunday.
There are some tough circumstances for the first-year player from Syracuse, most notably the absence of center Aaron Brewer to go along with that of IR'ed star running back De'Von Achane.
On the flip side, McCord will be going against an Indianapolis Colts team in the midst of a lost season, with a 2-7 record and four veterans traded away before or at the NFL trade deadline.
In that sense, let's just say the timing is better than if McCord's first start for the Dolphins after arriving as a trade acquisition over the summer had come next Sunday when Miami is scheduled to face the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium.
So how challenging is the task facing McCord, combining his lack of experience — shoot, his lack of any NFL regular season snaps — the team he'll be leading and the opponent? And how does it compare to the other instances over the past 10 years when the Dolphins have had to turn to their backup quarterback because of injuries?
Kyle McCord, 2026, Week 10 — Trade acquisition, first-year player, replacing starter Malik Willis against the 2-7 Indianapolis Colts
Analysis: The supporting cast performance was an issue for Willis when he was in the lineup, and that was before Brewer and WR Chris Bell were sidelined with injuries.
Quinn Ewers, 2025, Week 16 — Rookie seventh-round pick, replacing starter Tua Tagovailoa for 7-8 Dolphins against the 5-9 Cincinnati Bengals, was 20-for-30 for 260 yards with 0 TD, 2 INT and a 66.0 passer rating in a 45-21 loss
Analysis: What made things easier for Ewers was that the Dolphins already had been mathematically eliminated from playoff contention and he had gotten some game action before.
Tyler Huntley, 2024, Week 4 — Veteran free agent signing, replacing backup Skylar Thompson for 1-2 Dolphins against the 0-3 Tennessee Titans, was 14-for-22 for 96 yards with 0 TD, 0 INT and a 73.3 passer rating in a 31-12 loss
Analysis: The tough part for Huntley was that he really wasn't a great scheme fit for Mike McDaniel's offense, though he did have prior starting experience with Baltimore.
Skylar Thompson, 2022, Week 6 — Rookie seventh-round pick, replacing backup Teddy Bridgewater for 3-2 Dolphins against the 4-1 Minnesota Vikings, was 7-for-13 for 89 yards with 0 TD, 0 INT and a 75.5 passer rating before leaving with an injury in a 24-16 loss
Analysis: While the matchup was tough, Thompson basically had played the whole previous game after Teddy Bridgewater's exit after one play.
Teddy Bridgewater, 2022, Week 4 — Veteran free agent signing, replacing starter Tua Tagovailoa for the 3-1 Dolphins against the 2-2 New York Jets, was 0-for-1 before leaving with an injury in a 40-17 loss
Analysis: Bridgewater was in a good position to succeed in this one, even though he fell victim to the NFL's new zealousness about not missing concussion possibilities.
Jacoby Brissett, 2021, Week 3 — Veteran free agent signing, replacing starter Tua Tagovailoa for the 1-1 Dolphins against the 2-0 Las Vegas Raiders, was 32-for-49 for 215 yards with 0 TD, 0 INT and a 74.8 passer rating in a 31-28 overtime loss
Analysis: Brissett had starting experience, but this was against a good opponent.
Ryan Fitzpatrick, 2020, Week 12 — Veteran free agent signing in 2019, replacing starter Tua Tagovailoa for the 6-4 Dolphins against the 0-10 New York Jets, was 24-for-39 for 257 yards, with 2 TD, 0 INT and a 97.9 passer rating in a 20-3 victory
Analysis: Fitzpatrick had started the first six games of the regular season that year before giving way to first-round pick Tua Tagovailoa, so we might even be messing with semantics in calling him a backup here.
Brock Osweiler, 2018, Week 6 — Veteran free agent signing, replacing starter Ryan Tannehill for the 3-2 Dolphins against the 3-1 Chicago Bears, was 28-for-44 for 380 yards, with 3 TD, 2 INT and a 94.9 passer rating in a 31-28 overtime victory
Analysis: Osweiler had 25 career starts before this game, though this was a tough matchup for Miami.
Matt Moore, 2017, Week 8 — Veteran free agent signing in 2011, replacing starter Jay Cutler for the 4-2 Dolphins against the 3-4 Baltimore Ravens, was 25-for-44 for 176 yards, with 0 TD, 2 INT and a 47.2 passer rating in a 40-0 loss
Analysis: Though that Thursday night game turned into a horror show for the Dolphins, Moore was in a good spot beforehand with a lot of starting experience.
Matt Moore, 2016, Week 15 — Veteran free agent signing in 2011, replacing starter Ryan Tannehill for the 8-5 Dolphins against the 4-9 New York Jets, was 12-for-18 for 236 yards, with 4 TD, 1 INT and a 126.2 passer rating in a 34-13 victory
Analysis: This was a great spot for Moore, who had closed out a big overtime win against the Arizona Cardinals the previous week.

title: What Dolphins Teammates and Coaches Said About Kyle McCord Ahead of his First NFL Start
full_text:
The big storyline for the Miami Dolphins for their Week 10 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts obviously will be the NFL debut of quarterback Kyle McCord.
Less than three months after being acquired in a trade with the Green Bay Packers, McCord will start in place of Malik Willis after Willis landed on injured reserve with a core muscle injury.
Naturally, McCord was the big topic of conversation in interviews this week, with teammates and coaches offering their thoughts from different angles, from head coach Jeff Hafley to center Andrew Meyer, who likely will be making his first start of the season as well with Aaron Brewer dealing with a concussion.
"Good. I say that – he's mostly had the look team reps. He's done a good job in the look team reps that he's given us. The developmental periods that we have, I mean, it's why we do it, right? So say he's gotten 10 to 15 reps over the last 10 weeks, it's 100 reps of our plays. So he's done a good job in those periods. But it's going to be a lot different. I mean, him now being the starter and getting the game plan and playing every down and playing with a live rush and going through a real football game. So I'm excited to see what he can do. It opens a great opportunity for him and I'm happy that he'll get his chance."
"I mean, it's kind of the same as – we've had these discussions as we've gone through the year. We lost De’Von (Achane). I know we had the same conversation about, how's the run game change? Everybody that's in this building is in this building because we think they can run our offense and they can run our offense really well. I think there's things that make Malik different and special, like he can use his legs and he's got legit speed that no offense to Kyle, but Kyle doesn't have 23 miles an hour on the GPS in his body. So that's going to change how he approaches the game. But there's things we do in the pass game and the run game that he can handle and he likes doing and he excels at. So it's not going to change all that much. Probably just going to be things that are less running down the field."
"I think the biggest thing when you watch him play, he's a good processor. He sees the field well. He processes information well. He's really good in and out of the huddle. You know the simple things that a quarterback needs to do, he does well. He's a tough kid. I mean, obviously when he was in Philly, he's playing in preseason games at the end, taking a beating. He got up, kept playing, which is obviously impressive. And I think when you just look at the way he carries himself, he's very professional. The guys gravitate around him. Around him, you can see their energy, his energy. He's kind of a quieter guy, but he's got some swag to him, which is obviously important in that position."
"I think he's got good poise. I know we've thrown some different things at him. Apparently last week we probably practiced a lot of twists. But I think he's got good poise. I'm excited to see him. Just like I'm excited to see a lot of guys that have an opportunity this Sunday."
"I think that it helps a lot. I mean obviously we've built a chemistry in there between just the snap exchanges, stuff like that and we have a really good relationship so I think that it's comforting for sure like just knowing like that we've both gotten a lot of snaps together. Knowing that that's who I'm going to be out there with, it's definitely a little comforting."
"Me and Kyle have been building a great chemistry, caught enough balls. Ready to go out there on Sunday and compete."
"I mean, I think that's something that you definitely can hang your hat on. Being at a school like Ohio State and then playing some big games at Syracuse too, I think should give you confidence that you’ve played on a big stage before, you’ve played against some of the top guys in the league right now. So I think the confidence level coming from those games is definitely there."

title: Breaking Down the Good News/Bad News Regarding Dolphins WR Chris Bell
full_text:
Rookie wide receiver Chris Bell likely won't play for the Miami Dolphins against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 10, but the update on his status actually wasn't terrible news in the big picture.
Head coach Jeff Hafley said that Bell likely would be listed as doubtful for the game at Lucas Oil Stadium because of a knee injury, but the good news here is that it's not related to the torn ACL that Bell sustained last November during his final season at Louisville.
Instead, Bell was injured in practice Wednesday when he took a hit to the knee. He wound up being listed as limited for that day, didn't practice Thursday and Hafley he also wasn't going to practice Friday.
It's a setback of sorts, for sure, for the rookie third-round pick, but anytime we see Bell and knee on the injury report, there's reason for concern.
It's overall been a tough rookie season for Bell, though he did surpass a lot of expectations by being ready for the start of the regular season.
The production, however, has been very pedestrian.
Bell has appeared in all eight games this season, but he's got only 12 catches for 148 yards for a 12.3-yard average with no touchdowns. Worse, he's been held without a catch three times, including during the 19-9 loss agianst the Detroit Lions last Sunday when he was targeted only once.
On that pass attempt, Bell failed to get separation on a slant, an issue that's popped up regularly this season.
Some of that, of course, could be attributed to Bell still working his way back after the knee injury.
The hope, of course, is that Bell can finish with a flurry this season to possibly carry some momentum heading into 2027 because he did flash high-end potential in college.
Bell's status was just one of the injury updates that Hafley provided Friday when he also indicated, as expected, that center Aaron Brewer will miss the Colts game because he's still in concussion protocol.
Hafley confirmed that Andrew Meyer will take his place at center in the starting lineup.
The only other player that Hafley said would be out is wide receiver Jared Wayne, who sustained a quad injury in practice Thursday. His absence should mean a return to the lineup for veteran wide receiver Jalen Tolbert, who's had a pretty forgettable season after signing with the Dolphins as a free agent in the spring.
Tight end Will Kacmarek should be ready to go after missing practice Wednesday with quad and knee issues.
Cornerback Darrell Baker Jr. probably won't be activated off PUP for this game after completing his first week of practice.
Lastly, Hafley repeated what he had said before about rookie linebacker Trey Moore, who remains on IR with a pretty significant ankle injury he sustained in the preseason opener at Washington. Hafley said he was "hopeful" that Moore would be able to return at some point this season, though that time doesn't appear imminent and it's probably 50-50 that he'll be back at all in 2026.

title: Three Bold Predictions for the Miami Dolphins Against Indianapolis
full_text:
Following a disastrous week that saw significant injuries for two of their most important players, the Miami Dolphins will face the Indianapolis Colts at Lucas Oil Stadium in Week 10.
Both teams are looking to begin the second half of the season on the right track, so here are some trends they could rely on, along with some predictions based off of them.
The Colts traded away many of their biggest pieces at the deadline, hoping to recoup draft capital in what may be a lost season. They did, however, hold on to three-time Pro Bowl running back Jonathan Taylor and 10-year veteran defensive tackle Grover Stewart.
Notably, both of these players’ matchups have become substantially easier in light of the Dolphins’ recent injuries. Zach Sieler, a crucial piece of Miami’s defensive interior, is now out for the season, while All-Pro Center Aaron Brewer is in concussion protocol and is expected to miss this game.
With potentially renewed clarity following the trade deadline and a lack of continuity across from them, Taylor and Stewart could have big days. With Brewer, Miami’s offensive line struggled mightily in their Week 9 matchup against Detroit’s interior. On the other side, Sieler’s ability as a gap penetrator and the Dolphins’ best one-on-one winner is one they’ll have to try to replace with their trio of 2025 draftees. It will certainly take them time to find cohesion without their veteran leader.
The Indianapolis Colts have been among the worst teams in attempting to protect their quarterback. Their 41.8% pressure rate allowed is the sixth-worst mark in the NFL, and they rank fourth-quickest in time to pressure against, per NextGen Stats.
Even though Miami won’t have Sieler, who is crucial to their pass rush plan, their edge defenders, Chop Robinson and Josh Uche, really have begun to jell in recent weeks. Robinson’s wide-nine alignment often allows solo opportunities, which he took advantage of in Week 9. Meanwhile, Uche’s impact on his teammates and recent standout performance landed him a spot as a captain in light of the aforementioned Sieler injury.
Indianapolis’ defensive line has been non-threatening this season. The Colts are dead last in pressure rate and 30th in how quickly they get to the quarterback. However, the aforementioned Brewer injury combined with a first-time starting quarterback in Kyle McCord leaves much to be desired in terms of sorting out protections. Miami has allowed the league’s third-highest pressure rate, and now they face long-time defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo, who is more than willing to trot out unorthodox blitz looks against a young QB.
The formula for a Dolphins win is relatively simple: avoid catastrophic mistakes in Kyle McCord’s first start . The easiest way to mitigate risk is to run the ball, which Miami demonstrated in its lone win this season.
Ollie Gordon’s career high of 25 carries came in that Week 7 win against the Jets when Miami played the entirety from positive and neutral game script. That may be difficult against Indianapolis, but if Gordon’s early carries are successful against a Colts defense that ranks 29th in yards per carry allowed (4.9), then he’ll likely see a massive workload.
Maybe Jeff Hafley will even carry him back to the locker room, as he once joked when referencing De’Von Achane’s potential touches.
Tyler DeSena is currently a journalism student at the University of Central Florida. Prior to joining Dolphins On SI in 2026, DeSena worked with dolphinstalk.com, and created independent social media content on X, YouTube and TikTok.

title: More Bad News for the Dolphins' Most Disappointing Position Group
full_text:
While it was expected — or at least likely — that the Miami Dolphins would experience some growing pains this season, there was legitimate hope that the offensive line could lead the way on offense.
With few exceptions, though, it hasn't played out that way and the offensive line has had its share of struggles. And now comes the disappointing news with center Aaron Brewer, who missed a second consecutive practice with a concussion Thursday and now looks at best like a long shot to play against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday.
This looks like the same path as rookie guard Kadyn Proctor, who missed the Week 8 game against the New England Patriots, after not practicing at all during that week because of a concussion.
This makes it almost a certainty that third-year player Andrew Meyer will be starting at center against the Colts, and that's obviously not going to do anything to help the offense.
Brewer and wide receiver Chris Bell were the only two Dolphins players who didn't practice Thursday.
Because of the arrival of Proctor as the 12th overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft and the return of Brewer following his All-Pro performance of 2025 and Patrick Paul having established himself as a solid, maybe more, left tackle, there were some expectations that the offensive line could make a big step forward this season.
A lot of the focus has gone on right tackle Austin Jackson and his struggles in pass protection, but it's not fair to point the finger only at him for the offensive line not performing up to expectations.
Brewer, for one, hasn't played nearly as well as he did last year when he emerged as one of the top centers in the NFL. For those who trust Pro Football Focus, Brewer is ranked 17th out of 36 qualifying centers (based on snaps). Not terrible, but also not great and certainly not up to the 2025 standards.
The other PFF rankings for the Dolphins starting offensive linemen have Paul at 47th out of 71 tackles, Jackson at 71st, Proctor comes at 35th among 75 guards, with Jonah Savaiinaea landing at number 69, which isn't great but still better than last year when he was dead last at his position.
The run blocking had a nice little stretch right before and after the bye, but it's also not been quite consistent enough, but it's in  pass protection where the deficiencies have been glaring.
Those absolutely played a key role in the struggles of Malik Willis and the passing game, though there are contributing factors ranging from receivers not getting open or running the wrong routes, to Willis sometimes not seeing open receivers or hesitating a bit before letting the ball go.
With Brewer, Paul and Proctor, there clearly is potential on this line, and the hope is that progress starts happening in the final weeks of the regular season.
Not having Brewer against Indianapolis is the kind of setback that offensive line could do without, though.

title: What Are Realistic Expectations for Dolphins QB Kyle McCord's First NFL Start?
full_text:
Kyle McCord will be getting a huge opportunity when he starts for the Miami Dolphins against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday, the 2025 sixth-round pick heading for his NFL debut after not being on an active roster as a rookie.
The Dolphins believed in McCord enough this summer that they traded a future sixth-round pick to the Green Bay Packers and immediately made him their backup behind another former Packers player, Malik Willis.
McCord obviously is an unknown quantity as an NFL quarterback because his rookie season was spent on the Philadelphia Eagles practice squad and he hasn't taken a snap so far for the Dolphins.
His scouting report comes from his time at Ohio State and Syracuse, along with what he did during the preseason, both with the Eagles last summer and withthe Packers this year.
"I pride myself on just being the ultimate competitor out there on the field," McCord said Wednesday. "And then on top of that, I feel like being able to process information at a quick rate and getting the ball out and being accurate and being on time, I feel like those are all things throughout college and into my preseason games in the NFL that I had success with. So I'm just trying to keep that rolling."
But McCord just said it right there, "throughout college and into my preseason games."
NFL regular season games just aren't the same.
So what should we expect to see from McCord, based on circumstances and precedent?
McCord will become the seventh quarterback to make his NFL debut in a Dolphins uniform since 2000, joining Sage Rosenfels in 2004, John Beck in 2007, Chad Henne in 2009, Ryan Tannehill in 2012, Tua Tagovailoa in 2020, Skylar Thompson in 2022 and Quinn Ewers in 2025.
Beck, Henne, Tannehill and Tagovailoa were either first- or second-round picks, so their situation was a bit different — regardless of how things played out for them — and that makes Rosenfels, Thompson and Ewers better comps from a Dolphins standpoint.
Ewers actually is a very good comp because, like McCord before him, he was a sixth-round pick who had played against big-time competition in college, in his case at Texas — not even mentioning that both Ewers and McCord started off at Ohio State.
After beginning the season as the No. 3 quarterback behind Tagovailoa and veteran Zach Wilson, Ewers moved up to number 2 and was given the keys to the offense for the final three games of the 2025 season after Miami had been
His first start came against the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 16 and Ewers completed 20 for 30 passes for 260 yards. The good news is he had completions of 20 yards or more to four different receivers — tight ends Greg Dulcich and Darren Waller, and wide receivers Malik Washington and Jaylen Waddle — and the bad news was he threw two picks.
More importantly, he didn't look overwhelmed or out of place.
Skylar Thompson's first NFL start deserved an asterisk because before he started against the Minnesota Vikings he had played all but one snap the previous week after veteran Teddy Bridgewater, in for the injury Tagovailoa, was pulled by a concussion spotter after the Dolphins' first snap of the game.
Like Thompson and Ewers, Rosenfels also had seen action before making his first NFL start, which came in the 2004 season finale when the Dolphins had a 4-11 record.
Beck and Tannehill are the only two whose NFL debuts came in their first appearance, Tannehill in the 2012 season opener and Beck in a Week 11 game against the Philadelphia Eagles. Unlike Ewers last year, Beck did look overwhelmed and he wound up going 9-for-22 for 109 yards as a clear early indicator the Dolphins had made a poor second-round selection.
So it bears repeating, the best comp for McCord's situation clearly is Ewers.
One big difference between Ewers last year and McCord this year, though, is the talent on offense.
While Dulcich and Washington are back for the Dolphins, Waddle and Waller are gone and De'Von Achane is on injured reserve.
That's not going to make things easy for McCord, who watched from the sideline Malik Willis struggling to put up big numbers with a very young and inexperienced supporting cast on offense.
The Colts are struggling this season with a 2-7 record, and their defense has recorded only two interceptions all season despite the presence of quality cornerbacks Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward. Indianapolis also is coming off a game where it allowed 508 yards of offense in an overtime loss against the Dallas Cowboys.
That was Indy's first game without stud defensive tackle DeForrest Buckner after he was traded to the San Francisco 49ers.
The Colts made four trades in all before the deadline, but the other three involved offensive players.
It's been a lot season for Indy, but the Colts at least now no longer have to deal with the uncertainty of whether key players like Jonathan Taylor or Daniel Jones would be traded and maybe that will give them some juice the rest of the season.
In any case, we're certainly not expecting the Dolphins to put 508 yards against Indy on Sunday.
And we're not expecting McCord to light up the Colts secondary in his first NFL action. Matching Ewers' completions and yardage might even be a very bold goal, although a bigger key might be avoiding those interceptions.
So maybe a fair expectation, based on what we know of McCord and the Dolphins' offensive production this season, would be something along the lines of, say, 215 passing yards with one touchdown and no picks.

title: How the Dolphins Stand in the Race for No. 1 After the Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins' major setbacks this week with Malik Willis and Zach Sieler going on IR very well might slow down or stop the progress they had made in recent weeks, but they could prove beneficial if the objective is for the team to land the highest possible pick in the 2027 NFL draft.
In fact, it's not outrageous to suggest they might have taken the lead as the most likely to land the No. 1 overall pick.
The Dolphins currently hold the No. 3 position with their 1-7 record, standing behind only the winless Los Angeles Chargers and the Tennessee Titans. The Titans have the same 1-7 record as the Dolphins, but would have the tiebreaker advantage with the strength of schedule, where the weaker the opponent combined winning percentage the better for these purposes and Tennessee has a huge advantage right now at .428 compared to .627 for Miami.
That .627 is the highest in the NFL, which will punish the Dolphins two different ways, and even now it's probably fair to suggest the Dolphins will lose out in just about any tiebreaker scenario.
The question then becomes whether the Dolphins will finish with the worst record in the NFL, which has become more of a possibility after the losses of Willis and Sieler, and who their competition will be for that distinction.
In that sense, it actually was a pretty good trade deadline for Miami.
Heading into Week 10 of the 2026 regular season, seven teams find themselves with two or fewer wins, and Washington has one tie along with their two wins.
The other six are the Chargers, Titans, Dolphins, Philadelphia Eagles, New York Jets and Indianapolis Colts.
Among those teams, the players who were traded this week were Jets safety Andre Cisco, Eagles defensive tackle Jordan Davis, Titans safety Amani Hooker, and Colts wide receivers Josh Downs and Keenan Allen.
But it could have been a lot worse.
The Eagles had a trade to send edge defender Arnold Ebiketie to the Cincinnati Bengals before it was nixed when the Bengals discovered it might hurt them with compensatory picks down the line. The Chargers had a trade in place to send starting linebacker Daiyan Henley to the Denver Broncos for two draft picks until the Broncos rescinded the deal overnight.
And then there were the other players who once were believed to be on the move who stayed put. The Colts, for example, once were believed to maybe be trading Jonathan Taylor and/or Daniel Jones. The Chargers supposedly would entertain the idea of moving Khalil Mack and/or Derwin James.
Hanging on to those players could or should help the Chargers and Colts win some games down the line — maybe in the case of the Chargers as dysfunctional as their offense has been all season.
That's obviously good for the Dolphins.
The Dolphins will face both of those teams down the stretch, starting with the Colts this Sunday, where a loss will be a win when it comes to the 2027 draft.
The next two weeks are big for the Chargers — and consequently for the Dolphins — with a Monday night game against the Ravens and new starting quarterback Jacoby Brissett followed by a home game against the Jets.
The Titans had their bye last weekend after tough losses against the Cleveland Browns and Cincinnati Bengals, but don't have many games down the stretch that would be categorized as very winnable — the two that come to mind are home games against Washington in Week 13 and Indianapolis in Week 15.
With Simmons and Hooker gone from the defense, Tennessee looks like a strong candidate to end up with the first overall pick for the second time in three years.
The Dolphins, meanwhile, looked like they were ready to win some games after their close losses against New England and Detroit, but the outlook has changed because they'll now be starting a quarterback who's never played a down in the NFL and be without one of their best defensive players.
The Dolphins will face the Colts and the Jets over the next three weeks when Willis will be on IR and Kyle McCord will be at quarterback, but maybe Willis will be back for the Week 16 game against the Chargers, one that could have major draft ramifications.
The bottom line is the Dolphins look more likely to have a shot at the top pick now — after the Willis and Sieler news and after the trade deadline — than they did at the start of the week.

title: Where Sieler, Achane Rank Among the Most Impactful Dolphins Season-Ending Injuries of the Past 10 Years
full_text:
Injuries are inevitable in the NFL, but for the Miami Dolphins unfortunately those have included this year losing two key players to season-ending injuries before reaching the halfway point.
Defensive tackle Zach Sieler was placed on injured reserve Tuesday, joining running back De'Von Achane on the sidelines for the remainder of the season, Sieler with a biceps injury and Achane with a torn ACL.
These were two of the most prominent players on a young, rebuilding Dolphins team already lacking in proven talent, so they're just not minimizing the impact of each loss.
Unfortunately, this continues a trend of front-line players the Dolphins have lost for the season before reaching the halfway point.
Over the past 10 years, you almost invariably can count on a key starter going down early, and sometimes it's more.
But how do the losses of Sieler and earlier Achane compare to some of the major losses the Dolphins have suffered in the past 10 years.
Here's our ranking of the top 10 most impactful injuries for the Dolphins since 2017, with the stipulation being that the injury occur in the first half of the season and based on positional value and player quality.
10. WR Will Fuller, 2021 — The Dolphins wide receiver corps in Tua Tagovailoa's second season got a boost with the addition of Jaylen Waddle in the first round of the draft, but Fuller also was supposed to help with his speed after arriving as a free agent from Houston. Instead, he sustained a finger injury in his second game with the Dolphins and never played again in the NFL.
9. G James Daniels, 2025 — Daniels was supposed to help solidify the Dolphins offensive line, but his first and only start for Miami lasted all of four plays. His absence was supposed to last a month or so, but he never came back and the Dolphins were left with trying to find an answer at right guard.
8. S Reshad Jones, 2019 — Jones easily was one of the Dolphins' best players of the 2010s and he was one of the remaining veterans on the rebuilding 2019 team, though he was done after four games.
7. CB Xavien Howard, 2019 — Similar to Jones, Howard was among those established players on that very young 2019 team, but an early knee injury slowed him down until he wound up on IR.
6. G Josh Sitton, 2018 — Sitton was a four-time Pro Bowl guard who really was going to help the Dolphins offensive line, but instead wound up on IR after sustaining a shoulder injury in the season opener and that became the end of his 11-year NFL career.
5. QB Ryan Tannehill, 2017 — Normally, we'd put losing a starting quarterback early in training camp higher on this kind of list, but the Dolphins were able to recover nicely by signing Jay Cutler, who turned in a performance similar to what Miami likely would have gotten from Tannehill.
4. OLB Jaelan Phillips, 2024 — The Dolphins already were going to play the 2024 season without Bradley Chubb as he continues his comeback from his brutal December 2023 knee injury, but then Phillips' own comeback from an Achilles injury ended with a torn ACL in the Week 4 Monday night game. And, just like that, the Dolphins found themselves struggling for pass-rushing help.
3. DT Zach Sieler, 2026 — Besides being easily the best interior defensive lineman on the team, Sieler also will be missed for his leaderhip and mentorship of a very young group at his position.
2. RB De’Von Achane, 2026 — It's a tough call here between Sieler and Achane, but we put Achane higher on our countdown because he was such a focal point for the offense, not only this year but the past two seasons as well. And in a group with so many young, unestablished players, he was the one player the Dolphins couldn't afford to lose.
1. WR Tyreek Hill, 2025 — An argument could be made that Hill shouldn't be No. 1 on the list because the Dolphins were 0-3 when he went down with that catastrophic knee injury last September, but the offense had had its moments in those three games and it just wasn't the same after Hill and his big-play threat were gone.

title: 3 Most Important Things Vikings Fans Must Watch for in Week 10 Road Clash vs. Packers
full_text:
There’s new hope in the Minnesota air after an embarrassing passing performance on Monday Night Football led to the reacquisition of former Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins from the Raiders.
Now, the Vikings head into Week 10’s matchup against the Packers with a fighting chance to showcase a competent offense , something that seemed impossible just a few days ago. With playoff seeding slipping away and the back half of a brutal four-game stretch now upon them, the urgency has never been higher for Cousins and the 2026 Vikings.
Here’s what to watch for as the Vikings look to get back in the win column.
It was a late October Sunday in 2023. Cousins and the Vikings had overcome a 1-4 start and were looking to complete the climb back to .500 with a win in Green Bay. Everything was clicking, even without an injured Justin Jefferson. Then, in the third quarter, disaster struck as Cousins hobbled off the field with a torn Achilles, ending his time in purple.
Vikings @ Packers this Sunday… Scriptwriters couldn’t have planned it any better. pic.twitter.com/PxPF9pMg0a
Even if he faces a hiccup or two after being named the Week 10 starter on Friday, the alternatives seem far worse , even as Cousins reacclimates. Safe to assume, then, that he’ll be making his return to the Vikings on the exact field he last donned the horned helmet on.
It’s hard to project exactly what we’ll see after only a couple of practices, but it will likely be a massive improvement over what we’ve witnessed with Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz.
If Cousins and Co. can walk away with a win, his teammates may have to bust out the chains and Rolexes again on the short flight home.
Sunday will mark the 10th matchup between Kevin O’Connell and Matt LaFleur since O’Connell took over as head coach in 2022. Both have been touted as two of the best offensive minds in the NFL, even as their own fan bases often criticize their play-calling and decision-making. Ironically, most NFL teams would gladly drop their current coach for a shot at either of them.
O’Connell will look to add a seventh win to his 6-3 record against the Packers, while LaFleur will be looking to make his series record a tad more respectable. With divisional and conference seeding in the balance, Sunday’s battle of the offensive minds should provide plenty of fireworks. That is, if another elite coach doesn’t have his say …
Make no mistake: the Vikings do not defeat the Packers in Week 1 without a stellar day from Brian Flores’s defense. Their ability to create short fields and turnovers set Wentz and the Vikings' offense up for a 39-22 comeback victory. But the Green Bay offense they’ll face this Sunday won't be the same as it was two months ago.
JORDAN LOVE CHRISTIAN WATSON PACKERS ARE DOMINATING GBvsNE on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/hxEPzs2KdC
The Packers' offensive line is healthier and much improved after allowing four sacks in Week 1. Their 17 sacks allowed through nine games are the 12th-fewest in the NFL this season. Their passing game is also finding its stride, with wideouts Christian Watson and Matthew Golden posting massive performances in a 45-27 victory against the Patriots last week.
Needless to say, the Vikings defense will need to bring its A-game against Jordan Love and the Packers offense on the road. Hopefully, their offense will now be able to get them some rest by sustaining a drive or two.

title: Vikings' Grim Week 10 Injury Report Will Likely Force Trio Into Bigger Roles vs. Packers
full_text:
The Vikings are entering their matchup against the Packers with key injuries on both sides of the ball. While this new guy at quarterback may provide some juice , there's no question that Minnesota still has to overcome significant hurdles against its division rival as injuries plague the roster.
The #Vikings final Week 10 injury report OUT: LB Blake Cashman, TE T.J. Hockenson, DL Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins, WR Jauan Jennings and QB Kyler Murray QUESTIONABLE: WR Jordan Addison (thumb), S Joshua Metellus (shoulder) and OLB Kyle Van Noy pic.twitter.com/WU1CfJg9Hr
With an injury report longer than Kirk Cousins' Kohl's shopping list, the Vikings will need to rely on their reserves to step up in a big way after ruling out multiple key players on Friday.
With Blake Cashman unable to clear the concussion protocol, Eric Wilson will likely be joined by a committee of Pace and rookie Jake Golday. Pace has seen his role reduced in recent years after a strong rookie campaign, but he did play very well last week against Buffalo, notching a sack in just 22 snaps.
Ivan Pace Jr. brings the pressure 💥 📺 Watch live on @NFLonDAZN , @SkySports and @talkSPORT pic.twitter.com/O7XREgogYK
Defensive coordinator Brian Flores will probably get Golday some looks as well after the rookie saw a career-high in snaps last week, but in all likelihood it'll be the veteran Pace who the defensive coordinator leans on. Pace's run discipline and pass coverage leave much to be desired, but if the Vikings need a Tasmanian Devil to get after Jordan Love before he finds a receiver 50 yards down the field, Pace is the man for the job.
The Vikings could also use more dime looks with Cashman out, and with how well the Packers stretch the field, it wouldn't be surprising at all. Still, Pace will have a chance at some redemption on Sunday in a contract year after falling out of favor over the last few seasons.
T.J. Hockenson has served as a great security blanket for the revolving door of Vikings quarterbacks this season, and now Kirk Cousins will have to play his first game back without the friendly face. The Vikings' second leading receiver will miss this Sunday's Packers game, and Bartholomew looks to be the next man up, with Josh Oliver already out for the year.
Bartholomew already stepped up big in one game this season, reeling in five catches against New Orleans after Hockenson went down early, and he'll now get called on again.
With Jauan Jennings also out, and Jordan Addison now potentially following suit, the Vikings' pass catchers will be awfully thin . Is it weird to say that Bartholomew will probably have a bigger game than Myles Price, Tai Felton or Odell Beckham Jr.?
Unfortunately, it doesn't seem weird in the slightest.
Banks was a healthy scratch last week, and now could be playing 30 or 40 snaps just days later at Green Bay. Head coach Kevin O'Connell confirmed that his benching last week was simply what the game plan called for, and now this week's will require that Banks plays "a ton."
"He'll be up and he's going to play a ton this week." - Head Coach Kevin O'Connell on DL Caleb Banks pic.twitter.com/1Rx5kBzmyw
The first-round pick hasn't made much of an impact yet, but with Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins out, Banks will get called upon whether he's ready or not. Banks was always looked at as a long-term developmental project, but early returns may be emphasizing the "long" aspect more than Minnesota had hoped.
Banks has the lowest Pro Football Focus grade among all rookie defensive tackles , but he's also only played 107 snaps. This week at Green Bay might provide the first real litmus test as to how far along the Vikings rookie actually is—or isn't.

title: Is Kirk Cousins Starting vs. the Packers in Week 10? Latest on Vikings QB's Return
full_text:
As the Vikings prepare to face the Packers for the first time since the season opener, fans across Minnesota are wondering one thing: Will Kirk Cousins be ready to suit up for Sunday's NFC North collision?
Even though Cousins has been around the block, it doesn't change the fact that he'd likely need some time to adjust to his old team again. Although some familiar faces from his last stint remain, these aren't the same Vikings from three seasons ago, and no one would blame him for sitting out at least one game to reacclimate .
Fortunately, Cousins is seemingly build different.
On Friday afternoon, Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell revealed that Cousins will be starting against the Packers this weekend . It'll be his first time putting on the Purple and Gold since tearing his ACL, ironically, against Green Bay in Week 8 of the 2023 season.
Head Coach Kevin O'Connell has announced that QB Kirk Cousins will start Sunday at Green Bay. pic.twitter.com/zSMqWo0pHQ
As great as it's been to see Cousins around his teammates and coaches this week, the only thing that truly matters is what he'll do on the field this weekend.
After all, Minnesota might be 6-2, but little of that success stems from the passing game. Whether it was Kyler Murray or Carson Wentz under center, the Vikings' offensive performance hasn't looked like it belongs to a team that's four games above .500. They currently rank 27th in points per game, 31st in total yards per game and 30th in yards per play.
The Packers' defense isn't as elite as the Vikings', but they still rank 11th in points and yards allowed per game. In other words, the status quo likely wouldn't be good enough, and all eyes are on Cousins to see if he can bring the improvements Minnesota's attack desperately needs. In fact, here's how he ranks among other QBs this season when it comes to:
It'll be nice to see Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison with a quarterback who can take full advantage of their talents.
Vikings fans still remember the magic that the Cousins-Jefferson connection created during the 2022 season, which saw the star WR pace the NFL in catches (128), receiving yards (1,809) and first downs before being named the AP NFL Offensive Player of the Year. Meanwhile, Addison posted a 36-482-7 stat line in the eight games he played with Cousins in 2023, making it interesting to see if they can rekindle that flame.
With T.J. Hockenson officially ruled out for Sunday , Cousins will need to maximize the damage he can do with each of his healthy weapons to keep the Vikings afloat at the top of the NFC North. Doing so will not only stop Minnesota's skid but also give fans an idea of what to expect for the rest of the season.

title: 3 Missed Vikings Trade Opportunities Nolan Teasley Should've Made at the Deadline
full_text:
The Vikings made one of the splashier trades before Tuesday's deadline by bringing back quarterback Kirk Cousins, but they also could've been a bit more active , too.
Ahead of the deadline, the Vikings were reportedly sniffing around deals for running back, offensive line, defensive line and more, but ultimately general manager Nolan Teasley called it a day after acquiring Cousins.
And while the Cousins deal should do wonders for the anemic offense , there were also three other deals the Vikings should've made.
Let's discuss how the deadline should've gone down after the QB reunion.
After the stunning Jordan Davis deal and the attempted Arnold Ebiketie trade, the Eagles were clearly open for business at the deadline. Guard Landon Dickerson's name had been floated as a potential trade piece with the 2-7 Birds entering a retool at bare minimum, but the 28-year-old stayed put.
And despite being one of the interested teams in Quenton Nelson a few weeks ago, the Vikings opted not to add a guard at the deadline.
The trade compensation for Dickerson likely would've been similar to that of the Cousins deal, and so it's always possible the Vikings weren't comfortable parting with both of their third-round picks. Still, a deal for Dickerson would've solidified the 2026 interior in front of Cousins and helped them move on from the underwhelming Will Fries in 2027.
The Vikings were reportedly looking at adding along the defensive front at the deadline, and one name that stuck out as a logical add was Robinson. The 31-year-old generated some interest around the league, but ultimately the Buccaneers never moved him.
Robinson has one of the more bizarre statlines for a defensive tackle this season with 24 tackles, one sack, eight quarterback pressures, and two interceptions. But what really sets Robinson apart is his run defense. His 86.2 Pro Football Focus grade against the run ranks second to someone Vikings fans may recognize: Jalen Redmond. Getting the top two-rated run defenders in the NFL on one roster would've made the league's best defense even more unstoppable, but it seems that no one was able to entice Tampa Bay enough.
The Vikings actually attempted to trade away Jennings to San Francisco , but the wide receiver essentially vetoed the deal. Perhaps no other teams had interest, but the Vikings clearly thought it best to move on from the failed free-agent signing and recoup whatever draft compensation they could.
Jennings has just six catches for 54 yards on the season, and potentially the addition of Cousins might ignite his production, but the Vikings were probably better off just getting their late-round pick and moving on. Tai Felton, Myles Price and Odell Beckham Jr. haven't exactly been stuffing the stat sheet either, but it was clear that there were some wide receiver-needy teams across the NFL willing to pony up.
In all, three receivers were moved before the deadline, but the Vikings will now hope Cousins can unlock Jennings a bit more.

title: Forgotten Vikings WR Suddenly Looks More Important Amid Jauan Jennings Injury Concerns
full_text:
The Vikings will look to avoid a third straight loss when they visit the rival Packers in Week 10 , but a lengthy injury list could make that job easier said than done. After Thursday, six veteran players have missed back-to-back practices to start the week , increasing the likelihood that head coach Kevin O'Connell & Co. will be shorthanded Sunday afternoon.
One of this week's absentees is wide receiver Jauan Jennings, who's been hampered by a calf injury. On Tuesday, his agent, Drew Rosenhaus, said he didn't expect Jennings's injury to be serious (h/t VikingzFanPage), but it's becoming concerning that the 29-year-old WR still hasn't seen the practice field this week.
#Vikings WR Jauan Jennings (calf) should be back next week, per his agent @DrewJRosenhaus . He is not expected to be traded before today’s deadline. pic.twitter.com/SCrlDgW2iI
Jennings hasn't done much this season (six catches for 54 touchdown-less receiving yards), but he was starting to step up recently. Assuming that trend would've continued against the Packers, who've allowed the T-14th-most receiving touchdowns (13) this season, it's safe to say that Jennings's absence might be felt.
When one door closes, another opens, though. A certain Minnesota WR has fallen off the radar recently, but a potential Jennings absence in Week 10 could put the forgotten playmaker back in a spot to make some noise this weekend.
When the 2026 NFL season began, Tai Felton was one of the bigger question marks in the Vikings' offense. The former 2025 third-round pick spent more snaps on special teams (293) than on offense (46) as a rookie, resulting in three catches for 25 receiving yards and a lot of questions about how Minnesota would use him behind top WRs Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison.
Year 2 started with nothing to write home about, as Felton failed to haul in two targets in the first three games and averaged 11.7 offensive snaps per appearance. Week 4 vs. the Dolphins seemed to be a turning point, as Felton recorded a then-season-high 14-yard reception before following that up with two catches for 27 yards against the Saints one week later.
It truly seemed like Felton was turning the page ahead of the bye week, but that's where his momentum stopped. Since Week 7, Felton has been targeted only once while playing 12 offensive snaps in the last three games, including when fellow depth WR Myles Price out-targeted him 4-to-0 against the Bills.
His present outlook isn't promising, but it's far too early to give up on Felton, who won't even turn 24 years old until March. His confidence might be shot at the moment, but that can quickly change with a solid effort in a must-win NFC North collision.
The Packers have done a commendable job defending the air this season, but that doesn't mean they're perfect.
After all, Green Bay has allowed an average of 255.0 passing yards in its last three games—not only noticeably above its season average (213.9), but also the eighth-most league-wide during that stretch. Sure, the Packers beat the Patriots last week despite those flaws, but it's worth noting that the Vikings' rival allowed 320 receiving yards and three TDs on just 22 catches in the win.
Hopefully, Felton and the rest of the Vikings' pass-catchers find a way to have a stronger performance against the Packers than they did in Week 1. Although Minnesota notched the season-opening win, Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz combined for only 15-of-24 passing for 151 passing yards, three touchdowns, and an interception.
It was good enough to get the job done that day, but now, with the NFC North's walls closing in, probably not?
A returning Kirk Cousins (assuming he plays) would be the first step toward having more aerial success against an arch-rival. Felton stepping up and proving why he was worthy of a Day 2 selection last year would be a solid second step.

title: Vikings Face Potential QB Conundrum If Kirk Cousins Doesn’t Play in Week 10
full_text:
Kirk Cousins should be expected to start at quarterback for the Minnesota Vikings against the Green Bay Packers on Sunday. However, there is a chance that the veteran passer won't be ready to suit up for the Week 10 contest.
Playing a game with a new team with less than a week to prepare is a huge challenge for any player, even someone with 15 seasons of experience. The problem is that if the recently acquired passer doesn't play, there aren't many good options. On Wednesday, Cousins even admitted that it was too "early" to say if he'd be ready to face the Packers (h/t Bring Me The Sports ).
"I don't think I can give you a fair answer only because of how early in the week it is." Kirk Cousins on if he's prepared to start for the Vikings on Sunday. pic.twitter.com/RMgcBDYNww
Any divisional game is a big game, but it feels even bigger when it is a border battle against the Packers. Deciding who should start at quarterback if it isn't Cousins is a tough choice, but head coach Kevin O'Connell would have to make it with confidence.
If Vikings fans hadn't just seen Carson Wentz have a historically bad game against the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football, he would have been the obvious choice. He finished with a Pro Football Focus grade of 22.3 and a QBR of 2.3, completing only 32% of his passes, fumbling, and throwing two interceptions without scoring a touchdown.
Minnesota can not feel comfortable starting him again any time soon. Considering he is 33 years old and in his 11th NFL season, that might have been his final start as a pro before his retirement. He is also limited in practice on the injury report with an ankle injury, which makes the odds of him playing even worse.
Kyler Murray missed the game against the Bills with a hamstring injury and is still not practicing for Minnesota on this week's injury report. If he is healthy enough to play, he becomes the best non-Cousins option on the Vikings' roster.
However, even when Murray is healthy, he hasn't been great for the Purple and Gold. Despite a 5-1 record as Minnesota's starter and a five-to-three touchdown-to-interception ratio, he has struggled to get the Vikings' offense going, averaging just 170.3 passing yards per game and an ESPN QBR of 45.7.
Before last week, Max Brosmer wouldn't have been an option. However, when he entered the game against the Bills after Wentz was benched, he looked solid. He completed six of seven passes against Buffalo for 58 yards. That's only 25 fewer yards than Wentz passes while he threw over three times as many passes.
Still, Brosmer is the QB4 in Minnesota for a reason, and it will take more than one solid showing in garbage time of a game to earn a start in Week 10. Cousins should be the man for the job, and if he can't play, Murray should be the next man up, if he is healthy.

title: 3 Bold Vikings Predictions Heading Into Week 10 Showdown Against Packers
full_text:
It seems like yesterday that the Vikings were hosting the Packers in Week 1 to kick off the 2026 season. Now, the two teams will conclude their regular-season series with a chilly match at Lambeau Field. Vikings fans are still riding the excitement from a major adrenaline injection early this week as the team reacquired quarterback Kirk Cousins via trade with the Las Vegas Raiders. What once looked like a potential beatdown in Green Bay now looks like a massive opportunity for the Vikings to end a two-game losing streak and sweep their biggest rival.
There’s still a lot up in the air, especially since head coach Kevin O’Connell hasn't technically named Cousins the starter yet. But let’s be real: Cousins is starting unless there's a major setback . So, let’s dive into some predictions for Sunday, assuming “Kirko Chainz” makes his triumphant return.
Frick it, Justin Jefferson is down there somewhere. There is perhaps no larger beneficiary of the Cousins’ reunion tour than Jefferson. The seventh-year wide receiver is on pace to have the worst year of his career after poor QB play wrecked his 2025 campaign. Needless to say, it’s time for Jefferson to reclaim his spot on the wide receiver throne.
Jefferson’s 98.9 receiving yards per game with Cousins far surpasses his 65 ypg average through six full games this season. Cousins’ mission on Sunday is simple: feed Jefferson. I’m predicting Jefferson will have a vintage performance with over 150 receiving yards and at least one touchdown.
#Vikings QB Kirk Cousins says he saw Justin Jefferson today, and is excited to play with him again: “You don’t go chasing things, but you understand the player he is, and you go where your reads take you. You know he tends to make it right when you throw in his direction.” pic.twitter.com/zOoSnvilDO
Green Bay’s 24 points per game ranks 12th-highest in the league through nine weeks, while Brian Flores and the Vikings defense are allowing a league-low 14.5 points per game to opposing offenses. Minnesota has held two of the league's best offenses, Detroit and Buffalo, to 19 and 23 points, respectively. This feat is even more impressive given the complete lack of help on the offensive side of the ball.
“This roster has earned the right to explore the potential to maximize where we can take this thing.” -Vikings GM Nolan Teasley on the decision to trade for Kirk Cousins pic.twitter.com/TkkJVs0fsp
This one is pretty straightforward: I have the Vikings righting the ship against a talented Packers team and ending their slide down the NFC North standings. While many had assumed star pass rusher Micah Parsons would be back by now, the Vikings have the distinct advantage of avoiding him in both regular-season matchups.
Two of these teams will miss the playoffs pic.twitter.com/7VewNM4oiT
With a reenergized offense, a motivated Cousins returning to the scene of a career-altering injury, and O’Connell in “prove it” mode, I think we finally see a well-rounded 2026 Vikings squad in action.
