title: 3 Vikings Coaching Decisions I'd Make If I Were Kevin O'Connell Ahead of the Packers Game in Week 10
full_text:
Kirk Cousins is back in purple , and his first game with Minnesota will be where everything changed the last time he was a member of the Vikings. It was at Lambeau Field that Cousins tore his Achilles three years ago, and now he'll get his first action as the newest Viking this weekend.
Getting the offense rolling is clearly a top objective, but the defense will also need to stay on top of the Packers' high-flying offense. It's a tall task, but the Vikings already took down the Pack once this season and can certainly do it again.
Here's everything I would do if I were in Kevin O'Connell's shoes this week.
Cousins didn't come here to play school, and while he hasn't been formally announced as the starter for Sunday, it's all but guaranteed. And while the temptation may be to reel things in a bit and let Cousins try to get his feet wet, that thinking is what's done the Minnesota offense in so far this season.
Trying to dink and dunk down the field hasn't resulted in any success this year, and while it's kept turnovers and big mistakes to a minimum, it also hasn't moved the ball. The Vikings' defense was on the field for an average of 38 minutes over the past two games, and that's clearly unsustainable.
Cousins can work the middle of the field, and while his arm isn't what it was, the mid-level throws are still very much in his wheelhouse. His 91.6 Pro Football Focus grade on intermediate throws (10-19 yards) ranks fourth in the NFL compared to Kyler Murray's 59.9. An interception or two isn't the end-all be-all so long as the offense moves the chains . What will spell doom, however, is refusing to let Cousins play despite his hurried attempts to relearn the offense.
Blake Cashman popped up on the Vikings injury report with a concussion, and with a short week, it does seem to be a question of whether he can clear protocol in time to suit up for Sunday.
If Cashman can't go, the Vikings will turn to Pace and Golday to fill his mostly irreplaceable shoes. And while Golday saw his highest share of defensive snaps last week against Buffalo, Pace should really be doing the heavy lifting this week.
Pace notched a sack on just 22 snaps against the Bills and played arguably his best game all season. His role has shrunk year after year since his breakout rookie campaign, but Pace's pass-rushing abilities are still second-to-none at the linebacker position, with a 90.1 PFF grade. Pace's coverage abilities are another story, but Jordan Love and the Packers tend to do most of their damage on the outside, with Matthew Golden and Christian Watson accounting for nearly two-thirds of all receiving yards.
Golday will get his chance, but Pace seems like the logical option to handle the lion's share if Cashman is sidelined.
The dreaded Bills rushing attack can't hurt the Vikings anymore, and they'll now be treated to an offense averaging just 68 rushing yards per game. It's the perfect opportunity to work the first-round rookie back into the mix.
Banks was sat against Buffalo simply because his pad level has mostly been awful this year. He's been washed away and was frankly becoming a liability. The Packers may offer a friendlier matchup with their high-octane passing attack, allowing Banks to get after the quarterback--something he's at least done to moderate success with three pressures from the interior.
His development is certainly crawling along, but the Vikings knew it would take some time before Banks was ready to contribute in a major way. Last week's healthy scratch was just a matchup decision, and there shouldn't be any concerns about his long-term outlook at this point. Banks should see his typical dozen or so snaps again this Sunday.

title: 3 Step Guide to Set Kirk Cousins Up for Success in His Vikings Return
full_text:
The Minnesota Vikings successfully completed a trade for Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins on Tuesday ahead of the league's 4 p.m. ET trade deadline. The 15-year pro should be an immediate upgrade at the position over Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz.
Cousins thrived in head coach Kevin O'Connell's offense during his previous time in Minnesota. The two were together in 2022 and 2023, when Cousins went 17-8 as a starter, completing 67.1 percent of his passes and throwing 47 touchdowns to 19 interceptions.
On Sunday, Cousins should be the starting quarterback for the Vikings. Although he'll have less than a week to prepare for the Week 10 game at Lambeau Field against the Green Bay Packers, O'Connell can set him up for success.
The Vikings have slowly phased fullback Max Bredeson out of the offensive game plan. In each of Minnesota's last two games, he played only seven offensive snaps. Instead, the team opted for tight end Ben Yurosek, who is a stronger pass blocker.
That said, keeping an extra blocker to protect Cousins is smart. He lacks the mobility of a quarterback like Murray, but can make good decisions and make defenses pay if he gets time in the pocket. Minnesota has allowed 23 sacks this year, the tenth most in the NFL. Keeping him upright and able to survey the field is essential, especially considering that the Packers' defense has recorded 26 sacks this season.
The best way to get a quarterback in a groove is to get early completions. Whether it is slants, screens, or other short passes, Cousins needs to get into a rhythm against Green Bay and get his blood flowing on what should be a chilly Green Bay day.
Vikings fans have seen enough of the team's quarterbacks struggling to force the ball down the field, even if it is a target for superstar wide receiver Justin Jefferson. Cousins has made a career out of taking what defenses give him, and with how opportunistic the Packers' defense is this season, with 19 takeaways and allowing a score on just 30.8 percent of their opponents' drives, Minnesota can't afford to struggle offensively.
O'Connell has a tendency to get fancy at times and try trickery or misdirection to keep opposing defenses on their toes. With a quarterback like Cousins, those plays get in the way of playing to his biggest strength: play-action passes.
Of course, that means the Vikings will need to establish the run early. Aaron Jones or Jordan Mason should be able to get some work done on the ground to open up opportunities for play-action passes, creating separation for the wide receivers against the Packers' defense.

title: Vikings Week 10 Mailbag: Kirk Cousins, Nolan Teasley Concerns, NFL Trade Deadline & More
full_text:
The Vikings’ season is saved! Well, that’s the hope anyway. Minnesota’s trade deadline acquisition of Kirk Cousins from the Raiders may just be the boost they need to end a two-game losing streak as they head to Green Bay this weekend.
I took to X to gather your questions and opinions, and to no one’s surprise, the Vikings’ new, or should I say old, QB was the hottest topic.
To submit your questions, reach out to Jason Harmon on X .
Anyone who was looking for a flurry of deadline moves by the Vikings certainly feels disappointed. There were multiple positions that could have been addressed, with guard and running back being the popular requests. While there were conflicting reports over the team’s interest in Quenton Nelson, the Vikings were heavily linked to Jonathan Taylor.
The Colts traded Nelson to the Seahawks two weeks ago, but ultimately decided not to greenlight any of the offers on the table for Taylor.
The biggest factor in Teasley’s approach was the deteriorating quarterback situation for the Vikings. A poor performance by Kyler Murray in Detroit was followed by a terrible showing by Carson Wentz in primetime the day before the deadline. The QB position immediately became the top need to help avoid wasting an elite defense.
"This is about doing what's best for the Vikings in totality" - GM Nolan Teasley pic.twitter.com/4MTaOMmdX2
Should Teasley have offered a first-round pick to Indy to pair Taylor with Kirk Cousins? It certainly would have changed the offense for the better. But Teasley was always walking a tight line by looking to improve the team now while still having ammo for his first draft as general manager. If Cousins elevates the offense to a true contender, Teasley will earn his roses.
Right now, it seems Kyler Murray’s hamstring injury will keep the QB room intact, with possible moves coming after he returns to full participation. My gut feeling tells me Max Brosmer will likely be released and re-signed to the practice squad. It’s hard to see Minnesota carrying four QBs on the active roster.
Full exchange with Kevin O’Connell and @jzulgad on what the Cousins trade means for Kyler Murray. pic.twitter.com/PLUINL1n8n
This is a real possibility that must be considered during a celebratory moment for the Vikings fanbase. This move was made with one goal in mind: to elevate the offense for a team that already has a championship-level defense. After years of failed QB decisions, this may be the ultimate test for head coach Kevin O’Connell.
The Justin Jefferson conversation is a tough but necessary one to have. Can the Vikings really count on his continued patience if he ends his seventh season without a playoff win or a long-term answer at QB? The pressure should be sky-high to make a run this season.
I’m sure every person at TCO Performance Center would be ecstatic with this outcome! Cousins was off to a great start with the Raiders, with his 20 passing touchdowns putting him behind only Joe Burrow’s 23 for the league lead. Now Cousins joins a Vikings offense with a much better wideout core led by his old friend Jefferson.
"You have to go make it mean something with the way you play" - @KirkCousins8 on the potential to play at Lambeau Field on Sunday pic.twitter.com/TzOmbF7js4
I’d imagine Cousins also takes the field with an extra level of motivation after his first Vikings tenure ended at Lambeau Field with a torn Achilles in 2023. If Cousins can get ramped up and comfortable, he may have a massive day in Green Bay.
Get Vikings On SI straight to your inbox: sign up for our free newsletter here .
Jason Harmon grew up a diehard Vikings fan and has been doing Vikings content and coverage since 2023. He is the Vikings Content Curator for Sleeper and is a host on Purple Daily’s in-season spinoff podcast “Before I Die”. Jason and his family moved to the Twin Cities from Arizona in 2025 as he started covering the team full time.

title: Predicting How Patriots Fare vs. Lions: Will Christian Gonzalez, Defense Bounce Back?
full_text:
The New England Patriots , for the second time in four seasons, are set to play in Germany. This time, instead of the Indianapolis Colts in Frankfurt, they'll do battle against the 6-2 Detroit Lions in Munich — a far tougher test for a team that's teetering on the edge.
"I think they know how to win. They've built, I would say, a program that I know that they're proud of, and Dan's (Campbell) a good football coach," Mike Vrabel said. "So, certainly it'll be a huge challenge. They don't turn the ball over offensively at all."
Ahead of Week 10, Patriots On SI beat reporters Ethan Hurwitz and Zac Ventola break down how the game will unfold, which players will be x-factors and predict a final score. Who do you think is right?
Last week, the Patriots defense got historically gashed. The Green Bay Packers used an air raid-style of offense to run up the scoreboard. 45 points later and the Patriots defense was embarrassed. That can't happen again, especially against an offense in the Lions that has more weapons than Green Bay currently has.
Jahmyr Gibbs, Amon-Ra St. Brown, Sam LaPorta, Jameson Williams and Jared Goff make up a five-headed monster that can spin the dial at you from any which way. It doesn't matter if the Patriots can score at ease offensively this week. They'll need to be able to stop the Lions from doing the same.
X-Factor: CB Christian Gonzalez
Maybe the headliner from last week's loss was Gonzalez , who was on the opposing end of Matthew Golden and Christian Watson nearly every play. In four seasons, it was easily the cornerback's worst game as a pro. If the Patriots want to win, they can't have their best players like Gonzalez (and quarterback Drake Maye, who threw a trio of picks), struggling. Gonzalez — and the Patriots — need a major bounce back.
Final Score Prediction: Patriots 29, Lions 27
Because A.J. Brown and potentially Rhamondre Stevenson are options to return into the starting lineup, this is not a New England team that was depleted like they were a week ago against the Packers. Sooner or later, Brown's first breakout with his new team will come and it will help elevate the Patriots offense. Is that this week? I'm betting it is (but I've been wrong before).
With its current 5-4 record, the Patriots are far from locked into a playoff spot. Assuming New England will need to finish 10-7 (at worst) to get a postseason spot, it needs near-perfection for the remainder of regular season play. With five of its eight remaining games coming against teams currently in the playoff picture, Sunday morning might be a must-win.
In addition to the Lions, the Patriots still have battles with the Buffalo Bills, Minnesota Vikings, Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos on the horizon. In all likelihood, New England will need to win a pair of those games, with Detroit potentially being among the easier of the group.
X-Factor: LB Christian Elliss
Against a well-rounded Lions squad, the Patriots will first need to slow down the ground game . Detroit running back Jahmyr Gibbs has become one of the most dynamic playmakers in the entire NFL. The 24-year-old currently sits third in the league in rush yards (847) and is tied for second in rush touchdowns (nine).
Although the run defense has been far from New England’s defensive gripe—it allows the ninth-fewest rush yards per game in the NFL — stopping Gibbs is an entirely different challenge. The Patriots will need a herculean performance from their leading tackler — Elliss — to have a chance on Sunday against the Lions and their ground attack.
Final Score Prediction: Lions 37, Patriots 30
While I do not expect the Patriots offense to falter, I find it hard to see a world where it can out-produce the Lions. Detroit has built the perfectly terrifying two-headed monster between wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown and Gibbs. Plus, it found an ideal game manager in quarterback Jared Goff.
By the end of the battle, Gibbs will have over 200 all-purpose yards and a pair of touchdowns, St. Brown will tally a score of his own and the Lions will be partying all the way back home from Munich.

title: Patriots' Playoff Hopes Could Hinge on Critical Lions Matchup
full_text:
The New England Patriots are preparing for an overseas battle against the Detroit Lions with significant implications for their playoff hopes. At 5-4, Sunday's contest isn't necessarily a must-win for New England, but it's about as close as it gets. With a difficult stretch of games looming after their upcoming bye week, the Patriots have little room for error as they look to remain in the AFC playoff picture. Here's why this matchup matters, along with what New England needs to do to come away with a win.
For the Patriots, 10 is the magic number. If they reach that win mark by season's end, they'll have a good chance of punching their ticket to the postseason. Five more wins, and you're (likely) in. But their remaining schedule is not forgiving; if anything, it got harder after the Nov. 10 trade deadline. After facing the Lions and having their Week 11 bye, New England will play the lowly Los Angeles Chargers before a rematch with the AFC-leading Buffalo Bills. From there, the Patriots will have a short week, hosting the Minnesota Vikings on Thursday Night Football. Minnesota boasts arguably the NFL's best defense, allowing the fewest points per game (14.5) and 280 yards per game, good for second-fewest in the league. Their Achilles ' heel was their offense, as the QB rotation of Kyler Murray, Carson Wentz, and Max Brosmer led to a passing game ranking 31st in yards per game (266.8). However, their deadline acquisition of Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins potentially makes this matchup far scarier for New England.
Trade: The Raiders are trading QB Kirk Cousins to the Vikings, per @rapsheet and me. pic.twitter.com/7Hxjt6TyR5
The Patriots will then face Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs, who traded for Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Josh Downs, on Monday Night Football before closing out the season against the New York Jets, Denver Broncos and Miami Dolphins. Realistically, New England has just three remaining games in which they will likely enter as the favorite: the Chargers, Jets and Dolphins. Say the Patriots can take care of business in those three matchups, they'll still need two additional victories against the Lions, Vikings, Bills, Chiefs or Broncos to reach the 10-win mark. Detroit is arguably one of New England's better remaining opportunities to pick up a quality win. Coming out of Munich with a win would put the Patriots in a much better position heading into their bye week, while a loss would leave them needing multiple upsets down the stretch.
Injuries have consistently limited New England's offensive personnel this season, but the Patriots could be getting some important contributors back for their bout in Germany. Wide receiver A.J. Brown returned to practice for the first time in two weeks as he continues dealing with ankle and knee injuries, the latter of which may be connected to a reported degenerative knee condition. Brown has been limited throughout the season, missing six games through the first nine weeks while recording just nine catches for 101 yards. He was a limited participant Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday and is listed as questionable for Sunday's matchup. Despite ESPN's Adam Schefter reporting that running back Rhamondre Stevenson is dealing with a knee tendon issue that could sideline him for a short period, the veteran back has made encouraging progress. After missing Wednesday's practice, he returned as a limited participant Thursday and again on Friday.
RB Rhamondre Stevenson (No. 38, knee) is working off to the side at Patriots practice in Munich. Still a chance he could play Sunday. pic.twitter.com/9froK0PKFZ
We've seen similar situations play out in New England this season. Offensive tackle Will Campbell was initially expected to miss time after suffering a reported knee sprain in Week 5 against the Las Vegas Raiders, while running back TreVeyon Henderson was reportedly dealing with a high ankle sprain the same week.
Both ultimately played the following game. "I think that's just, speaks to, you know, first off, the media not really knowing 100 percent what they're talking about a lot of the time," Maye said when asked about Stevenson practicing. Getting Stevenson back would be a significant boost for the Patriots; he's their leading rusher, and his work as a pass protector for Maye is invaluable. Fullback Reggie Gilliam (knee) and guard Greg Van Roten (hamstring), after spending time on injured reserve, have had their 21-day practice windows opened. Gilliam returned to practice this week, and Van Roten's window opened last week. Neither has been activated yet, but both are questionable for Sunday.
With fellow guard Walter Rouse also questionable while working through concussion protocol, the Patriots could have some important decisions to make regarding their offensive line depth. Getting even one or two of these players back would be a welcome development for an offense that has struggled to stay healthy. It could also come at an ideal time, as Detroit has been vulnerable defensively throughout the season. The Lions are allowing an average of 355 yards per game, tied for 26th in the NFL, and have struggled to create turnovers. Detroit has forced just eight takeaways through its first nine games, the same number as New England. The Lions have also ruled out safety Kerby Joseph and cornerback D.J. Reed for Sunday, potentially giving Maye and the Patriots' offense an opportunity to exploit a depleted secondary.
New England will have its hands full on the other side of the ball. Detroit's offense is one of the most volatile in the league, headlined by wide receivers Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams, along with running back Jahmyr Gibbs. With playmakers galore, Detroit's high-flying offense ranks 5th in yards per game (379.8). The Patriots will need a much better defensive performance than what they delivered last week against the Green Bay Packers. New England surrendered 478 total yards of offense and allowed the most points scored in Gillette Stadium to date (45). That change starts with Christian Gonzalez. The Patriots' star cornerback, who recently became the highest-paid cornerback in NFL history, is coming off one of the worst performances of his career. According to Pro Football Focus, Gonzalez allowed 11 catches on 12 targets for 192 yards and a touchdown against Green Bay. "As confident as I always am," Gonzalez said when asked about his confidence in bouncing back. "It's a new week. It's the same confidence that I always have, the same confidence I'll always go in with." New England cannot afford another performance like that against a Detroit offense with this much firepower. Gonzalez and the rest of the secondary will need to bounce back if the Patriots hope to leave Germany with a win.

title: Patriots' Drake Maye Faces Long MVP Odds Heading into Week 10
full_text:
Nine weeks into the season and the odds are currently not in Drake Maye's favor to win this year's Most Valuable Player award. After finishing second in the running in 2025, the New England Patriots quarterback is a bit away from that top spot.
But he's surprisingly closer than some people might have expected. Despite being tied for the league lead with 11 interceptions , Maye has the 12th-best odds to take him the trophy ( according to FanDuel Sportsbook ). He's right next to Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott with +10000 odds, and is a step above last year's MVP winner in Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford (+25000).
It's a quarterback award and 12 of the top 13 players all play the postion. Only Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs (who the Patriots are set to play in Munich, Germany, on Sunday) is the only non-quarterback with better odds than Maye (+8000).
Here's a look at where Maye currently sits when it comes to MVP odds heading into Week 10:
Players With Highest MVP Odds
Current FanDuel Odds (As of Nov. 13)
Cincinnati Bengals QB Joe Burrow
Buffalo Bills QB Josh Allen
San Francisco 49ers QB Brock Purdy
Jacksonville Jaguars QB Trevor Lawrence
Green Bay Packers QB Jordan Love
Minnesota Vikings QB Kirk Cousins
Chicago Bears QB Caleb Williams
Kansas City Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes
Houston Texans QB C.J. Stroud
Detroit Lions QB Jared Goff
Detroit Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs
New England Patriots QB Drake Maye
Dallas Cowboys QB Dak Prescott
Based on how Burrow, Allen and Purdy are playing to this point in the year, you'll be hard pressed to find someone who'll vote for Maye over those three. When you consider how injured this Patriots offense is though, that might warrant more of a discussion for Maye's case.
So far, he's played significant snaps without his top three wide receivers (A.J. Brown, Romeo Doubs, Mack Hollins), his top tight end (Hunter Henry), his second-best running back TreVeyon Henderson) and a myriad of offensive linemen (Mike Onwenu, Greg Van Roten, Alijah Vera-Tucker, Ben Brown).
Compared to last year, 2026 hasn't been as kind to Maye as last year was. Through nine games, the 24-year-old is 178-for-272 for 2,501 total yards and 21 total touchdowns. Through the first nine games of 2025, he was 189-for-255 for 2,555 total yards and 19 total touchdowns.
The records were also vastly different. Sitting at 5-4 now, the Patriots are clinging onto the final AFC playoff spot. They were sitting at 7-2 last year and atop the AFC East at this point a year ago today.
Some of that has fallen on Maye, who has two games this year with three interceptions. A rough September put the Patriots behind the 8-ball, but he'd rebound perfectly one month later. Maye was named the AFC Offensive Player of the Month for October and rounded into form as the Patriots started to win.
As it stands right now, Maye walking away with the MVP award is a little far-fetched. But if he's able to regain control of the train and start conducting it down the rails like he did a season ago, those odds could easily shoot up.
Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change.

title: Patriots Attempting to Snap Nearly Year-Long NFC Streak — Plus Major Playoff Implications
full_text:
An unfortunate trend started for the New England Patriots after taking a humiliating loss to the Seattle Seahawks in Super Bowl LX. Since losing to the Seahawks last February, the Patriots have now gone on a four-game losing streak against NFC opponents.
Back-to-back losses against Seattle in the Super Bowl and Week 1 of the 2026 season make up the first two dropped games. Then, a Thursday night football loss to Chicago in Week 7 and last week's let-down game against the Packers put the Patriots at an astonishing 0-4 in their last four games against NFC opponents.
The last win the Patriots had against an NFC opponent, came on December 1, 2025, when the eventual AFC Champions rolled past the New York Giants on Monday Night Football.
Heading into another game against an NFC opponent, the Patriots will try to right the ship against the Detroit Lions in Germany, Sunday morning.
The way NFL scheduling works requires each division to play another division within their conference and in the opposite conference. These matchups rotate every four years and this season, the AFC East was tasked with facing all AFC West and NFC North teams.
The Patriots have already won their first AFC West game, beating the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 5, but their series against the NFC North isn't going so well.
After dropping games to the Bears and Packers, the Patriots are 0-2 so far against the NFC North. This week's match against Detroit will be New England's third game in the series.
Widely considered to be the best and most competitive division in all of football, the NFC North has a combined record of 25-9 on the year and total four losses against non-division opponents.
The four teams in the North also have the highest point differential of any four divisional teams in the NFL, totaling a +145 point margin against all their opponents.
After playing the Lions in Week 10, New England will host the Minnesota Vikings in Week 14 to finish their slate against NFC opponents.
Unfortunatelty for New England, the four games they're assigned to play against the NFC North are arguably the four most difficult games they'll play all season. But, there is an upside to that.
While losing never helps your team secure a playoff spot, taking a loss against an NFC opponent has less implications on playoff seeding than losses against an AFC opponent.
When the NFL seeds playoff teams they look at each team in the following order: overall record, head-to-head matchups, common opponents, and strength of schedule.
Here's how the NFL playoff picture looks entering Week 10 Which team is the biggest surprise? pic.twitter.com/Ibm9GKA22N
Despite sitting just over a .500 record, the Patriots have only lost one matchup against an AFC opponent, dropping a Week 3 game in Jacksonville. The Jaguars are heavily favorited to win the AFC South, so this wouldn't have much of an effect on Wild Card seeding anyway.
Common opponents are the next layer of seeding considerations, and the Patriots have faired really well against the AFC. They have a valuable win over the Buffalo Bills, who have beaten every other team they've faced. Depending on how the rest of the season plays out, New England has held their own against AFC opponents, which sets them up for success when striving for a five through seven seed.
Lastly, the Patriots have one of the most difficult strength of schedules in the league. Not only did they play the best division in the NFC (and arguably the best division in the AFC), but they played a first-place schedule after winning the AFC East last year, which requires the Patriots to face other first-place teams like the Seahawks, Jaguars, and Steelers.
The NFC North is a PROBLEM 🔥 pic.twitter.com/mkox9AGH18
If the New England ends up in a tie-breaker situation with another Wild Card team, their strength of schedule will likely give them the higher playoff seed. Six of the last eight games for the Patriots are against AFC teams, and will have very decisive outcomes.
Regardless of AFC playoff seeding, if the Patriots can reverse their NFC misfortune this Sunday and enter the bye week at 6-4, they'll show that they're ready to compete with the rest of the NFL for the remainder of the season.

title: Patriots Explain How They're Adjusting to Germany, Time Change, International Schedule
full_text:
Hunter Henry has been on both of the New England Patriots ' most recent international trips to Frankfurt, Germany (2023) and London, England (2024).
Both of them ended up being bad losses for the Patriots and games that the tight end doesn't want to remember.
But those two weeks helped give the 31-year-old the knowledge about how to handle overseas flights. From the long flight, the time change and the switched-up schedule, it's a different animal. Henry knows what to expect.
"It can mess you up a little bit, but you just got to get over there and get adjusted," he said Wednesday. "Get your clock adjusted and get ready to go. I mean, at the end of the day, once we line up and go on Sunday, the ball kicks off, it'll be time to go."
Henry said there isn't much of a secret sauce when it comes to these games. Instead, he says it's just a lot of rest that helps the body.
"Just try to sleep and recover as much as I can," he said. "Be ready to go. I mean, I don't know. ... Just recover and sleep."
Last year, the Patriots didn't go abroad for a game. The Minnesota Vikings, however, took two weeks to hit Dublin, Ireland and London for games. That was exhausting for Walter Rouse, then a second-year tackle.
Now with the Patriots, Rouse knows everything that comes with these long experiences. He told Patriots On SI that everything — from the culture to the food — can be factors in these long trips.
"Getting used to the environment over there is completely different," Rouse said. "The food is different than what we used to in terms of what our bodies are used to with the foods here and whatnot. So there's all the different factors that go into it.
"I think mainly it's just the time difference. ... By the time it's game day, it's like a regular Sunday for us."
Rouse is working his way through the NFL's concussion protocol this week and his status for the game remains up in the air right now. He's been a limited participant in practice.
On social media, Mack Hollins often posts videos called "Mack Hacks" — where the wide receiver details different or innovative ways to perform a task. When asked if he had any hacks for dealing with an international flight, he had several.
"On the flight, (a) fun fact (is) that the humidity level is lower than the Sahara on a plane, so hydrating," Hollins said. "But if it's a long flight, you don't want to drink too much water because then you're up and down going to the bathroom instead of sleeping. Sleep aids, kiwi, bananas can help. Tart cherry juice. ... You don't want to just be pounding too much water."
Hollins was a second-year player when he was overseas with the Philadelphia Eagles in 2018. That trip helped give him a baseline of how to approach these trips.
"When you get there, sun exposure, the best you can," he said. "You can stay out in the sun, the better. I like to get in water if I can, cold walter. But yeah, if you can do all those things and then try to stay up as late as you can, like to get back on a regular schedule, you'll give yourself a good chance."
Hollins said that some of his teammates had never been outside of the United States, so that this trip will be their first taste of flying internationally. It's a great opportunity for a team just a hair over .500 to bond and try to take it the atmosphere.
"There's a lot of guys who got to get their passports this year. Like they've never left the country," Hollins said. "I got a passport because we went to London (in 2018). So they've never seen the world other than in pictures. So I do think you should take advantage of it if you can."

title: Patriots Have Ticking Clock When it Comes to Activating Veteran OG
full_text:
Just a few days until the New England Patriots take on the Detroit Lions in Munich, the Patriots haven't decided on who will be their starting left guard on Sunday.
The Patriots have 52 of their 53 roster spots filled up, and Mike Vrabel said prior to the trip that they plan to fill that final opening. One name — Greg Van Roten — sticks out as a possible candidate to be the 53rd player on the roster, considering how banged-up the offensive line is right now. He's dealing with a hamstring injury.
"I think we'll see how Greg comes out of practice today," Vrabel said Friday. "I know he's been returned to play. You know, see where Walter (Rouse) is in the protocol and then go from there."
Ben Brown, the starting left guard from a week ago, has already been ruled out and didn't make the trip to Germany. He injured his knee last week against the Green Bay Packers and wasn't spotted in the team's final practice before departing for the airport. Rouse, Brown's immediate backup, missed Wednesday's practice and continues to work his way through the league's concussion protocol.
Rouse was practicing in a red non-contact uniform. Both options have been limited this week.
So it feels like Van Roten has the opportunity to return to play for the first time since Week 4.
"We'll have to go through practice and kind of see where guys are this afternoon," Vrabel said about some of the players that are injured going through practice, which also includes running back Rhamondre Stevenson and wide receiver A.J. Brown .
But there isn't that much time left for the Patriots to make a decision on Van Roten. After missing time on IR, he's been designated to return and has until Nov. 24 to return.
If Van Roten doesn't end up being activated to the 53-man roster and the Patriots choose to plug up the gap with a temporary fix, they can elevate someone from the practice squad — which traveled to Germany for practices. Andrew Rupcich and Xavier Newman-Johnson are options at guard, and Newman-Johnson has already been elevated once before (Week 7 vs. Chicago Bears).
Right now, the Patriots are likely locked into an offensive line of Will Campbell at left tackle, Jared Wilson at center, Matt Pryor at right guard and Morgan Moses at right tackle. It's safe to assume that the left guard job will go to either Van Roten or Rouse — and Van Roten's experience is certainly the better option for the Patriots heading into Sunday's game.
Fullback Reggie Gilliam was also designated to return off of IR this week as well, so if Van Roten isn't able to go, he could end up grabbing that final roster spot.

title: Rhamondre Stevenson Injury Updates: Latest on Patriots RB for Week 10 vs. Lions
full_text:
After a gloomy outlook just more than 48 hours ago, the New England Patriots could end up getting some good news about starting running back Rhamondre Stevenson this week against the Detroit Lions.
Last week, Stevenson went down with a knee injury and wouldn't return to the game against the Green Bay Packers . One day later, it was reported that he's dealing with a knee tendon issue and would likely miss this week's game in Munich, Germany.
Well, while nothing has been confirmed yet about Stevenson's status for Sunday's game, the 28-year-old was spotted on the practice field for the Patriots' walkthrough on Thursday. While the rest of the team stretched and did several drills, Stevenson was off to the side running by himself.
On the team's second injury report, Stevenson was upgraded from DID NOT PARTICIPATE to LIMITED — a step in the right direction for him.
"I think that it speaks to - first off, the media, and not knowing 100% what they're talking about a lot of the time," quarterback Drake Maye said after practice. "And of a guy that wants to be out there. Wants to be back for his team. We’re in the midst of planning to make a run here and win a big one before the bye. So, this is a time for a lot of the players on this team to try and get out there, play with their teammates. He’s a great player and he can help us out."
Should Stevenson be able to suit up, he'll be one of three running backs on the active roster for the game against the Lions (along with Corey Kiner and Lan Larison). TreVeyon Henderson has already been ruled out for the game with an illness that's kept him out of the last two games.
The Patriots are glad to see Stevenson back on the practice field in some capacity and it's telling that his teammates, like DeMario Douglas, are speaking about his possible return to game action.
"He's a dog, man. I know some people that probably like, 'man, I ain't even finna try,'" Douglas said. "But his situation, man, I be talking to him be like, 'I finna try. I finna do what I can do. He's working. He's getting better. When the time comes, I know he working to get better."
Injuries have been the name of the game for New England throughout 2026, with key contributors getting banged up all season. Stevenson was just the latest to suffer some sort of injury this year and with the bye week looming, the Patriots could be wise to rest Stevenson.
Still, considering he's moving around in some capacity, the Patriots have to feel good about where their leader rusher is a few days ahead of Week 10.
"Anytime you lose players like that, you feel it because he’s such a valuable part of everything you do," offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels said. "But why we have a lot of guys that are taking reps in practice. We’ve had a lot of guys doing that all year long. They know what to do. It might not be the same volume of experience that certainly Rhamondre has, but we got a lot of guys in that room that we have confidence in."
Stevenson was one of 11 players who was limited on Thursday, and one of four (Cameron Latu, Walter Rouse, Brenden Schooler) who was upgraded from Wednesday's report.

title: Patriots QB Drake Maye Staying Level-Headed This Week vs. Lions
full_text:
It wasn't pretty for Drake Maye last week. For the second time this season, the New England Patriots quarterback threw three interceptions in a game in what turned into a 45-27 loss to the Green Bay Packers — a performance he said was disappointing.
Now that the page has turned to the Detroit Lions this week (in an entirely country), Maye is confident in himself and his Patriots teammates in righting the ship.
"I think just try not to get lost in why we're coming over here, to play a game and to win a football game," Maye said Thursday, later saying that there's pressure every week to perform.
Maye has been up-and-down this season. Some weeks, he's on fire. Others, like last week against the great Packers defense, it's not that great. With the Week 11 bye week looming on the horizon, the Patriots need to find a way to get a win against the Lions .
That will start with how the 24-year-old quarterback plays.
"I think you're trying to not to get too high or low through the highs and lows," Maye said. "That's part of this game, especially this position. This game will humble you and also give you some special moments for the rest of your life to remember, so just reminding (myself of) that and just trusting my work throughout the week, trusting my teammates, my coaches and just going out there and trusting my ability."
This year, Maye is among the worst when it comes to turning the ball over.
But his abilities at making plays happen with his legs and his arm strength are going to be critical as the Patriots continue to battle injuries. The hope is that Maye, despite earlier struggles, will carry the offense on his shoulders to their first international win since 2017 (a 33-8 win over the then-Oakland Raiders in Mexico City).
Maye is confident in himself. So is his head coach. Against a potential playoff team like Detroit, it's another opportunity for the former All-Pro to prove himself.
"I think that he'll come back, he'll bounce back," Mike Vrabel said Monday on his quarterback. "He's made a lot of plays for us and helped us win, and he'll continue to do that. He did that at times (Sunday). I know Drake, I know he's already back to work and focused on how he can improve and how he can help this football team."

title: Patriots Get Encouraging Injury Updates at First Germany Practice
full_text:
After flying through the night to Germany, the New England Patriots took to the pitch for a Thursday walkthrough in Munich. Getting ready for their Week 10 matchup with the Detroit Lions, the 5-4 Patriots have some work to do if they want to get back into the win column.
Part of that is getting healthy. Injuries continue to plague this team all year and it's led to several players missing practice throughout the season. On Wednesday, before their flight, the Patriots had practice with seven players missing.
Now in Munich, they got good news about some of those banged-up players. Tight end Cameron Latu (hamstring), offensive guard Walter Rouse (concussion protocol), safety Brenden Schooler (hamstring) all returned to practice after missing yesterday's session.
Running back Rhamondre Stevenson, who missed the first practice with a knee injury, returned, but was working out by himself at the start of practice.
Stevenson, who suffered a knee injury against the Green Bay Packers last week, would be a surprise if he ended up playing against the Lions. Reports indicate he's dealing with a tendon issue that could hold him out of Sunday's game.
Having him back on the field in some capacity is a good sign for one of the team's most consistent players.
"There's a chance that anything could happen, but I'm not going to speculate on any of that," Mike Vrabel said when asked about if Stevenson lands on IR. "You guys are just – let's get past the injuries here. Let's try to focus on the Lions and what we need to do to try to find a way to win the game. But the injuries and the injured reserve, I mean, if you pay attention, we don't have too many spots left here to bring guys back on injured reserve."
If Stevenson isn't able to go, the brunt of the running game will fall on Corey Kiner and Lan Larison. Terrell Jennings is also on the practice squad as a depth option.
Ahead of their trip, the Patriots already ruled out three players — running back TreVeyon Henderson, offensive guard Ben Brown and cornerback Carlton Davis. Henderson has dealt with a neurological health scare that sent him to the hospital , while both Brown and Davis left last week with knee injuries.
It's been a trying season for Brown and Davis, who have spent a lot of time trying to get healthy at different points in the year.
The Patriots will have another practice on Friday ahead of their game on Sunday against a really good Detroit team .
"I'm excited to get ready for the Lions," Vrabel said. "That's it. It's what we were trying to do before. I think it was good to be able to get in here Tuesday afternoon to kind of get a jump start on things, understand the schedule and how we're traveling and the intent of it. It's another good football team, so that's where our focus is."

title: Lions Pose Difficult Threat to Patriots Defense This Week
full_text:
It's not going to get any easy for the New England Patriots this week. They have to fly halfway across the world to suit up for a game in Munich, Germany, and have to face off against one of the NFC's top teams yet again.
The 6-2 Detroit Lions, a week removed from a 19-9 win over the Miami Dolphins, are looking like they are rounding into a true form offensively. For a Patriots team that gave up 45 points to the Green Bay Packers a week ago , they'll need to be able to bounce back and limit a unit that is deep beyond belief.
Jared Goff. Jahmyr Gibbs. Amon-Ra St. Brown. Jameson Williams. The Lions have weapons to push a defense to its limit, and it's worked this year.
"I think they know how to win," Mike Vrabel said Wednesday. "They've built, I would say, a program that I know that they're proud of, and Dan's (Campbell) a good football coach. I think Jared's playing at a high level. Continued the last three years, he's been at a high level. Great skill players, speed, physical. ... They don't turn the ball over offensively at all."
Goff's ability to get better and better in this Lions offense is part of the reason why they've been so good. He was limited in Detroit's Wednesday practice with a chest injury — something that shouldn't impact his availability for the game. He's 185-for-273 for 2,134 yards and 15 touchdowns. He also doesn't turn the ball over carelessly.
He's thrown just two interceptions in eight games, and the Lions in total have turned it over just five times, good for the second-lowest mark in the entire NFL.
"I think that's just because they haven't really put the ball in harm's way," Vrabel said. "They've created X plays. Gibbs leads the league in touches. Coordinator wise, I think the run game and the scheme kind of mirrors what it's always mirrored. I know there's a few pass game wrinkles, but I still think some of the same things and same concepts that they liked have carried over, and (Lions offensive coordinator) Drew's (Petzing) done a good job. He gives Jared a lot of autonomy at the line of scrimmage to get him in the right play.
Gibbs is a threat to score every time he touches the ball, as is wideout St. Brown. They've combined for 16 touchdowns on the year this far. Based on how New England's defense looked last week, that could be easy pickings for Detroit.
The Patriots have already landed in Germany , while the Lions are flying out later tonight. We'll have a few days to break down this matchup further, but based on how the team's are trending going into this one, the Lions offense certainly has a leg up.

title: Saints Injury Report: Tyler Shough Loses Two Key Protectors Against Panthers
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints will be short-handed in Sunday’s rivalry game with the Carolina Panthers , with the heaviest hits being on the offensive line.
Head coach Kellen Moore ruled out multiple players with injuries, including two starting offensive linemen: center Erik McCoy (bicep) and right tackle Taliese Fuaga (knee). The team will also miss rookie running back CJ Donaldson (shoulder) and second-round defensive lineman Christen Miller (knee).
The Saints got a little more than three quarters of football out of their starting five offensive linemen last week before McCoy exited with an injury. Then Fuaga suffered a knee sprain in practice. Moore said Fuaga isn’t expected to miss enough time to land on injured reserve, but McCoy’s outlook is less certain.
A few other players are questionable for Sunday’s game with the Carolina Panthers. Running back Travis Etienne Jr. (hamstring) is the big name, but cornerback Martin Emerson Jr. is one to watch, too. We’ll find out for sure when the inactives list is published on Sunday.
The Saints got more than three quarters of action from their starting offensive line in last week's win over the Cleveland Browns before McCoy exited with a biceps injury.
The situation worsened when Fuaga suffered a knee sprain during practice, leaving New Orleans without two important pieces of its offensive front.
Moore indicated Fuaga's injury is not expected to require a stint on injured reserve, although McCoy's recovery timeline remains uncertain.
McCoy's absence could prove particularly challenging as he plays a critical role in identifying defensive fronts, communicating protection adjustments and helping maintain continuity across the offensive line as the center.
Without him, New Orleans must rely on Cesar Ruiz to handle those responsibilities while adjusting to a reshuffled interior with Jeremiah Wright taking Ruiz’s spot at right guard.
Fuaga's injury creates another significant concern at right tackle, where Asim Richards could be called upon to step into the starting lineup.
The Saints also dealt with injuries involving left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. (ankle) and guard David Edwards (knee) throughout the week. While both returned to full participation Friday, it’s another sign that this unit is not even close to 100%.
Even with Banks and Edwards, losing two starters makes it hard for an offensive line that has struggled with pass protection and consistency in the running game.

title: Saints Stock Up: Audric Estimé Makes a Statement, Pass Rush Keeps Rolling
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints gave their home crowd reason to celebrate on Sunday at Caesars Superdome, clinching a thrilling 23-22 victory in overtime over the Cleveland Browns .
While improving the Saints to 3-5 and snapping a home slump, the win was far from flawless.
The result grants head coach Kellen Moore a brief reprieve, but ongoing flaws demonstrate that his standing stays uncertain.
With a tough slate ahead, New Orleans needs to fix key errors to sustain progress.
Below are the Saints players and units whose stock rose after Sunday's thrilling finish.
Despite rejoining the Saints via waivers after getting cut after training camp, running back Audric Estimé made a compelling argument for an expanded role in New Orleans' backfield despite being back in New Orleans for a week.
The second-year running back rushed for 72 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries, averaging 4.8 yards per attempt.
His biggest contribution came late in regulation when he powered into the end zone from 2 yards out to give New Orleans a 16-13 advantage.
Beyond the touchdown, Estimé provided the physicality and downhill running that the Saints have struggled to establish consistently.
Charlie Smyth made the most of his opportunity after he became the starter after the Saints released Daniel Carlson .
The Irish-born kicker connected on three of his four field-goal attempts against Cleveland, converting from 30, 27 and 48 yards.
With both offenses struggling to finish drives, Smyth accounted for all nine of New Orleans' points through the first three quarters.
His 48-yard field goal in the fourth quarter briefly gave the Saints a 9-6 advantage.
The Saints' pass rush continues to emerge as one of the team's biggest strengths, with Carl Granderson and Chase Young leading a pass rush that made life miserable for Cleveland quarterback Shedeur Sanders .
Granderson recorded two sacks against the Browns, extending his streak of games with multiple sacks to four. According to the Saints, he became the first NFL player since 2013 to accomplish that feat.
Young added his eighth sack of the season, while Kaden Elliss and Khristian Boyd also got into the action as New Orleans finished with five sacks.
The Saints' defensive front also made its presence felt against the run, limiting Cleveland to 95 rushing yards while consistently disrupting the Browns' offensive rhythm.
Perhaps the unit's most impressive moment came near the goal line, when New Orleans delivered a critical fourth-down stand to keep Cleveland out of the end zone.
Although the Saints' secondary remains vulnerable to explosive plays, the defensive front has become a reliable source of pressure and physicality.

title: Saints Trading DL Godchaux to Jaguars Signals Continued Youth Movement on Defense
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints are finalizing a trade that will send veteran defensive tackle Davon Godchaux to the Jacksonville Jaguars , another move signaling the organization's willingness to prioritize its future over veteran experience.
NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported that New Orleans will receive a 2028 sixth-round draft pick that could become a 2027 sixth-round pick if Jacksonville acquires one through a trade or the compensatory process.
The deal comes just one day after the Saints secured a thrilling 23-22 overtime win over the Cleveland Browns , improving to 3-5.
While the trade provides New Orleans with additional draft capital, it offers little immediate financial relief.
For salary cap reasons, the Saints had restructured Godchaux's contract by converting the bulk of his pay into a signing bonus, leaving only $650,000 of his $1.3 million base salary.
As Godchaux turns 32 this week and approaches the final year of his deal, he became an expendable veteran for a team placing greater emphasis on nurturing younger talent.
New Orleans initially acquired the Plaquemine, Louisiana native from the New England Patriots in March 2025, surrendering a 2026 seventh-round pick while assuming the remaining two years and $11 million of his contract following a restructuring.
Although Godchaux appeared in all eight games this season, his role has gotten smaller and smaller by the week. Godchaux started the first five games, but hehas  played just eight, 18 and 12 defensive snaps over the last three games.
However, Godchaux still contributed to one of the Saints' biggest defensive plays Sunday, helping stop Cleveland on a critical fourth-and-goal opportunity.
The departure of Godchaux opens up substantial playing time for the Saints' younger defensive linemen, most notably Khristian Boyd and rookie second-round selection Christen Miller .
Boyd, who recorded a sack and a tackle for loss Sunday and played a key role alongside Godchaux in the goal-line stand, is expected to see an expanded workload at center of New Orleans' defensive line.
At the same time, accelerating Miller's progress becomes more urgent, especially since the rookie was a healthy scratch for the matchup against Cleveland.
Ultimately, this deal signifies more for New Orleans than just swapping a veteran player for late-round draft compensation.
It reflects a clear strategic shift by the front office to assess its youth roster while continuing to stockpile future draft assets.
How well New Orleans fills the void left by Godchaux upfront will largely hinge on whether Boyd and Miller can take full advantage of their new opportunities.

title: The Good, Bad and Ugly From Saints' Wild Overtime Win Over Browns
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints finally gave their home crowd something to celebrate Sunday, securing a thrilling 23-22 overtime victory over the Cleveland Browns at Caesars Superdome.
But while the Saints improved to 3-5 and snapped their home winless streak, the victory was far from pretty.
For Kellen Moore , the victory provided some much-needed relief, but it also exposed several problems that continue to plague his team and will keep him on the hot seat.
With a difficult stretch of the schedule ahead, the Saints have plenty to clean up if they want to build momentum.
Here’s a look at the good, the bad and the ugly from New Orleans' dramatic overtime victory over Cleveland.
Tyler Shough continues to show his clutch gene, even if the organization he plays for is in shambles.
Shough completed 21 of 35 passes for 265 yards and a touchdown while adding 51 rushing yards on 10 carries. While he didn’t do much for most of the game, it’s when his team needed him the most he stepped up. His composure in critical situations stood out.
Trailing 13-9 late in the fourth quarter, Shough orchestrated a 55-yard touchdown drive in just 50 seconds, highlighted by a 33-yard completion to Chris Olave that set up Audric Estimé 's 2-yard touchdown run.
After Cleveland forced overtime, Shough responded again, leading an 11-play, 74-yard touchdown drive capped by a perfectly placed 15-yard pass to ever-reliable tight end Juwan Johnson . That drive was his fifth game-winning drive of the season.
The performance was particularly encouraging, given that Shough was sacked five times and played late in the game without starting center Erik McCoy .
Estimé also provided an unexpected spark, rushing for 72 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries just days after being claimed off waivers.
Despite scoring 23 points, the New Orleans Saints ' offense struggled again.
The Saints didn't score a touchdown until Estimé’s run with 58 seconds remaining, settling for field goals despite moving the ball effectively at times. The Saints also only converted on two of their five red zone opportunities.
Their struggles were particularly evident in the first half, when New Orleans outgained Cleveland 176-80 but entered halftime tied 3-3.
The offensive line also had its share of problems, surrendering five sacks and repeatedly forcing Shough to escape pressure.
Even with left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. back, the Saints struggled to protect their quarterback consistently.
Sure, several individuals had encouraging performances, but New Orleans still lacks inspiration on offense and the ability to put opponents away.
Without starting quarterback Deshaun Watson , the Saints had multiple chances to take control against Cleveland but instead needed late-game heroics.
The Saints won't always be fortunate enough to overcome those shortcomings. The Carolina Panthers are up next, but the following three games: two road games back-to-back against the Chicago Bears and the Cincinnati Bengals and a home matchup against the Green Bay Packers .
If there's one area that should frustrate Kellen Moore more than anything else, it's the Saints' inability to protect the football.
New Orleans committed two costly second-quarter turnovers, both involving rookies, that completely changed the complexion of the game.
First-round pick Jordyn Tyson , making his NFL debut after missing the first seven games with a hamstring injury, fumbled near Cleveland's goal line moments after making his first career reception on the same play.
The turnover wasted a promising scoring opportunity after Shough connected with Barion Brown for a 52-yard gain.
Things somehow got worse moments later.
After the defense forced a punt, Brown fumbled the return, giving Cleveland possession at the Saints' 19-yard line.
Fortunately for New Orleans, the defense bailed out the offense and special teams, stopping Quinshon Judkins on fourth-and-goal from the 1-yard line.
But the mistakes weren't limited to turnovers.
The Saints' defense also surrendered a 64-yard touchdown pass from Shedeur Sanders to KC Concepcion Jr. immediately after taking a 9-6 lead in the fourth quarter.
Then, after Estimé put New Orleans ahead with 58 seconds remaining, the defense allowed Cleveland to move into position for a game-tying 51-yard field goal.
And even after Shough delivered an overtime touchdown, the Saints surrendered a 39-yard touchdown reception to Harold Fannin Jr. , forcing the defense to make one final stand.
New Orleans escaped with a victory, but the combination of turnovers, blown coverage and late defensive breakdowns nearly turned a much-needed win into another devastating loss.

title: Saints Turn Snoozefest Into Thriller, Escape With Overtime Win Over Browns
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints secured their first home victory of the season in thrilling fashion on Sunday at Caesars Superdome, defeating the Cleveland Browns 23-22 in overtime.
Quarterback Tyler Shough connected with tight end Juwan Johnson for a 15-yard touchdown pass with 4:17 remaining in the extra period, giving New Orleans a seven-point lead. Cleveland quickly countered with a touchdown drive of its own, but the Saints’ defense shut down the Browns’ potential game-winning two-point conversion attempt to seal the dramatic win.
With the victory, the Saints improved to 3-5 while snapping a frustrating home winless streak. The loss dropped the Browns to 5-4. What began as a sluggish defensive battle turned into one of the wildest finishes of the NFL season, featuring 20 fourth-quarter points and an overtime showdown after three quarters dominated by field goals.
Shough delivered an impressive performance, completing 21 of 35 passes for 265 yards while adding 51 rushing yards on 10 carries.
On the other side, Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders was equally stellar, throwing for 297 yards and two touchdowns on 19-of-31 passing.
However, running back Audric Estime proved to be New Orleans’ secret weapon. Re-joining the team just days before kickoff after being cut following training camp, Estime provided a massive spark with 15 carries for 72 yards and a touchdown to open up the offense.
The game reached peak chaos late in the fourth quarter. Up 9-6, New Orleans watched Cleveland reclaim the lead on a dramatic 4-yard touchdown connection from Sanders to receiver Concepcion with 5:21 left. Sanders hit Concepcion on a deep route before the receiver cut left and sprinted into the corner of the end zone, stunning the home crowd.
Unfazed, the Saints executed a swift scoring drive that took just 50 seconds. Shough found wideout Chris Olave for a 33-yard completion to Cleveland’s 10-yard line, setting up Estime’s 2-yard touchdown run with 58 seconds remaining to put New Orleans ahead 16-13.
Cleveland answered immediately as Sanders orchestrated a quick drive into field goal range. Browns kicker Andre Szmyt drilled a 51-yard field goal as regulation expired to tie the game at 16-16 and send it into overtime.
In overtime, Shough led the Saints downfield and found Johnson for a touchdown to take a 23-16 lead. Sanders responded once more, connecting with tight end Harold Fannin Jr. for a 39-yard touchdown pass to make it 23-22.
Rather than kicking the extra point to force a possible tie, Cleveland aggressively went for two. However, a crucial holding penalty pushed the Browns back, and Sanders’ forced pass attempt fell incomplete to preserve the Saints’ victory.
The frantic second half stood in stark contrast to the opening two quarters, which ended in a 3-3 deadlock. Despite outgaining Cleveland 176-80 in total yards during the first half, the Saints struggled to finish drives due to costly mistakes.
Saints kicker Charlie Smyth opened the scoring with a 30-yard field goal midway through the first quarter after missing a 52-yard attempt earlier in the game. Szmyt answered for Cleveland with a 41-yard field goal with 10:30 remaining in the second quarter.
New Orleans had multiple opportunities to take control early. Following Szmyt’s field goal, Shough hit receiver Barion Brown for a 52-yard completion to Cleveland’s 11-yard line. However, rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson fumbled at the Browns’ 2-yard line, turning the ball over and squandering a prime scoring chance.
The Saints’ defense provided key plays to keep Cleveland contained. Linebacker Kaden Elliss executed a goal-line stand late in the second quarter, stopping Browns running back Judkins for no gain on fourth-and-goal from the 1-yard line to preserve the tie entering halftime. Defensive end Cameron Jordan and edge rusher Carl Granderson also recorded key sacks on Sanders during the game.

full_text:

The New Orleans Saints (3-5) earned their first home win of the season, beating the Cleveland Browns (5-4) 23-22 in overtime at Caesars Superdome.
Saints win a wild one at home 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/eZ52EBujMt
After three field-goal-dominated quarters, the game erupted with 20 fourth-quarter points. Cleveland took a 13-9 lead on a 4-yard touchdown pass from Shedeur Sanders to Concepcion with 5:21 left. New Orleans answered 50 seconds later with a 2-yard touchdown run by Audric Estime —set up by a 33-yard pass from Tyler Shough to Chris Olave . Cleveland’s Andre Szmyt hit a 51-yard field goal as regulation expired to force overtime tied at 16-16.
In overtime, Shough threw a 15-yard touchdown pass to Juwan Johnson with 4:17 remaining. Cleveland responded with a 39-yard touchdown pass from Sanders to Harold Fannin Jr. , but after a holding penalty on their two-point conversion attempt, Sanders’ pass fell incomplete to secure the Saints’ victory.
Shough finished with 265 passing yards, a touchdown, and 51 rushing yards. Sanders threw for 297 yards and two touchdowns. Estime, re-signed days before kickoff after being cut in training camp, added 72 rushing yards and a touchdown on 15 carries.

title: Giants 2027 NFL Draft Watch: Four College Prospects to Track This Weekend
full_text:
As the New York Giants (5-3-1) absorb their 24-21 Week 10 loss to the Washington Commanders on Thursday Night Football at MetLife Stadium, several Big Blue scouts will be watching closely. College football’s Week 11 slate is about to unfold.
While several potential targets make their case for being selected in the 2027 NFL Draft, the team’s biggest needs are becoming clearer.
In addition to their most pressing need at defensive tackle, coach John Harbaugh and his staff may also want to add players who can bolster their depth charts on offense and on special teams.
Here are four players the Giants may be keeping an eye on this weekend.
Gilliam is rapidly becoming one of the nation’s most fearsome defensive tackles, as evidenced by his rising draft stock.
The 6-foot-2, 305-pound lineman has amassed 26 total tackles, six sacks and two forced fumbles in nine games this season with the Volunteers.
His ability to hold his position against the run, combined with his elite first step when rushing the passer, should make him an immediate upgrade on any NFL defensive line he joins in 2027.
Because he projects best as a three-technique in a 4-3 scheme, Gilliam may not be the big, two-gap tackle the Giants are expected to pursue during the draft.
However, he could be an effective weapon in sub-packages within the Giants’ 3-4 defense, especially when the unit shifts into four-man nickel fronts on passing downs.
With Tennessee set for a marquee matchup against Texas A&M, Gilliam is expected to play a major role in disrupting the Aggies’ offense, led by quarterback Marcel Reed.
Should the Giants prioritize power when scouting potential interior offensive linemen, Knapp is likely to be among their top prospects. The Roswell, Ga., native has appeared in eight games this season at left guard for the Fighting Irish.
With experience in both zone and gap schemes, the Notre Dame product appears ready to make an impact in any pro-level offensive system.
With the Irish set to face Boston College’s aggressive defense, Knapp will be called upon to remain a reliable presence in both pass protection and run-blocking alignments.
With John Michael Schmitz likely heading to free agency after being replaced in the starting lineup by Bryan Hudson, the 6-foot-4, 305-pound Knapp could be an intriguing option for New York, with the versatility to play either guard or center.
While Brown may not be the three-down workhorse New York reportedly coveted at the trade deadline, his skill set could be an intriguing fit within their current stable of running backs.
At 5-foot-9 and 190 pounds, Brown is a bit on the lighter side to handle lead-back duties at the pro level. Still, he could be an impactful change-of-pace option or an effective pass-catcher out of the backfield.
If the Giants show interest in Brown, it may be to pair him with Cam Skattebo.
With Skattebo as their physical, between-the-tackles runner atop the depth chart, Louisville’s standout could add an explosive dynamic to New York’s backfield.
If he’s effective against North Carolina’s defense under coach Bill Belichick, Brown may force the Giants to take a good look at him come draft time.
Given rookie Dominic Zvada’s continued struggles, the Giants have been the subject of rumors at kicker. Fortunately for Big Blue, several college kickers could draw interest, including Woodring.
In nine games for the top-ranked Bulldogs this season, Woodring has made 9 of 13 field goals, with his longest coming from 49 yards. He has also made a perfect 47 of 47 extra-point attempts. In 2025, Woodring connected on 17 of 19 field goals (89.5%), with a long of 53.
Despite his struggles this season, including a 49-yard miss against Ole Miss in Week 10, Woodring has the power and consistency to be a reliable kicker in his rookie season. While the Giants have expressed their support for Zvada, they are likely keeping their options open.
If Woodring can score points on Saturday against Missouri, it may help improve his draft stock with positionally needy teams like the Giants.

title: Why Cam Skattebo Stayed Put on Giants’ Key Third-and-1 Against Commanders
full_text:
To the casual observer, New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo looked like he had fallen asleep at the snap, staying in his stance for nearly two seconds on a third-and-1 rushing play by quarterback Jameis Winston that did not pick up the first down.
But the play, which many assumed was a tush push given how often the Giants have run it this year, wasn’t what it looked like, and Skattebo did what he was supposed to do.
“That wasn’t a tush push. That was a different kind of play,” head coach John Harbaugh explained.
“It was a normal quarterback sneak and a certain check involved in it that is part of the play, but it wasn’t a tush push. So (Skattebo) wasn’t supposed to be up there pushing.”
Weirdest play of a weird night. If you’re going to run the Tush Push, you have to … you know … push. 🤷🏻‍♂️ pic.twitter.com/Sf65ZJ1vrF
The play occurred with the Giants leading 21-17. After a third-down try that initially appeared to give Winston the first down before officials reversed the call, the Giants tried to draw the Commanders offside on fourth-and-1. Still, it didn’t work, and a delay of game penalty led to a punt.
Given the Giants' success with the tush push, it was surprising they didn’t bring extra bodies to help Winston get the first down.
The Giants have converted first downs on 43.5% of their quarterback rushing attempts, which is the fifth-best mark in the NFL.
While that stat doesn’t differentiate between tush pushes, sneaks, designed runs, and scrambles, it shows the Giants have succeeded when deploying their quarterbacks to do so.
Only Harbaugh and offensive coordinator Matt Nagy know the logic behind running a sneak over a tush push. Still, it raised eyebrows, given Skattebo’s late arrival to the play and the fact that fullback Patrick Ricard was also not involved in Winston’s attempt to move the chains.
“We have four or five of those different types of calls and motions and pushes, not pushes, check-with-me plays. There are different things we have. One of those was called,” Harbaugh explained.
“We have different calls that go with quarterback sneaks, so we didn’t call the same one that we’ve been calling. That’s really the only answer I have for you. We didn’t call the same play. He wasn’t supposed to be up there pushing.”
But with that call not resulting in a first-down conversion, questions will linger over whether it was the right call to make at that juncture.

title: Giants Mailbag: Malik Nabers, Kayvon Thibodeaux, and More
full_text:
Welcome to the weekly New York Giants On SI mailbag! From offseason moves to game-day strategies, we'll do our best to answer your questions. (Some questions have been edited for brevity and clarity.)
If Nabers fancies himself as one of the best in the league, he needs to play like it.  No more dropping touchdowns.  No more fumbling the ball.  No more temper tantrums.  Time for him to ascend.  Will anyone have an honest conversation with him?
Mike, I asked Nabers about that in a round about way. Here was his response: "I had a talk with (Quarterbacks) Coach (Brian) Callahan, and we had a good talk and he said some things in our conversation. He was just like, ‘Just play the one play that we call, don't try to do too much.’ Don't try to do a lot on the play, we just need you to be you. So just be you at the end of the day.
"And like I said, just not pressing. I'm getting a lot of different coverages on my side. I'm getting a lot of cloud, getting a lot of double teams. So, every opportunity I have to get the football I think I'm just trying to do too much with the football instead of just let the game come to me and just play the game. So, I think just like Coach Calli said, just playing that one play, just locking on that one play and then focus on the next play when it comes."
Now that the Giants did not trade Thibedeux what are the chances that he is resigned. Hopefully it will not be another Saqoun situation.
Moose, my gut says they don't re-sign Thibodeaux. He's going to want a top-dollar deal, and I think someone will give it to him.
I could see a world where Arvell Reese gets more snaps on the outside, and you also have to remember that Thibs has been playing in his natural spot ever since Brian Burns's season-ending injury. So I think Thibs moves on in free agency.
Why do you suppose o-line got away from pulling guards, and running trap plays like week one against Dallas. Seems like more straight up blocking to me now. Did Dart's injury force a change to the blocking scheme?
The injury to Dart may have had something to do with it — remember, they have only now run what, three games with J.J. McCarthy under center, a guy who can run the RPO game unlike Winston?  But I think the bigger issue was the injuries at running back.
First, you have Tyrone Tracy Jr. on IR, and of course you had Skattebo miss a game due to injury (as well as one due to a quasi-benching). As a result, the Giants leaned a little bit more on inside zone runs.
Second, I think they've leaned more on a pistol formation in their running game, with the fullback serving more as a trap blocker while the o-line has focused on DUO blocking.  The Giants only ran the pistol on 1.1% of their plays in Week 1.
Since then that perentage has jumped up to 3%, which might not seem like a huge jump but actually is considering how many rushing attempts they average per game.
What are the future ramifications to the Eagles salary cap since they are the biggest users of voidable years. How will it impact their rebuild.
Jim, I cover the Giants, not the Eagles so I can't sit here and tell you how their cap is going to be impacted down to the penny.
What I can tell you is that they have a lot of draft picks next year which means they'll have a lot of players on rookie deals -- two first rounders, one second, and a projected third round comp pick are their premium picks.
The cap is also going to rise so whatever dead money they accrue as a result of voidable years won't be as harsh in terms of the bite it takes out of their cap as it might be if it the hit were taken this year.
John Harbaugh says that Zavada has a problem on the right hash. Are you able to go back to see how many of his misses were from the right hash?
Kris, I was the one who mentioned Zvada's misses this year coming from the right hash, something Harbaugh didn't disagree with.
I brought up the question because I noticed they all came from the right hash. So to your question—I already did the groundwork on it, not that I was the only one to do so, I'm sure.
