title: Seahawks Mailbag: 4 Questions Leading Into The Raiders Game
full_text:
I won’t pretend that all is well after a convincing, but unmemorable, win over the Arizona Cardinals. But all winning streaks have to start somewhere. I asked my discord server what their biggest questions about the team are right now. Let’s take a look at what’s on the mind of the fans. The wording of the questions has been lightly edited for this article.
“Does Brian Fleury open up the playbook for Lock this week?”
I doubt it. Given the state of the opponent, as well as the injuries the Seattle Seahawks are bringing into the game, this seems like the recipe for a simple, basic, boilerplate gameplan. Run the ball, quick easy reads, avoid negative plays, punt the ball a bunch, and wait for a one-dimension Las Vegas Raiders offense with a rookie QB to give the game away.
Even if this were a tougher game, Lock’s arm still isn’t 100% , which probably disqualifies him from making a bunch of downfield throws. What’s really disappointing about this is that it makes it almost impossible for Lock to have a big game that could realistically give the coaches something to think about when naming a starter after the bye week.
“What’s the most likely long term answer for the quarterback position, particularly with our cap being pretty limited?”
There’s still a non-zero chance it’s Darnold, although I think it’s going to require a massive turnaround after the bye week that’s nearly impossible to imagine . There are some interesting bridge QB options, but none of them are long term answers. Of course, you can make a big swing trade for Justin Herbert or CJ Stroud if they come available.
But far more likely than any of this is someone in the draft, combined with a bridge. There are so many appealing prospects in this draft, someone will be there at Seattle’s first round pick, and there may even be someone still standing by their second round pick. It’s the right draft to need a young quarterback. I’ll say we get Jayden Maiava, with Lock as a bridge.
“What is Sam Darnold’s true trade value?”
Sam Darnold is a super bowl champion, 29 years old, and played at an MVP-level from 2024 through the first half of 2025. He’s a former #3 overall pick. A few years ago, I remember Bill Belichick describing him as someone that NFL coaches and executives were enamored with and couldn’t give up on despite the bad start to his career. He has value.
A bit more than ten years ago, the Philadelphia Eagles traded Sam Bradford to the Minnesota VIkings for a first round pick. At that point in time, Bradford was the same age Darnold is now, had a career record of 25-37-1, a career QB rating of 81, no playoff appearances, and had missed an entire season to injury. I think we can pull a first for our Sam too .
If you want to argue that NFL teams have gotten smarter since 2016, think about all the teams this offseason that will feel like they’re a quarterback away from contention. Minnesota, Pittsburgh, Atlanta (if Penix gets hurt again), even the New York Jets might go for it. As long as Darnold plays solid football post-bye, I think a second plus is the minimum.
“What do we make of the Bears' success against us and immediate follow up with a stinker against the Buccaneers?”
Let’s get a little perspective first. The Chicago Bears gained 363 yards and averaged 5.2 yards per play. Seven of their points came on a drive that started at Seattle’s 6 yard line. It was the worst game this defense has played this season , but by no means was it an especially bad game. Particularly given how the offense had so many quick punt drives.
To speak more broadly, I think the NFL is more of a week-to-week league than ever before. Sometimes, teams that are good and have every reason to be good just don’t bring it on gameday. When I was younger, it felt like the better franchises took bringing their A-game every week much more seriously. Blame the heavily-reduced practice times in the new CBA.

title: What to Expect From Seahawks' RB Split vs. Raiders
full_text:
Both Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price made their long-awaited return in Week 8 for the Seattle Seahawks, helping energize an offense that has been one-dimensional at times throughout the season.
Charbonnet returned from a nine-month recovery after tearing his ACL in the 2025 postseason. Price, the Seahawks’ first-round pick in this year’s draft, was working through a chest injury that landed him on injured reserve.
The split between the two running backs shifted in Week 9, as Charbonnet, who would’ve been the de facto No. 1 running back if not for his injury, continues to work back into game speed. But both players should be expected to see a healthy workload the rest of the season.
What should fans expect from the duo in Week 10 against the Las Vegas Raiders ? The usage of each player from the last two weeks provides plenty of intel.
In Charbonnet’s first game back in Week 8, Price earned more snaps and got the ball more frequently. That wasn’t surprising, as Price’s injury was far less significant and he had already played this season. Charbonnet was just getting warmed up.
However, that flipped in Week 9 , as Charbonnet played quite a bit more. Charbonnet is far better in pass protection, so it’s no surprise that he will both get more snaps and see a lower usage rate as a result.
Expect Charbonnet to continue seeing more snaps and more rushing attempts. Price showed a lot as a receiver against the Arizona Cardinals, so he should keep seeing more targets in the passing game. That creates a solid one-two punch that mirrors the Charbonnet and Kenneth Walker III duo of the past.
As long as their production remains similar, it’s unlikely one gains a massive advantage in snaps. But Charbonnet should be the focal point as he ramps back up to full health.

title: Seahawks Injury Report Reveals Situation With Nwosu, Cross, and More
full_text:
Time for the third and final injury report of the week, and for those of you who don’t like ambiguity, I have good news . The Seattle Seahawks do not have a single player with a game status of Questionable or Doubtful. So we know exactly what the team has for this one. Let’s take a look, running through the significant amount of good news first.
A.J. Barner (finger) and Jaxon Smith-Njigba weren’t listed on the report today at all, so we’re good there. Anthony Bradford (knee), Uchenna Nwosu (ankle) , Connor O’Toole (foot), and Pat O’Connell (toe) made the climb from limited to full, and are in. Brandon Pili (back) and Jarran Reed (personal) went from DNP to full and similarly have no game status.
Drew Lock (right elbow, oblique) was limited, as he manages his injury, but will play. Rashid Shaheed (knee) held out at full all week and is good to go . Interestingly enough, Derick Hall (back) missed practice entirely, but still has no game status. Probably just rest, but it could also be something that limits him on Sunday without taking him off the field entirely.
The four players who are out are big ones, although their lack of availability this week is no surprise. Charles Cross (ankle) posted a DNP and is out . Being out is not surprising, missing practice after a limited one yesterday is a bit more notable. Could be rest, could be part of the process, could be a setback, but Mike thinks Cross will be back in week 12.
He was similarly positive about the return of Sam Darnold (ribs, quadricep) after the bye, although he’s of course out this week. Quenton Nelson (knee) is recovering from his procedure and is out too. Leonard Williams (stinger) was the one longshot we had some hope for, but he is out, and per Macdonald his return is a little fuzzier than the others.
The Las Vegas Raiders have enjoyed a lot of good health this year, although they remain a very limited team in what they can do. Folorunso Fatukasi (shoulder, back), Trey Zuhn (concussion), and Ian Thomas (ankle) all got full practices in and have no status. Thomas Booker (ankle) also had full participation, but is questionable. I expect him to play.
One wrinkle is the new inclusion of Dont’e Thornton (back), who has apparently gotten hurt in practice and is now questionable after missing Friday entirely. Not a major player in that Raiders offense, but still a piece of it. His odds I’m less rosy on, but I imagine we’re seeing a fairly simplified offense this weekend with Mendoza playing quarterback anyway.

title: Why the Seahawks Won the Trade Deadline in the NFC West
full_text:
Should the Seattle Seahawks have made a trade before Tuesday’s deadline ? Maybe. Maybe not. Everyone has their own take. For my money, standing pat was totally understandable and probably correct. In fact, I believe that by standing pat, the Seahawks fared better than any of the other teams within the NFC West. Let’s run through it.
If the Cardinals believe themselves to still be in play for a playoff spot this season (which is absurd, of course), then they did nothing at the deadline to bolster their thin roster. Of course, I seriously doubt that’s the case, and I would never suggest the Cardinals were wrong to not acquire any players. The real issue is their failure to trade veterans for assets.
Supposedly, the Buffalo Bills put a second round pick on the table for Budda Baker, a 30 year old safety who is entering his contract year in 2027. Passing up that deal feels like malpractice given Arizona’s situation. They also retained Josh Sweat, who requested a trade months ago. Failing to get picks for these veterans makes the Cardinals a deadline loser.
The Rams also sat the deadline out, which strikes me as a pretty big mistake. I would have understood it if they had tapped out more aggressively, trading away some pieces that aren’t part of their long term so they can replenish their meager draft picks. Or they could have taken another step into the all-in waters and traded for some help. They did neither.
This leaves the Rams incredibly destitute at wide receiver and defensive tackle, and also weak at cornerback. They’ll cross their fingers for players like Puka Nacua, Davante Adams, and Kobie Turner to come back and play well. Keep in mind that, even when moderately healthy, this Rams team has been fairly lackluster this year. It might be Brandon Aiyuk or bust .
Knock on wood, but by doing nothing, it feels like the Rams are likely going to be out of the playoff race with the next month or so. Their schedule is brutal, and many of their top players will be missing important games. That helps clear the way for the Seahawks. And if they really are giving up on their superteam, with low draft capital next year, it's a dream for Seahawks fans.
Like the Seahawks , the 49ers made their major acquisition a couple weeks ago. DeForest Buckner for a 4th round pick is a good move, although with all the injuries San Francisco has eaten at defensive tackle it’s more of a ‘keep your head above water’ trade. They did have one more acquisition before the curtain fell, Keenan Allen for a 6th round pick.
In a vacuum, the trade is fine, and Allen has been modestly productive this season for the Colts. But given that the 49ers have a pretty serious need for wide receivers, and many fans had their sights set on Garrett Wilson, getting someone like Allen almost feels like a punchline. It’s a bargain bin move that probably won’t move the needle.
Clearly, the 49ers are hoping what they have is good enough, and they’re trying to avoid giving up massive assets. Understandable, but if Mike Evans can’t bounce back from his achilles injury and De’Zhaun Stribling doesn’t hit the ground running when he returns, it’s hard to imagine such a lackluster receiver core winning anything. No gamble, no future.

title: 3 Matchups That Will Decide Seahawks’ Week 10 Clash vs. Raiders
full_text:
The defending Super Bowl champions have dug themselves a little bit of a hole when it comes to the NFC West. The San Francisco 49ers own a 7-1 record and a win over the 5-4 Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field. Mike Macdonald’s club comes off a workmanlike 17-3 win over the Arizona Cardinals. Now they take on an improved Las Vegas Raiders’ club that has already won one more game than it did the previous season.
Here’s a look at some key encounters in regards to Sunday’s contest at Allegiant Stadium. By all indications, Drew Lock will make his second straight start for Macdonald’s team.
Talk about familiarity? It was this duo that obviously spent the 2025 season together in the Pacific Northwest under head coach Mike Macdonald. So it will be interesting to see what the newest head coach of the Silver and Black has in store for his former colleague.
Of course, the first overall pick in April’s draft is making his first NFL start against the league’s top-ranked defense. Unfortunately for Fernando Mendoza, the Raiders’ running attack is next-to-last in the league at 71.2 yards per game. The clubs has been held to fewer than 100 yards on the ground in six straight games and totaled less than 20 running plays in three of their last five contests. Can Kubiak find a way to generate a ground attack and keep Mendoza out of harm’s way?
It’s interesting to note than after nine games last season, Seattle’s ground attack was averaging a so-so 114.3 yards per game. Kenneth Walker III (539) and Zach Charbonnet (313) combined for 852 of the team’s 1,029 yards on the ground, and nine of the team’s 11 rushing touchdowns—six by Charbonnet.
This season, there’s no Walker and there’s barely been Charbonnet. But the Seahawks have still managed to churn out 110.8 yards per game rushing. However, consistency and continuity has been lacking as four different players have run for at least 100 yards and totaled at least 20 carries. Last week, Charbonnet finished with a team-high 16 carries and 77 yards in the 17-3 win over the Cardinals.
The Raiders have the league’s worst defense in terms of total yards (385.4) and rushing yards (151.2) allowed per game. And it’s worth noting that 2026 free-agent pickup Nakobe Dean easily leads the team with 99 tackles. The five-year pro could be very busy on Sunday.
Brock Bowers with the big catch and run 🏃 LVvsSF on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/xTQFPX5h3K
Seattle’s Julian Love has certainly made his share of appearances in this weekly feature. Of course, that’s what happens when your schedule includes the likes of Trey McBride, George Kittle, Travis Kelce, and now the Raiders’ top pass-catcher.
Brock Browers leads Las Vegas with 48 receptions, 658 yards, and a team-best six touchdowns. Entering Week 10, the Silver and Black were ranked fifth in the league in passing yards per contest. And he’s currently the top-graded player at his position (90.4) by Pro Football Focus —a full eight points ahead of Kittle (82.4).
Of course, Love is no slouch. He’s PFF’s No. 13 safety and when it comes to pass coverage, only six players at his position have a higher grade. He’s also tied for team lead with a pair of interceptions and leads Seattle with six passes defensed.

title: 5 Key Things to Know About Seahawks vs. Raiders in Week 10
full_text:
The reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks face an uphill battle if they are to win the NFC West for the second straight year. Mike Macdonald’s 5-4 team, which comes off a 17-3 home win over the Arizona Cardinals, trails the 7-1 San Francisco 49ers, and has already lost a home game to Kyle Shanahan’s club.
This week, the ‘Hawks have not been definitive on who their starting quarterback will be on Sunday. Sam Darnold is out and Drew Lock is having his own issues (oblique). Could second-year pro Jalen Milroe make his first NFL start?
On the other hand, Seattle’s opponent this certainly know who their field general will be. On Tuesday, the Las Vegas Raiders sent veteran Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings for a third-round pick in 2027. That opens the door for 2025 Heisman Trophy winner and national champion Fernando Mendoza, who has seen only reserve action in one game this season.
Klint Kubiak, the Seahawks’ offensive coordinator this past season, has led the Silver and Black to a 4-5 record, one more win than the club had in 2025. An upset of the Seahawks would speak volumes for a Raiders’ team that has made some strides—especially on offense.
JOSH JACOBS WALKS OFF THE SEAHAWKS pic.twitter.com/zIjh6Cqblc
These former AFC West rivals have met just six times since realignment in 2002, and the franchises have split those half-dozen encounters. The last meeting between the clubs took place in 2022 at Lumen Field, with the Raiders coming away with a rousing 40-34 overtime victory.
The last time the Silver and Black was the host team in this series was in 2018, when they fell to Pete Carroll’s Seahawks in London, 27-3. Hence, this is the ‘Hawks first regular-season contest in Las Vegas (they lost a preseason game at Allegiant Stadium in 2021).
In their five wins, Mike Maconald’s club has a combined 169 running plays for 670 yards—totaling at least 30 attempts in four of those contests. In their four setbacks, there’s been a total of 89 attempts for only 327 yards. Entering Week 10, the Raiders are surrendering an NFL-worst 151.2 rushing yards per contest.
In each of their last six games, the Raiders have allowed 30-plus points. That ties the NFL single-season mark set four previous times. No NFL team has even allowed 30 or more points in seven straight games in the same season. The overall record is eight games, set by the 2020 Lions (last 6 in 2020, first 2 in 2021).
Byron Murphy II gets home for the SACK 💪 @LACvsSEA on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/JNAsNnxZCj
Seattle’s defense entered Week 10 as the league’s top-ranked unit in terms of fewest total yards and fewest passing yards allowed per game. Third-year pro Byron Murphy II has a 75.5 pass-rushing grade from Pro Football Focus —tied for 13th among interior defenders. He also leads Seattle with four sacks.
Raiders’ wideout Tre Tucker is in the midst of his fourth NFL season, and could wind up having another career campaign. He’s fourth on the club with 33 catches, but ranks second in receiving yards (529) and touchdown grabs (4). Tucker was a 17-game starter in 2025, totaling 57 grabs for 696 yards and five TDs.

title: Trades the Seahawks Shoud've Made at the Trade Deadline but Didn't
full_text:
The 2026 NFL Trade Deadline has come and gone. From an overall perspective, the final hours of the Trade Deadline could be considered a disappointment, as there were trades that were broken or rejected. The Seattle Seahawks made a big trade move, but it was made a few weeks before the trade deadline. The Seahawks traded for eight-time Pro-Bowl guard Quenton Nelson, who was the big addition for the Seahawks.
Seattle had a chance to improve their roster more by making a move in the final hours of the trade deadline. Instead, the front office decided to hold back on trading any more picks to improve some of the most-needed position groups on the team. While the Seahawks didn’t make a move in the final hours of the Trade Deadline, there is a conversation that they should have.
There were reports that the Seahawks sought to trade for a number two wide receiver after Jaxon Smith-Njigba. He leads the league in receiving yards with 1,036 yards and touchdowns with nine because he is the best receiver in the league, but also because the Seahawks don’t have a consistent pass-catching target. Cooper Kupp is past his prime and Rashid Shaheed isn’t utilized efficiently and is injured.
​The Seahawks should have traded for a dynamic, talented receiver who can get open on diverse routes. A prime target for Seattle to trade for would’ve been Cleveland Browns’ Jerry Jeudy, who has lost opportunity as the Browns want younger options. Jeudy, however, was still young at 27 years old and was capable of being a solid second for either quarterback Sam Darnold or Drew Lock.
​The Seahawks’ Dark Side Defense is one of the top defenses in the league in most of the major categories. Seattle possesses the top-ranked total defense and passing defense this season due to the elite play of their secondary. Their pass rush, however, remains more to be desired. The Seahawks rank 13th in the league in sacks accounted for (21), largely thanks to their interior defensive linemen and some of their blitzing schemes.
Only Derick Hall has accounted for more than one sack this season coming from an edge rusher or a true defensive end. The Seahawks not only could’ve used reinforcement at the edge and, potentially, a starter. Uchenna Nwosu is hurt and Hall is limited. Meanwhile, DeMarcus Lawrence will retire at the end of the season and Dante Fowler Jr. has been non-existent.
​If the Seahawks traded for an eager and established veteran like New Orleans’ Chase Young or Los Angeles Chargers’ Tuli Tuipulotu, the need for an edge rusher with a first or second-round pick for the 2027 NFL Draft would’ve been pushed back two years. The Seahawks would have traded for a win-now pass rusher to go along with their win-now defense.

title: NFL Trade Deadline Grade: Seahawks Deserve Praise for Quenton Nelson Deal
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are on the other side of the NFL trade deadline , but they certainly weren't the most aggressive team on the market.
The Seahawks made a swing ahead of the deadline , though, acquiring Quenton Nelson from the Indianapolis Colts in exchange for a third-round and fifth-round pick. Nelson made his Seahawks debut in Week 8 against the Chicago Bears, but a knee injury is holding him out for at least two games. The team is hopeful he can make a return without needing to go to injured reserve.
As the team's primary move, I felt that this made the Seahawks' trade deadline a massive success, especially given the price on the move.
The Seahawks could have been more aggressive by possibly trading for a running back, wide receiver, or tight end. They also could have gotten some depth at the linebacker position after some injuries on that side of the ball. Ultimately, the Seahawks felt confident in the group they have, but still made the decision to upgrade at left guard.
The Seahawks' offensive line has been a matter of controversy for the past several years. It often was the team's weak spot on the entire roster and held them back from achieving more. Last season, the team selected Grey Zabel in the first round to be their left guard of the future. This move is now shifting him to the right side to allow Nelson, an eight-time Pro Bowler, to take his natural spot at left guard.
The move is risky because it forces the Seahawks to make some changes in the middle of the year, but the price for Nelson, who is one of the best interior offensive linemen in the league, was an absolute steal.
The Seahawks have an excess of draft picks as a result of several compensatory selections, on top of the team getting an additional third-round pick for Nolan Teasley heading to the Minnesota Vikings to be their general manager.
With Teasley gone and multiple additional picks coming in, the Seahawks could afford to part ways with a fifth-rounder to acquire one of the best offensive linemen in the league. Nelson is a free agent at the end of the season, but the Seahawks could go in multiple directions with him and his future.
Ultimately, the Seahawks fleeced the Colts on this trade, as he likely would have gone for a higher price in other places. If they had waited a little longer until the deadline, the Seahawks swooped in, got their guy, and improved their team going into the second half of the season, making them a legitimate threat to go to the Super Bowl once again.

title: 3 Bold Predictions for Seahawks vs. Raiders in Week 10
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are hoping to start a win streak as they take on the Las Vegas Raiders in their Week 10 matchup at Allegiant Stadium in Sin City.
The Seahawks are fighting for positioning in the NFC playoff picture , and a win against the Raiders would go a long way toward being on the right side of the postseason. Here's a look at three bold predictions for the matchup.
The Raiders lead the NFL in an unfortunate category: they give up 151.2 rushing yards per game. As a team, they also allow the worst-scoring defense in the league, giving up 29.8 points per game.
The Seahawks have a dynamic duo in the backfield with Jaderian Price and Zach Charbonnet, both of whom have played two games since returning from their respective injuries. In their first game, they didn't get off to much of a rhythm against the Chicago Bears because Seattle was trailing for most of the contest. The team started to see a bit of momentum against the Arizona Cardinals when they ran for 120 yards.
Seattle has been trying to build an identity around rushing the football all season long, but they haven't had the personnel to do it. Now that they have both of their top running backs healthy and are facing off against a team that really struggles against the run, the game plan will be angled toward beating them at the line of scrimmage.
Perhaps the Seahawks can break off a long run or two, which could help them increase their total. 200 yards isn't totally out of the question for a Seahawks offense that has really struggled on the ground this season.
The Seahawks smell blood in the water as they face off against No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza in his first career NFL start. In the last two wins, the Seahawks have held their opponents to just a single field goal, one of those being Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs.
The Seahawks' defense has been very impressive as of late, but that doesn't mean they will be perfect against Mendoza and the Raiders. Las Vegas head coach Clint Kubiak was Seattle's offensive coordinator last season, and he should have a special game plan set up for his team, especially on the offensive side of the ball.
I think Kubiak's expertise will help the Raiders score some points, but not enough to beat Seattle in the end. I think Mendoza scores a touchdown, but it may come towards the end of the game when things are a bit out of reach.
I don't think Drew Lock is going to do anything extraordinary or outstanding in this game, but he will do a good job taking care of the football . Lock is the epitome of a backup quarterback: he isn't going to take over the game on his own, but he will do enough to get the team a victory. With a defense like Seattle's, that's all Lock really needs to do.
If he improves to 3-0 as a starter, it could raise the question of whether the team should stick with him after the bye week instead of Sam Darnold, who has struggled to avoid turnovers this season.
Ultimately, the Seahawks will likely go back to Darnold once he is healthy, potentially as early as Week 12 against the Niners, but Lock's performance will be enough to spark conversations during the bye week about a potential switch.

title: What Recent Moves Mean for 49ers Wide Receiver Jordan Watkins
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers have an interesting decision to make at wide receiver moving forward. They just acquired Keenan Allen; they are expected to get Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel back soon, Demarcus Robinson just returned, and Jordan Watkins is starting to ascend.
General Manager John Lynch made one thing clear: the team is not going to take Watkins off the field while he is so hot.
"I don't see him coming off," Lynch said on the John Lynch Show . "You play like he has been playing, and I think now we're starting to see it out front where everyone can see it, but the nitty-gritty, the tough stuff ... he's been doing the little stuff, and that will get you on the field around here.
Still, it raises an interesting question of how the room will shake out if Watkins continues to see the field.
Watkins is averaging an impressive 1.98 yards per route run. More important for the 49ers, his average depth of target is 17.5 yards downfield. Mike Evans is the only receiver close, and his is 14.9 yards downfield.
Deebo Samuel and Christian McCaffrey are under three. George Kittle and Keenan Allen are both around nine. So, when Evans is not on the field, Watkins is the only player in the group who can stretch the defense.
Evans has had multiple injuries throughout the season. More than that, the team is 7-1, and Evans has missed the past couple of weeks. They do not need him right now, and their best bet is to rest him. Without Evans on the field, they need to play Watkins to keep a vertical element to their offense.
Watkins would be the vertical outside threat, while Allen would work the slot and Deebo Samuel could threaten underneath. This is their most likely pairing in Week 10.
Brandin Cooks, Demarcus Robinson, and Jacob Cowing would likely have minor roles. Cooks and Cowing have not done more to earn snaps, and while Robinson is just coming back from an injury, he is not guaranteed playing time.
The big question will be what the team does with Watkins when Evans returns. They would either have to push one of Samuel or Allen to a reduced role. Perhaps the rise of Watkins is a signal that Evans will not return soon.

title: 49ers Have 6 Players Poised for Second-Half Breakouts
full_text:
Now that the San Francisco 49ers are at the halfway point of the 2026 season, who are some players poised to look better in the second half than they did in the first half?
Mustapha should have a better second half considering he played 48 snaps in the first four weeks as a reserve. An injury pushed him back into the lineup, and he does not appear to be giving it up. The 49ers rotated three safeties in Week 9, and he led the trio in snaps. This could lead to a strong finish.
The 49ers have put a lot on the rookie fifth-round pick’s plate. He has played a surprising 254 snaps. Dugger was expected to be a projectable player with more ceiling than immediate impact. So, the ceiling from here could get better.
Odighizuwa had to carry an injured defensive line all season. Now, the team added DeForest Buckner, and they are getting C.J. West back healthy soon. They just got James Thompson back healthy as well so things are about to get a lot easier for the offseason trade acquisition.
Williams is a second-year player coming back from an ACL injury. It is going to take him time to get into the swing of things. Still, he already matched his sack total from his rookie season. With Nick Bosa back and the interior stronger, Williams should get better.
Height was asked to take on a lot. At his best, he is a Bryce Huff type of player who does not take many run defense snaps. However, He has 150 pass rush snaps compared to 78 run defense snaps. Last year, Huff had 400 pass rush snaps and 172 run defense snaps. Now that Bosa and Williams are back to defend the run, the team should lean into asking Height to rush the passer. His numbers could improve without the burden of run defense.
Watkins has been on fire in the past three weeks and has taken a step forward in year two. The 49ers are starting to get crowded at wide receiver, but between Mike Evans, Keenan Allen, and Deebo Samuel, it appears someone will be missing time. This will leave snaps open for the former fourth-round pick. He could continue to flash to end the year.

title: 5 49ers With Jobs on the Line Against Cowboys
full_text:
As the San Francisco 49ers take on the Dallas Cowboys in Week 10 there will be a lot on the line for a few players whose roles could be changing soon. Who is going to have to be at their best?
When Watkins plays, he has produced for the 49ers. He has eight receptions for 164 yards in the past three weeks. However, the 49ers receiver room just got more crowded, which will bring questions as to how much Watkins will play.
If he keeps producing, he will have to play. If not, the 49ers will push him below Deebo Samuel, Keenan Allen, and eventually Mike Evans.
The 49ers started Marques Sigle next to Brown in Week 1 because Malik Mustapha was banged up in training camp. However, Sigle played so well that when Mustapha was healthy, they stuck with Sigle. When Sigle went down, Mustapha stepped in and played well. So, they cannot bench him.
If Mustapha and Sigle are both playing well and can’t be benched, it might be Brown who is phased out of the rotation next . He needs to keep playing well.
Thompson has flashed every time he is on the field. He just returned from a high ankle sprain and looked good. Still, he is a rookie UDFA, and the team is about to get CJ West back. They obviously will play DeForest Buckner and Osa Odighizuwa over him. The 49ers will lean on Thompson as their third lineman and run-defense option in Week 10. Will he continue to play legitimate snaps in Week 11 if West is back?
The receiver room might be pushing Watkins down, and it might push Cowing out. They are getting healthier and deeper in the room. If Evans and Samuel return soon, he will be the sixth receiver at best. His only role is in the return game, and if Samuel is rotating in on offense, he could take on a bigger role there. Cowing might be losing his job.
Prysock played two snaps in Week 7 and then seven snaps in Week 9. The team is easing him in as a dime option. Renardo Green and Deommodore Lenoir are banged up and Nate Hobbs is about to return. The 49ers rookie might not have a better chance to make a statement than this week.

title: 49ers List 7 Players Questionable for Week 10 vs. Cowboys
full_text:
For the first time since Week 1, the San Francisco 49ers have a pretty positive injury report heading into game day.
They've listed seven players as questionable for their Week 10 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys . Mike Evans is the only player ruled out with Achilles tendinitis.
That was the expected bad news, and it will remain that way for several more weeks. The good news is that the 49ers are getting Deebo Samuel back.
He doesn't carry an injury designation, which is tremendous. He's feeling no lingering issues from his hamstring injury that he suffered in Week 5 against the Seattle Seahawks.
His return will be an added boost to the 49ers' offense, specifically the passing game. Brock Purdy can now spread the ball around efficiently.
Usually, a player who is questionable isn't much of a concern. However, both of the 49ers' starting cornerbacks , Deommodore Lenoir (foot) and Renardo Green (back), are compromised.
Both players missed practice on Wednesday and Thursday. It wasn't until today that they got in a limited session, so they're clearly playing through pain.
They probably don't fall under the usual questionable status. I don't think they're guaranteed to play, but if they do, they will be toughing it out.
If either Lenoir or Green is inactive against the Cowboys, it will be tough on the 49ers' defense. They need Lenoir and Green out there against CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens .
Even though they're compromised, it's better than rolling out Jack Jones. Rookie Ephesians Prysock might be okay, but he hasn't played much.
The 49ers' pass rush will need to take over in this game to help out the secondary. Otherwise, they'll struggle to get stops and limit the damage.
In typical 49ers fashion, Trent Williams and Dre Greenlaw got dinged up in practice on Thursday. Williams hurt his shoulder and didn't participate in Friday's practice.
Kyle Shanahan is hoping it's enough time for Williams to feel sufficient. If he can't go, the 49ers will turn to Vederian Lowe.
Greenlaw hurt his knee, but unlike Williams, he didn't sit out of Friday's practice. He was good enough to participate in a limited capacity, which is encouraging.
As for the other three questionable 49ers: Nate Hobbs (abductor), Upton Stout (shoulder, neck), and C.J. West (knee). Expect them to play in Week 10.

title: 49ers Could Claim 5 Major NFL Awards After Hot Start
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers are 7-1, so they are obviously going to be well represented when awards season comes. However, Bill Barnwell of ESPN went through his midseason awards, and there is a strong chance that five different awards will belong to the 49ers when the season ends.
Barnwell put Purdy second behind Joe Burrow. Still, he is going to be right in the mix until the season ends. Purdy has a new receiver he has to work with every week. However, he continues to produce and win. This will be his best chance at an MVP since 2023.
Shanahan has surprisingly never won Coach of the Year. Right now, Barnwell has him as the top coach, beating out Ben Johnson and Liam Coen. Shanahan is winning with new receivers. The team lost Nick Bosa. He handled a trip to Australia and has built them a huge lead in what is known as the toughest division in the game. This could be his year.
Barnwell has Warner second behind Will Anderson and just ahead of Aidan Hutchinson. Warner is one of the bigger impact players in the game and clearly the best player at his position. Most would argue Myles Garrett is better than Anderson and Hutchinson, although he will not win the award due to injury. The sack totals get the awards, but no one is impacting the game like Warner.
Williams was named the best lineman of the year so far by Barnwell. He put Williams over Amarius Mims and Zach Frazier. Williams is essentially the reason this even is an award. He needs more recognition for how dominant he is at his position. So, it is only right that he winds up winning the award at some point.
These two are behind Patrick Mahomes, according to Barnwell. The three-time Super Bowl champion will be hard to knock off. Still, they are second and third. Both have returned from season-ending injuries and are dominating in ways that could not have been predicted.
Warner is a bit more expected, and he is a bit more dominant. Kittle has overcome an injury later in the year and a bit tougher to come back from. His return has been remarkable.

title: 49ers Have 2 Major Threats to Overcome Against the Cowboys
full_text:
Similar to facing the Las Vegas Raiders , the San Francisco 49ers should have no issue moving the ball and scoring points on the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday.
That is not where they will face any threat. The real threat resides with Dallas’ offense. Let’s dive into the two major threats the 49ers have to overcome on the road in Week 10 against the Cowboys.
It should surprise no one that the first and foremost major threat for the 49ers against the Cowboys is the lethal wide receiver duo of CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. These two are a problem.
A problem the 49ers will hope to solve. Lamb has been on a tear this season, tallying 70 catches for 904 yards and seven touchdowns. All three stats trail only Jaxon Smith-Njigba.
Stats aside, Lamb is always an issue. So is Pickens, who hasn’t been as great as last season. That’s mostly been because he’s been forced to play second fiddle to Lamb. The ball can only be shared so much.
Still, Pickens can go off at any moment. He’s still put up solid numbers this year, reeling in 39 catches for 533 yards and two touchdowns. The 49ers must not fall asleep on him, assuming he plays.
He missed last week with a hamstring injury. Speaking of injuries, the 49ers might be without both Renardo Green and Deommodore Lenoir , as they’re both nursing injuries.
If one or both of them play, they could be compromised, making this matchup a lot tougher than it already is. The 49ers’ pass rush will need to take over to make it easy on them.
One of the more underrated players in the NFL is running back Javonte Williams. He had a breakout year in 2025 and a career resurgence. He’s definitely a high-level player who is a threat to every defense.
Williams has the ninth-most rushing yards (629) and is tied for the second-most rushing touchdowns (9). He will be a handful for the 49ers despite not being much of a receiving threat.
The bright side is that the 49ers are one of the best rushing defenses in the NFL. They’re allowing the second-lowest rushing yards per game at 80.9. They also have only allowed five rushes of 10 yards or more, which is No. 1.
Williams has only ripped off 12 rushes of 10-plus yards, so the 49ers should do well against him if they play up to their standard. Otherwise, if Williams gets going, they’ll be in trouble.

title: 49ers DC Raheem Morris Details Challenge of CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens
full_text:
It would be surprising to see the San Francisco 49ers face much of a challenge offensively against the Dallas Cowboys.
The Cowboys have one of the worst defenses in the NFL. I’m sure Kyle Shanahan is chomping at the bit to unleash his incredible offense against them. It won’t be a challenge for them.
The real challenge for the 49ers will be on defense. Dallas boasts one of the best wide receiver duos in the league: CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. On Thursday, Raheem Morris detailed the challenges of facing the lethal duo.
“CeeDee [Lamb], when you start with him you’re talking about a guy that’s highly targeted, a bunch of receptions. He’s a volume player. He gets the ball a lot. They put the ball in his hand,” Morris said. “He’s like all those guys, JSNs, Nacua’s and all the guys in our division, where they target him a lot and he’s heavily targeted.
“Then you’ve got that freak on the other side, [George] Pickens, sometimes on the same side. He’s got freak-like ability. He’s a great mover. He’s very versatile, can do a bunch of different things. He can shock you in all types of ways down the field, vertical or with catch and run. They’re a very, very difficult crew. Very excited about the matchup.”
Lamb is the second-leading receiver in receptions, yards, and touchdowns. Only Jaxon Smith-Njigba is putting up better numbers than him. That shows how elite Lamb is performing this season.
The 49ers have done a fine job against him in the past. However, he’s on a different level this year, so he may be too tough to slow down. Keeping it silent will be nearly impossible.
Especially because Pickens is on the other side. He hasn’t been as great as last season, but he’s still an issue. He’s liable to pop off in a game at any moment.
This makes the status of the 49ers’ starting cornerbacks critical. Renardo Green (back) and Deommodore Lenoir (foot) have missed two practices this week .
If they can practice on Friday, they’ll likely play against the Cowboys. But they might be compromised, making it an even greater challenge facing Lamb and Pickens.
The 49ers’ pass rush will be key to limiting the damage Lamb and Pickens can do. Green and Lenoir are the only capable corners to match up with Dallas’ lethal duo.
If neither can go, it’ll likely be a long day for rookie Ephesians Prysock, Nate Hobbs, and Jack Jones. What a terrible time for Green and Lenoir to be hurt.

title: Why 49ers QB Mac Jones is So Glad the NFL Trade Deadline is Over
full_text:
One of the key stories from the trade deadline is that backup San Francisco 49ers quarterback Mac Jones is still on their roster.
Jones is in the second and final year of his contract, yet despite incessant rumors about his departure from San Francisco, he's still here. That's likely because the front office won't let him go for anything less than a Day 1 or second-round draft pick.
With Jones set to back up Brock Purdy for the remainder of his contract, he admitted that he had an inkling that a potential departure was on the horizon.
“I figured something was going on,” Jones told NBC Sports Bay Area on Wednesday. “I mean, when everyone starts talking about it, I guess you have to eventually think something was going on.
“The whole offseason, that’s all you hear about,” he said. “And you know, if one guy gets hurt, I’m one of the first names that comes up. That’s great. But, also, I like the situation I’m in."
Jones acknowledged that he can now maintain his approach and work ethic, knowing that he remains with the team.
"I'm not taking anything for granted, and I know that at some point this year, if I'm needed, I'll be ready and I'm going to go sling it," he stated.
“I’m just grateful for that and knowing that my time will come when God wants it to happen. And right now I'm in that waiting-slash-preparing phase and supporting phase with Brock. I’m going to do whatever I can to help him get ready.
"I just really want to keep winning and not be a distraction. I'm glad that the trade deadline is over."
Despite rumors that have circulated for the better part of a year, Jones has, to his credit, once again stated that his full focus is fulfilling his contract with the 49ers.
“No, no, no,” Jones said. “I like it here. To be honest, I'm treating it like I just got traded here today. So I'm going to continue to prove that I can play and be here when I'm needed.
“There's always speculation at the trade deadline, and to be talked about is good. But, obviously, it's over and I'm really happy to be here. It would be one thing if I were on a team I didn't want to be on.”
The 49ers should provide him with an extension in the offseason, with Jones hinting at what a new one could look like: “What's the price tag on that?” Jones asked. “To me, it's multiple millions of dollars to have fun and be on a winning team because I've been on the other side of that, too, when you're not really having fun and you're not winning.”

title: 5 Major Questions that will Determine Whether the 49ers Beat the Cowboys
full_text:
As the San Francisco 49ers get ready for their Week 10 matchup, there are plenty of questions that will be answered.
The 49ers room could look crowded or empty depending on who is healthy that week. In Week 10, we are looking for the status of Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel. Right now, it appears the 49ers are going to take things easy with Evans, so he might be leaning towards out. Samuel is closer to playing.
The question will be how that impacts things. The 49ers added Keenan Allen; they got Demarcus Robinson back last week, and Jordan Watkins has started to take steps. Who starts and plays most?
Allen just played against the Dallas Cowboys last week and had four catches for 26 yards. Now, he is in a completely different offense facing the same team. More than that, Allen is not going to get a bye week this season. So, do the 49ers ease him in? Do they start him? What is his role?
The 49ers opened the practice windows for Nate Hobbs and CJ West. Right now, it sounds like Hobbs is most likely going to return this week. West is more likely to come back the following week. Still, whether or not the return happens, and then how much either depth piece sees the field, will be worth following on Sunday.
The team had to finish the game without Renardo Green and Deommodore Lenoir. Both are expected to be day-to-day at practice, and their game status will be monitored. San Francisco is thin at cornerback. They have rookie fourth-rounder Ephesians Prysock behind those two. They could get Hobbs back, but he has been out since before the season started. Then, they just brought back Jack Jones, whom they cut. Does this signal they are worried about their depth?
The 49ers appear to have a three-man safety rotation that is not going away any time soon. Kyle Shanahan confirmed they will lean into Marques Sigle, Malik Mustapha, and Ji’Ayir Brown and rotate all three together. Who leads the way this week, and does anyone see their snaps reduced?

title: These Two 49ers Could Get Cut when Players Return from Injury
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers opened the practice window for defensive tackle C.J. West and cornerback Nate Hobbs. Both of them could be back on the roster as soon as this week, and if not, they will likely get called up the following week. It raises the question of what the 49ers will do to open roster spots for these two.
The initial thoughts are that adding a cornerback and defensive tackle would mean waiving a player from each spot. Still, they placed Gracen Halton on the IR to add Keenan Allen. They have been thin at defensive tackle as well.
They could cut Sebastian Valdez, who would likely be inactive when West comes back. Valdez will likely make it back to the practice squad. Still, he has flashes during his limited time, and the team needs his depth.
At cornerback, they already cut Jack Jones, who is back on the practice squad. Renardo Green and Deommodore Lenoir are both banged up. Siran Neal is a cornerback but is mostly on the roster for special teams. So, their only outside cornerback depth is Ephesians Prysock. They are not going to cut any cornerbacks to bring Hobbs back.
Two names stand out that are better bets to get released than Valdez. The 49ers should release Brandin Cooks and Khalil Kareem.
At receiver, Cooks had a role, but it is fading. Jordan Watkins produces more, Keenan Allen was added, and Demarcus Robinson is now healthy after returning in Week 9. He was ahead of Jacob Cowing on the receiver pecking order, but Cowing has return duties.
At best, Cooks is the 49ers' fourth receiver. If one of Evans or Samuel can return to the lineup, Cooks would have to be inactive in Week 10. With both likely back soon, his role is phased out.
If the 49ers do not activate West this week, it could give Cooks one more week. However, that should be the swap.
Hobbs is almost definitely coming back this week, and the name to cut is Kareem, who was inactive last week. The 49ers added Kareem when the depth chart was thin. Since then, Nick Bosa and Mykel Williams have returned to the lineup. With Romello Height and Keion White in the mix, his depth is not needed. He will also be easy to bring back to the practice squad.
The first name to get cut when Hobbs gets back is Kareem. When West is healthy, Cooks should get cut.

title: Buccaneers Offense On Pace to Achieve Rare NFL Feat
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers aren't dead in the water just yet despite their 3-6 record.
They sit just half a game out of the NFC South lead, but enter the midway point of the season on a bye week, where they could drop further down.
The Bucs have been great defensively and running the ball, but they have struggled to get anything going in the passing game, leading to the offense being one-dimensional.
That one-dimensional offense has them on pace for a rare NFL feat if things are to stay the course.
Tampa Bay currently has 1,475 rushing yards to 1,277 passing yards at the midway point of the season. Not a single other NFL team can say the same.
It's an interesting statistic, to say the least, and it drastically shows just how poor the passing game has been for the Bucs in today's modern NFL.
The last time a team finished a season with more rushing yards than passing yards was when the Chicago Bears did so in 2022, when they ran for 3,014 yards and threw for 2,219. They finished the season 3-14.
Baker Mayfield has not lived up to the contract extension that he made such a big deal about leading up to the season, putting up the worst statistical season of his veteran career.
Mayfield also missed time due to injury, meaning the Bucs had to rely on the ground game more with undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels at the helm.
The play-calling by Zac Robinson and the lack of elite weapons on the outside have also been inhibitors of the passing attack.
It would be shocking to see the Bucs outpace their passing yardage with rushing yardage, but that is how things are rolling as of now.
The hope is that things can get figured out when it comes to throwing the ball over the bye week, thus making the offense more balanced. If they are able to do so, then it will be tough for opposing defenses to try to cover every aspect of the offense, leading to more points on the board and more wins.

title: One Major Buccaneers Concern Must Be Addressed During Bye Week
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are spending their bye week searching for answers.
The Bucs are just half a game out of the NFC South, but they're 3-6 and in danger of plummeting further. Tampa Bay has an elite defense and an elite running game, but their passing game is among the NFL's worst and is dragging the whole team down.
Much has been discussed about the passing game as a whole, but there's one specific part of it that's a major concern for Tampa Bay through nine weeks — and the Bucs need to find a way to fix it fast if they want the passing game to take off.
The best teams in football — and even average ones, for that matter — find ways to pass to the middle of the field. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have failed spectacularly when it comes to this, and their pass game is paying for it as a result.
The league average for passes between the hashes is at 10.4% this year so far. The Bucs have thrown just 11 passes to the middle of the field all year (Baker Mayfield has thrown eight and Jalon Daniels has thrown three). That's just 4.9% of their attempts so far this year, and both their total attempts to the middle of the field and their percentage of throws to the middle of the field rank 31st in the NFL — only the Denver Broncos are worse in both categories, per SumerSports.
The best team in the league at finding the middle of the field is the Houston Texans in both attempts and percentage of attempts. Some of the NFL's best offenses lead the league in middle-of-the-field percentage, like the Jacksonville Jaguars (No. 2), the Chicago Bears (No. 3) and the San Francisco 49ers (No. 4), among others.
Tampa Bay's passing offense has the entire area blocked off at the moment, and the team is suffering for it. But why aren't they getting the ball there so far this season?
There are multiple factors, of course.
The Buccaneers don't seem to have any receivers who can survive in high-traffic areas and have the route-running acumen on inside-breaking routes to thrive there. This also involves physical toughness — first-round draft pick Emeka Egbuka has struggled with that for most of his NFL career to date; Chris Godwin is in the tail end of his career and his age makes it harder to take those hits; and wideout Tez Johnson is among the smallest wideouts in the NFL.
That could be making offensive coordinator Zac Robinson spooked, and could prevent him from putting first reads between the hashes in a progression-based read system. Mayfield could also be frightened to throw to the middle of the field as many NFL quarterbacks have been in the past, but with Daniels throwing there at just as little a rate, Robinson's scheming could be more of the culprit.
No matter what the reason is, the Bucs need to figure out how to unlock that part of the field in the passing game. Getting it to at least a league-average rate would be very beneficial for this team, but it will take a combination of multiple parties on the offensive side of the ball to make that happen.
Tampa Bay will play the Detroit Lions on the road in Week 11 after their bye week this weekend.

title: Why Bucs Bringing Back Bruce Arians Would Be a Big Mistake
full_text:
When many think of the idea of Bruce Arians returning to coaching, specifically to the Buccaneers, there's excitement and a desire for it to happen. I fall into this camp — Arians would give the team a jolt of energy they have missed since he left following the 2021 season.
However, there are factors that need to be considered here when we look at the entirety of the picture of what it would truly mean for this organization if Arians were to once more be the head coach of this football team..
This first question that needs to be asked — Would Bruce Arians genuinely be ok with the Bucs firing Todd Bowles so he could take his job?
Remember, Arians retired in part so Bowles could have a chance to be a head coach again, and for his health. Arians is incredibly loyal to his coaches, and Bowles has been a friend and protege to Arians for many years. I still believe the Buccaneers will move on from Bowles after this season, but it needs to be mentioned that Arians might not be keen on joining the team that fires his close friend.
The second question that needs to be asked is whether Baker Mayfield and this offense would be a good fit for Arians if he were to come back.
Tom Brady, Mike Evans and more aren't around anymore, and I think Mayfield has a great arm, but there could be a lot of similarities to the 2019 Jameis Winston season rather than the great years of Brady.
Also, how would Emeka Egbuka and the other receivers look? This hasn't exactly impressed with Zac Robinson as offensive coordinator, so would they be a good fit in Arians' offense? Would we see a big dip in usage of Bucky Irving, one of the Bucs' best offensive players? Arians loves passing the football and it always felt that the running game would get put to the side. Would you be okay with potentially the best offensive player on the team, Irving, getting the ball less?
Finally, one must consider that Arians would bring back many of his guys on the offensive coaching staff, I imagine. Byron Leftwich could be back as OC, or Harold Goodwin, or even Thad Lewis. Also, I imagine either Larry Foote, Kacy Rodgers or James Bettcher would be DC without Bowles coming back to fill the role.
It also must be said that in a scenario where Arians coaches for a couple more seasons and retires again, would the Bucs simply promote a Leftwich, Goodwin, Lewis, Foote or Rodgers to the head coaching role as they did with Bowles? Would you be okay with that potential future? I would say that this is the biggest question one would need to ask themselves.

title: Will Buccaneers Regret Not Trading Away Players?
full_text:
We are at the midway point of the NFL season, and the trade deadline has come and gone without the Tampa Bay Buccaneers making any moves whatsoever.
At 3-6, the Bucs could have decided to sell off some of their players in order to obtain some draft capital or become buyers to elevate certain positions on their roster to make a strong run at the NFC South and a playoff run.
General manager Jason Licht and company decided to do neither, standing pat with what they currently have. But was not selling and looking ahead to the future the right move?
The argument for selling usually comes from recognizing when a team's ceiling doesn't match its financial layout or expectations, allowing the front office to accelerate into its next chapter rather than trying to force a square peg into a round hole.
The Bucs' ceiling is pretty obvious at this point — potentially make the playoffs with a likely first-round exit.
For a roster that currently has aging "star" players taking up large portions of the cap with heavy extensions, injecting cost-controlled, youthful talent and draft picks into the future of the team might have been the better move. Especially given how weak the division is.
In today's modern NFL, maximizing your asset value comes at a premium, and it appears that Licht and company missed the ball on that once again when they could have received mid-to-high draft capital from contending teams for the services of guys like Vita Vea and Antoine Winfield Jr.
With how weak the NFC South currently is, the Bucs remain in the thick of things, just half a game back of the division lead. With the front office deciding not to move anyone at the deadline, they believe they have a legitimate chance of winning the division behind their strong running game and top defense.
Trading away key veterans mid-season would have signaled that the organization is looking ahead rather than fighting for its playoff hopes in the present. For Todd Bowles and his staff, waving the white flag when you still have a shot at making the playoffs would ruin the recent momentum and could fracture the dynamic within the locker room.
Whether management will come to regret not selling at the deadline will remain to be seen until the results start piling up on the field over the back half of the season.
If the Bucs somehow pull things together and make the playoffs, not selling would seemingly have been the right move.
However, if they miss the playoffs for a second consecutive season, then all aspects of the organization will come under scrutiny for not doing what it takes to either win or set the team up for a better future.

title: Bruce Arians Not Against Returning to Buccaneers Job 'If It Were Open'
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are a long way out from their Super Bowl run. It's only been six years, but since then, the Bucs have had a winning record just twice and have won a single playoff game after winning it all in 2020.
Head coach Todd Bowles has been under fire for some time now following a late-season collapse last year and a 3-6 run at the moment. Bowles took the job in 2022 after head coach Bruce Arians stepped down due to health issues, and since then, Tampa Bay has been up and down.
Arians has been out of the game for a bit, but during a recent podcast appearance with Jordan Schultz, he said that he's now open to coaching again — and that maybe, if his old job were open, he wouldn't be against taking it.
“This is the first time I had the itch again. I had no desire to go back,” Arians said. “After open-heart surgery, I have so much more energy. It's amazing... we'll see what happens."
News: Super Bowl-winning HC Bruce Arians tells me he wants to return to coaching. “This is the first time I had the itch again. I had no desire to go back. … After open-heart surgery, I have so much more energy.” Full interview drops soon! pic.twitter.com/QyNbIYmsyi
It gets more interesting, though. Tampa Bay Times writer Rick Stroud contacted Arians after the clip and asked if he would be interested in returning to Tampa Bay as head coach. His response?
I asked Bruce Arians if he would consider returning to the Bucs. “If it were open, yes,” he said. https://t.co/akaIE1rPTw
Arians is no longer tied to Tampa Bay as a head coach, so no team would have to trade for him. He would be free to pursue any coaching job he would want to pursue, and that would include Tampa Bay's should Bowles be fired at any point before or after the regular season.
Arians is arguably the most successful coach in Bucs history, winning a Super Bowl with the team and netting a .655 winning percentage with 31 wins — the best mark in the franchise.
The Bucs had a strong tenure with Arians, but Bowles hasn't been fired just yet, and Arians would be an older candidate in a league that is increasingly turning toward younger coaches as offense and defense evolve at a rapid rate.
It remains to be seen just how much interest Arians will draw, even from Tampa Bay. For right now, though, the Bucs are 3-6 and resting during their bye week before trying to string some wins together for the remaining eight games of the season.

title: Buccaneers' Most Disappointing Players at Halfway Point of 2026 Season
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers were looking to win the NFC South in a big way in 2026, but nine games into the season, they've won just three games.
The Bucs are 3-6, and although they are technically tied for the NFC South lead, they've had some major struggles over the course of the year. They were looking to count on a number of players to help them win this offseason, and some of those players haven't been delivering.
Here are some of Tampa Bay's most disappointing players this season so far:
The Buccaneers were searching for a leading wide receiver after the departure of Mike Evans, and Emeka Egbuka, who the Bucs drafted in the first round a year ago, was primed to take that spot. Halfway through the year, the Bucs are still looking.
Egbuka has been hurt for a few games this year, but even then, he's netted just 31 receptions for 278 yards. The passing game as a whole is brutal at the moment, but he doesn't seem to have the ability to beat his man from rep to rep and make things happen on his own accord.
Egbuka started off strong last year, but now, he's struggled to stand out. For a first-round pick, that's tough.
Another first-round pick, Rueben Bain Jr. will have plenty of time to course-correct. But the Bucs thought they got a steal with Bain in the draft, and so far, that has been far from the truth.
Bain only has two solo tackles across the entire year. He has one sack and one forced fumble, and he has just a 9.9% pressure rate on his pass-rushing snaps, per SumerSports.
Bain has been dropped in coverage a lot and he's still getting used to the NFL level. But the Buccaneers thought they drafted a game-wrecker, and Bain has had very little impact over the first nine games of the year.
Perhaps the most concerning name on this list, Mayfield signed a three-year extension worth $55 million a year before the season started. The move was controversial at the time, and Mayfield hasn't done much to silence his doubters over the first frame of the season.
Mayfield did miss three games with a dislocated thumb injury, but outside of those games, he has played very poorly. He's thrown just three touchdowns to four interceptions (one a pick-six) and has turned the ball over seven total times.
Mayfield's pressure-to-sack ratio is just under 32%, and he has a dropback EPA/play of −0.297 so far this season — dead last among qualifying quarterbacks, per SumerSports. The entire passing offense has been awful in Tampa Bay, and while offensive coordinator Zac Robinson and the wideouts have a part in that, Mayfield is also a fairly big one.
Winfield Jr. has been hurt a lot this season, and he might miss some time again with an ankle injury after leaving the game against the Chicago Bears. Even when he's been in, though, he hasn't lived up to his four-year, $81 million deal.
Winfield has 22 solo tackles, one forced fumble and one pass defended in six games played. His replacement while injured, Ifeatu Melifonwu, has played well in his stead, and Winfield hasn't done much to stand out from him, even when healthy.
The Bucs will look for him to make a bigger impact going forward in the back half of the season.
The Bucs re-signed Riley Dixon this offseason, knowing that he was one of the worst punters across the league last year. So far, that gamble isn't exactly paying off.
Dixon is 31st in the NFL in yards per punt (44.4) and he's dead last in the NFL in net yards per punt (38.4). The Bucs have an excellent defense, but Dixon is doing them no favors with his lack of distance, and his poor punting has hurt the team a few times this year when it came to flipping the field.
The Bucs appear to be rolling with Dixon for the rest of the year, and if Tampa Bay wants to win games, Dixon will have to be much better.

title: Bucs Had Something Other NFL Teams Desperately Wanted Before Trade Deadline
full_text:
Just a few weeks ago, the chances of Jason Licht and Tampa Bay Buccaneers becoming sellers at the NFL trade deadline seemed like more of a certainty than a possibility.
However, back-to-back victories over the Panthers and Falcons — the Bucs' first divisional games of the season — quickly altered the likelihood of that scenario coming to fruition. Not only were the Buccaneers 3-5 and undefeated in the NFC South all of a sudden, but the two teams they were chasing in the standings were no longer out of reach.
Although the Buccaneers were unable to defeat the Chicago Bears on Sunday Night Football less than 48 hours before the trade deadline, Todd Bowles' defense put together another incredible performance that (largely because of the atrocious play of Baker Mayfield ) still wasn't enough to keep the winning streak alive.
However, with the Buccaneers looking like a defensive juggernaut and just one game outside of first place in the division to boot, it wasn't a surprise to see the team stand pat at the deadline in the end.
According to NFL Insider Jeremy Fowler , the Buccaneers had plenty of interest in one of their defensive players.
"The Bucs had strong interest in veteran defensive lineman A'Shawn Robinson, but they rarely trade at the deadline and are still in the NFC South race."
Although there had been plenty of chatter about defensive players like Vita Vea and Yaya Diaby being possible trade candidates when the Bucs' were considered potential sellers, 31-year-old Robinson was the player who other teams were coveting most.
When Robinson was signed as a free agent in the offseason, there wasn't exactly a ton of fanfare regarding the acquisition. However, since joining the Buccaneers, there's no denying that the veteran DT has been one of Bowles' best players.
Beyond bringing a nasty edge to the field and vocal leadership to the locker room, Robinson has been extremely consistent and productive for the Bucs so far. Not only has Robinson produced 24 total tackles, one sack, eight QB pressures, three passes defended and two interceptions, but he's been very good against the run as well.
In fact, Robinson's 88.3 run defense grade is the second-highest among all interior defensive linemen in the NFL. His overall defensive grade is nearly as impressive at 85.8, which is the third-best mark in the league at his position.
It doesn't really matter now, but it's still interesting to learn that Robinson was one of (if not the most) desirable trade targets on the Buccaneers' roster ahead of the trade deadline. That being said, once you dive into the impact he's made on the field for his new team, it's pretty easy to see why.
It's also easy to see why the Buccaneers decided to keep him around. If the team hopes to make a push in the second half of the season to take control of the division and make the playoffs, they're going to need Robinson to play a big part in that. Just like he has so far.

title: Buccaneers' Passing Game Could Be Historically Bad in 2026
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have an electrifying run game that ranks among the best in the league and a suffocating defense that might actually be the best in the league. So why are they 3-6 during their bye week?
The answer is in their passing offense. Tampa Bay's passing offense is last in the league in yards per game (141.9) and yards per pass (5.9). But it goes a lot deeper than that once you dive in to advanced metrics.
This Buccaneers passing offense isn't simply bad — according to success rate, it may be historically bad.
Tampa Bay's is last in the NFL EPA/dropback (-0.297) and 28th in explosive pass rate. But when you take success rate into account, the offense has been dire so far.
Success rate is defined by successful plays. A successful play is typically considered to be 40% or more of the required yards on first down, 60% or more of the required yards on second down and then 100% or more of the required yards on third or fourth down.
Tampa Bay's success rate in the passing game so far this year is a paltry 35.4%. As CBS reporter JP Acosta noted on Twitter, that's only bad, it's the 11th-worst passing offense by success rate since 2010 in Weeks 1-9.
According to @TruMediaSports , these are the 20 worst offenses in the NFL since 2010 through weeks 1-9 when it comes to Passing Success Rate. 4 teams from 2026 being on here is...staggering, and the 2026 Broncos just missed the cut! pic.twitter.com/h94onOVPpx
Obviously, there is still time for this to change for Tampa Bay going forward. The list also, interestingly enough, features three other teams from 2026 — the Los Angeles Chargers at No. 4, the Philadelphia Eagles at No. 6 and the Minnesota Vikings at No. 17.
That shouldn't distract from the fact that, if this trend continues, the Bucs could be a historically bad passing offense. That falls on everyone involved, from offensive coordinator Zac Robinson to quarterback Baker Mayfield and his largely ineffective receiving corps.
The Bucs don't have a ton of time to turn things around, but they'll have to do their best. Every NFC South team currently has three wins at the moment, so the division is all for the taking — and to take it, Tampa Bay will have to get going through the air.

title: Buccaneers Are Wasting One of Their Defense's Best Seasons
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers achieved one of their biggest goals heading into 2026 — they boast one of the best defenses in the NFL.
That hasn't been winning them games, though. The Buccaneers are 3-6 at the moment, and despite a weak NFC South keeping the team in the hunt, they've generally struggled throughout the year. There are a few places to attribute those struggles, but the main culprit is the other side of the ball — Tampa Bay's offense has been greatly failing it.
But just how good is Tampa Bay's defense, and just how bad is its offense?
To say that the Bucs defense is playing great football right now might even be an understatement. They're playing some of the best defense in franchise history.
The Bucs defense boasts the best EPA/play in the NFL, per SumerSports (-0.21) and the sixth-best defensive success rate (41.73%). They're first in the league in EPA/dropback (-0.253) and fourth in the league in EPA/rush (-0.141), and they're the seventh best team in the league when it comes to stopping explosive plays of 20 or more yards.
Their real success this season, however, has been turnovers. Tampa Bay leads the league with 16 interceptions, three more than the second-place Green Bay Packers, and they lead the NFL in total turnovers with 21. Incredibly, 12 of those 21 turnovers have come in their last three games.
The Bucs are generating turnovers at an unsustainable rate, so that may dry up at some point. But even so, they have the passing game and running game prowess to suffocate defenses, and that makes them one of the NFL's best units.
This is the unit head coach Todd Bowles has wanted out of his defense all along. It should be winning them games, but it isn't — and that's because his team's other unit is losing them.
Tampa Bay's rushing offense has been inflated a tad analytically due to its incredible rushing efforts against the Carolina Panthers and the Atlanta Falcons, but it remains elite — it's the best rushing offense in the NFL in yards per game, ranks 10th in rushing EPA/play and fourth in explosive rushing plays of 12 or more yards.
That's not the problem. The passing offense is.
Tampa Bay's passing offense ranks dead last in EPA/dropback (-0.297) and 28th in explosive pass rate. The team's quarterback, Baker Mayfield, also ranks dead last among 33 qualified quarterbacks in EPA/dropback (-0.324), ranks 27th in completion percentage (60.6%) and net yards per attempt (5.27) and 30th in passer rating (74.9).
Mayfield also continues to take unnecessary sacks that hurt his team. His 10.59% sack rate is 31st in the league despite facing just the 16th-most pressure.
No wide receiver in Tampa Bay has over 300 receiving yards, and Emeka Egbuka leads the team with 278. Nothing about the pass game works or is even average, and it's dragging the entire team down week after week — especially when the Bucs have to play good opponents.
Tampa Bay needs to figure out its passing game fast if it wants to do anything meaningful in the postseason (should it even get there at all). the Bucs have an excellent defense that can hang with any team, but with a passing offense that can hang with none of them, that defense is largely going to waste.

title: Why Didn't the Buccaneers Make a Move at the Trade Deadline?
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline has come and gone, and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers have completely stayed put.
The Bucs did not make any trades, neither selling off a player nor buying from another squad. General manager Jason Licht and head coach Todd Bowles are confident in what they have — at least including the cost of giving up or trading for a player, anyway — as the pair try to win another NFC South title.
That being said, the Bucs are 3-6 and started the season 0-4 — so why stay put at the deadline? To keep it simple, it's a little complicated.
To go more in depth, the Buccaneers were in a sort of trade limbo.
The Bucs were not good enough at the deadline to buy. There are a lot of problems with this team's offense, from the coaching to the talent, and an extra wide receiver or tight end probably wouldn't fix things. That would also require giving up draft capital — a luxury for teams competing, not for teams with a losing record like the Bucs.
At the same time, though, Tampa Bay isn't quite bad enough to sell. The Bucs are still just a half a game out of the NFC South (and will likely be a game back once the Saints and Panthers play), so they're in contention to win the division, as crazy as it seems.
Selling off a player like Vita Vea or Antoine Winfield Jr. may seem appealing for the long term future, but Bowles and Licht need to win now. To do that, they need all the players they can muster, including the team's aging stars on the roster.
There's also the fact that the Bucs rarely trade in season at all. Licht has done it just once, trading for Jets defensive tackle Steve McLendon and giving up a sixth-round pick. Licht highly values draft capital — perhaps more than any other GM in football — and he isn't interested in shuffling around his players while the season is ongoing.
The Bucs stayed put at the deadline. Now, they have to prove that it was a good idea by winning the division and making the playoffs.

title: Best — and Worst — Case Scenario for Titans' Week 10 Matchup With Jaguars
full_text:
It's always a weird feeling to return to weekly football after a team is out on the bye, but it's especially weird when that bye crossed over with the trade deadline. The Tennessee Titans experienced a lot of moving and shaking, and haven't played a football game in two weeks.
The Titans won't at all be welcomed back onto the scene by the Jacksonville Jaguars. 6-2 and leading the AFC South with ease, the Jaguars bulked up at the deadline in an effort to make a legitimate Super Bowl push this year.
Tennessee may have prioritized their draft future at the deadline, but multiple players on this team still have something to prove right now; leader among them is Cam Ward. As best we can tell, here's the best and worst-case outcome for the Titans in Week 10.
The Jaguars won't be entirely stopped, but if Tennessee can initiate another score-for-score battle like they did against the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 8, a few adjustments could lead to a victory here.
Ward, of course, would have to outpace QB Trevor Lawrence in that case. Lawrenece had a similarly poor start to his career as Ward, but has since had the time to come into his own as a franchise-leading player. The Titans are hoping the same of Ward, and his first 300-yard game in Week 8 promised that such a development could be on the way.
In Tennessee's best-case, Ward comes up with similar numbers and a weakened TItans defense does just enough at home to keep Lawrence and company at bay. It should help Ward that newly-acquired All-Pro S Jessie Bates won't be competing for Jacksonville just yet.
Although it will certainly hurt Ward that WR Carnell Tate isn't playing. On top of their best offensive playmaker, the Titans will also be without standout rookie LB Anthony Hill Jr., veteran LB Cody Barton, and multiple starters on the offensive line.
In the Titans' worst outcome, these absences lead to gaps that Tennessee just can't fully seal against a great team. Lawrence runs away from the Titans' defense, and Ward fails to overcome the piling injuries on his side of the ball.
This one may be the likeliest of the two, but again, Ward has a lot to prove. It'd be fair to say going in that his performance, in spite of the injuries around him, will define the first game of the Titans' season that couldn't be defined as a "must-win."
It's a must-improve game, wherein all eyes are on the QB who could decide it.
